title: Banished

flavor.value: ''Take command of this mobile host of angelic warriors that have sided with Hell to reclaim their home.''

summary: Banished [[File:ClanBanished.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]]. It is available at the start of the game.

title: Fel

flavor.value: The brilliant and resourceful commander of the Banished, Fel vows to free Heaven from her brother's tyranny. Whether or not her wounded heart will ever heal, however, is yet to be seen.

tables: Fixed bug where text on Fel's Unchained path would sometimes be incorrect. Fixed bug where Fel's Unchained upgrade line would give extra Valor on Shift.
summary: Fel is the default [[Champion]] of the [[Banished]] clan. All three of her paths revolve around {{IconLink|Valor}}, which can grant her enormous damage and defense if used properly. She also starts with {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} regardless of path, which lets her double the additional {{Attack}} from each point of {{IconLink|Valor}}. Her starter card is [[Just Cause]].

title: Talos

ability.value: {{AbilityBox|Flight|2|Move to a targeted location on any floor.}}

flavor.value: Talos has a personal score to settle with Heaven for casting her out. Loyal, passionate, and often terrifying, she is the fearsome right-hand angel and friend to Fel.

tables: Battle Cleric I & II attack increased from {{Attack|8}}, {{Attack|15}} -> {{Attack|15}}, {{Attack|20}}. Celestial Radiance stats increased from {{AttackHealth|10|16}}, {{AttackHealth|15|25}}, {{AttackHealth|30|50}} -> {{AttackHealth|15|20}}, {{AttackHealth|25|35}}, {{AttackHealth|40|60}}.
summary: Talos is the alternate [[Champion]] of the [[Banished]] clan. Unlike [[Fel]], she is intended as a support unit, buffing your other units rather than being powerful in her own right. Depending on the path used, she can either buff their damage through status effects or provide permanent scaling over the course of the run. Her starter card is [[Inspire (spell)|Inspire]].

title: Just Cause

flavor.value:
"Put away that toy, sister. You've never been able to fight me."
"Maybe before I couldn't. But now, I must."

tables: Putting '''Emberstone''' on '''Just Cause''' often provides a no-frills way of improving your {{Ember}} economy.

'''Smolderstone''' also accomplishes what '''Emberstone''' does while also adding [[Consume]]. While '''Just Cause''' can be a good card, it still doesn't feel bad consuming it most of the time either.

'''Twinstone''' allows you to trigger {{IconLink|Shift}} twice with one card play, which is very useful for {{IconLink|Shift}} builds. This upgrade should almost always be used alongside '''Emberstone''', as without it you need to pay for the card twice.
summary: Just Cause is [[Fel]]'s starter card. It moves a unit to the front and gives them {{IconLink|Valor|2}}.

title: Inspire (spell)

flavor.value: To the surprise of all, it was Talos who stood before her fellow soldiers and urged them to continue fighting. "For our homes, for our lives, and for a united future!" she cried.

tables: '''Emberstone''' makes '''Inspire''' free to play, allowing it to always provide some value when drawn.

'''Smolderstone''' makes '''Inspire''' free to play as well, but also gives it '''Consume''', allowing it to get out of the way after your first deck cycle in favor of drawing more high-impact cards later.
summary: Inspire is [[Talos]]'s starter card. It grants {{IconLink|Valor|1}} to all friendly units on the floor.

title: Upbeat Warbler

flavor.value: "Some souls live with rage in their hearts, others with a song. Anyway, does anyone know what this brass thing is? It sure does make a groovy sound."

tables: '''Heartstone''' is good for this unit to ensure it doesn't die to {{IconLink|Sweep}}.

While niche, '''Speedstone''' can be a sensible upgrade with [[Iron-tongue]] if you don't have other units that can effectively wield it, as '''Upbeat Warbler''' would otherwise be a good candidate for it due to his low {{Attack}} but he doesn't give himself {{IconLink|Quick}}. (Plus, if you're using '''Upbeat Warbler''', you don't have much other use for this upgrade anyway.)
summary: Upbeat Warbler is a common [[Banished]] unit. He gives all friendly units on his floor {{IconLink|Quick}}.

title: Lead Songbird

ability.value: {{IconLink|Valor}} on friendly units adds {{Attack|+1}} per stack.

flavor.value: "Holding the mic in my feet, Destroying the enemies to my beat, Won't ever admit defeat!"

tables: '''Lead Songbird''''s main priority is to stay alive, and '''Heartstone''' is a cheap upgrade that helps with that. '''Largestone''' can be considered if your plan is to put '''Lead Songbird''' on a relatively empty floor and then move it to your main floor, as in that case {{Capacity}} doesn't matter.
summary: Lead Songbird is an uncommon [[Banished]] unit. It grants all friendly units an extra {{Attack|+1}} per stack of {{IconLink|Valor}} they have.

title: Punk Shredder

flavor.value: "Punk rock will always be there for you when nothing else is."

tables: [[Punk Shredder]]'s main priority is to stay alive, and '''Heartstone''' is a cheap way to accomplish just that. '''Largestone''' can be considered if your plan is to put '''Punk Shredder''' on a relatively empty floor and then move it to your main floor, as in that case {{Capacity}} doesn't matter.
summary: Punk Shredder is an uncommon [[Banished]] unit. It has an {{IconLink|Enchant}} ability that grants other friendly units {{IconLink|Trample}}.

title: Avenger

flavor.value: Once the keepers of Heaven's Walls, their flails now protect Fel's army from their former allies.

tables: '''Dualstone''' causes '''Avenger''' to apply twice as much {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} on {{IconLink|Revenge}}, causing enemies to take three times as much damage from the first incoming attack instead of twice.

'''Largestone''' gives a significant boost to [[Avenger]]'s stats, providing him with increased survivability and enough damage to kill a [[Fallen Champion]] with no support. The boosted {{Health}} also pairs well with Shield of Wyngh.

'''Speedstone''' is useful when you want one of [[Avenger]]'s allies to make use of the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} he applies, as it prevents the unit from consuming his own {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}}.
'''Titanstone''' grants {{IconLink|Titanite}}, halving the damage '''Avenger''' takes, allowing him to survive for far longer and reducing the need to stack {{IconLink|Valor}} on him.

'''Savage Heart''' is an incredible upgrade for '''Avenger''', especially alongside {{IconLink|Dualism}} and {{IconLink|Trample}}. His {{Attack}} will naturally skyrocket due to his nature as a frontliner, and with {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} to complement him, he can easily deal thousands of damage in a single blow by the later rings. If '''Avenger''' is granted {{IconLink|Trample}}, he can clear whole waves of enemies effortlessly.
summary: Avenger is an uncommon [[Banished]] [[banner unit]]. He possesses a {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger that applies {{IconLink|Melee Weakness|1}} to the attacker.

title: Battle Dancer

flavor.value: "I used to say, 'dance is for everybody.' Now, I say the same of death."

tables: '''Frenzystone''' should be the most highly sought-after upgrade if '''Battle Dancer''' will be your main source of damage. When supported properly and taken with the right context, '''Battle Dancer''' will reach high {{Attack}} values very quickly, and capitalizing on this by giving it {{IconLink|Multistrike}} doubles the efficiency of this already rapid scaling.

'''Dualstone''' is always good on '''Battle Dancer'''. With {{IconLink|Dualism}}, its {{IconLink|Valor}} gain on {{IconLink|Shift}} grows from 3 to 6, making it even more efficient offensively and defensively.

'''Smidgestone''' is a strong pickup for '''Battle Dancer'''. Because '''Battle Dancer''' is most often used as a damage unit that ramps quickly, many lines will want to make multiples of it, slotting as many '''Battle Dancers''' on a floor as possible to not only increase the number of hits but also turn movement cards into floor-wide scaling. Reducing its size makes it much easier to assemble such lines without having to take [[Heaven's Light]]. However, if you have other solutions to fit multiple units on the floor such as Ascend/Descend cards with {{IconLink|Seekstone}}, you may want to take another upgrade instead.

'''Titanstone''' is a rare pickup for '''Battle Dancer''', but can work if your goal is to use it as a tank. With its fast {{IconLink|Valor}} gain, it is serviceable as a frontline tank in a pinch. {{IconLink|Titanite}} also protects '''Battle Dancer''' on early turns, making it easier to tank the first few waves and begin the process of converting its {{IconLink|Valor}} into {{IconLink|Armor}}.
summary: Battle Dancer is an uncommon [[Banished]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever it moves, it gains {{IconLink|Valor|3}}.

title: Demonic Fledgling

flavor.value: "Is it time for a break yet?"

tables: '''Frenzystone''' is excellent due to [[Demonic Fledgling]]'s high damage potential.

'''Dualstone''' doubles the amount of {{IconLink|Rage}} and {{IconLink|Valor}} the unit gains, making his damage scale much faster. It also makes him an even better user of [[Everlasting Light]], particularly when combined with '''Frenzystone'''.

Since '''Demonic Fledgling''' is most effective with lots of allies, '''Smidgestone''' can be worth consideration to more easily fit him onto a floor. This is unnecessary if you are overstacking his floor, however.

'''Largestone''' is not an ideal upgrade, but it provides a very relevant stat boost in the early game before your {{IconLink|Shift}} engine really comes online, and the increased {{Capacity}} is irrelevant if you are overstacking his floor with '''[[Ascend]]''' or '''[[Descend]]''' effects.
summary: Demonic Fledgling is an uncommon [[Banished]] [[banner unit]]. He gains {{IconLink|Valor|1}} on {{IconLink|Strike}}, and {{IconLink|Rage|2}} on {{IconLink|Shift}}.

title: Firebrand

flavor.value: They were once tasked with dousing the flames along the Rail. Now, they set the rails aflame.

tables: '''Dualstone''' is the strongest upgrade for '''Firebrand''', doubling the amount of {{IconLink|Valor}} gained on {{IconLink|Revenge}}, allowing '''Firebrand''' to stack up {{IconLink|Valor}} much faster and increasing both defense and damage. Combining '''Titanstone''' and '''Dualstone''' can make '''Firebrand''' virtually invincible, while combining '''Frenzystone''' and '''Dualstone''' gives her the equivalent of {{Attack|+8}} every {{IconLink|Revenge}}, skyrocketing her damage.

'''Titanstone''' represents a massive survivability boost for '''Firebrand''', cutting all damage taken in half allows her to both survive long enough to stack up {{IconLink|Valor}} and gain double the benefit from the {{IconLink|Valor}}'s {{IconLink|Armor}} effect.

'''Frenzystone''' allows '''Firebrand''' to hit twice, taking advantage of her high {{IconLink|Valor}}. However, if '''Firebrand''' is not your main damage dealer, then this upgrade might be better used elsewhere.

'''Largestone''' is a viable upgrade to prevent '''Firebrand''' from dying before she has a chance to build up {{IconLink|Valor}}, and the increased {{Capacity}} is usually not a concern, both because the Banished have several movement options and because '''Firebrand''' will often hold down a floor on her own. It also makes [[Shield of Wyngh]] much stronger thanks to giving her a total of {{Health|80}}.

All of [[Savagery's Boons|Savagery's boons]] are excellent on '''Firebrand''': * '''Savage Skin''' grants {{IconLink|Titanskin|5}} and allows the unit to become even harder to kill when combined with '''Titanstone''' and/or '''Dualstone'''. * '''Savage Heart''' grants permanent {{IconLink|Rage}} on {{IconLink|Revenge}}, which can provide a ridiculous amount of damage by the endgame, especially when combined with {{IconLink|Trample}} or {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, perhaps from [[Punk Shredder]] or [[Deathmetal Hymnist]]. * '''Savage Spirit''' boosts her {{Attack}} for every missing {{Health}} and grants her {{Health|+40}}, which is useful both for Shield of Wyngh and for ensuring she is not killed before she can build up {{IconLink|Valor}}.
summary: Firebrand is an uncommon [[Banished]] [[banner unit]]. She possesses a {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger that gives her {{IconLink|Valor|2}} whenever she takes damage.

title: Steadfast Crusader

ability.value: {{AbilityBox|Slam|2|'''[[Advance]]'''. Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to this unit's current {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Armor}}.}}

flavor.value: Heaven lost their most loyal soldiers when they cast the Crusaders from the Maw's gate.

tables: '''Largestone''' gives '''Steadfast Crusader''' the ability to kill frontliners with his ability through Ring 6, and the [[Banished]]'s proclivity to floor overstacking means the increased {{Capacity}} can be worked around.

'''Heartstone''' is a solid incremental improvement for '''Steadfast Crusader''', improving his durability and early-to-midgame utility, and his upgrade slots aren't too in-demand, making it a solid upgrade overall.
'''Titanstone''' grants {{IconLink|Titanite}}, and as '''Steadfast Crusader''' is a tank that values his {{Health}} this is appeciated.
summary: Steadfast Crusader is an uncommon [[Banished]] banner unit. His {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, Slam, [[Advance]]s the Steadfast Crusader, then deals damage equal to its current {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Armor}}. It has a cooldown of 2.

title: Swordmaiden

ability.value: {{IconLink|Summon}}: Draw an equipment card from your deck. {{IconLink|Artificer}}: Gain {{IconLink|Valor|8}}.

flavor.value: When they begin their training, the Swordmaidens chain themselves to their swords. They grow and live with their weapons until it is as much a part of themselves as a limb.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' takes full advantage of how efficiently '''Swordmaiden''' can gain {{IconLink|Valor}}. It also synergizes with [[Everlasting Light]] to increase floor-wide {{IconLink|Valor}} even further.
'''Dualstone''' drastically accelerates [[Swordmaiden]]'s {{IconLink|Valor}} scaling, granting her the equivalent of a [[Divinity]] and a half for every piece of equipment played.
'''Titanstone''', which grants {{IconLink|Titanite}}, is worthwhile if using '''Swordmaiden''' as a tank, as she will have plenty of {{IconLink|Armor}} after the first turn.

The '''Red Crown''', from the [[Cult of the Lamb]] event, will equip '''Swordmaiden''' with a random piece of equipment when she is played. This can get absurd fast if you duplicate the '''Swordmaiden''' with this upgrade.

'''Ascetic Penance''' and '''Ascetic Absolution''' grant {{Ember|3}} when played, which can potentially allow you to draw and play an expensive piece of equipment like [[Void Armament]], [[Soulsmelter]], or merged equipment. It can also let you duplicate '''Swordmaiden''', as many times as your {{Capacity}} and circumstances will let you, and load your deck with equipment cards for each of them to draw. You can get off to a very fast start, gaining tons of {{IconLink|Valor}} from the get-go (not to mention a floor full of equipped units). This upgrade gives you the {{Ember}} to pull this off.
summary: The Swordmaiden is an uncommon [[Banished]] [[banner unit]]. She draws an equipment card when played and gains {{IconLink|Valor|8}} whenever a friendly unit on her floor is given equipment.

title: Deathmetal Hymnist

flavor.value: "We're all a flash in the abyss, a song in the void. Dust will be our legacy!"

tables: '''Deathmetal Hymnist''''s main priority is to stay alive, and '''Heartstone''' is a cheap way to accomplish that. '''Largestone''' can be usable if using floor overstacking, depending on what you're doing.
summary: Deathmetal Hymnist is a rare [[Banished]] unit. It grants {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} to all other friendly units on the floor.

title: Death's Dancer

flavor.value: "Dance is a poem in which each kill is a step."

tables: '''Frenzystone''' grants {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, which can allow '''Death's Dancer''' to become your primary damage dealer when duplicated sufficiently. With three '''Death's Dancers''' with '''Frenzystone''', each {{IconLink|Shift}} trigger will add {{Attack|72}} to the floor in total, and this increases the more copies you can fit. If this seems likely to be your strategy, '''Speedstone''' makes up for the unit's low {{Health}}, but it should not be a priority otherwise.
'''Smidgestone''' reduces the unit's size, making it easier to fit many copies on the floor in the absence of '''[[Ascend]]''' and '''[[Descend]]''' effects.

'''Discarded Wings''' grants the '''Flight''' ability along with a small stat boost, which is highly useful for '''Death's Dancer'''. '''Archus' Wing''' is identical, but provides slightly more stats; those extra stats are usually not worth the risk of losing the wings entirely, however. '''Wings of Light''' is usually a downgrade, mostly because the '''Flying Strike''' ability has '''Cooldown 4''' instead of '''Cooldown 2'''.
summary: The Death's Dancer is a rare [[Banished]] [[banner unit]]. It grants {{Attack|+4}} to friendly units on {{IconLink|Shift}}.

title: Divine Dancer

flavor.value: "They clipped our wings, made us believe we were worthless. But I learned to dance in Hell, and even Heaven now fears my steps."

tables: '''Smidgestone''' reduces the unit's size, making it easier to fit many copies on the floor in the absence of '''[[Ascend]]''' and '''[[Descend]]''' effects.

'''Heartstone''' makes '''Divine Dancer''' less fragile at the start of combat, which could be important against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]] as he might otherwise be able to break through with the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} he applies.

'''Discarded Wings''' grants the '''Flight''' ability along with a small stat boost, which is highly useful for '''Divine Dancer'''. '''Archus' Wing''' is identical, but provides slightly more stats; those extra stats are usually not worth the risk of losing the wings entirely, however. '''Wings of Light''' is usually a downgrade, mostly because the '''Flying Strike''' ability has '''Cooldown 4''' instead of '''Cooldown 2'''.
summary: The Divine Dancer is a rare [[Banished]] [[banner unit]]. It grants {{IconLink|Armor|5}} to friendly units on {{IconLink|Shift}}.

title: Hostguard

ability.value: {{AbilityBox|Heavenly Slam|3|Move to a targeted location on any floor. Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to this unit's {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Armor}}.}}

flavor.value: "Seraph ripped the wings from my back. That pain will be dealt back tenfold."

tables: '''Largestone''' can make [[Hostguard]]'s stats even higher and increases '''Heavenly Slam''''s power significantly, and the increased {{Capacity}} is usually irrelevant.
'''Titanstone''' can be very helpful if you plan to use him as a frontliner.
summary: Hostguard is a rare [[Banished]] [[banner unit]]. His {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, Heavenly Slam, moves Hostguard to any position on any floor and then deals damage to the front enemy unit equal to the his {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Armor}}. It has a cooldown of 3.

title: Challenge

flavor.value:
"The new recruit stood on the bodies of her fallen enemies and pointed towards the Walls. Although she spoke no words, the challenge to Heaven was clear."
—Tome of the Lost Path

tables: '''Stackstone''' increases this card's utility against tanky frontliners like [[Avowed Gladiator]].
'''Twinstone''', coupled with an {{Ember}} discount, can double this card's disruptive power, either on the same target or different ones.
'''Emberstone''' is fairly practical here for {{Ember|-1}} on use, especially with '''Twinstone''', as this card is fairly easy to benefit from playing.
summary: Challenge is a common [[Banished]] card. It advances its target to the front and applies {{IconLink|Melee Weakness|1}} to it.

title: Cleave

effect.value: Deal damage to enemy units equal to {{Attack}} of the front friendly unit.

flavor.value: "Although my brother taught me that strength is in dominion, the Banished proved that true might is in our unity."

tables: '''Keepstone''' allows you to play this card every turn, allowing it to substitute for or supplement {{IconLink|Multistrike}} on your power units, letting them tear through challenging lategame waves with multiple tanky enemies. It also means most troublesome backliners will die before doing anything, and with a good enough frontline unit, this includes nasty Chosen variants.

'''Seekstone''' guarantees that you will be able to play '''Cleave''' from the very beginning of combat, as well as decreasing its cost. '''Emberstone''' can also suffice, especially if you intend to set up on higher floors.

'''Twinstone''' could be considered, especially if you have e.g. [[Boiler Room]] to help you pay for the copy, further enhancing this card's ability to clear waves and better handling enemies with {{IconLink|Reanimate}}.
summary: Cleave is a common [[Banished]] spell. It does damage to all enemies equal to {{Attack}} of the front friendly unit on the floor.

title: Divinity

flavor.value: "Fel bathed her warriors with an unfamiliar light. Heaven's Light, usually harsh and blinding, became soft. Her warriors sensed it, perhaps Heaven's Light had found a new steward."

tables:
'''Smolderstone''' is one of the main upgrades you should consider for '''Divinity'''. It fixes the card's high cost immediately for a very cheap price, allowing a burst of {{IconLink|Valor}} into a crucial unit while getting out of your way for future deck cycles if you do not need sustained {{IconLink|Valor}} generation, or have other sources of {{IconLink|Valor}} that this card can help ease the scaling process for.

If you have this upgrade, you can also consider '''Eternalstone''' if you need to replay this card; however, with a large enough deck, you're unlikely to draw it more than once, so you may be better off using a different upgrade to increase its power the first time you play it.

'''Seekstone''' is a powerful upgrade, possibly in combination with '''Smolderstone''', guaranteeing {{IconLink|Valor|10}} on your critical unit on turn 1. You can then duplicate this card at [[Empyrean Well]]s at no penalty whatsoever to your deck cycling (as '''Intrinsic''' cards do not take up a card draw on turn 1) and increase this frontloaded {{IconLink|Valor}} as your run progresses, making your tanks even more impenetrable, or spreading the {{IconLink|Valor}} into your damage units to get them going faster.

'''Emberstone''' is a straightforward way to make this more affordable without adding [[Consume]]. You could even add a second one for the same effect as '''Smolderstone''' + '''Eternalstone''' later.
'''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Valor}} gain of this card to 20, making it even more draw-efficient. You will need a lot of {{Ember}} to make the most of this.
summary: Divinity is a common [[Banished]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Valor|10}} to its target.

title: Rising Rage

flavor.value: A simmering fury bubbled in the angel's throat. "You clipped my wings," they cried, their voice echoing against Heaven's high walls, "but now I fly higher than ever before!"

tables: '''Seekstone''', in addition to discounting this to {{Ember|0}}, also gives you this card on turn 1 reliably, letting you get your kill floor together faster and reliably on turn 1.
'''Twinstone''' gives you two of these for the price of one, letting you Ascend two units together and letting you get your kill floor together faster.
'''Keepstone''' lets you draw this card very turn, which is useful if you are using it to trigger {{IconLink|Shift}} repeatedly.
summary: Rising Rage is a common [[Banished]] spell. It [[Ascend]]s then [[Advance]]s a unit.

title: Selfless Sacrifice

flavor.value:
"When you have no more weapons in your arsenal, all you can offer is yourself."
—Banished motto

tables: '''Eternalstone''' and '''Smolderstone''' is a fantastic upgrade combination on this card, letting you duplicate it freely and letting you spam this card to simultaneously scale your units with {{IconLink|Shift}} and accumulate {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} to your units, helping solve both [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] and [[Ragewing Assassin]]s and [[Chosen Assassin]]s.

'''Stackstone''' can be considered to double the {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} applied, either to enhance your defensive plan in general or to better allow backliners with {{IconLink|Valor}} to survive a turn in front.

The '''Eternalstone''' + '''Smolderstone''' combo is preferable, but if you don't find that, or if you have [[Lightstone Casing]], this works. If you find [[Entropy's Crystals]] after applying '''Eternalstone''' + '''Smolderstone''', '''Entropic Stone''' is a boon to add, granting a whopping {{IconLink|Damage Shield|6}}.
summary: Selfless Sacrifice is a common [[Banished]] spell. It [[Advance]]s its target and applies {{IconLink|Damage Shield|2}}.

title: Begone

effect.value: '''[[Retreat]]''' the front enemy unit. Apply {{IconLink|Melee Weakness|1}} to enemy units.

flavor.value: "Will you stop your preaching?!" cried Fel. With a single flutter of her wings, she sent a dozen angels tumbling to the ground.

tables: '''Emberstone''', or any other cost reduction upgrade, can make it much easier to play '''Begone'''.
'''Smolderstone''' lets you play '''Begone''' for {{Ember|0}} at the cost of [[Consume]], which can help increase your damage early on before your units have had a chance to scale.
'''Keepstone''' can double your damage against every wave of enemies, as long as you can play '''Begone''' consistently.
summary: Begone is an uncommon [[Banished]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Melee Weakness|1}} to all enemies on the floor and moves the front enemy to the back.

title: Benediction

effect.value: Apply {{IconLink|Valor|2}} and {{IconLink|Damage Shield|1}} to friendly units.

flavor.value: "I am now the Judge of Souls and I find you all lacking." said Seraph. "Do not worry, I will rectify your flaws."

tables: '''Smolderstone''' can decrease the high cost of this spell. One advantage '''Benediction''' has over [[Sanctuary]] is that '''Smolderstone''' can be applied immediately. '''Seekstone''' and '''Emberstone''' are reasonable choices as well.
'''Stackstone''' doubles your {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} stacks, making it more likely to consistently answer backline threats as well as providing a bit more {{IconLink|Valor}}.
summary: Benediction is a Banished spell, which grants {{IconLink|Damage Shield|1}} and {{IconLink|Valor|2}} to all friendly units on the floor.

title: Deadly Plunge

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Deal damage to the front enemy equal to '''3x''' this friendly unit's {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Armor}}.

flavor.value:
"When all seemed lost, Commander Fel descended on our enemies with a divine strike."
—Tome of the Lost Path

tables: '''Eternalstone''' and '''Smolderstone''' is an excellent combo on this card if you have a unit that is able to kill [[Avowed Gladiator]]s with it. The card becomes very spammable and duplicatable, and can substitute for {{IconLink|Multistrike}} in a small enough deck, particularly against [[Heaven's Maw#Champion of Savagery|Champion of Savagery]].

[[Consume]]. Deal damage to the front enemy equal to 3x this unit's {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Armor}}. >>> [[Consume]]. Deal damage to the front enemy equal to 3x this **friendly** unit's {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Armor}}.
summary: Deadly Plunge is an uncommon [[Banished]] spell. It targets a friendly unit and deals 3x that unit's combined {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Armor}} to the front enemy unit.

title: Demonize

flavor.value:
"Should I ever return to Heaven, will my brethren still consider me one of their own?"
—Talos

tables: '''Smolderstone''' reduces card's cost to {{Ember|1}}, making it easier to play as a way to bring down and kill tanks that slipped past early in fights, or overstack a floor. It can be paired with {{IconLink|Seekstone}} if used to overstack, or {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} if you want to preserve it.
'''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} applied, making it do more against [[Dominion]] and [[Flying Bosses]].
summary: Demonize is a [[Banished]] spell. It moves the target down one floor and applies {{IconLink|Melee Weakness|2}}.

title: Heroic Dive

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
'''[[Descend]]''' then '''[[Advance]]''' a friendly unit. Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to '''2x''' this unit's {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Armor}}.

flavor.value: I flew past arrows until I found Talos defending the southern gate. The sight of her wounds pushed me forward. I called upon my strength. I was almost there, she only had to hold on!

tables: '''Seekstone''' ensures this card will be in your hand turn one, which is useful if you need to immediately assemble your bottom floor and don't want to take [[Heaven's Light]]. It also makes the card free.
'''Twinstone''' is particularly useful in tandem with '''Seekstone''', allowing you to Descend two units instead of just one.

'''Eternalstone''' lets you preserve this card to play again. Since you cannot target enemies with this spell, its utility will diminish once you reach the seven-unit limit on the bottom floor, but if you can produce lots of {{IconLink|Valor}} with units like '''Unchained''' [[Fel]] or [[Battle Dancer]], it can instead be used as a damaging spell.
summary: Heroic Dive is an uncommon [[Banished]] spell. It [[Descend]]s and [[Advance]]s a friendly unit, then damages the front enemy based on that unit's {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Armor}}.

title: Liquid Courage

flavor.value: Sunlight with a sprinkle of courage in a bottle.

tables: '''Stackstone''' doubles the amount of {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} and {{IconLink|Valor}} generated. While this isn't the highest-impact way to apply this upgrade on its face, this card is easy to duplicate, and if you do that your '''Stackstone''' can go a long way. More {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} can be crucial for allowing its targets to survive being at the front in the lategame.
'''Emberstone''' is a simple way to improve {{Ember}} economy by making this card free.
'''Twinstone''' can be applied for an effect similar to '''Stackstone''', ideally with an {{Ember}} upgrade.
summary: Liquid Courage is a [[Banished]] card. It grants a unit {{IconLink|Damage Shield|1}} and {{IconLink|Valor|4}}.

title: Eagleheart

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
'''[[Advance]]'''. Apply {{IconLink|Valor|5}} to a friendly unit, then it attacks immediately.

flavor.value: "And as she was lifted in the air, Fel felt the will of her soldiers give her strength." —Tome of the Lost Path

tables: This combo removes [[Consume]] and makes this spell free, making it an excellent duplication target and making it an excellent way to answer the high-{{Health}} waves the lategame throws at you.
'''Freezestone''' can help you save this spell for the more dangerous later waves in lategame combats.
summary: Eagleheart is a rare [[Banished]] spell. It advances its target, gives it {{IconLink|Valor|5}}, and then it immediately makes an extra attack mid-turn.

title: Heavensward

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
'''[[Ascend]]''' friendly units, then '''[[Advance]]''' the highest {{Health}} friendly unit on the new floor.

flavor.value: "And as we follow the Rail into battle to reclaim Heaven from the Titans, the spirit of the fallen will be carried by those who yearn for freedom. For we that have been tried in the furnace of expulsion will form a single, tremendous force that will bring peace to all!" —final chapter of the Tome of the Lost Path

tables: '''Seekstone''' allows you to immediately play this card to trigger {{IconLink|Shift}} many times and consolidate two floors into one.
'''Emberstone''' reduces this card's cost, improving your {{Ember}} economy.
summary: Heavensward is a rare [[Banished]] spell added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It [[Ascend|Ascends]] all friendly units, then [[Advance|Advances]] the highest {{Health}} friendly unit on the new floor.

title: Sanctuary

flavor.value:
"The Outpost would become a sanctuary for all those threatened by Heaven—be they Angel or Demon—and a place of safety from the plague that had consumed the Empyrial Palace."
—Tome of the Lost Path

tables: '''Eternalstone''' lets this card stay in the deck, and allows the application of '''Smolderstone''' to defray its cost. With this combination and with a trimmed deck, and/or if it's copied, this can be your answer to dangerous threats like [[Ragewing Assassin]] and [[Chosen Assassin]] as well as generally making your units hard to break through.
'''Stackstone''' means this gives {{IconLink|Damage Shield|4}}, which buys your backline a lot of time against [[Ragewing Assassin]].
If you are facing [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]], you will likely need to get your {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} up ASAP. '''Seekstone''' ensures you have this card from the start of the fight.
summary: Sanctuary is a Banished spell, which grants {{IconLink|Damage Shield|2}} to all friendly units on the floor.

title: Spike of the Banished

flavor.value:
"Talos asked me if I was certain. Once the Spike was in the Rail, we would forever be tied to the clans of Hell. I nodded. This is what Herzal would have wanted."
—Tome of the Lost Path

tables: '''Emberstone''' and other {{Ember}} upgrades can increase this card's potency. '''Seekstone''' is especially good, allowing you to gain {{IconLink|Armor}} from your {{IconLink|Valor}} as quickly as possible.

'''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Valor}} applied, which is potent if you can put a lot of {{Ember}} into it. '''Entropic Stone''' can be strong for the same reasons, and is better than '''Entropic Energy''' if you play it for {{Ember|3+}}.
'''Eternalstone''' can allow you to replay this card, and adding '''Smolderstone''' can provide a strong {{IconLink|Valor}} boost.
summary: Spike of the Banished is a rare [[Banished]] spell. It uses all of your {{Ember}} and applies {{IconLink|Valor|4}} for each {{Ember}}.

title: Tome of the Lost Path

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Apply {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}: '''Flight''' to a friendly unit. {{AbilityBox|Flight|2|Move to a targeted location on any floor.}}

flavor.value:
"If one day I fall, I hope that this record will remind future fighters of the sacrifices Finna made to them."
—Tome of the Lost Path

tables: '''Twinstone''' lets you move two units for the price of one card, letting you better overstack a floor and trigger {{IconLink|Shift}} more often on it.

'''Seekstone''' lets you stack your units immediately and get your scaling going from the start of the fight, and makes the card cost {{Ember|0}} for '''Twinstone'''. '''Emberstone''' is an alternative if your deck is small or '''Seekstone''' isn't available.
summary: Tome of the Lost Path is a [[Banished]] spell. It grants the Flight ability to a friendly unit, allowing them to move freely to any position once every two turns.

title: Wyngh's Radiance

flavor.value: "With an aching heart, Lieutenant Talos lifted her old friend's spear and prayed to Wyngh for protection. She felt a familiar warmth fill her heart. Perhaps it was her friend, not Wyngh, who answered."

tables: '''Stackstone''' doubles the amount of {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} generated, doubling the effect of each {{Ember}} invested.
In the right deck, this card can solve just about any wave, making it a potential candidate for a '''Keepstone'''.

One or both copies can be played at {{Ember|0}} to {{IconLink|Shift}} a unit. This is can be very valuable with the '''Celestial Radiance''' path of [[Talos]] as she does not start with [[Just Cause]].

{{Ember}} upgrades can all add to this card's power. While you'll often want to keep the card around, '''Smolderstone''' can be desirable if you're going to duplicate the card a lot, and '''Entropic Energy''' is very strong should you find it. All these upgrades do take away your ability to play this card on your own units without applying {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} to them, however.
Fixed [[Wyngh's Radiance]] not fully showing effects of [[Card Effects#Doublestack|Doublestack]] upgrade on card text.
summary: Wyngh's Radiance is a rare [[Banished]] spell. It moves its target to the front of the floor and applies X {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} to it.

title: Penitent's Bloodsuit

effect.value: {{IconLink|Shift}}: Take '''30''' damage. Can be equipped on enemy units.

flavor.value: "I regarded the Bloodsuit and felt myself shudder. This instrument of pain had left a mark on many angels in Heaven, it was time we used it for our own purposes." —Finna the Doomed

summary: Penitent's Bloodsuit is a common [[Banished]] equipment. It deals 30 damage to its wearer on {{IconLink|Shift}}, and can be equipped on enemy units.

title: Windblade

flavor.value: None can escape the Windblade's path, whose blade turns a breeze into a slice and a gust into a cut. For who can dodge the very air they breathe?

summary: Windblade is an equipment card from the [[Banished]] clan, which grants the user {{IconLink|Valor|1}} on {{IconLink|Shift}} and triggers {{IconLink|Shift}} at the end of each turn. (This will trigger all the unit's {{IconLink|Shift}} abilities, not just the one granted by this equipment.)

title: Everlasting Light

flavor.value:
"I gripped my spear, knowing they would take it away from me. They blamed it for my success in the arena. In the end, I gave it to Talos. May it serve her as well as it did I."
—Finna the Doomed

summary: Everlasting Light is an uncommon [[Banished]] equipment. It grants its wielder a {{IconLink|Strike}} ability that gives all friendly units on the floor {{IconLink|Valor|2}}.

title: Penitent's Deathsuit

effect.value: {{IconLink|Shift}}: Gain {{IconLink|Melee Weakness|1}}. Can be equipped on enemy units.

flavor.value:
"No angel could survive this device. And I was the monster who created it. Perhaps I truly was more a demon now."
—Finna the Doomed

summary: Penitent's Deathsuit is an uncommon [[Banished]] equipment. It gives its wearer {{IconLink|Melee Weakness|1}} {{IconLink|Shift}}, and can be equipped on enemy units.

title: Shield of Wyngh

effect.value: {{IconLink|Revenge}}: Deal damage to the attacker equal to this unit's {{Health}}.

flavor.value: If the Windblades are the piercing gust of a storm, then the Shield of Wyngh is the gale that deflects any attacker.

tables: '''Meat Shield''' boosts {{Health}} a bit, but it also provides some healing every turn. This is useful for units like Firebrand, as they will generally lose a lot of {{Health}} in the early turns of combat before they can build up enough {{IconLink|Armor}}.

'''Oldgrowth''' is a powerful option when partnered with the [[Awoken]], as every {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} trigger raises the damage that '''Shield of Wyngh''' can potentially deal. Combine with [[Unleash the Wildwood]] for best results, allowing you to instantly fill up your empty max {{Health}} and deal hundreds of damage on {{IconLink|Revenge}}.
Though expensive when merged, '''Loamcoat''' provides {{IconLink|Regen}} and a sizable {{Health}} boost. You can also combine this with [[Amorous Enoki]] to boost max {{Health}}.

If you can afford to pay the price for this merged equipment, '''Organ Harvester''' can grant an enormous amount of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. This can set the unit up to become virtually invincible against the boss, although if you're remaining at {{Health|1}} using {{IconLink|Reanimate}} the [[Shield of Wyngh]]'s damage output will be unimpressive. Combine this with any source of {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} to constantly refill the unit's {{Health}} and continue dealing damage.
summary: Shield of Wyngh is an equipment card from the [[Banished]] clan. It deals damage equal to the equipped unit's current {{Health}} (after deducting any damage from the attack) when attacked.

title: Cursed Twinblade

flavor.value:
"She told me the blades would kill me. I laughed and took the weapon. I was living on borrowed time anyway."
—Finna the Doomed

tables: If your intended recipient doesn't have any features that {{IconLink|Silence}} would ruin, '''Stoic Platemail''' can be an excellent merge candidate, as it'll shut off the bad {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger in addition to complimenting your offense with defense.
'''Everlasting Light''' can instead capitalize on the {{IconLink|Multistrike}} while offsetting the {{Attack}} loss with {{IconLink|Valor}}.
Assuming you can {{IconLink|Slay}}, '''Bloodthirsty Blade''' can also capitalize on the {{IconLink|Multistrike}} while offsetting the {{Attack}} loss, and metascaling your {{Attack}} in the process.
'''Equalizing Rings''' locks your {{Attack}} to your maximum health, negating the attack loss entirely.
'''Iron-tongue''' locks your {{Attack}} at 30, negating the attack loss entirely; the {{IconLink|Multistrike}} is also extremely powerful when combined with the Iron-Tongue's {{IconLink|Sweep}}.
'''Herzal's Hammer''' profits from the {{IconLink|Multistrike}} while more than compensating the {{Attack}} loss with its own {{IconLink|Strike}} effect.
summary: Cursed Twinblade is a rare [[Banished]] Equipment card. It grants {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} and {{IconLink|Strike}}: {{Attack|-1}}.

title: Imprisoned Zephyr

flavor.value: "Before they were corrupted, many angels were sent to the dungeons of Heaven to test their loyalty to Seraph. Many did not survive."

summary: Imprisoned Zephyr is an uncommon [[Banished]] room. It causes friendly units in it to [[Advance]] when they attack.

title: Bloodsoaked Arena

flavor.value:
The Crimson Arena claimed many disobedient angels, whether by combat or by fall. Those who proved their worth became useful champions, but always held under a tight leash.
—Tome of the Lost Path

summary: Bloodsoaked Arena is a rare [[Banished]] Room card. Friendly units in the room gain {{IconLink|Valor|6}} on {{IconLink|Slay}}.

title: Pyreborne

flavor.value: ''Use the powerful abilities of the Dragons and their attendant Drakes who have emerged from the Gilded Core.''

summary: Pyreborne [[File:ClanPyreborne.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]]. It is available at the start of the game.

title: Lord Fenix

ability.value:
{{AbilityBox|Fenix Fire|3|Deal damage equal to this unit's attack.
Apply {{IconLink|Pyregel|4}} to enemy units.}}

flavor.value: Lord Fenix once dreamed that his prose would live on in the hearts of dragons to come and inspire them to look beyond the gleam of the coin. Those dreams are long gone, replaced by the love for gold.

tables: [[Fenix]] killing himself with activated ability will now trigger {{IconLink|Conjure|bold=f}} effects.
summary: Lord Fenix is the default [[Champion]] of the [[Pyreborne]]. His {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}} Fenix Fire deals damage to a targeted unit and applies {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to all enemy units. His starter card is [[Firestarter]].

title: Lady Gilda

flavor.value: Heiress to the Pyregel fortune, she might have been born with a golden spoon in her mouth but this dragon has a vicious business acumen. Entire circles of Hell have fallen due to her machinations.

tables: [[Lady Gilda#Gilded Egg|Gilded Egg]] and the variants can now attack if given an attack bonus.
summary: Lady Gilda is the alternate [[Champion]] of the [[Pyreborne]]. She is a primarily supportive champion, capable of applying large amounts of {{IconLink|Pyregel}}, or generating lots of {{DragonsHoard}} or {{Gold}}. Her starter card is [[Bloated Whelp]].

title: Firestarter

flavor.value: An incendiary mixture developed by the Pyreborne to add a little spark to battle.

tables: '''Surgestone''' has a dual purpose on '''Firestarter''', making it able to snipe most important backline targets, and as a soft Purge.
'''Powerstone''' can be considered instead if you really need consistent backline removal and can't afford to replace it with a different card, as it will still hit most relevant threats at 11 power.

'''Emberstone''' pairs nicely with '''Powerstone''', and as '''Firestarter''' is fairly easy to play and its upgrade slots aren't in demand, this upgrade can be a no-frills way to improve your {{Ember}} economy.
summary: Firestarter is [[Lord Fenix]]'s starter card. It deals 1 damage and then applies {{IconLink|Pyregel|2}} to any target.

title: Bloated Whelp

flavor.value: "Look, I know I'm gold-intolerant, but I'm not going to stop eating coins."

tables: '''Immortalstone''' applies {{IconLink|Endless}}, letting a '''Bloated Whelp''' last you the whole combat. This is relevant when using Lady Gila's '''Bloat Matron''' path, if you have the Sacrificial Kris to apply {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to all enemy units on death, or if you are relying on Attuned Manacles to reduce '''Cooldown''' for units like [[Hot Head]].
summary: Bloated Whelp is [[Lady Gilda]]'s starter card. Its {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, Indigestion, allows it to die instantly, dealing 1 damage to all enemies on the floor.

title: Snotty Whelp

ability.value: {{AbilityBox|Gellysneeze|2|Deal '''1''' damage then apply {{IconLink|Pyregel|12}} to the front enemy unit.}}

flavor.value: The carrier whelps are excellent at delivering important materials quickly, just so long as you don't mind a little mucus.

tables: '''Dualstone''' increases the {{IconLink|Pyregel}} applied by '''Gellysneeze''' from 12 to 24.
'''Immortalstone''' applies {{IconLink|Endless}}, letting you use '''Snotty Whelp''' as a chump blocker and reuse its ability immediately every time you replay it.
summary: Snotty Whelp is a common [[Pyreborne]] unit. Its {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, Gellysneeze, deals a single point of damage and then applies {{IconLink|Pyregel|12}} to the front enemy unit.

title: Stuck Up Whelp

flavor.value: "I'm not stuck up, I just know you're not worth my time."

tables: '''Dualstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Avarice}} applied by its ability.
'''Immortalstone''' grants {{IconLink|Endless}}, allowing the ability to be re-used on every resummon.
summary: Stuck Up Whelp is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] unit. Its {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, Expensive Taste, has Cooldown 3 and applies {{IconLink|Avarice|2}} to friendly units.

title: Wealthy Whelp

flavor.value: Keen business dragons with an eye for all that sparkle. They hold their coins close to their chest.

tables: '''Immortalstone''' applies {{IconLink|Endless}}, allowing you to use '''Wealthy Whelp''' as a chump blocker and activate '''Moneymaker''' more frequently, as its ability cooldown will be reset whenever it dies and is resumonned.
Moneymaker's gold gain reduced from {{Gold|+7}} -> {{Gold|+5}} and cooldown reduced from 3 -> 2.
summary: Wealthy Whelp is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] unit. Its {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, Moneymaker, has Cooldown 2 and gains {{Gold|+5}} for each {{Icon|DragonsHoard}}.

title: Gildmonger

flavor.value: To protect their eggs, dragons encase them in gold and give them to the care of Gildmongers until they are ready to hatch. Whether or not they are good caretakers, that is more of a toss-up.

tables: '''Immortalstone''' applies {{IconLink|Endless}}, allowing the unit to be replayed after death for multiple {{IconLink|Extinguish}} triggers.

'''Wickstone''' is only available with the [[Melting Remnant]], but is very powerful with '''Immortalstone''', guaranteeing that '''Gildmonger''' will die every turn and earning plenty of {{DragonsHoard}}.
'''Frankenstone''' comes from the [[Lazarus League]], but lets '''Gildmonger''' activate its {{IconLink|Extinguish}} trigger twice before dying, doubling {{DragonsHoard}} production.

'''Frailty Penance''' can actually be beneficial with a source of {{IconLink|Endless}}, letting you potentially farm {{DragonsHoard}} off of repeatedly killing '''Gildmonger'''. You probably don't want to let this become {{IconLink|Frailty Absolution}} since the {{IconLink|Fragile}} is the point!

In the other direction, this unit is actually one of the Pyreborne's better tanks, meaning '''Titanstone''' and '''Heartstone''' can be applied to it. It can notably defend [[Lord Fenix]] at base room {{Capacity}}, or hide [[Magma Cultist]]s or [[Zealot]]. If using '''Gildmonger''' in this way, '''Immortalstone''' is still very valuable, both for potentially getting an extra {{DragonsHoard}} or two and letting it continue to serve its role even if it dies.
summary: Gildmonger is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. It provides {{DragonsHoard|1}} on {{IconLink|Extinguish}}.

title: Hot Head

ability.value: {{AbilityBox|Fire Breathing|2|Deal damage equal to this unit's attack to enemy units, twice.}}

flavor.value: The guard dragons for Lady Gilda chew magma all day, just in case they ever have to give a special spew to a tax collector.

tables:
'''Largestone''' is one of the most critical upgrades for '''Hot Head'''. It gives an immediate injection of stats, allowing it to survive longer to kill more waves and also hit harder with '''Fire Breathing''', notably pushing it well over the threshold for {{IconLink|Titanskin}} trials. As '''Hot Head''' will often be on a floor on its own, the space increase will rarely be a detriment.

If you already have '''Largestone''', '''Titanstone''' boosts [[Hot Head]]'s survivability even further, while '''Smidgestone''' allows '''Hot Head''' to reap all the benefits of '''Largestone''' while canceling out its drawback completely. This can allow you to slot '''Hot Head''' into a dense floor if you plan to duplicate it and have it play a more active role in your run. However, neither of these upgrades should usually be taken without already having '''Largestone'''.

'''Strengthstone''' powers up '''Hot Head''' and its '''Fire Breathing''' for a cheap price, allowing it to make much larger dents in frontline tanks in the early- and mid-game. It can also be taken as a supplement to '''Largestone''' if you are just looking to fill out upgrade slots. Equivalent clan-specific stones like {{IconLink|Furystone}} or {{IconLink|Echostone}} work as well.

'''Greedstone''' can earn tons of money over the course of a run, as '''Fire Breathing''' has the potential to hit a very high number of times, allowing you to earn a very steady stream of {{Gold}} as long as you can keep '''Hot Head''' alive. However, it does not provide any combat benefit to '''Hot Head''' and thus falls off over the course of a run.
summary: Hot Head is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. Its {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}} is Fire Breathing, which deals damage to all enemy units on the floor equal to [[Hot Head]]'s {{Attack}} twice, and has a cooldown of 2.

title: Greed Dragon

flavor.value: These Master Keepers of the Coin tend to take their job to the literal conclusion and hoard every small gold flake they can find.

tables: '''Immortalstone''' applies {{IconLink|Endless}}, allowing for the bonus stats to be applied multiple times as described above.

'''Smidgestone''' reduces the unit's capacity from {{Capacity|3}} to {{Capacity|1}}, allowing it to more easily fit on floors. This allows you to more easily duplicate this unit and have space for each copy. This is especially important if you have '''Immortalstone''' as floor overstacking won't help if you're constantly resummoning this unit.
'''Frenzystone''' is good on this unit, as it is on any unit that can reach high {{Attack}}.

'''Speedstone''' can be considered if you aren't running '''Immortalstone''', as with its high {{Attack}} it can keep itself healthy until the boss. (If you do have '''Immortalstone''', you want to die to enemies anyway, and you get healed on resummon, so there's no need for this.)
summary: The Greed Dragon is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. It gains {{AttackHealth|+10|+10}} per {{DragonsHoard}} you currently have on {{IconLink|Summon}}.

title: Magma Cultist

flavor.value: ''"One day Fhyra will rise again. When she does, she will coat us in gold, and we will shine like magma in the gloom."''

tables: '''Dualstone''' lets '''Magma Cultist''' apply {{IconLink|Pyregel|2}} per trigger, and is the best upgrade for it in general despite its relatively small impact. However, the more other synergies you have available, the less this upgrade is strictly necessary.

Although only available with the Stygian Guard, '''Runestone''' is the best upgrade to enhance '''Magma Cultist''''s longevity, providing it with plenty of {{IconLink|Armor}} and thus protecting it from effects like {{IconLink|Corruption}}, {{IconLink|Spikes}}, and {{IconLink|Sweep}}. It is also doubled by '''Dualstone'''.

'''Frenzystone''' can be considered if you intend to duplicate the unit, are not worried about its survivability, and lack a better unit to put it on. {{IconLink|Pyregel}} gets better the more individual attacks you have per floor, so although '''Magma Cultist''' is a weak attacker on its own it can still deal quite a bit of damage this way.

'''Heartstone''' grants '''Magma Cultist''' a bit of durability if '''Runestone''' is not available, and is a cheap way to fill its slots. No other upgrades dramatically improve the unit's effectiveness.
summary: Magma Cultist is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. It applies {{IconLink|Pyregel|1}} to all enemies on {{IconLink|Incant}}.

title: Magma Mauler

flavor.value: "You better pay what you owe to Lady Gilda, or I'll squash your toes!"

tables: '''Frenzystone''' is the highest priority upgrade for '''Magma Mauler''', letting it attack twice per turn and thus apply twice as much {{IconLink|Pyregel}}. Additionally, its second hit will be powered up by the {{IconLink|Pyregel}} applied by the first. This upgrade also improves the effects of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} amplifiers like Hellfurnace.

'''Dualstone''' lets '''Magma Mauler''' apply {{IconLink|Pyregel|16}} per {{IconLink|Strike}}, and can be a strong alternative to another '''Frenzystone''' if it already has one; a '''Magma Mauler''' with a '''Frenzystone''' and '''Dualstone''' will apply more {{IconLink|Pyregel}} than one with two '''Frenzystones''', but deal less damage. It also becomes much stronger if you have other methods of providing it with {{IconLink|Multistrike}}.

'''Largestone''' makes '''Magma Mauler''' a far better tank, with a whopping {{Health|75}}, and a smaller boost to its {{Attack}} as well. However, the {{Capacity}} increase can be problematic. '''Smidgestone''' reduces '''Magma Mauler''' to just {{Capacity|1}}, letting more units fit behind it on the floor, but should really only be considered if already upgraded with '''Largestone'''.

'''Speedstone''' makes '''Magma Mauler''' {{IconLink|Quick}}, which is useful when not using the unit as a frontliner. This ensures it will apply its {{IconLink|Pyregel}} before its allies can attack, maximizing its damage output.
summary: Magma Mauler is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. It applies {{IconLink|Pyregel|8}} on {{IconLink|Strike}}.

title: Miser

flavor.value: To be a Miser is the highest honor amongst the Pyreborne and is only given to those who have shown such love of coin that they refuse to spend it for anything.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' lets '''Miser''' hit twice per turn, generating more {{Gold}}. However, its poor stats mean that often another unit could see more use out of this upgrade.

'''Strengthstone''' and '''Heartstone''' improve [[Miser]]'s pathetic stats somewhat, and are cheap and accessible upgrades. Sometimes this will be necessary to survive early rings, and the opportunity cost is quite low because '''Miser''' is a support unit anyway and will quickly earn you back the {{Gold}} spent.

Similarly to the above upgrades, '''Largestone''' is an early game-focused upgrade that grants a solid stat boost, making '''Miser''' much more durable. Notably, the much greater boost to {{Health}} compared to {{Attack}} is usually favourable for {{IconLink|Relentless}}, letting '''Miser''' get many more hits in against the boss before dying and thus earning much more {{Gold}}. However, this upgrade forfeits the unit's {{Capacity|1}}, making it noticeably harder to stick on a floor as a "free" unit.
'''Greedstone''' grants slightly more {{IconLink|Avarice}}, since that is the unit's main purpose anyway.

Although '''Miser''' does not have any {{IconLink|Summon}} or {{IconLink|Extinguish}} effects, '''Immortalstone''' can let it function as a decent chump blocker. Its value as a unit declines towards the end of the run, but as a {{Capacity|1}} unit it can often fit in front of a floor to block an attack, and it has the advantage of being available during deployment, unlike similar units that must first be drawn.
summary: Miser is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. Its stats are poor, but it generates lots of {{Gold}}.

title: Goldtooth

ability.value:
{{IconLink|Avarice|5}}.
{{Attack|+15}} per {{Gold|100}} you started the turn with.

flavor.value: "Do I have gold in my teeth?"

tables: '''Frenzystone''' is a natural pick for '''Goldtooth''', doubling its effective {{Gold}} scaling and also allowing it to benefit from its inherent {{IconLink|Avarice}} twice.
'''Speedstone''' is a solid pick due to '''Goldtooth''''s relatively low {{Health}} and can allow it to kill enemies before they can strike back.
'''Smidgestone''' reduces the unit's {{Capacity}}, allowing you to play more copies of it. An upgraded '''Goldtooth''' is an excellent duplication target, as all copies will scale the same.
'''Dualstone''' grants the unit {{IconLink|Avarice|10}}, boosting its {{Gold}} production. However, if you have a Miser, this upgrade may be better prioritized on it instead.
summary: Goldtooth is a rare [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. Its {{Attack}} scales with the amount of {{Gold}} you have.

title: Pyreblooded

ability.value: {{AbilityBox|Empower|3|Gain {{Attack}} equal to {{IconLink|Pyregel}} stacks on all units.}}

flavor.value: Some dragons take their obsession with gold to a new level. Entranced by the golden hues of the Pyre, these dragons insert pyregel directly into their veins. Somehow, they survive the process.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' is crucial on '''Pyreblooded''', as an offensive unit. This doubles its scaling and lets it kill multiple enemies.
'''Speedstone''' can help make up for its general fragility by killing enemies before they can attack.

'''Immoralstone''' can be an oddly decent option for '''Pyreblooded'''. If it dies and is replayed, '''Empower''' will immediately refresh, letting it scale faster. If combined with '''Speedstone''', it can even kill a tank each round before dying.
summary: Pyreblooded is a rare [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. Its {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, Empower, grants the unit {{Attack}} equal to {{IconLink|Pyregel}} stacks on all units on the floor, with a cooldown of 3.

title: Zealot

flavor.value: Debtors to the Pyreborne imprisoned in The Pit learn that the Zealot's tongue is just as harsh as their whip.

tables: '''Speedstone''' is one of the most critical upgrades for any unit with {{IconLink|Sweep}}. A {{IconLink|Quick}} sweeper will kill all enemies on the floor with lower {{Health}} than the attacker's {{Attack}} before they can retaliate, ensuring that dangerous backline enemies will never get to attack. This will keep '''Zealot''' and your other units healthy throughout a combat, and allow them to continue eliminating enemy waves.

'''Frenzystone''' is a strong consideration for any unit with {{IconLink|Sweep}}. If you have ways of scaling {{Attack}} quickly, giving {{IconLink|Multistrike}} to a sweeper is one of the most damage-efficient upgrades you can make. '''Zealot''' can take further advantage of {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, as each of its hits will trigger the {{IconLink|Pyregel}} that it just applied to each enemy.

'''Largestone''' is a strong upgrade if '''Zealot''' will be placed alone on a lower floor, further increasing its survivability while increasing its {{Attack}} threshold to be able to comfortably clear many lategame backliners.
'''Dualstone''' is a viable upgrade for '''Zealot''', doubling its {{IconLink|Pyregel}} application and softening up high-{{Health}} tanks for the rest of your units to take down.

'''Greedstone''' is a fringe option for '''Zealot''' as it is able to take good advantage of the {{IconLink|Avarice}} given, due to the number of hits it will deal to enemies. However, '''Zealot''' is not a unit that often has disposable upgrade slots for auxiliary upgrades such as '''Greedstone''', and it is preferred to combine two of the aforementioned major upgrades to allow '''Zealot''' to unleash its full potential.
summary: Zealot is a rare [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. It applies {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to all enemies on its floor before attacking with {{IconLink|Sweep}}.

title: Flicker

flavor.value:
"A small flicker can still burn."
—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #37

tables: '''Twinstone''' allows this card to be played twice in a row, which is quite efficient as the card costs {{Ember|0}}. It triggers {{IconLink|Incant}} twice, which is great when using Magma Cultist or when partnered with the [[Stygian Guard]].
'''Powerstone''' makes this spell into a respectable source of area-of-effect damage, even without {{IconLink|Pyregel}} or {{IconLink|Conduit}} support.
'''Keepstone''' lets you play this card every turn, which is quite useful in order to consistently get rid of fragile backliners before they can attack.
summary: This article is about the Pyreborne spell. For the Melting Remnant Champion, see [[Rector Flicker]].

title: Lava Flow

flavor.value: When Hell froze, so did the mighty lava river beneath the Pyreborne caves. Once the Pyreborne melted the celestial ice, they restored the river to its ancient might.

tables: '''Twinstone''' and '''Stackstone''' both double the {{IconLink|Pyregel}} applied. '''Twinstone''' is usually a little better, as it triggers {{IconLink|Incant}} twice for cards like [[Cursed Dragonstaff]] and benefits twice from amplifiers like [[Hellfire Bellows]] and [[Hellfurnace]], but they're very similar overall. Applying both can even allow the card to apply {{IconLink|Pyregel|16}} to an entire floor of enemies.
'''Eternalstone''' lets you play this card multiple times during a combat.
summary: Lava Flow is a common [[Pyreborne]] spell. It applies a small amount of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to all enemy units on the floor.

title: Pyrecask

flavor.value: A barrel full of Pyregel is perfect, not just for dousing enemies. It is also a wonderful option to bring to a potluck.

tables: '''Eternalstone''' removes [[Consume]] from the card, allowing it to be played repeatedly.
'''Freezestone''' reduces the spell's cost to {{Ember|0}} and lets you save it for a specific enemy, such as a non-flying boss.
summary: Pyrecask is a common [[Pyreborne]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Pyregel|10}} to its target.

title: Golden Touch

flavor.value:
"If you have to pay taxes, make sure you bury the tax demon."
—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #12

tables: '''Powerstone''' raises this card's damage to 15, letting it kill enemies like [[Enthralled Ardent]], [[Deafening Herald]], and [[Harpist Protector]]. It also lets it remove a {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stack from [[Deformed Duo]]s. This makes it much easier to score kills in the late game.
'''Freezestone''' ensures that you can hold onto this card if you don't have a good target available when you draw it. It also reduces its cost to {{Ember|1}}, which makes it more affordable.

The combination of '''Seekstone''' and '''Keepstone''' can allow you to play this card every turn, maximizing {{DragonsHoard}} gain and reducing its {{Ember}} cost. However, this means you cannot put a damage upgrade on it. [[Sizzling Firecracker]] is an excellent choice if you put these upgrades on it, boosting its damage to 11.

'''Entropic Growth''' functions as a blend of '''Freezestone''' and '''Powerstone''', letting you hold onto '''Golden Touch''' for an optimal turn and also permanently boosting its damage for each turn you don't play it. This can let you kill much stronger enemies like [[Nourishing Cherub]]s and [[Chosen Assassin]]s. However, you also need to spend several turns not playing the card, which may harm your {{DragonsHoard}} production early. Additionally, the Pyreborne have many other spells which are better targets for this upgrade, such as [[Pyreball]] and [[Make It Rain]]. It is rare for '''Golden Touch''' to be the best option for this event.
summary: Golden Touch is a common [[Pyreborne]] spell. Though it is expensive for its low damage output, it generates {{DragonsHoard|1}} when it kills its target.

title: Pyreball

flavor.value: "Do you think the angels will be able to fly around it?" asked Fenix. "I would like to see them try," replied Lady Gilda.

tables: '''Smolderstone''' reduces this card's {{Ember}} cost to 0, making it easier to play as an early combat solution for backliners.

'''Powerstone''' can be considered to allow '''Pyreball''' to be able to kill [[Chosen Supplicant]] with just a bit more help. It also allows it to kill [[Discordant Heretic]]s by targeting [[Deformed Duo]]s or [[Misshapen Fiend]]s.
summary: Pyreball is a common [[Pyreborne]] spell. It deals 20 damage to its target, and has the [[Explosive]] keyword, meaning any overkill damage is applied as floorwide enemy damage.

title: Alchemy

flavor.value:
"A clever dragon can convince all others that they can make air into gold."
—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #53

tables: The combination of '''Eternalstone''' and '''Smolderstone''' removes [[Consume]] and makes the card cost only {{Ember|1}}, turning this into a {{DragonsHoard}}-generating machine.

'''Twinstone''' grants a second copy of the card after being played. If you can afford to play '''Alchemy''' twice, perhaps with the help of [[Boiler Room]] or [[Ancient Pyretap]], it's quite nice to double its effect.

'''Freezestone''' lowers its {{Ember}} cost slightly and prevents it from being reshuffled, which can prevent you from losing out on precious {{DragonsHoard}} because you happened to draw it on a turn in which you couldn't afford to play it.

If you have the ability to play '''Alchemy''' any time it's drawn, '''Holystone''' can provide some Pyre healing. This can keep the card relatively useful in the late game when {{DragonsHoard}} is less useful, helps offset Pyre damage from leaked enemies or [[Devilish Details]], and if combined with [[Ancient Pyretap]] effectively makes the card free to play, as the {{PyreHealth}} lost will immediately be restored.
summary: Alchemy is a common [[Pyreborne]] spell. When played, you get {{DragonsHoard|2}}.

title: Pyreborne Brainspike

flavor.value:
"And in your minds, I will hide the true location of my Hoard. However, only those willing to use my key will find it."
—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #20

tables: '''Seekstone''' applies [[Intrinsic]], as well as reducing the cost of the card, allowing the player to maximize {{Gold}} gained from {{IconLink|Avarice}}.
'''Stackstone''' makes this card apply twice as much {{IconLink|Avarice}} for even more {{Gold}} generation.
summary: Pyreborne Brainspike is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] spell. It spends all {{Ember}}, applies {{IconLink|Avarice|2}} for each {{Ember}}, and reduces the cooldown on the unit's ability (if it has one) by 1 for each {{Ember}}.

title: Fanning the Flame

effect.value:
'''[[Explosive]]'''.
Deal '''3''' damage to a random enemy unit.
{{IconLink|Slay}}: Increase damage by '''3''' permanently.

flavor.value:
"Fan the flames of war. It's good for business."
—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #19

tables: '''Keepstone''' lets the card be played every turn, maximizing its scaling.
'''Seekstone''' reduces its {{Ember}} cost and allows it to be played from the first turn of battle.
'''Powerstone''' can help make up for losing out on a few kills if you have fallen behind on scaling its damage. However, at that point it may be better to just not bother using this spell.

'''Twinstone''' could be considered to give you a second chance to hit frail backliners if the first hits a tank, and generally can allow you to double-dip on a strong copy of this spell. The copy won't scale the original, however, making this a luxury upgrade if you have a powered-up copy of '''Fanning the Flame''' in the lategame with an extra upgrade slot, perhaps because you received [[Lightstone Casing]].
summary: Fanning the Flame is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] spell. It deals 3 damage to a random enemy on the floor. It is [[Explosive]], meaning that any "leftover" damage will be dealt to all enemies on the floor. For each enemy it kills, either through its initial damage or the Explosive effect, it permanently gains an additional 3 damage.

title: Greed

effect.value:
Deal '''20''' damage to all units.
{{IconLink|Slay}}: Gain {{Gold|10}}

flavor.value: ''Leave the gold for the dragons or else they'll add you to their treasure pile.''

tables: '''Keepstone''' is a crucial upgrade unless your deck is small. Using this spell is asking you to give up using your bottom floor for units, so you want to maximize the payoff it gives you. Playing it every turn amasses tons of {{Gold}} and means your units can focus on tanks and bosses, trusting that backliners are mostly taken care of. '''Seekstone''' also negates its {{Ember}} cost while ensuring you're getting your {{Gold}} from the start of the fight.
'''Powerstone''' can be considered, especially on Covenant 10 if [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] is your boss, as it might allow you to kill [[Chosen Supplicant]]s with just a little more help.
summary: Greed is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] spell. It deals 20 damage to all units, including friendly units. For each unit killed, enemy or friendly, you gain {{Gold|10}}.

title: Inequivalent Exchange

effect.value: Deal damage equal to '''25x''' your {{DragonsHoard}}, then lose {{DragonsHoard|1}}.

flavor.value: "Here's your change," said a voice. These words were the Angel's only warning before a barrage of coins flew straight towards him.

tables: '''Emberstone''' makes this card free to play, other than the {{DragonsHoard}} you have to spend.

'''Twinstone''' lets you play this card twice to take out an [[Avowed Gladiator]] or kill two minor enemies. However, you'll need good {{DragonsHoard}} production to make sure you'll recoup your losses from playing this spell many times.
summary: Inequivalent Exchange is an uncommon Pyreborne spell. It deals damage equal to 25 times the current amount of {{IconLink|Dragon's Hoard|png=DragonsHoard}} at the cost of one {{DragonsHoard}}.

title: Make It Rain

effect.value: Deal '''5''' damage to enemy units. Spend {{Gold|5}} and repeat this card's effect, up to three more times.

flavor.value: ''Although it goes against the instincts of every dragon in Hell, sometimes you have to loosen the purse strings to win the battle.''

tables: '''Keepstone''' applies '''[[Holdover]]''', allowing the card to be played repeatedly as a solution for consistently clearing backline enemies. It'll cost you a significant amount of {{Gold}} per combat, so make sure you can account for that.

'''Powerstone''' is an effective +40 damage modifier as the 10 '''[[Magic Power]]''' applies to every hit. Crucially, this lets it kill most Chosen backline enemies on Covenant 10, making it a must-buy on that difficulty level unless you can supplant it with liberal {{IconLink|Pyregel}} or {{IconLink|Conduit}} application.

'''Emberstone''' and '''Seekstone''' can be considered as alternatives to '''Powerstone''' if you are below Covenant 10 and aren't afraid of [[Cael, Lord of the Cherubs|Cael]]'s cherubs, as this card doesn't need the extra power otherwise. They can also be applied in addition to the other two if you have [[Lightstone Casing]].
summary: Make It Rain is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] spell. It deals 5 damage to all enemies, then repeats this process up to three more times at the cost of {{Gold|5}} each.

title: Pay Off

flavor.value:
"So, you'll do it?" said Fenix.
"For a price," replied the angel.
"Though I have to say, I thought you were on the side of Hell."
Fenix paused. "I'm on my own side," he said.

tables: '''Eternalstone''' removes '''[[Consume]]''', allowing this card to repeatedly heal the Pyre during the battle. Once you have this upgrade, '''Smolderstone''' makes this card cost {{Ember|0}}.
Fixed '''Pay Off''' spells rigged with {{IconLink|Holystone}} upgrades incorrectly scaling the amount of bonus Pyre healing.
summary: Pay Off is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] spell. It heals {{PyreHealth|2}} for each {{DragonsHoard}} the player currently has.

title: Dragon's Breath

effect.value: Apply {{IconLink|Pyregel|10}} and deal '''10''' damage to enemy units.

flavor.value: As Keeper of Hell's Heart, Fhyra was a tenacious guardian. Those who tried to enter the caves beneath the last circle and steal her treasure would meet a fire hotter than Heaven's might.

tables: '''Powerstone''' allows this spell to kill [[Nourishing Cherub]]s and [[Vampiric Cherub]]s (assuming the latter does not have {{IconLink|Titanskin}} from a [[Chosen Bastion]]).

'''Stackstone''' makes this spell apply {{IconLink|Pyregel|20}} to all enemies. Like '''Powerstone''', this also allows it to take out {{Health|30}} enemies, and is more effective against tanks and bosses.

'''Smolderstone''' reduces this spell to a mere {{Ember|1}}, but makes it '''[[Consume]]'''. This is usually fine if you do not need this spell consistently and just want a bit of burst damage, but if you want to keep it around, '''Eternalstone''' will do just that.
'''Keepstone''' is a niche upgrade, but works well if you have a way to get around its high {{Ember}} cost.

Obtained from [[Entropy's Crystals]], both '''Entropic Energy''' and '''Entropic Stone''' can be viable. The former instantly makes '''Dragon's Breath''' free to play, making it a potent duplication target, while the latter makes it apply a whopping {{IconLink|Pyregel|30}}. However, note that with '''Entropic Stone''', drawing '''Dragon's Breath''' and [[Entropic Crystals]] in the same hand can be a problem, as it costs {{Ember|5}} to play both unless you have [[Sinner's Salve]].
summary: Dragon's Breath is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] spell. When played, it applies {{IconLink|Pyregel|10}} to all enemies, then deals 10 damage. {{IconLink|Pyregel}} is applied before the damage is dealt, and thus increases the damage the spell deals.

title: Soldier of Fortune

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Draw a unit. If you have {{Gold|30}}, spend it to apply {{Attack|+30}}, {{IconLink|Avarice|15}}, and {{IconLink|Armor|15}}.

flavor.value:
"A soldier who goes to war without the promise of pay is a fool with a sword."
—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #22

tables: '''Seekstone''' ensures you will have this card immediately. With a sufficiently slim deck, this can guarantee that you draw a particular unit like [[Hot Head]], [[Primordium]], or [[Dante the Dependable]] (unless you also happen to draw that unit on the first turn). This lets you gain the maximum number of {{IconLink|Avarice}} triggers. Alternatively, you can use it to draw out a specific non-banner unit like [[Deathmetal Hymnist]] or [[Moon Pixie]].

'''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Avarice}} and {{IconLink|Armor}} applied to the drawn unit. Notably, this means you will make back the {{Gold}} spent with just a single attack from the drawn unit, and every subsequent attack is profit.

'''Freezestone''' allows you to hold onto this spell, which helps you line it up with the unit you want to target. If there are no units in your draw pile but there are in your discard pile, the most recently discarded unit will be drawn.
summary: Soldier of Fortune is a rare [[Pyreborne]] spell. It draws a unit and spends some {{Gold}} if available to strengthen them.

title: Devilish Details

flavor.value: Nothing is off the market, not even the Pyre itself.

tables: If you're a daredevil or have [[Pay Off]] (and preferably more than one copy), one selling point of this card compared with [[Alchemy]] or [[Golden Touch]] is how easy it is to attach a '''Twinstone''' to it.
There aren't too many other upgrades that make sense here, so saving an {{Ember}} with '''Emberstone''' makes sense.

'''Eternalstone''' can allow '''Devilish Details''' to be played multiple times each battle. If you have a way to deal with the {{PyreHealth}} loss, this can be one of the fastest methods to gain {{DragonsHoard}}. However, without an extremely strong healing method - either Pay Off or an expensive spell with {{IconLink|Holystone}} - this is usually a bad idea.
summary: Devilish Details is a rare [[Pyreborne]] spell. It grants {{DragonsHoard|3}} but deals 8 damage to your Pyre.

title: Smelted Treasure

effect.value: Spend {{Gold|50}}. Apply {{IconLink|Armor|50}} to a friendly unit.

flavor.value: "And Fhyra's great, beloved greed demanded more from gold. The ancient dragons of the Pyre set forth to learn greater uses for their coin. It was the young whelp, Em Ber, who mixed gold with Pyregel." —Tales of Fire and Gold

tables: '''Stackstone''' is the most efficient upgrade for '''Smelted Treasure''', granting a titanic {{IconLink|Armor|100}} while still costing only {{Gold|50}}.

'''Emberstone''' makes '''Smelted Treasure''' cost {{Ember|0}}, so the only price to play it is the {{Gold|50}}. '''Smolderstone''' achieves the same effect, but adds [[Consume]]; this is usually a negative, but it may be useful if you cannot afford to cast the spell more than once and therefore want to remove it from your deck after a single use.

'''Freezestone''' reduces its {{Ember}} cost and allows you to hold onto the card until you absolutely need it, which can be worthwhile if you are not flush with {{Gold}} to ensure you aren't spending it unnecessarily.
'''Seekstone''' reduces its {{Ember}} cost and lets you cast it immediately, which can be vital in combats that threaten immediate high damage output like [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]].
Fixed [[Smelted Treasure]] still granting armor even with no gold.
Fixed [[Smelted Treasure]] spell with upgrades incorrectly requiring more than 50 gold.
summary: Smelted Treasure is a rare [[Pyreborne]] spell added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It applies {{IconLink|Armor|50}} to a friendly unit, but costs {{Gold|50}} when played.

title: Tome of Contracts

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Reduce a unit's '''[[Cooldown]]''' Timer by '''1''' to a minimum of 1.

flavor.value:
"All dragons must sign their name in the ledger and give half their yearly coin to my temple. If they break their contract, refer to the second Rule."
—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #1

tables: '''Seekstone''' can make your build more reliable if an ability is a core part of your strategy, especially if you have a large deck - discounting it by {{Ember|1}} too.
'''Twinstone''' can let you get a Cooldown 3 ability to be usable every turn, or two Cooldown 2 abilities.
summary: Tome of Contracts is a [[Pyreborne]] spell. It reduces the target's [[Cooldown Timer]] by 1, but cannot reduce it below 1.

title: Deathroar

effect.value: Transfer all {{IconLink|Pyregel}} on this floor to a unit then deal '''5''' damage five times.

flavor.value: ''Lady Gilda turned away from the conversation. Her bodyguard, Vagar, was a loyal dragon but his breath was terrible.''

tables: '''Powerstone''' affects each hit separately, adding a significant amount of damage to the spell.
'''Emberstone''', or any other source of cost reduction, can make it much easier to play '''Deathroar'''.
