summary: Deathroar is a rare [[Pyreborne]] spell. It moves all {{IconLink|Pyregel}} from all units on the floor to the target, then deals 5 damage to the target five times.

title: Superheated

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Double the amount of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} on a unit.

flavor.value:
"Beneath the Pyreborne's caves flows a river of Pyregel that runs so hot, it erodes the very stone itself. Watch where you step, you might get a superheated surprise."
—Dante's Travel Guide

tables: '''Freezestone''' reduces this card's cost, and lets you hold onto it until you have applied a sufficient amount of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to your ideal target.
Though '''Twinstone''' is hard to pull off due to this card's high cost, if you have the {{Ember}} to support it, it can allow you to quadruple a target's {{IconLink|Pyregel}}.

'''Eternalstone''' lets you hold onto this card, amplifying the {{IconLink|Pyregel}} it applies over time. Once you have this upgrade, '''Smolderstone''' can be applied to drastically reduce its cost.
summary: Superheated is a rare [[Pyreborne]] spell. It doubles the amount of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} on the target.

title: Pyreclasm

flavor.value:
"And when you have followed my commandments and led a life devoted to gold, then your spirit will experience an explosive transformation."
—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #1071

tables: '''Emberstone''', '''Seekstone''', and '''Freezestone''' all reduce this card's {{Ember}} cost, allowing it to be played without a source of {{Ember}} generation.
'''Powerstone''' has its '''Magic Power''' bonuses multiplied by five due to the '''Attuned''' attribute.
'''Keepstone''' allows this powerful spell to be used every turn, as long as you have the {{Ember}} to play it.

Two of [[Entropy's Crystals]] upgrades can be extremely strong here. '''Entropic Growth''', after a few turns of leaving it in your hand, allows this card to completely annihilate even [[Avowed Gladiator]]s. '''Entropic Energy''', on the other hand, makes it free to play and therefore a compelling target for duplication effects.
summary: Pyreclasm is a rare [[Pyreborne]] spell. It deals 150 damage to the target, and has [[Explosive]], meaning that any leftover damage is dealt to all enemies on the floor. It is also [[Attuned]], meaning that [[Magic Power]] increases its damage five times as much as normal.

title: Lava Armor

flavor.value:
"Fenix does love to dote on me, but I have to say, my favorite gift was the patent for this armor of his that uses lava to protect the wearer. It's his most profitable creation yet!"
—Lady Gilda

summary: Lava Armor is a common [[Pyreborne]] equipment. It grants its wearer {{Health|+10}} and a {{IconLink|Revenge}} ability that applies {{IconLink|Pyregel|3}} to the attacker.

title: Mind Cage

flavor.value:
"All dragons who turn their thoughts towards pointless pastimes such as art, music, or poetry will submit to the mindcage until they reform."
—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #3

summary: Mind Cage is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] equipment. It reduces a unit's ability cooldown by 1 at end of turn. This means that abilities with Cooldown 2 can be used every turn, and abilities with Cooldown 3 can be used every other turn.

title: Soulsmelter

flavor.value: A creation by the Pyreborned smelters and infused with a blessing by Fhyra, this staff consumed the souls of the bearer's enemies and transformed them into gold.

summary: Soulsmelter is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] equipment. It grants {{Attack|+10}}, and lets its user accumulate {{IconLink|Soul}} as enemies die. It also gives its target a {{IconLink|Celebrate}} trigger that gives you {{DragonsHoard|1}} for every 4 {{IconLink|Soul}} if it survives the whole battle.

title: Cursed Dragonstaff

flavor.value:
"An eye for an eye makes for a cursed eye, better to leave them blind."
—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #16

summary: Cursed Dragonstaff is a rare [[Pyreborne]] equipment. It deals 1 damage to all enemies whenever you cast a spell.

title: Sacrificial Chamber

flavor.value:
"If a dragon cannot pay their yearly tribute, they will pay their tithe with their life."
—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #2

summary: Sacrificial Chamber is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] room. It gives the player {{Gold|10}} when any unit dies, including both friendly and allied units.

title: Hellfurnace

effect.value: When a unit gains '''Pyregel''', it gains '''+3''' stacks.

flavor.value: ''"We're behind schedule! Pick it up, double-time!" Fenix's voice blared from the forge speaker. The dragonsmiths hammered away, determined to meet their quota.''

summary: Hellfurnace is a rare [[Pyreborne]] room. Whenever Pyregel is applied to a unit in this room, it adds an extra {{IconLink|Pyregel|3}}.

title: Luna Coven

flavor.value: ''Align with the secretive Luna Coven and tap into the mercurial power of the Moon to empower spells and weapons alike.''

summary: Luna Coven [[File:ClanLunaCoven.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]]. It is unlocked after defeating 40 enemies using spells.

title: Ekka

flavor.value: The High Witch of the Luna coven, Lady Ekka led the Selene in both ritual and life. Though even she did not know of the prophecy looming over the coven until it was far too late.

tables: Silver Empress I & II stats increased from {{AttackHealth|12|8}}, {{AttackHealth|20|12}} -> {{AttackHealth|15|10}}, {{AttackHealth|20|15}}

Silver Empress stats updated from {{AttackHealth|15/10}}, {{AttackHealth|20/15}}, {{AttackHealth|30/20}} >>> {{AttackHealth|20/20}}, {{AttackHealth|25/25}}, {{AttackHealth|30/30}}. Silver Empress I {{IconLink|Conduit}} increased from '''15''' >>> '''20'''.
summary: Ekka is the default [[Champion]] of the [[Luna Coven]]. She can provide a lot of {{IconLink|Conduit}} to her floor, or scale both {{Attack}} and {{Health}} on {{IconLink|Mooncycle}}, but she tends to be vulnerable in the early game. Her starter card is [[Witchweave]].

title: Arduhn

flavor.value: As head of the Silent Guard, Arduhn is the keeper of the Coven's darkest secrets. Perhaps had he gone against his oath and revealed the prophecy, he could have saved his family and home.

tables: Mystic Hammer II & III stats increased from {{AttackHealth|20|40}}, {{AttackHealth|40|80}} -> {{AttackHealth|25|45}}, {{AttackHealth|50|90}}.
Updated Hierophant [[Arduhn]]. "Silent units gain double armor" >>> "Silent units gain '''+1'''/'''2'''/'''3''' {{Attack}}."
summary: Arduhn is the alternate [[Champion]] of the [[Luna Coven]]. His attack damage is enhanced with {{IconLink|Mageblade}} and scales with {{IconLink|Conduit}}. His starter card is [[Moon Ritual]].

title: Witchweave

effect.value: Deal '''1''' damage to an enemy unit or restore {{Health|1}} to a friendly unit.

flavor.value: As the fighting continued outside the temple walls, Lady Ekka prepared her strike. "May the moon's light and darkness unite," she whispered.

tables: '''Surgestone''' has a dual purpose on '''Witchweave''', making it able to snipe most important backline targets even without support, and as a soft Purge.
'''Powerstone''' can be considered instead if you'd rather this card stick around, but have some utility even on floors without {{IconLink|Conduit}}.
summary: Witchweave is [[Ekka]]'s starter card. When cast on enemy units, it deals 1 damage; when cast on friendly units, it heals them for 1.

title: Moon Ritual

flavor.value:
"Each new moon phase calls for a new ritual with your fellow fae."
—The Ritual Tome

tables: For decks that are simply looking to keep the moon at the same phase, '''Freezestone''' can improve your consistency at doing so.

You could consider '''Keepstone''' to make this card the only one you need to keep the moon at your desired phase, with the idea of Purging the rest.

This only works consistently for moon effects that are checked mid-turn, such as [[Heavenfall]], unless you have additional moon support or upgrades - '''not''' ones checked at end of turn. You may draw this card during your desired moon phase. In that case, you'd have to choose between playing this card, cycling to the undesired moon phase, or not playing the card, meaning you won't draw it next turn. For more flexibility, you can add {{IconLink|Twinstone}} to get '''Spellchain'''. Then you can freely play the card each turn (for the Holdover effect), and then play or skip the additional copy, as required.
summary: Moon Ritual is [[Arduhn]]'s starter card. It applies a tiny amount of {{IconLink|Conduit}}, but more importantly, it changes the current moon phase. An [[Ephemeral]] version is also generated each turn by [[Lunar Priestess]].

title: Meddler

flavor.value: "You can't take the dust out of stardust just as you can't take the meddle out of the meddler."

tables: '''Heartstone''' can help you keep this unit alive against incidental damage like {{IconLink|Sweep}} and {{IconLink|Spikes}}.

'''Immortalstone''' gives '''Meddler''' {{IconLink|Endless}}. If you can kill it and redraw it every turn, it gives you two {{IconLink|Mooncycle}}s each play between its {{IconLink|Summon}} effect and ability, or it can ensure the moon phase will always be what you want (by using or not using your ability as needed every turn). If that plus a chump blocker is worth one less card draw per turn, this upgrade can be considered.
summary: Meddler is a common [[Luna Coven]] unit. Like the other [[:Category:Fae units|Fae units]], the Meddler serves a supportive purpose on the train, allowing for manual phasing of the moon.

title: Moon Pixie

flavor.value: "These sands of Limbo are no moon rock. They will have to do for my night blooms."

tables: '''Dualstone''' grants {{IconLink|Dualism}}, doubling the value of '''Moon Pixie''''s {{IconLink|Conduit}}, and is by far the most important upgrade for this unit.
'''Glimmerstone''' is a cheap upgrade that further improves '''Moon Pixie''''s {{IconLink|Conduit}}.
'''Heartstone''' makes the unit less fragile, protecting it from effects like {{IconLink|Spikes}}, and allows it to be moved by [[Gravity]] without killing it.
summary: Moon Pixie is a common [[Luna Coven]] unit. It has {{IconLink|Conduit|3}}, and grants {{IconLink|Conduit|3}} to all other friendly units on the floor.

title: Aurora Weaver

flavor.value: "Oh, your aura! It feels so... malevolent! Do not worry, I'll cut away the negative energy with my blade!"

summary: Aurora Weaver is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] unit. It gains {{IconLink|Conduit|1}} per each {{IconLink|Mooncycle}}.

title: Mooncaller

flavor.value: "I used to sing to the moon as one voice of thousands. Now, my voice is alone among their spirits."

tables: '''Heartstone''' makes it easier for '''Mooncaller''' to stay alive.
'''Glimmerstone''' provides some extra {{IconLink|Conduit}} to the floor. '''Mooncaller''' is generally not desperate for upgrades, so this can be worthwhile.

If (and only if!) you are using '''Mooncaller''' alongside '''Lunar Steward''' Ekka, then all units on the floor - including '''Mooncaller''' - will eventually gain high {{Attack}}. Due to its low {{Capacity}}, '''Frenzystone''' can be a very damage-efficient upgrade if you plan to repeatedly duplicate the card. Other damage-focused upgrades like {{IconLink|Speedstone}} can be useful for the same reason.
summary: Mooncaller is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] unit. It causes all {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} effects on its floor to be triggered twice.

title: Astrologer

flavor.value: "Let me look at your star chart. I see you were born under the Blessed Moon? Oh dear, that's no good..."

tables: '''Speedstone''' can be a pseudo-defensive upgrade by killing enemies before they are able to attack.
'''Smidgestone''' makes it easier to duplicate her and play multiple copies on a single floor.

'''Largestone''' and '''Heartstone''' bolster her relatively low health pool. '''Largestone''' does so more effectively, but increases her {{Capacity}}. However, this upgrade can be vital to surviving the early rings if you are lacking in defensive measures, and the good news is it is relatively uncommon for '''Astrologer''' to be a primary aspect of your deck in the long term, so putting this upgrade on her is usually not tremendously harmful.
summary: Astrologer is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] [[banner unit]]. She gains {{Attack|+5}} on {{IconLink|Mooncycle}}.

title: Lunar Priestess

ability.value: {{IconLink|Resolve}}: Add a '''[[Moon Ritual]]''' spell with '''[[Ephemeral]]''' to your hand.

flavor.value: "One day we will return to the space beyond the skies and I will resume my duties. Until then, I will keep the rituals alive in my memory."

tables: '''Heartstone''' is useful, as it makes '''Lunar Priestess''' slightly less fragile.
If you plan to fit '''Lunar Priestess''' behind your other units on a floor, '''Glimmerstone''' a decent cheap upgrade, providing a little {{IconLink|Conduit}} to the floor.

'''Largestone''' is best if you intend to keep '''Lunar Priestess''' alone on the top floor, giving her significantly more durability. She can even be used as a tank in the earlier game this way, though this comes at the cost of her natural {{Capacity|1}}.
Fixed card art not loaded when you obtain characters like [[Lunar Priestess]] when not playing [[Luna Coven]] who then creates a [[Moon Ritual]] card.
summary: Lunar Priestess is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] [[banner unit]]. She adds a copy of [[Moon Ritual]] with [[Ephemeral]] to the player's hand at the end of each turn.

title: Nightingale

flavor.value: ''"I don't need magic to disappear into the night."''

tables: As an offensive unit, '''Frenzystone''' is worth consideration even with its natural {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}}, and also serves dual-duty for padding over turns in the early-game where you cannot Phase to {{IconLink|New Moon}}.
'''Speedstone''' can help make up for [[Nightingale]]'s poor {{Health}} by letting it attack before enemies.
'''Smidgestone''' is best used alongside Eclipse Chamber or '''Hierophant''' Arduhn, allowing more copies of the card to fit onto the floor and thus increasing your scaling.

'''Largestone''' improves [[Nightingale]]'s poor stats, its {{Health}} especially. It's best used alongside '''Smidgestone''' to avoid the increased {{Capacity}}, but is a perfectly respectable choice if you just need to survive the early combats.
'''Heartstone''' provides a cheap {{Health|20}} boost, which may sometimes be necessary to survive early rings if {{IconLink|Largestone}} is not offered.

'''Dualstone''' grants '''Nightingale''' {{IconLink|Stealth|4}}. This upgrade should really only be considered alongside Shadow's Sheath or if using '''Nightingale''' exclusively as a lure for flying bosses.

'''Immortalstone''' is a bizarre upgrade for '''Nightingale''', and should usually not be considered. However, if you started with '''Nightingale''' early or took it and found no way to improve it, its {{IconLink|Stealth|2}} alongside {{IconLink|Endless}} can prevent [[Savagery]]'s {{IconLink|Resolve}} trigger on an empty floor, saving {{PyreHealth|5}} per cycle in the Titans fight. Note that you will also need a {{Health}} upgrade to pull this off. '''Heartstone''' is usually best for this as it ensures '''Nightingale''' can tank [[Dominion]]'s {{IconLink|Corruption}} for just long enough, while ensuring it dies when its {{IconLink|Stealth}} wears off, allowing it to replayed to block Savagery again.
summary: The Nightingale is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] [[banner unit]]. It enters with {{IconLink|Stealth}}, and gains {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}} during {{IconLink|New Moon}}.

title: Selene Acolyte

flavor.value: "During the Plenilune I asked the moon about your fate. Her answer was clear: you will be defeated."

tables: '''Speedstone''' can be a pseudo-defensive upgrade by killing enemies before they are able to attack. It's particularly important on '''Selene Acolyte''' because of her {{IconLink|Sweep}}, allowing her to kill enemies like [[Ragewing Assassin]] before they get to attack.
'''Frenzystone''' doubles her damage, and is probably the most important upgrade for this unit if you plan to use her as your main source of damage.

'''Largestone''' is not ideal, but can provide an initial damage boost and, more importantly, an enormous amount of {{Health}}. If you cannot deal with the extra {{Capacity}}, '''Heartstone''' can also work. This may be necessary to keep her alive if you have no defensive spells, especially against [[Legion]], who will otherwise kill her quickly in Ring 2 and potentially lead to an early loss.
summary: Selene Acolyte is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] [[banner unit]]. She has {{IconLink|Mageblade|2}}, and has {{IconLink|Sweep}} during the {{IconLink|Full Moon}}.

title: Shadeguard

ability.value: {{IconLink|Resolve}}: If it is {{IconLink|New Moon}}, gain {{Attack|+10}} and {{Health|+15}}.

flavor.value: ''"When the fighting was done, when we had stopped falling through the skies, I lit my lantern and looked around. All of it, the temple walls, the home I called my own, it was all gone."''

tables: '''Smidgestone''' is always a good choice, decreasing '''Shadeguard''' from {{Capacity|3}} to {{Capacity|1}}. This makes it much easier to fit units behind it and keep them protected. If you don't have either a '''Smidgestone''' or access to overstacking through cards like [[Gravity]] or [[Hexscalation]], '''Shadeguard''' can be somewhat impractical.
'''Titanstone''' doubles the impact of '''Shadeguard''''s defensive scaling.
'''Frenzystone''' doubles the impact of '''Shadeguard''''s offensive scaling.

'''Savage Skin''' and '''Savage Heart''' are very strong on '''Shadeguard''' if you happen to find the [[Savagery's Statue]] event, as it is a frontline unit that will be tanking a lot of hits. '''Savage Heart''' lets it build up a huge amount of {{IconLink|Rage}} over the course of a run, while '''Savage Skin''' grants {{IconLink|Titanskin|5}}, bolstering its durability. However, be aware that [[Savage Shackles]] can be quite detrimental, since '''Shadeguard''' is already an expensive unit.
summary: Shadeguard is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] [[banner unit]]. It gains {{Attack|+10}} and {{Health|+15}} at the end of each turn if the current phase is {{IconLink|New Moon}}.

title: Silent Sentinel

ability.value: {{AbilityBox|Spell Slam|3|Restore to full health. Apply {{IconLink|Spell Weakness|1}} to enemy units.}}

tables: '''Titanstone''' doubles the effective value of {{Health}} and healing, making '''Silent Sentinel''' a better tank.
'''Heartstone''' gives the unit {{Health|60}}, raising the amount of health that '''Spell Slam''' can heal and increasing the unit's damage threshold before it dies.
If you need more {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}}, '''Dualstone''' causes '''Spell Slam''' to apply {{IconLink|Spell Weakness|2}}.
summary: Silent Sentinel is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] [[banner unit]]. His {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, Spell Slam, heals him to full {{Health}} and applies {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} to all enemies, with a cooldown of 3.

title: Ethereal Seelie

ability.value:
{{IconLink|Conduit|5}}.
Apply '''+1''' stack of {{IconLink|Conduit}} each time it is applied.

flavor.value: When the seelie sing their duets, misfortune is said to be near. However, it is when they are silent that true calamity is feared.

tables: [[Ethereal Seelie]]'s main priority is to stay alive. {{IconLink|Largestone}} is usually impractical, however, because the Luna Coven need all the {{Capacity}} they can get. '''Heartstone''' provides a simple {{Health}} boost.
'''Glimmerstone''' is a cheap upgrade that adds a bit more initial {{IconLink|Conduit}}.

It may seem absurd to put '''Frenzystone''' on a unit with such poor stats. Usually, this is exactly correct, and this upgrade should not be considered. However, if you have Fae's Nook and decent {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} potential, '''Ethereal Seelie''' can actually be a respectable damage dealer, especially when duplicated. It also lets the unit make better use of the Moonlit Glaive, if that is your main damage output. Just be sure you do not have another unit who needs this upgrade more.
summary: Ethereal Seelie is a rare [[Luna Coven]] [[banner unit]]. It applies an additional stack of {{IconLink|Conduit}} whenever {{IconLink|Conduit}} is applied.

title: Moonguard

flavor.value: Although a gentle folk, the Moonguard had to put aside their love for learning and defend the coven during desperate times.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' is the ideal upgrade, letting '''Moonguard''' kill more than one enemy per turn. If shops cooperate, two copies of this upgrade is ideal.
'''Speedstone''' lets it turn its massive {{Attack}} into much-needed defensive utility by killing one or two enemies before they attack, particularly if you don't have [[Fae's Blessing]].
'''Smidgestone''' makes it easier to put two of these units together to multiply their offensive ability, though this requires {{DeploymentEmber}} as well.

'''Titanstone''' gives {{IconLink|Titanite}}. If you have defensive spell support from e.g. [[Fae's Blessing]], this doubles the impact of that support, and [[Moonguard]]'s relatively decent {{Health}} makes it a decent tank candidate.
summary: Moonguard is a rare [[Luna Coven]] [[banner unit]]. It has {{IconLink|Mageblade|3}}, which increases to a total of {{IconLink|Mageblade|6}} during {{IconLink|New Moon}}.

title: Scrivener

flavor.value: "All my books, lost in the Fall. It will take me centuries to rewrite them. I just hope my memory is correct..."

tables: '''Scrivener''' mainly needs survivability, which '''Heartstone''' provides at a low cost.
'''Glimmerstone''' is a great Luna Coven upgrade for any backline utility unit.

'''Immortalstone''' is not ideal for keeping '''Scrivener''' alive, since she costs {{Ember|2}} and 1 card draw to resummon. That said, {{IconLink|Endless}} provides survivability against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]]'s {{IconLink|Corruption}}, which might otherwise be hard to deal with. A unit replayed with {{IconLink|Endless}} can also immediately reactivate its {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, which in [[Scrivener]]'s case immediately recoups 1 card draw and gains a persistent {{Ember|1}} discount on a spell (unless it already cost {{Ember|0}}). This can turn '''Scrivener''' into something vaguely resembling a {{Ember|1}} [[Votivary]] chump blocker: not generally useful, but potentially helpful in specific decks and situations, in particular for combats like [[Clash with the Titans]] that apply {{IconLink|Corruption}} to the front unit.
Fixed [[Scrivener]] ability Spellweave cost reduction not stacking.
[[Scrivener]] ability Spellweave updated to only target non-starter cards.
summary: Scrivener is a rare [[Luna Coven]] [[banner unit]]. Her {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, Spellweave, draws a non-starter spell and reduces its cost by {{Ember|-1}}, with a cooldown of 2.

title: Bloody Moon

flavor.value:
"When Seraph came to destroy our home, the moon shone red. At the sight, Lady Ekka grieved the souls that would fall in the upcoming battle."
—Ardania the Forbidden

tables: '''Holystone''' heals {{PyreHealth|2}} for what is functionally {{Ember|0}}, as long as you kill something.
'''Emberstone''', '''Seekstone''', and '''Freezestone''' all discount '''Bloody Moon''', so if it kills its target you will gain {{Ember}} overall.

'''Powerstone''' lets this card kill [[Chosen Supplicant]]s. If your floor has at least {{IconLink|Conduit|15}} or another Magic Power source, like [[Enchanted Chamber]], it can also kill [[Chosen Assassin]]s.
'''Twinstone''' lets you snipe two enemies per wave for what is functionally {{Ember|0}}.
summary: Bloody Moon is a common [[Luna Coven]] card. It deals 25 damage to any target, granting {{Ember|2}} if it kills.

title: Celestial Storm

effect.value:
Deal '''10''' damage to enemy units.
{{IconLink|Full Moon}}: '''[[Attuned]]'''.

flavor.value:
"Lady Ekka fell silent as she called upon her ancient ally: the sky. Seraph's army had underestimated her might."
—Ardania the Forbidden

tables: '''Smolderstone''' makes this spell more affordable to play at the expense of adding [[Consume]]. This can be a good idea if you need this spell to decimate an early problem wave but can scale to beat later ones.
'''Powerstone''' means this always kills [[Discordant Heretic]] and can kill Chosen variants as long as you have {{IconLink|Full Moon}} applied.
'''Emberstone''' and '''Freezestone''' discount this by {{Ember|1}}, and '''Freezestone''' lets you save it for when a problem wave arrives on your floor with {{IconLink|Conduit}}.

'''Keepstone''' is ambitious, but if you have a run where you can satisfy this card's requirements, such as having [[Boiler Room]] in play, taking advantage of it every turn can be your way to get through the endgame's tough waves.

'''Entropic Growth''' lets the card gain permanent '''[[Magic Power]]''' on '''[[Reserve]]''', allowing it to scale to insane heights without even needing other [[Magic Power]]. Alternatively, '''Entropic Energy''' eliminates its {{Ember}} cost.
summary: Celestial Storm is a common [[Luna Coven]] spell. It deals 10 damage to all enemies, and when played on the {{IconLink|Full Moon}}, it has [[Attuned]].

title: Fae's Blessing

effect.value: Restore '''5''' health. Healing over max health applies {{IconLink|Armor}} instead.

flavor.value: "Arduhn stretched out his hand towards the fae, who touched him in return. And so a pact was made. The fae would assist the coven so they could return home."

tables: '''Emberstone''' makes the spell cheaper, which is useful for a spell that you will want to play every time you draw it.

'''Twinstone''' lets you play '''Fae's Blessing''' twice whenever it's drawn, letting you double the amount of {{IconLink|Armor}} on a unit or apply {{IconLink|Armor}} to two different units. This is especially effective if combined with cost reduction, such as through '''Emberstone''' or '''[[Seekstone]]'''.
'''Entropic Growth''' lets the card gain permanent '''[[Magic Power]]''' on '''[[Reserve]]''', letting it apply massive amounts of {{IconLink|Armor}} even without {{IconLink|Conduit}} support.
'''Keepstone''' lets you play '''Fae's Blessing''' every turn, which is useful if you need a steady stream of {{IconLink|Armor}} for your units.
summary: Fae's Blessing is a common [[Luna Coven]] card. It restores 5 health, unless the target has lost less than 5 health, in which case it turns any extra healing into {{IconLink|Armor}}.

title: Gravity

flavor.value:
"Seraph had defeated us and left us with no choice. If we could no longer rise above Heaven and Hell, we would have to fall."
—Ardania the Forbidden

tables:
'''Seekstone''', in addition to discounting this card to {{Ember|0}}, also gives it to you on turn 1 reliably, letting you get your kill floor together immediately.

The moon phase will always be {{IconLink|Full Moon}} on turn 1, so even without any moon manipulation this can make this functionally a [[Hidden Passage]] with upside and downside. Having this on turn 1 also means you can play it before scaling up your {{IconLink|Conduit}}, giving you the best chance of playing it safely.

'''Twinstone''' gives you two of these for the price of one, letting you Ascend/Descend two units together and thus put your kill floor together faster, or just generally increasing its utility. You could even use one copy to [[Ascend]] and the other to [[Descend]] or vice versa if you can [[Phase]] the moon between plays.
summary: Gravity is a common [[Luna Coven]] spell. It deals 5 damage and either [[Ascend]]s the target if the {{IconLink|Full Moon}} is active, or [[Descend]]s it if the {{IconLink|New Moon}} is active.

title: Silver Strike

effect.value:
Deal '''25''' damage to the front enemy unit.
{{IconLink|Full Moon}}: Deal damage twice instead.

flavor.value:
"Our defeat was certain but Lady Ekka urged us to continue until the full moon. Then, she explained, she might be able to alter our fates."
—Ardania the Forbidden

tables: '''Surgestone''' has a dual purpose on '''Silver Strike''', allowing it to deal a respectable {{Health|90}}, which is enough to severely dent if not kill frontliners through Ring 6, while also soft-purging it from your deck for later rings.
'''Emberstone''' pairs nicely with '''Surgestone''', or as a standalone upgrade, for a no-frills way to improve your {{Ember}} economy.
summary: Silver Strike is a common [[Luna Coven]] spell. It deals 25 damage to the front enemy unit, then hits again if the phase is {{IconLink|Full Moon}}.

title: Starstruck

flavor.value: "Seraph is at our temple gates! Stars, won't you protect us?"

tables: '''Twinstone''' and '''Stackstone''' both essentially doubles the amount of {{IconLink|Dazed}} on this card. One could even apply both upgrades to inflict up to 4 stacks of {{IconLink|Dazed}} on one singular enemy.
'''Entropic Stone''' is just a better '''Stackstone''', so if you find this event and do not have a better target for the '''Triplestack''' then consider adding it to this card.

'''Keepstone''' allows you to play this card every turn in order to permanently inflict {{IconLink|Dazed}} on a dangerous enemy or to use it on different enemies each turn. With '''Twinstone''' or '''Stackstone''', this can even be used to shut down a boss throughout the fight '''without''' moon phase support in a pinch, applying {{IconLink|Dazed|2}} every other turn.

'''Freezestone''' is useful if you plan on using the effect of {{IconLink|Dazed}} to shut down a particular enemy or to buy more time during {{IconLink|Relentless}} and want to guarantee that you have this card in your hand when it is needed. It also can be a substitute for phase control.
summary: Starstruck is a common [[Luna Coven]] spell. It deals 5 damage to its target, and if the {{IconLink|Full Moon}} is active that target will also suffer {{IconLink|Dazed|1}}.

title: Cosmic Bolt

flavor.value: A flash was all the warning Seraph got.

tables: With a '''Keepstone''', this card can be your deck's answer to tanky enemies like [[Avowed Gladiator]].

'''Emberstone''', '''Seekstone''', or '''Freezestone''' go nicely with '''Keepstone''' to discount it by {{Ember|1}}. '''Seekstone''' or '''Freezestone''' can add utility depending somewhat on how you're using it.

While '''Powerstone''' can feel like a drop in the bucket compared to the damage {{IconLink|Conduit}} can provide, a '''Powerstone''' does allow this spell to kill threats like [[Chosen Supplicant]] and [[Chosen Assassin]] without needing any additional power, letting you pick those units off before they threaten you if you set up on higher floors.
'''Entropic Growth''' lets the card gain permanent '''[[Magic Power]]''' on '''[[Reserve]]''', allowing it to scale to insane heights without even needing other [[Magic Power]].
summary: Cosmic Bolt is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] spell. It deals 35 damage, and has the [[Attuned]] keyword, giving it 5 damage for each point of [[Magic Power]], such as through {{IconLink|Conduit}}.

title: Cover of Night

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
'''[[Phase]]''' to {{IconLink|New Moon}}. Apply {{Attack|+5}} and {{IconLink|Stealth|1}} to friendly units.

flavor.value: ''Seraph's soldier turned, having heard a sound behind him. He froze. There, perched atop a moon cliff, was a creature, unlike any demon or angel he had ever seen.''

tables: '''Freezestone''' allows you to retain the card in your hand. This can be useful if you plan on using this card's {{IconLink|Stealth}} to keep units alive during a particular dangerous round of enemies.

'''Twinstone''' allows you to double the output of this card on one floor or apply its effect on two different floors. Note that you do not double the amount of [[Phase|phasing]] this card does unless you play another phase card in between each copy of this card. '''Stackstone''' only allows you to apply {{IconLink|Stealth|2}} to a floor, but that could be good enough for some decks.
'''Eternalstone''' removes the consume of this card, useful if you want to play it multiple times in a single combat.

If you have upgraded the card with '''Eternalstone''', then upgrading it with '''Keepstone''' will allow you to play this card every turn in order to continuously apply {{IconLink|Stealth}} to your units and if it is the last [[Phase]] card played on your turn, then it will also permanently keep {{IconLink|New Moon}} active.
summary: Cover of Night is a uncommon [[Luna Coven]] spell. It applies {{Attack|+5}} and {{IconLink|Stealth|1}} to all friendly unit on a floor while also [[Phase|phasing]] to {{IconLink|New Moon}}.

title: Glittering Draught

flavor.value:
"Once done, this draught will transform sunlight into moonlight and heal a fae of any wound."
—The Ritual Tome

tables: For runs where this card fits as a defensive aid, '''Eternalstone''' lets it stick around, providing sustainability while also providing a solid amount of {{IconLink|Conduit}} scaling. It'll scale its own future healing. It also allows '''Surgestone''' to be applied without adding [[Consume]], which helps in a relatively low-{{IconLink|Conduit}} environment.
summary: Glittering Draught is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] spell. It heals its target for 20 and applies {{IconLink|Conduit|4}} to it.

title: Hexscalation

flavor.value:
"Draw the runes on the ground and wait for your enemy to arrive. They will be welcomed by a nasty surprise."
—The Ritual Tome

tables: '''Seekstone''', in addition to discounting this card to {{Ember|0}}, also gives it to you on turn 1, letting you overstack a floor reliably right away.
'''Twinstone''' gives you two of these for the price of one, letting you Ascend two units together and letting you get your kill floor together faster.
'''Stackstone''' can be used if you're looking to use this to amass {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}}, such as against [[Flying Bosses]].
summary: Hexscalation is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] spell. It ascends a unit and applies {{IconLink|Spell Weakness|2}}.

title: Lunacy

flavor.value:
"Some believed that the Selene control the moon and her phases. What lunacy. The moon cannot be forced to do what she does not wish. Time, on the other hand, can be manipulated."
—The Ritual Tome

tables: Given that ideally, you're playing this for a lot of {{Ember}}, '''Holystone''' lets you also heal off of that investment.
'''Emberstone''' and the family of upgrades that discount {{Ember}} can be applied to staple another copy of [[Moon Ritual]] onto this card.

'''Seekstone''', in addition to getting another [[Phase]], can be used to get {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} scaling units to a decent level of power from the start of the fight if you can spike {{Ember}} then.
'''Freezestone''', in addition to getting another [[Phase]], can be used to wait for a turn where you can spike {{Ember}} to play it.
'''Keepstone''' can be useful both for triggering {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} many times per turn, and for maintaining a specific moon phase if you could not find other ways of doing so.
summary: Lunacy is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] spell. It [[Phase]]s the moon X times and applies X {{IconLink|Conduit}} to its target.

title: Moonbeam

effect.value: Deal '''20''' damage to the front enemy unit '''X''' times.

flavor.value:
"As our beloved moon fell, our home had one last gift to give our coven. When it shattered, all the magic we had stored inside struck Seraph."
—Ardania, fallen guard to Lady Ekka

tables: Upgrades can help you up the value of X you play it at. '''Freezestone''' or '''Seekstone''' in particular can help line it up with [[Silver Ink]] if you have it.
Larger decks with consistent {{Ember}} generation and {{IconLink|Conduit}} could use '''Keepstone''' to use this to capitalize on both against every wave.

If you encounter [[Entropy's Crystals]] with this artifact, you could also consider '''Entropic Growth''' if you already have a lot of {{Ember}} and less {{IconLink|Conduit}} as it does capitalize well on the [[Magic Power]] you can build up with it. That said, '''Entropic Energy''' is more likely to be the better choice from that event, as the [[Luna Coven]] are better at amassing {{IconLink|Conduit}} than {{Ember}}.
summary: Moonbeam is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] spell. It deals 20 damage to the front enemy unit X times.

title: Moonrise

flavor.value:
"I wove the cloth across my wrists and waited on the moon to rise. As I saw it peak over the horizon, my powers grew."
—The Ritual Tome

tables: Very well-trimmed decks could consider '''Eternalstone''' in the lategame to use this as a consistent form of phase control, and trading draw for {{Ember}}. In this case, '''Twinstone''' would add one more {{Ember}} per turn, or '''Keepstone''' can act as a pseudo-[[Hell's Flame]] in exchange for one draw per turn while also maintaining {{IconLink|Full Moon}} at all times.
summary: Moonrise is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] spell. It gains {{Ember|1}} and [[Phase]]s to {{IconLink|Full Moon}}.

title: Coven's Spike

flavor.value:
"I wove Ekka's sash around the shard of our shattered moon and drove it into the Rail. With that, Hell would be our home now."
—Arduhn, Head Guard of the Silent

tables: '''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Conduit}} applied. If this card is good, doubling it is better!
'''Emberstone''' and the family of upgrades that discount {{Ember}} can be applied to increase {{IconLink|Conduit}} applied.

'''Seekstone''', in addition to increasing {{IconLink|Conduit}} applied, can be used to get {{IconLink|Mageblade}} scaling units and your spells to a decent level of power from the start of the fight if you can spike {{Ember}} then.
'''Freezestone''', in addition to increasing {{IconLink|Conduit}} applied, can be used to wait for a turn where you can spike {{Ember}} to play it.
Given that ideally, you're playing this for a lot of {{Ember}}, '''Holystone''' lets you also heal off of that investment.
summary: Coven's Spike is a rare [[Luna Coven]] spell. It gives its target {{IconLink|Conduit|3X}}.

title: Duality

effect.value:
'''[[Attuned]]'''.
Deal '''10''' damage to an enemy unit or restore '''10''' health to a friendly unit.

flavor.value:
"Silent or Selene, magic user or fighter, we are each a part the whole."
—The Ritual Tome

tables: '''Twinstone''' lets you use this powerful spell twice, letting you kill more than one threat per draw.

'''Emberstone''', '''Seekstone''', or '''Freezestone''' go nicely with '''Twinstone''' to discount it to {{Ember|0}}. '''Seekstone''' or '''Freezestone''' can add utility depending somewhat on how you're using it.
With a '''Keepstone''', this card can be your deck's answer to tanky enemies like [[Avowed Gladiator]]. Pair with a '''Twinstone''' for even more power.

While '''Powerstone''' can feel like a drop in the bucket compared to the damage {{IconLink|Conduit}} can provide, a '''Powerstone''' does allow this spell to kill threats like [[Chosen Supplicant]] and [[Chosen Assassin]] without needing any additional power, letting you pick those units off before they threaten you if you set up on higher floors.
'''Entropic Growth''' lets the card gain permanent '''[[Magic Power]]''' on '''[[Reserve]]''', allowing it to scale to insane heights without even needing other [[Magic Power]].
summary: Duality is a rare [[Luna Coven]] spell. It deals 10 damage when targeting a enemy unit, or heals for 10 health when targeting a friendly unit. It has the [[Attuned]] keyword, meaning any sources of [[Magic Power]], such as {{IconLink|Conduit}}, are 5 times as effective.

title: Heavenfall

effect.value:
Deal '''80''' damage to enemy units.
{{IconLink|Full Moon}}: Deal damage on all floors instead.

flavor.value:
"If I must fall, may I at least grant you time to escape."
—last words of Ardania, forbidden younger sister of Arduhn and Ekka

tables: '''Emberstone''', '''Seekstone''', and '''Freezestone''' all accomplish the same goal of making this card's {{Ember|4}} cost easier to stomach. With any combination of two of these upgrades, it will cost a much more reasonable {{Ember|2}}.

'''Smolderstone''' gives {{Ember|-2}} for a single upgrade, at the cost of making this spell '''[[Consume]]'''. This isn't a bad deal overall. However, if you can then find '''Eternalstone''', this downside is removed and you can replay this spell as often as you can draw it, although this is more expensive than just giving it two '''Emberstones''' for the same effect, and is less efficient than an '''Emberstone''' plus a '''Seekstone''' or '''Freezestone''', which gives it some extra effect other than {{Ember|-2}}.

If you have some way to "cheat" {{Ember}} costs, like [[Ancient Roots]] or [[Split Anvil]], '''Keepstone''' lets you draw this extremely powerful spell every turn, wiping out all backliners except the [[Chosen Ardent]] even with no {{IconLink|Conduit}} and severely denting even the highest-{{Health}} tanks as they ascend.

Should you be lucky enough to find the [[Entropy's Crystals]] event with this card, '''Entropic Energy''' makes '''Heavenfall''' completely free and therefore an unbelievably good candidate for mass duplication. This is more than worth the [[Entropic Crystals]] you will be forced to take in exchange, especially if you can apply '''Keepstone''' or even {{IconLink|Twinstone}} afterwards.
Fixed [[Heavenfall]] card saying "Russian>><<" in the middle of the card in that language (and others).
Fixed [[Heavenfall]] doing only 60 damage instead of 80 in certain cases.
summary: Heavenfall is a rare [[Luna Coven]] spell. It deals 80 damage to all enemy units on the floor. During {{IconLink|Full Moon}}, it instead deals damage to all enemies on all floors.

title: Ritual Tome

flavor.value:
"May all fae, noble or not, write their spells in this tome. For each voice belongs to the coven's chorus."
—The Ritual Tome

tables: '''Stackstone''' is the most important upgrade for this card, as the difference between {{IconLink|Titanskin|2}} and {{IconLink|Titanskin|4}} is much wider than you might think. Alternatively, if you are offered '''Entropic Stone''', that is a strict upgrade over '''Stackstone''', applying {{IconLink|Titanskin|6}}. Unfortunately, you cannot apply both upgrades to the same card.
'''Seekstone''' lets you put {{IconLink|Titanskin}} on your frontliner immediately, saving them the most damage overall across the fight. It also reduces the card's {{Ember}} cost.

'''Eternalstone''' prevents this card from being '''[[Consume]]d''', so you can add more and more {{IconLink|Titanskin}} over the course of the fight. Against combats with continuously-ramping damage like [[Clash with the Titans]], this can be relevant, but will almost always need a strong supplement like a {{IconLink|Conduit}}-boosted [[Fae's Blessing]] alongside it.
summary: Ritual Tome is a rare [[Luna Coven]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Titanskin|2}} to a friendly unit.

title: Silver Ink

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Apply '''[[Attuned]]''' and '''+3 [[Magic Power]]''' to spells in your hand.

flavor.value:
"Take stardust and mix it with oil. Cast a blessing. Only the fae shall read your words written in this ink."
—The Ritual Tome

tables: '''Freezestone''' and '''Seekstone''' both reduce this card's {{Ember}} cost and help you line it up with the right spells. These upgrades are quite good in tandem, in fact, ensuring that you never have to draw this card and reducing its cost to a mere {{Ember|1}}.
summary: Silver Ink is a rare [[Luna Coven]] spell.

title: Stardust Invocation

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''. '''[[Distinct]]'''.
'''[[Phase]]'''. Create an '''[[Ephemeral]]''' copy of a spell in your hand.

flavor.value:
"Take a handful of stardust and whisper an incantation over it. Your spell's power will be doubled."
—The Ritual Tome

tables: You will usually have a specific spell that you want to target with '''Stardust Invocation'''. '''Freezestone''' makes it significantly easier to line up that combination, while also discounting it to {{Ember|0}}.
'''Seekstone''' ensures you will have this card on the first turn of combat, which can be useful if you are also guaranteed to see the spell you want to copy turn one.

'''Eternalstone''' is best in combination with '''Freezestone''', letting you play a powerful spell twice every deck cycle. Alternatively, if you are in desperate need of moon phase control, you can use this upgrade with {{IconLink|Keepstone}}, but there are usually much easier ways to accomplish this.
Updated card text for cards that exclude themselves with new keyword '''[[Distinct]]'''. [[Stardust Invocation]] and [[Unearth Treasure]] are examples.
summary: Stardust Invocation is a rare [[Luna Coven]] spell. It changes the moon phase, then gives you an [[Ephemeral]] copy of a spell in hand.

title: Tidal Turning

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Restore '''10''' health to friendly units. Healing over max health applies {{IconLink|Armor}} instead.

flavor.value: Moonlit shores attract millions of tiny fae to bathe in the moonlight. As the night deepens, the Selene dance, guided by the water's glow.

tables: '''Seekstone''', in addition to discounting this card's {{Ember}} cost, also puts it in your hand on turn 1 reliably, and since keeping backline units alive is this card's main niche, doing so reliably on turn 1 is nice.

'''Freezestone''' also discounts this spell, and gives you the chance to potentially amass some {{IconLink|Conduit}} before playing it, if you're setting up on higher floors and don't need it immediately.
'''Eternalstone''' can allow this spell to be played multiple times, providing massive defense to the entire floor. It also allows you to take '''Smolderstone''', making it much cheaper to play.
Tidal Turning base healing nerfed from {{Health|20}} -> {{Health|10}}.
summary: Tidal Turning is a rare [[Luna Coven]] spell. It heals all friendly units by 10, and excess healing applies {{IconLink|Armor}}.

title: Dusk Mantle

flavor.value: "When the divine moonlight wanes, do not fear. For the Silent will don their mantles and defend us against all those who crawl from the Void."—torn page from The Ritual Tome

tables: Fixed [[Dusk Mantle]] not properly enabling Moon mechanics when acquired when playing clans other than Luna Coven.
summary: Dusk Mantle is a rare [[Luna Coven]] equipment added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It grants a unit {{IconLink|Titanskin|5}} during {{IconLink|New Moon}}.

title: Luna Cyclestaff

flavor.value:
"Under a full moon, take the staff made of the lunar shard and cast a circle. Watch the sands of Limbo flow towards you. A moon will be made for your coven to call home."
—The Ritual Tome

summary: Luna Cyclestaff is a rare [[Luna Coven]] equipment. Whenever the moon phase changes, it gains {{Attack|+1}} permanently.

title: Moonlit Glaive

flavor.value: At the end of the Plenilune, the priestess return all weapons to the Silent. For now that the blades have been blessed by an Empress Moon, they have no place in her temple.

summary: Moonlit Glaive is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] equipment. It grants {{IconLink|Mageblade|3}}.

title: Eclipse Chamber

effect.value: {{IconLink|New Moon}} effects are always active. Silent units gain {{Attack|+15}} on {{IconLink|Resolve}}.

flavor.value:
"The angels found us waiting for them. I brought up my shield. The coven priestesses would be protected. If they failed to bring the eclipse, we were doomed."
—Ardania the Forbidden

summary: Eclipse Chamber is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] room. It maintains {{IconLink|New Moon}} on its floor, and grants [[:Category:Silent units|Silent units]] {{Attack|+15}} each turn.

title: Planetarium

flavor.value: The home of the Astrologers and where they pore over star charts and judge who was born under a auspicious moon.

summary: Planetarium is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] room. It grants {{IconLink|Conduit|5}} to all friendly units on the floor.

title: Underlegion

flavor.value: ''Join with the mushroom folk of the Rotwood as they turn death and decay into victory.''

summary: Underlegion [[File:ClanUnderlegion.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]]. It is unlocked after consuming 75 cards.

title: Bolete the Guillotine

flavor.value: A polymath from the Wild Woods, Bolete would settle against the roots of the Fatal Elm with his books, a few old friends, and a flask of sap. Those dreams will have to wait. For now, caps must roll.

tables: [[Bolete|Headsman]] III {{Attack}} increased from '''100''' >>> '''160'''. Executioner [[Bolete]] upgrade line updated from: "{{IconLink|Harvest}}: Gain {{IconLink|Regen|2/3/5}} and {{IconLink|Rage|2/3/5}}." >>> "{{IconLink|Siphon}}: '''[[Spawn]] 2/2/3'''. {{IconLink|Troop}} adds {{Health|+1/2/3}} per stack." Stats updated from {{AttackHealth|10/30}}, {{AttackHealth|30/60}}, {{AttackHealth|50/120}} >>> {{AttackHealth|30/20}}, {{AttackHealth|50/50}}, {{AttackHealth|80/100}}.
Fixed the first tier of [[Bolete]] Executioner's path missing text that described the {{IconLink|Troop}} benefit.
summary: Bolete the Guillotine is the default [[Champion]] of the [[Underlegion]]. He leads the fungi of the Underlegion, either becoming extremely powerful with {{IconLink|Rally}} synergies, or supporting allies with [[Spawn]] and [[Propagate]] effects. His starter card is [[Eager Conscript]].

title: Madame Lionsmane

flavor.value: She is the Mistress of the Scent, the Rot Perfumer. Her concoctions will make you fall in love as they melt your heart.

tables: Sporesinger [[Madame Lionsmane]] III updated "When a unit gains {{IconLink|Decay}}, it gains +4 >>> +5 stacks."
summary: Madame Lionsmane is the alternate [[Champion]] of the [[Underlegion]]. She focuses primarily on weakening enemies through {{IconLink|Decay}}, but can also provide [[Spawn]] support. Her starter card is [[Sporetouch]].

title: Eager Conscript

flavor.value: You never fight just one shroomfolk. Beneath Hell's topsoil is an army that can decay the mightiest of oaks.

tables: Putting '''Emberstone''' on '''Eager Conscript''' helps you spam it more, and in many cases this is a straightforward way to get more value out of your turn.

'''Smolderstone''' also accomplishes what '''Emberstone''' does, while sort-of purging the card. This also means it interacts with [[Morel Mistress]]'s {{IconLink|Etch}} trigger and fills the Consume pile to power up cards like [[Unearth Treasure]].
summary: Eager Conscript is [[Bolete the Guillotine]]'s starter card. It [[Spawn]]s 1, summoning [[Funguy]] or giving an existing [[Funguy]] 1 {{IconLink|Troop}} stack.

title: Sporetouch

flavor.value: Before the angel could react, Madame Lionsmane gave a flick of her fan and sent a cloud of toxic fumes that dissolved his skin and his eyes.

tables: '''Smolderstone''' reduces its {{Ember}} cost to 0 and makes it [[Consume]], both getting it out of your deck and potentially enabling {{IconLink|Etch}} strategies. (It probably isn't what you want if you draft [[Unearth Treasure]], though.)
summary: Sporetouch is [[Madame Lionsmane]]'s starter card. It applies {{IconLink|Decay|2}} to any unit, dealing 6 damage at the end of the turn.

title: Funguy

flavor.value: N/A

tables: Fixed an issue with [[Funguy]] incorrectly resetting equipment cooldowns when adding {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks.
summary: Funguy is a unique, stackable Shroom unit from the [[Underlegion]] clan. They are always {{IconLink|Cardless}}, as there is no card that explicitly represents them. Instead, any [[Spawn]] X effect will summon a Funguy to the front of the floor, regardless of the floor's {{Capacity}}, with X {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks. Additional Spawn X effects on a floor with a Funguy stack on it will cause them to gain X {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks, regardless of where they are on the floor. Their {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks can also be increased via [[Propagate]] effects, as they'll always have at least {{IconLink|Troop|1}}.

title: Green Recruit

flavor.value:
"One day, I'll command the soldiers of the Fatal Elm and be the greatest warrior in all of Limbo!"
—unnamed soldier now deceased

tables: '''Immortalstone''' lets you keep playing '''Green Recruit''' over and over, and is by far the most important upgrade for this unit. If you are able to consistently play '''Green Recruit''' and have it die, it's a more {{Ember}}-efficient [[Spawning Pods]].

'''Wickstone''' is only available with the [[Melting Remnant]], but it guarantees that '''Green Recruit''' dies every turn, even if no enemies attack it. This makes it easier to play with other '''Spawn''' effects, as it will die even if it is behind Funguy. Many Melting Remnant units have {{IconLink|Harvest}} triggers as well, which synergize excellently with '''Green Recruit'''.

'''Frankenstone''' can only be found with the [[Lazarus League]], but it essentially doubles [[Green Recruit]]'s {{IconLink|Extinguish}} effect, making it a solid choice; note that after dying for the first time it will spawn [[Funguy]] in front of it, preventing it from dying again.

All three of the [[Inscryption]] upgrades work excellently on '''Green Recruit''': * '''Worthy Sacrifice''' lets it die immediately and grants {{Ember|3}}. * '''Many Lives''' lets its {{IconLink|Extinguish}} trigger happen four times per play. * '''Fecundity''' lets you play it multiple times on different floors. Together, these three upgrades on '''Green Recruit''' can break the game wide open with any {{IconLink|Rally}} support from the rest of your train, allowing you to build up huge [[Funguy]] stacks, on multiple floors if desired. See the [[Inscryption]] page for how to get all three upgrades.

'''Discarded Wings''' lets '''Green Recruit''' fly to any position on the train, eliminating its {{Capacity}} and positioning problems. However, this comes at a small cost, since '''Discarded Wings''' also grants {{Health|+10}}, making it slightly harder to kill.
summary: Green Recruit is a common [[Underlegion]] unit. It spawns 4 [[Funguy]] when killed.

title: Cheery Deathcap

flavor.value: "In a world of mulch and rot, I've learned to put on a happy face."

tables: '''Dualstone''' grants {{IconLink|Dualism}}, doubling the {{IconLink|Decay}} applied to 14. This makes the total damage if applied on the bottom floor with no other sources of 117.
'''Immortalstone''' grants {{IconLink|Endless}}, allowing its {{IconLink|Summon}} ability to be triggered multiple times.
If you can find the [[Inscryption]] event and have given '''Cheery Deathcap''' {{IconLink|Endless}}, applying '''Worthy Sacrifice''' and '''Fecundity''' to it can break a run wide open.
summary: Cheery Deathcap is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] unit. It applies {{IconLink|Decay|7}} to enemy units on {{IconLink|Summon}}.

title: Truffles

ability.value: {{AbilityBox|Fetch|2|Add a random [[Equipment]] with '''[[Ephemeral]]''' to your hand and apply {{Ember|-1}}.}}

flavor.value: "Mush-woof!"

tables: '''Immortalstone''' grants {{IconLink|Endless}}. Cooldown is reset on {{IconLink|Summon}}, so '''Truffles''' can be replayed in the frontline to block and generate new equipment.
[[Truffles]] ability Fetch cooldown decreased from 3 to 2.
summary: Truffles is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] unit. Her {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, Fetch, has a 2 turn cooldown and adds a random [[Equipment]] with [[Ephemeral]] that costs {{Ember|-1}} to your hand.

title: Waxcap

flavor.value: "Why is it so sticky everywhere I go?"

tables: '''Dualstone''' grants {{IconLink|Dualism}}, doubling the {{IconLink|Sap}} applied to 6. This is potent and can make the wave it's played against become fodder for the Pyre.

'''Immortalstone''' grants {{IconLink|Endless}}, allowing its {{IconLink|Summon}} ability to be triggered multiple times. You will need to have a way to kill it, as its {{IconLink|Sap}} means the enemies won't do this reliably.

'''Wickstone''' is only available with the [[Melting Remnant]] and is incompatible with '''Dualstone''', but it ensures '''Waxcap''' will die at the end of each turn, which is sometimes difficult due to its {{IconLink|Sap}} application.
If you can find the [[Inscryption]] event and have given '''Waxcap''' {{IconLink|Endless}}, applying '''Worthy Sacrifice''' and '''Fecundity''' to it can break a run wide open.
summary: Waxcap is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] unit. It applies {{IconLink|Sap|3}} to enemy units on {{IconLink|Summon}}.

title: Amorous Enoki

flavor.value: A lover of love and all things lovely, this mushroom can charm the bark off a tree.

tables: '''Dualstone''' grants {{IconLink|Dualism}}, doubling the {{IconLink|Regen}} applied. However, this does not affect {{Health}}, and may be better used on units like [[Spore Launcher]] or [[Enchantrelle]].
'''Heartstone''' can help '''Amorous Enoki''' avoid being killed early on, before she has a chance to buff herself and the rest of the floor.
The Underlegion tend to be very hungry for {{Capacity}}, so '''Smidgestone''' is a solid investment, allowing you to fit more {{IconLink|Rally}} units on her floor.
summary: Amorous Enoki is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever a friendly unit is summoned, she increases the {{Health}} of all friendly units by 1 and applies {{IconLink|Regen|1}} to all friendly units.

title: Cluster Colonel

flavor.value: "I would be willing—no, happy—to lead these Caps to battle every day!"

tables: '''Smidgestone''' is easily the most impactful upgrade one can put on '''Cluster Colonel'''. Reducing him to {{Capacity|1}} makes it easier for multiple copies to be played on the same floor, as long as you have the necessary {{Ember}}.

Simple defensive upgrades like '''Heartstone''', '''Shieldstone''', and '''Runestone''' are often the next best choice if trying to fill out '''Cluster Colonel''''s slots. These upgrades can protect him from {{IconLink|Corruption}} and {{IconLink|Spikes}}.

'''Discarded Wings''' is the most useful event upgrade for '''Cluster Colonel'''. It allows you to move him to any spot on any floor, effectively turning him into a {{Capacity|0}} unit and eliminating concerns about space. This makes him a much stronger choice for duplication as well, as you no longer need to play all copies during the Deployment phase but can simply fly them down to your main floor as you draw them. It is typically not worth fishing for {{Icon|ArchusWings}} '''[[Archus' Wing]]''' or {{Icon|WingsOfLight}} '''[[Wings of Light]]''' because of the risk of losing the upgrade, and because '''Cluster Colonel''''s stats are generally unimportant.
summary: Cluster Colonel is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. At the end of the turn, he [[Spawn|Spawns]] 4.

title: Morel Mistress

flavor.value: "A mushroom's rotting scent tells you all you need to know about them."

tables: '''Dualstone''' grants {{IconLink|Dualism}}, which is the best upgrade for '''Morel Mistress''', letting her apply {{IconLink|Decay|16}} per {{IconLink|Etch}}.
'''Smidgestone''' makes '''Morel Mistress''' {{Capacity|1}}, allowing you to fit multiple copies of her onto a floor.

'''Heartstone''' provides a simple boost to {{Health}}, letting '''Morel Mistress''' survive longer in early rings and granting protection against enemies that threaten the backline. '''Morel Mistress''' has few desirable upgrades, so this can be useful just to fill out her slots for cheap.

If '''Morel Mistress''' is your backline removal, and you're up against e.g. [[Champion of Savagery]] or unprepared for [[Savagery's Final Assault]], then {{IconLink|Endless}} from '''Immortalstone''' is one method of keeping her available each turn against backline enemies with {{IconLink|Sweep}} that would otherwise kill her. She will still be unable to remove waves with a [[Deafening Herald]], however, and redrawing her means you will draw fewer Consume cards that turn. Plus if your floor is overstacked with a [[Funguy]], then you won't be able to replay your {{IconLink|Endless}} '''Morel Mistress''' once she dies.
summary: Morel Mistress is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever a card is Consumed on her floor, she applies {{IconLink|Decay|8}} to all enemies on the floor.

title: Prickly Puffball

flavor.value: Although they do not possess much dangerous strength, they are hard to defeat as the Puffballs were born and raised in the burls of the Fatal Elm itself.

tables: '''Dualstone''' grants {{IconLink|Dualism}}, allowing '''Prickly Puffball''' to apply {{IconLink|Decay|10}} on {{IconLink|Revenge}}. If equipped with Loamcoat, it also grants an extra stack of {{IconLink|Regen}} each turn.

'''Titanstone''' grants {{IconLink|Titanite}}, halving the damage taken from all sources. In combination with {{IconLink|Regen}}, this can allow '''Prickly Puffball''' to become nigh-invincible, healing all damage taken every round.

'''Largestone''' bolsters '''Prickly Puffball''' with a considerable amount of {{Health}} and a bit of {{Attack}}, increasing its survivability. The increased {{Capacity}} is often not an issue, as the unit will often hold down a floor on its own.

'''Immortalstone''' ensures that '''Prickly Puffball''' can be replayed if it is killed. If you anticipate that it will eventually be overwhelmed by the amount of damage it will take, such as when facing [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], this is a good way of keeping it alive.

'''Mossystone''' and '''Heartstone''' provide a decent amount of survivability if you are not offered other upgrades, or if you simply want to fill out [[Prickly Puffball]]'s slots. However, be aware that if you can afford to reroll the shop, you are guaranteed to see at least one of the major upgrades listed above.

'''Courage''', from the [[Path of the Angel]] event, deserves special mention for '''Prickly Puffball'''. In addition to increasing its durability tremendously by granting a full heal and {{IconLink|Armor}} every three turns, its innate '''[[Advance]]''' effect makes it far easier to use alongside {{IconLink|Rally}}-based strategies, as you can move '''Prickly Puffball''' in front of Funguy as soon as it spawns. This preserves Funguy's {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks, making it a more effective attacker, while still letting '''Prickly Puffball''' do its job, and even lets it benefit from units like [[Amorous Enoki]].
summary: Prickly Puffball is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. It applies {{IconLink|Decay|5}} to the attacker on {{IconLink|Revenge}}.

title: Spore Launcher

flavor.value: Pulled into war after the Fatal Elm's destruction, the Spore Launchers never desired weapons and war. All these gentle shroomfolk desired was to reintroduce the native Hell Inferno Mushroom to Hell.

tables: '''Smidgestone''' allows multiple '''Spore Launchers''' and other units like [[Cluster Colonel]]s to be easily played on a single floor. The Underlegion really values its {{Capacity}}, making this quite important in many runs.
summary: Spore Launcher is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. It applies {{IconLink|Decay|2}} to enemy units on {{IconLink|Rally}}.

title: Squad Leader

flavor.value: "Come on you sorry sprouts! Get those gills in gear and fight!"

tables: '''Heartstone''' helps keep '''Squad Leader''' alive without affecting its {{Capacity}}.
summary: Squad Leader is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. It buffs the {{Attack}} of the floor's [[Funguy]] and adds {{IconLink|Trample}}.

title: Balmabello

ability.value:
{{IconLink|Regen|6}}. {{IconLink|Spikes|6}}.
{{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Apply this unit's '''[[Buff]]''' stacks to friendly units.

flavor.value: "On victory, you deserve a glass of my special Spore-brew. Upon defeat, you'll need it."

tables: '''Dualstone''' is the most important upgrade one can put on '''Balmabello'''. Doubling its natural buff stacks, alongside any other buff upgrades given to it, is extremely strong.

'''Furystone''', '''Bravestone''', and '''Glimmerstone''' are all valuable damage-boosting buffs for their respective clans, especially when paired with '''Dualstone'''. They also have the advantage of being guaranteed to see in the shop if you can afford a reroll.

'''Frankenstone''' provides '''Balmabello''' with free {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, letting its ability trigger multiple times. Like the above upgrades, it is a minor upgrade and thus guaranteed with a reroll.

These upgrades from the [[Inscryption]] event are a tremendous boon for '''Balmabello'''. '''Many Lives''' grants {{IconLink|Reanimate|3}}, like a more powerful '''Frankenstone''' available to any clan, while '''Worthy Sacrifice''' allows you to not only kill '''Balmabello''' at will, but gain {{Ember|3}} for doing so, potentially offsetting its cost. If you get the follow-up event, you can put both of these upgrades on it, allowing you to immediately give your entire floor {{IconLink|Spikes|6}}, {{IconLink|Regen|6}}, and {{IconLink|Reanimate|2}} while also gaining {{Ember|3}} - and that's without '''Dualstone'''.

'''Savage Heart''' is a game-breaking upgrade for '''Balmabello'''. Due to its high {{Health}}, it needs to be placed at the front of the floor in order to die anyway, which means it will accumulate unbelievable amounts of {{IconLink|Rage}} over time, and as soon as it dies that {{IconLink|Rage}} will be shared with every other unit on the floor.

'''Frailty Penance''' is mostly useful on '''Balmabello''' due to making it {{IconLink|Fragile}}, which gives you a huge amount of control over exactly when it dies. Because the "drawback" of this upgrade can actually be beneficial, it's often advisable '''not''' to replace it with {{IconLink|Frailty Absolution}} when offered.

Although '''Immortalstone''' can allow repeated usage of '''Balmabello''', this isn't an ideal upgrade. '''Balmabello''' is very expensive to play multiple times, and it takes away an upgrade slot that could otherwise be used to expand the buffs it passes on.
summary: Balmabello is a rare [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. It starts with {{IconLink|Regen|6}} and {{IconLink|Spikes|6}}, and when it dies, all of its [[Buff]] stacks are applied all friendly units on the floor.

title: Deathcapped Prophet

flavor.value: "Don't listen to those other so-called 'prophets.' I'm the real seer around here!"

tables: '''Heartstone''' is the only worthwhile upgrade on '''Deathcapped Prophet''', granting him a buffer against {{IconLink|Sweep}} and {{IconLink|Spikes}}.
summary: Deathcapped Prophet is a rare [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. He grants +1 card draw next turn for each {{IconLink|Rally}} on his floor.

title: Enchantrelle

flavor.value: "I know a mushroom has fallen in love with me when they fear to sleep. My lovely spores give them nightmares of their heart's greatest fear: being away from me."

tables: '''Smidgestone''' reduces '''Enchantrelle''' to {{Capacity|1}}, making it easier to fit other {{IconLink|Rally}} units on her floor, even though it is usually infeasible to duplicate her due to her high {{Ember}} cost.
'''Heartstone''' allows '''Enchantrelle''' to survive {{IconLink|Spikes}} and [[Qel the Corruptor]] and [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]]'s {{IconLink|Corruption}}.
summary: Enchantrelle is a rare [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever a friendly unit is summoned on her floor, she applies {{IconLink|Sap|1}} to all enemy units.

title: Glow Up

flavor.value: The lantern knight giggled. A spa stay and a makeover was exactly what he needed to lift his spirits.

tables: '''Keepstone''' allows you to play this card every turn, which is useful if you need to [[Propagate]] a frontliner consistently.
'''Emberstone''' makes this card free to play, which is always a nice benefit.
'''Twinstone''' allows you to [[Propagate]] effects on a fragile backline unit, then move a tank back in front of them before the enemies can attack.
summary: Glow Up is a common [[Underlegion]] card. It brings a unit to the front of the floor and [[Propagate]]s 2.

title: Gooey Flask

flavor.value: The shroomfolk harvest the sap of the Fatal Elm when the leaves are at their most putrid. Once boiled, the sap becomes a tasty syrup that makes you want to curl up beneath a root and sleep.

tables: '''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Sap}} applied, which more than doubles its impact.
'''Twinstone''' also accomplishes this, perhaps with a {{IconLink|Emberstone}}, or perhaps with '''Stackstone''' to really shut down one problematic wave even late in the game.

'''Eternalstone''' can be considered as a way to lean into {{IconLink|Sap}} as a strategy, though it's hard to do that well with this card without [[Lightstone Casing]]. It's usually better to duplicate this card or invest in other {{IconLink|Sap}} sources.
summary: Gooey Flask is a common [[Underlegion]] card. It applies {{IconLink|Sap|2}} to enemy units.

title: Proliferate

flavor.value: Within moments, the shroomfolk had devoured the demon's hand and began consuming their way toward his head.

tables: '''Eternalstone''' lets you keep this useful card around throughout the fight, letting you make it a more core part of your strategy.
'''Keepstone''' can be excellent if you can manage to apply it after '''Eternalstone''', turning just a few buff/debuff cards into strategies all on their own.
'''Emberstone''' is also a great add, as this card is very easy to play and adding '''Emberstone''' improves your {{Ember}} economy. It makes this card more spammable if duplicated too.
'''Twinstone''' doubles this card's output, effectively making it Propagate 4, or letting you play it on two different floors.
summary: Proliferate is a common [[Underlegion]] card. It [[Propagate]]s 2 on the floor it's cast on.

title: Spawning Pods

flavor.value: "Finally! We're free!" cried the first young mushroom. "What do you want to do first?" asked the second. "I don't know, is there any mulch to eat?" answered the third.

tables: You could apply '''Eternalstone''' to let you replay this card in smaller decks looking to leverage a lot of {{IconLink|Rally}} triggers. It also allows the addition of '''Smolderstone''' to reduce it to {{Ember|0}}. That said, there are several incentives the [[Underlegion]] have towards a larger deck, making '''Eternalstone''' less useful, and it will turn off {{IconLink|Etch}}. So this requires a specific kind of run.
'''Seekstone''' reduces this card's cost and allows you to start building up a Funguy stack and triggering {{IconLink|Rally}} right from the start of the fight.
summary: Spawning Pods is a common [[Underlegion]] card. It spawns 4 Funguys.

title: Rot

flavor.value: ''When he drew his hand back from the tree's roots, he found spores had settled on his skin like dust. First, he felt warm, then hot. Until his limb was engulfed in the unbearable pain of rotting alive.''

tables: '''Stackstone''' doubles the amount of {{IconLink|Decay}} this provides - if you can stall out {{IconLink|Decay|30}}, the boss will take a total of 1320 damage from this card. That's enough to single-handedly kill bosses through Ring 5, including [[Ajax the Unyielding]] for runs that are otherwise countered by him.

'''Smolderstone''' helps make this card be affordable {{Ember}}-wise, and while adding [[Consume]] isn't great, it also means that it interacts with {{IconLink|Etch}} triggers and empowers cards like [[Unearth Treasure]]. It's a fine target to be retrieved by [[Unearth Treasure]] with this upgrade as well.
'''Emberstone''' is helpful either instead of or in addition to '''Smolderstone''' to bring the {{Ember}} cost down, as can '''Seekstone'''.

'''Freezestone''' can be considered if you're relying on this card as your answer for non-Flying bosses like [[Ajax the Unyielding]] or [[Rax the Overblessed]]. It also reduces its {{Ember}} cost slightly.
summary: Rot is a common [[Underlegion]] card. It deals 15 damage and applies {{IconLink|Decay|15}} to a target.

title: Dig Deep

effect.value: '''[[Spawn]] 1'''. For every '''10''' cards in your deck '''Spawn 1''' more.

flavor.value: "Come sit with us in the shade. Don't worry, we won't hurt you."

tables: In a large deck, '''Dig Deep''' is good, but you won't draw it that often. '''Keepstone''' solves that problem nicely, and can allow a {{IconLink|Rally}} based build to thrive. '''Seekstone''' can also be valuable in larger decks to ensure you'll see it soon enough, as well as reduce its cost.
If {{IconLink|Rally}}/[[Funguy]] isn't the primary focus of your deck, '''Smolderstone''' makes '''Dig Deep''' affordable and synergizes with {{IconLink|Etch}}.
summary: Dig Deep is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] spell. It [[Spawn]]s 1 for every 10 cards in your deck.

title: Fertile Ground

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
'''[[Spawn]] 1'''. '''Spawn 1''' more for each card in your consume pile.

flavor.value: "Poor soldier. We'll put him back together," whispered the fungi beneath the battlefield. "Your body will be a perfect place for us to grow."

tables: '''Freezestone''' helps solve this card's {{Ember}} cost and helps when you draw this card early, letting you save it for when more cards are in your [[Consume]] pile without having to draw it again.

If you have [[The Great Decay]], '''Eternalstone''' keeps this card around to be replayed over and over once the rest of the deck has [[Consume]]d, allowing you to [[Spawn]] an absurd number of [[Funguy]]. Because The Great Decay applies {{Ember|-1}}, any cost reduction upgrade will be enough to bring this spell's cost to {{Ember|0}}.

While The Great Decay is highly recommended with this, any deck with a large concentration of [[Consume]] spells can make this combo work well - in that case, other non-Consuming spells should be high Purge priorities.
summary: Fertile Ground is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] spell. It [[Spawn]]s 1, plus 1 more for each card in the consume pile.

title: Inhale

flavor.value: Even the smallest shroomfolk have found ways to defend themselves. Some, when inhaled, consume the lungs of their victims from the inside out.

tables: '''Powerstone''' and '''Surgestone''' let '''Inhale''' kill some higher-{{Health}} targets. '''Surgestone''' lets it kill [[Vampiric Cherub]]s and [[Nourishing Cherub]]s, and also synergizes with {{IconLink|Etch}} as well.

If you're looking to use this as a way to ensure you can consistently kill your own units like an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Cheery Deathcap]] or [[Waxcap]], '''Keepstone''', possibly with a '''Seekstone''', can accomplish that.
summary: Inhale is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] spell. It deals 10 damage to its target, and on {{IconLink|Slay}} [[Spawn]]s 2.

title: Mulch

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Draw '''+1''' next turn. For every '''15''' cards in your deck, draw '''1''' more.

flavor.value:
We grow in the shadow of Death.
—old Underlegion saying

summary: Mulch is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] card. It draws +1 on the next turn, and another +1 for every 15 cards in the deck.

title: Mushroom Cloud

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
'''[[Sacrifice]] 1 [[Funguy]]'''. Deal '''10''' damage and apply {{IconLink|Decay|10}} to enemy units.

flavor.value: "PORCINI GO BOOM!"

tables: It can be worth using '''Eternalstone''' on '''Mushroom Cloud''' due to its power if you have a small deck. However, the [[Underlegion]]'s {{IconLink|Etch}} triggers and incentives towards larger decks means this shouldn't be considered every run.
'''Stackstone''' causes this spell to apply {{IconLink|Decay|20}} to all enemies, representing 171 total damage just from the {{IconLink|Decay}} alone by the time enemies reach the top floor.
summary: Mushroom Cloud is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] spell. It removes a single stack of {{IconLink|Troop}}, then deals 10 damage and applies {{IconLink|Decay|10}} to all enemies on the floor.

title: Pandemic

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Apply {{IconLink|Decay|8}} and {{IconLink|Sap|2}}. Add a copy of this card to your discard pile.

flavor.value: "I know she's our enemy, but I just can't help myself, I'm in love!" said the angel. "You too?! I feel as if I've been infected with love!" hissed his captain.

tables: '''Emberstone''' reduces '''Pandemic''''s cost, making it easier to play, which you will be doing frequently. '''Freezestone''' and '''Seekstone''' have the same cost-reducing effect, but are more expensive. '''Seekstone''' at least lets you get '''Pandemic''' into play as early as possible.

'''Stackstone''' causes '''Pandemic''' to apply {{IconLink|Decay|16}} and {{IconLink|Sap|4}}, which is a tremendous upgrade. Few cards should be prioritized more highly if you are offered '''Stackstone'''.

'''Entropic Stone''' is an incredible upgrade for '''Pandemic'''. Applying '''Triplestack''' causes the card to apply {{IconLink|Decay|24}} and {{IconLink|Sap|6}}, which can rapidly render enemies completely harmless and is almost always worth the [[Entropic Crystals]]. It makes '''Pandemic''' a very potent target for duplication effects as well, to cast it as often as possible. However, it is incompatible with {{IconLink|Stackstone}}.
Removing Consume via '''Eternalstone''' can let this card flood your deck after a few turns. It also allows you to apply '''Smolderstone''', to reduce its cost to {{Ember|0}}.
'''Twinstone''' can provide some extra {{IconLink|Etch}} fuel, essentially letting you play the card three times per deck cycle.
summary: Pandemic is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Sap}} and {{IconLink|Decay}}, and although it [[Consume]]s, it also puts a copy of itself in the discard pile when played, letting you draw it again.

title: Pox

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Deal '''20''' damage and apply {{IconLink|Decay|10}} to all units.

flavor.value: The soldiers moved with uncertain steps towards the Fatal Elm. "Pray to your gods," came a whisper from beneath the mulch. Spore clouds erupted. "For you are to receive the Mushroom's Kiss.

tables: If you can afford its high cost in terms of both {{Gold}} and {{Ember}}, the combination of '''Eternalstone''' and '''Keepstone''' lets you play this spell consistently, clearing out whole waves of enemies. Alternatively, '''Smolderstone''' can reduce its cost to {{Ember|0}} once '''Eternalstone''' is applied, making it much easier to play and a better choice for duplication.
The more common way to use this card repeatedly involves duplicating it, making '''Emberstone''' helpful to make this more affordable.
'''Stackstone''' can be considered to double the {{IconLink|Decay}} applied.
summary: Pox is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] spell. It deals 20 damage to all units on the floor, including both enemies and friendly units, and applies {{IconLink|Decay|10}}.

title: Contagious

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Enemy units '''[[Propagate]] 4'''. Add a copy of this card to your discard pile.

flavor.value: The Angels once had an outpost where the roots of the Wild Woods met the sands of Limbo. That is, until the Fatal Elm decided it had had enough of their presence and released its spores.

tables: '''Emberstone''' reduces '''Contagious''''s cost, making it easier to play, which you will be doing frequently. '''Freezestone''' does the same, but is more expensive in exchange for adding '''[[Permafrost]]''', letting you hold onto the card until the right moment.
'''Twinstone''' lets you Propagate 8 with one card draw.
summary: Contagious is a rare [[Underlegion]] spell. It [[Propagate]]s 4 on enemy units. Despite having [[Consume]], it adds a copy of itself to the discard pile when played, so it can be played repeatedly.

title: Deadly Variant

flavor.value: The angel tried to escape the frenzy of the battle but it was too late. The Fatal Elm had its spores in him. Soon, they would eat away at him and transform his body until he was more fungus than flesh.

tables:
'''Eternalstone''' lets you play this repeatedly, and in particular lets you play it on each of the [[The Great Abyss#Clash with the Titans|Titans]] once they've been {{IconLink|Sap}}ped. You can pair this with '''Smolderstone''' to make it cost {{Ember|0}}.
