'''Eternalstone''' can potentially synergize with [[The Great Decay]], letting you finish off {{IconLink|Sap}}ped [[Flying Bosses]] and [[The Great Abyss#Clash with the Titans|Titans]] quickly once your deck is gone. (Make sure you have an answer to dangerous non-flying bosses like [[Rax the Overblessed]] in this case, however.)
'''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Decay}} applied, letting it finish off weakened [[Flying Bosses]] faster.

'''Freezestone''' is a solid choice as well, as this is a timing-sensitive card that needs to be played after {{IconLink|Sap}} is applied but in time to let its {{IconLink|Decay}} damage add up. The {{Ember|-1}} is appreciated as well.
summary: Deadly Variant is a rare [[Underlegion]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Decay|5}} to the target for each stack of {{IconLink|Sap}} they have.

title: Funguy in a Suit

flavor.value: "I'll be the arm!" said one mushroom. "And I'll be the head!" said another. A small voice spoke from the bottom of the armor, 'Why do I have do be down here?"

tables: '''Eternalstone''' is an important upgrade for this spell, as letting you cast it more than once means you can continue to build more and more {{IconLink|Armor}}, keeping {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks high even during {{IconLink|Relentless}}. It also allows you to add '''Smolderstone''' to massively reduce its cost.
summary: Funguy in a Suit is a rare [[Underlegion]] spell. It [[Spawn]]s 3, then adds a significant amount of {{IconLink|Armor}} to Funguy.

title: Spike of the Legion

flavor.value: Whenever anyone tried to build the Rail through the Underlegion's realm, they found the iron overcome by spores and fungi.

tables: '''Emberstone''' and other {{Ember}} upgrades can increase this card's potency. Depending on what you're using it for, '''Seekstone''' or '''Freezestone''' can give you access to it at the right moment in combat. '''Entropic Energy''' can be potent if found.
'''Eternalstone''' can allow you to replay this card if your deck is small or has many [[Consume]] cards, and allows application of '''Smolderstone''' to provide a stronger {{Ember}} discount.
summary: Spike of the Legion is a rare [[Underlegion]] spell. It [[Propagate]]s 2X on its target, increasing all [[Buff]]s by 2X if used on a friendly unit, or [[Debuff]]s by 2X if used on an enemy unit.

title: The Great Decay

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]].'''
Apply '''[[Consume]]''' and {{Ember|-1}} to all spells in your deck.

flavor.value: "Spore to mycelium, mushroom to mulch, the Great Decay is the cycle that rules our lives. To go against the Decay is to go against life."—Traditional epitaph found on the graves of the Underlegion

tables: '''Seekstone''' reduces the cost of this spell, as well as guaranteeing that you can play it instantly. This gets your Consume engine going immediately, and clears out your unwanted cards as soon as possible.
'''Emberstone''' and '''Freezestone''' can also be used to reduce this card's cost.

'''Twinstone''' is best with an {{Ember}}-reducing upgrade, but allows you to reduce the cost of all spells in your deck by {{Ember|2}} while adding no further downside. This can allow even un-upgraded copies of [[Pandemic]] and [[Contagious]] to cost {{Ember|0}}.
summary: The Great Decay is a rare [[Underlegion]] spell added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It applies [[Consume]] and {{Ember|-1}} to all spells in your deck.

title: Tome of Evergrowth

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Apply {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}: Evergrowth to a friendly unit.
{{AbilityBox|Evergrowth|1|Apply {{IconLink|Regen|3}} and {{IconLink|Sap|3}}.}}

flavor.value: ''The archives of the Wild Woods and the Hell Oak from which Underlegion are spawned.''

tables: When you want this ability, you often want multiple units to have it. '''Twinstone''' helps you do just that with the help of an [[Empyrean Well]] or two.

As you'll want to be spamming this spell early, it's nice to put a '''Seekstone''' on it to draw it on turn 1 and play for {{Ember|0}}. If you can't find a Seekstone, an '''Emberstone''' can at least help with the cost reduction.

If you have a lot of units, you could consider '''Eternalstone''', either with a small deck or with '''Keepstone''', to take your spamming of '''Evergrowth''' to the next level.

Note that even once you don't have a unit without the '''Evergrowth''' ability, this spell can allow a unit with '''Evergrowth''' on cooldown to use '''Evergrowth''' again this turn.
summary: Tome of Evergrowth is a rare [[Underlegion]] spell. It applies the {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}} Evergrowth to a unit, which has a 1 turn cooldown and applies {{IconLink|Sap|3}} and {{IconLink|Regen|3}} to a target unit on the same floor. (A unit with Evergrowth can target itself.)

title: Unearth Treasure

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''. '''[[Distinct]]'''.
Return '''1''' random spell from your consume pile that isn't Unearth Treasure. If there are at least '''5''' cards in the consume pile, return '''1''' more.

flavor.value: Beneath the mulch in the Wild Woods, treasure from before the Covenant can be found.

tables: '''Eternalstone''' allows you to keep '''Unearth Treasure''' around for the entire combat. Combine this with '''Keepstone''', and for {{Ember|1}} you can essentially put [[Holdover]] on any Consume card in your deck.

[[Unearth Treasure]] wording changed from "Draw a random spell from your consume pile..." >>> "Return a random spell from your consume pile..." due to 'draw' being inaccurate to what the card is actually doing.
Updated card text for cards that exclude themselves with new keyword '''[[Distinct]]'''. [[Stardust Invocation]] and [[Unearth Treasure]] are examples.
summary: Unearth Treasure is a rare [[Underlegion]] spell. It returns a [[Consume|consumed]] card back to your hand (or two cards if you have at least five or more Consumed cards).

title: Wracking Pain

effect.value: Deal damage equal to '''3x''' the '''[[Debuff]]''' stacks on this unit.

flavor.value:
"The pain... What an amazing olfactory note for my latest scent."
—Madame Lionsmane

tables: '''Freezestone''' lets you save this card for the right moment.
'''Emberstone''' is a solid addition, as this card doesn't really need any particular upgrade in many cases.
'''Twinstone''' can be a solid way to double your output, especially with '''Emberstone'''.
summary: Wracking Pain is a rare [[Underlegion]] spell. It deals damage equal to 3x the total stacks of debuffs on the target.

title: Loamcoat

flavor.value: The dapperling special ops unit knows the importance of good soil to a shroom's performance. They went one step further and found a way to bring soil to the battlefield.

tables: Fixed bug where [[Loamcoat]]'s [[Propagate]] was impacted by {{IconLink|Dualism}}.
summary: Loamcoat is a common [[Underlegion]] equipment. It grants its wearer {{Health|+20}} and gives it a {{IconLink|Resolve}} trigger that first gives it {{IconLink|Regen|1}}, then [[Propagate]]s 2, increasing all of its buff stacks, including {{IconLink|Regen}}, by 2.

title: Mitosis Cap

effect.value: {{IconLink|Celebrate}}: Gain a permanent copy of this unit. Cannot be equipped to [[Champion]] or {{IconLink|Cardless}} units.

flavor.value: Death is an opportunity to make a new, better version of yourself. This is a lesson many have known for as long as the roots of the Fatal Elm are deep.

summary: Mitosis Cap is a rare [[Underlegion]] equipment. Each time a unit equipped with Mitosis Cap survives a battle, the {{IconLink|Celebrate}} trigger adds a permanent copy of that unit to the deck.

title: Grow Room

effect.value: All units '''[[Propagate]]''' 1 at the end of combat.

flavor.value: "Do you think they'll be angry that we're in here?" whispered a small crimini. "If they are," began his brother, "We'll take care of them."

tables: New card text says "at the end of combat" instead of "at the end of turn".
summary: Grow Room is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] room. It makes all units, including enemies and friendly units, [[Propagate]] 1 at the end of combat each turn.

title: Infectory

flavor.value: "Thanks for the ride!" cried the funguy as they leapt from the demon's torso. The angel gurgled in horror.

summary: Infectory is a common [[Underlegion]] room. It spawns a [[Funguy]] whenever any non-Funguy unit is killed.

title: Mushy Room

effect.value: Apply {{IconLink|Sap|3}} to enemy units at the end of combat.

flavor.value:
"Do you think they'll make a wonderful perfume once the fungus is done with them?"
—Madame Lionsmane

summary: Mushy Room is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] room. It applies {{IconLink|Sap|3}} to enemy units at the end of combat.

title: Lazarus League

flavor.value: ''Mix in powers of the mad scientists and their dangerous experiments. Their power over life and death will lead to victory, and if it doesn't you can always use the pieces they leave behind.''

summary: Lazarus League [[File:ClanLazarusLeague.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]].

title: Orechi

flavor.value: Fired from academia, Dr. Orechi returned to his family's estate in Trans-HELL-vania and set up a private laboratory. No one in Hell quite knows what he does, but many know not to set foot inside.

summary: Orechi is the primary [[Champion]] of the [[Lazarus League]] clan. Fittingly for his mad doctor persona, his paths vary wildly in effect, from turning into a living bomb to brewing infusions to help his team. His starter card is [[Secret Ingredient]].

title: Baron Grael

flavor.value: He has no noble lineage yet calls himself 'Baron' and forever pursues a cure to a disease he does not suffer from. Some assistants believe his work is not for his sake, but for one he holds very dear.

tables: Living Armory I health increased from {{Health|5}} -> {{Health|10}}.

[[Baron Grael]] Learning Limb stats updated from {{AttackHealth|15/25}}, {{AttackHealth|30/40}}, {{AttackHealth|60/60}} >>> {{AttackHealth|10/25}}, {{AttackHealth|20/45}}, {{AttackHealth|40/80}}. Permanent {{Attack}} granted to equipment increased from '''2/4/6''' >>> '''3/6/9'''. [[Baron Grael]] It Hungers {{Health}} reduced from '''25/45/85''' >>> '''20/40/80'''.
summary: Baron Grael is the alternate [[Champion]] of the [[Lazarus League]]. His paths revolve around the usage of equipment and the {{IconLink|Graft}} units that hold it. His starter card is [[Erratic Assistant]].

title: Secret Ingredient

flavor.value: Not all ingredients in this concoction are rare, fragile, or even illegal. Sometimes all you need is a bit of salt to make a potion all the more potent.

tables: Putting '''Emberstone''' on '''Secret Ingredient''' helps you spam it more, and in many cases this is a straightforward way to get more value out of your turn.

'''Twinstone''' doubles the amount of mixing you can do, and '''Keepstone''' gives you consistent access to it. '''Keepstone''' is particularly good with [[Progress Pacemaker]], letting you consistently get your bonus [[Mix]]. If you have a lot of {{Ember}}, you could apply both, or with [[Lightstone Casing]] you could apply both and an {{Ember}} discount. Despite this card being a starter card, these upgrades can be worth applying in some runs - a testament to how useful [[Infusion]]s can be.
summary: Secret Ingredient is [[Orechi]]'s starter card. It [[Mix]]es, granting the player an [[Infusion]] or upgrading their existing one. See the [[Infusion]] page for more details.

title: Erratic Assistant

flavor.value: "I traded my hands with the doctor's topiary trimming monstrosity. I think I got the better end of that deal."

summary: Erratic Assistant is [[Baron Grael]]'s starter card. She has [[Scissor Hands]] grafted to her.

title: Overworked Assistant

flavor.value: "After The Incident, I followed Dr. Orechi to Trans-HELL-vania to continue my research. Maybe I should have stayed at the university. Even as a PhD student I wasn't given so much work."

tables: '''Dualstone''' is highly desirable for the extra {{IconLink|Unstable}} generation and additional {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stack.
'''Frankenstone''' is a worthwhile pickup for this unit, since most other [[Merchant of Steel]] upgrades are either useless or actively harmful.

'''Immortalstone''' isn't needed if trying to stack significant amounts of {{IconLink|Unstable}} (which is lost on death). But when combined with a few {{IconLink|Incant}}s, an {{IconLink|Endless}} '''Overworked Assistant''' is an option for clearing low-health backliners if you aren't able to stack {{IconLink|Reanimate}} to sufficient levels.
summary: Overworked Assistant is a common [[Lazarus League]] unit. He gets {{IconLink|Unstable|4}} on {{IconLink|Incant}}.

title: Sanguine Assistant

flavor.value: "Have you seen the new implants in my teeth? Now, with just a nibble here and there, my body feels as good as new!"

summary: Sanguine Assistant is a common [[Lazarus League]] unit. She has [[Vampire's Tooth]] grafted to her, which provides a consistent source of {{IconLink|Lifesteal}}.

title: Twisted Assistant

flavor.value: "Dr. Inga was the only one who would look at me like a human, not a creation."

summary: Twisted Assistant is a common [[Lazarus League]] unit. He has [[Twisted Back]] grafted to him, which grants {{IconLink|Trample}} and {{IconLink|Rage|2}} on {{IconLink|Strike}}.

title: Pufferflesh

flavor.value: "Dr. Inga had an aquarium filled with the most devilish fish. When she got hurt, I promised her I would take care of her pets. I think Dr. Orechi heard me because the next day I looked like this."

summary: Pufferflesh is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] unit. He starts with [[Spiky Skin]] grafted onto him, which grants {{IconLink|Spikes}} on {{IconLink|Revenge}}.

title: Hulking Mass

flavor.value: "Don't judge a book by its cover. I might not look like it but I have dancer's feet. Literally."

tables: '''Dualstone''' is one of the strongest possible upgrades for '''Hulking Mass''', significantly improving both its initial and scaling defense. It doubles both its initial {{IconLink|Armor}}, as well as each instance of {{IconLink|Armor}} gained from being {{IconLink|Reanimated}}, from 40 to 80. {{IconLink|Dualism}} also doubles buffs added by equipment, several of which are ideal for '''Hulking Mass''' in-clan, such as [[Organ Harvester]] and [[Spiky Skin]] from [[Pufferflesh]].

'''Titanstone''' serves a similar purpose to '''Dualstone''' and is also a strong consideration. With {{IconLink|Titanite}}, '''Hulking Mass''' has more effective frontloaded defense (being able to tank 120 damage upfront instead of 100), and effectively gains the same amount of scaling defense, being able to tank 80 damage after each {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. However, it does not have the same synergy with equipment and other upgrades that {{IconLink|Dualism}} offers. If {{Capacity}} is not a concern and you have good enough Merchants of Steel to hold out for upgrades, it can be very strong to combine both '''Dualstone''' and '''Titanstone''', as they stack multiplicatively, giving 160 effective {{Armor}} whenever {{IconLink|Reanimated}}.
'''Smidgestone''' shrinks '''Hulking Mass''' from {{Capacity|3}} to {{Capacity|1}}, making it easier to fit other units behind it.

'''Frankenstone''' is a strong consideration to fill out upgrade slots, adding {{IconLink|Reanimate|1}} to get '''Hulking Mass''' going and provide security in case your {{IconLink|Reanimate}} engine is slow to come online. If you happen to find the [[Inscryption]] event, '''Many Lives''' is essentially a supercharged '''Frankenstone''', and is an incredible upgrade for '''Hulking Mass'''. Both of them synergizes well with '''Dualstone''', doubling the {{IconLink|Reanimate}} granted.
summary: Hulking Mass is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] [[banner unit]]. It starts with {{IconLink|Armor|40}} and gains another {{IconLink|Armor|40}} when {{IconLink|Reanimated}}.

title: Makeshift Golem

flavor.value: "I am made of mud but I have a heart of gold."

tables: '''Dualstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Armor}} '''Makeshift Golem''' applies, both on {{IconLink|Extinguish}} and when played. It will also double the stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} gained from Organ Harvester if used with a source of {{IconLink|Spikes}}, making the unit much more self-sufficient.
'''Frankenstone''' provides immediate {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, and is doubled if used alongside '''Dualstone'''.

'''Immortalstone''' ensures that '''Makeshift Golem''' won't stay dead, even if you cannot give it enough {{IconLink|Reanimate}} in time. This upgrade is strong if you have inconsistent {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, but does not work well with [[Tome of Horrors]] or [[Faulty Body]], as those effects will be cleared on death. It '''does''' work well with [[Scrap for Parts]], as this will effectively trigger its {{IconLink|Extinguish}} ability immediately and grant it {{Attack|+40}}.
'''Smidgestone''' allows you to play more units behind '''Makeshift Golem''' and thus increase the recipients of its {{IconLink|Armor}}.
summary: The Makeshift Golem is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] [[banner unit]]. It grants {{IconLink|Armor|12}} to friendly units on {{IconLink|Extinguish}}.

title: Meathook

flavor.value:
"One day, he just dragged himself to the lab and never left. Nobody knows where he came from. And honestly, I don't want to know."
—Baron Grael

tables: '''Dualstone''' is the most critical upgrade for '''Meathook''', doubling the {{IconLink|Dazed}} he applies from 1 to 2. This can help buy an extra turn in {{IconLink|Relentless}} or send dangerous enemies that cannot immediately be killed into the Pyre room with a buffer before they can attack. With '''Meathook''' on your floor or even a two-floor setup, this allows you to perpetually stunlock flying bosses until {{IconLink|Relentless}}, preventing them from activating their gimmicks for the entire fight.
'''Smidgestone''' shrinks '''Meathook''' to {{Capacity|1}}, allowing you to more easily slot him into floors with other units.
If playing '''Meathook''' alone, '''Largestone''' improves his damage and survivability significantly, allowing him to more effectively clean up units on higher floors.
summary: Meathook is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] [[banner unit]]. Once every two turns, he can pull a unit forward and apply {{IconLink|Dazed}}.

title: Pincushion

flavor.value: "Greeeeeeegh!"

tables: '''Frenzystone''' is nice on '''Pincushion''' due to her potential for high {{Attack}}. It is practically mandatory if you are using '''Pincushion''' as an attacker, as otherwise she scales too slowly, even with many copies.
'''Smidgestone''' makes '''Pincushion''' much easier to copy many times after she has been scaled up. This is the other best way to use the unit offensively.
'''Immortalstone''' is useful when using the unit as a tank, as it ensures that even if '''Pincushion''' is killed, she can be replayed.
'''Titanstone''' grants {{IconLink|Titanite}}, halving all damage taken and making '''Pincushion''' a practically unparalleled tank that has the potential to strike back hard.
summary: Pincushion is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] [[banner unit]]. She scales her {{Attack}} and {{Health}} permanently when {{IconLink|Equipped}}.

title: Plague Doctor

ability.value: {{IconLink|Strike}}: Apply {{IconLink|Unstable}} equal to the damage dealt.

flavor.value: "Nothing is quite so poetic as an ancient plague. For some reason, no one wants to hear about my research at dinner parties."

tables: '''Frenzystone''' is the most critical upgrade for '''Plague Doctor''' and is incredibly efficient if you can scale her. {{IconLink|Multistrike}} doubles her damage output as well as her {{IconLink|Unstable}} application, and as she takes only {{Capacity|1}}, she can easily slot into dense floors while increasing the number of hits on the floor.
'''Heartstone''' patches up '''Plague Doctor''''s poor survivability, providing her with recourse against {{IconLink|Spikes}}, {{IconLink|Sweep}}, and {{IconLink|Corruption}} enemies.

'''Largestone''' gives '''Plague Doctor''' a much better statline, with a respectable amount of {{Attack}} and a ton of {{Health}}. However, this forfeits her {{Capacity|1}}, which can be a fairly major drawback.

If you do not need extra {{Health}} or have other ways to protect '''Plague Doctor''', '''Speedstone''' is a much more aggressive upgrade with a high ceiling. If you can scale '''Plague Doctor''' extremely quickly, she will be able to use {{IconLink|Quick}} to kill the frontline enemy and then blow up the entire enemy floor before they can retaliate.

If you are using '''Plague Doctor''' to power up the '''It Hungers''' variant of Baron Grael, '''Strengthstone''' and '''Frankenstone''' are good considerations. These upgrades mostly forfeit the unit's ability to participate meaningfully in combat, but can give Baron Grael a guaranteed {{Attack|+138}} at max level over the first two turns of combat, or even more if you can give her a strong [[Deployable]] equipment like [[Glass Cannon]]. Remember to focus {{Attack}} buffs like [[Risky Operation]] on her, rather than Grael.
summary: For the Celestial Alcove event, see [[Plague Doctor (event)]].

title: Test Subject Alpha

flavor.value: The first subject of <nowiki>'Operation Pecan'</nowiki> and the only one to have survived the series of experiments to create a fully functional, non-aggressive zombie soldier.

tables:
'''Largestone''' is the most critical upgrade for '''Test Subject Alpha''' if it will be placed alone on a lower floor. It fixes his single weakness of low stats immediately, allowing him to survive to the {{IconLink|Relentless}} phase in most combats while taking down all backliners along the way.

If '''Test Subject Alpha''' will not be part of your main floor and you must take {{IconLink|Frenzystone}} on more important scaling units, '''Strengthstone''' is an acceptable fill for an empty slot. The combination of '''Largestone''' and '''Strengthstone''' notably puts '''Test Subject Alpha''' at {{Attack|34}} - barely enough to kill Cael's [[Vampiric Cherub|Vampiric]] and [[Nourishing Cherub]]s without investment. Be aware, however, that this will miss out on Vampiric Cherubs granted {{IconLink|Titanskin}} by [[Chosen Bastion]]s, and will also fail to kill [[Chosen Supplicant]]s, in both cases by a single point of damage. To hit this breakpoint without external support, you might instead apply two '''Largestones'''.

'''Frenzystone''' is a strong consideration for any unit with {{IconLink|Sweep}}. If you have ways of scaling {{Attack}} quickly, giving {{IconLink|Multistrike}} to a sweeper is one of the most damage-efficient upgrades you can make.

A simple {{Health|+20}} from '''Heartstone''' can patch up '''Test Subject Alpha''''s survivability for a cheap price while not increasing his {{Capacity}} should you need to fit him on a floor with other units.

While it may seem strange to put '''Dualstone''' on a unit with no inherent use for it, it can be a solid investment if you intend to use '''Test Subject Alpha''' as your main carry, because {{IconLink|Dualism}} also affects held equipment. Thus, you can double the {{IconLink|Valor}} from [[Everlasting Light]], the {{IconLink|Reanimate}} from [[Organ Harvester]], the {{IconLink|Unstable}} from [[Combustion Suit]], and the {{IconLink|Rage}} from [[Twisted Back]]. It also makes event upgrades like {{IconLink|Savage Heart}}, {{IconLink|Many Lives}}, and {{IconLink|Dominating Power}} more powerful should you be offered them later.
Increased the cost of [[Test Subject Alpha]] from {{Ember|2}} to {{Ember|3}}.
summary: Test Subject Alpha is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] [[banner unit]]. It is the only unit in the game which naturally has both {{IconLink|Quick}} and {{IconLink|Sweep}}.

title: Double-Edged Bearer

flavor.value: "Why not be entirely machine, you ask? Trust me, Dr. Orechi tried. Turns out a body's much easier to manage with a soul inside."

summary: Double-Edged Bearer is a rare [[Lazarus League]] unit. He starts with [[Double-Edged Arms]] grafted to him, which grants {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}}.

title: Hydra Armed Horror

flavor.value:
"Look, I needed someone to hold all my tools while I worked!"
—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

tables: '''Largestone''' amps up '''Hydra Armed Horror''''s stats, and the effect of {{Attack|+15}} is much greater due to its high potential {{IconLink|Multistrike}}.
'''Speedstone''' grants a modest {{Attack}} boost and helps '''Hydra Armed Horror''' with defense by slaughtering enemy waves before they can attack.
'''Strengthstone''' gives nearly as much {{Attack}} as '''Largestone''' and is much cheaper. It also does not increase '''Hydra Armed Horror''''s {{Capacity}}.

Since it is not uncommon for '''Hydra Armed Horror''' to accumulate {{IconLink|Multistrike|10+}}, '''Dominating Power''' and '''Dominating Control''' are both extremely powerful, as they add {{IconLink|Strike}} triggers to the unit. Which one is preferable depends on your deck. If you are relying on sheer number of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} stacks to make up for individually weak hits, or you are trying to get early kills on flying bosses for [[Score]] purposes, '''Dominating Power''' is better. If you can scale '''Hydra Armed Horror''''s {{Attack}} through effects like {{IconLink|Valor}} or {{IconLink|Rage}}, then '''Dominating Control''' will be more powerful.
summary: Hydra Armed Horror is a rare [[Lazarus League]] [[banner unit]]. He gains a stack of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} whenever he is {{IconLink|Equipped}}, but the equipment is instantly removed and the Hydra Armed Horror does not gain any of its stat boosts or effects.

title: Nine-Lived Nightmare

flavor.value:
"Inga's cat still looks for her in the lab. She keeps looking at Dr. Orechi with feline hate. I think she knows something."
—Baron Grael

tables: '''Dualstone''' is the most important upgrade for '''Nine-Lived Nightmare''', giving her {{IconLink|Reanimate|16}}. This is a massive boost, and often sufficient for her to tank through whole combats with almost no support.

'''Immortalstone''' ensures that, even if '''Nine-Lived Nightmare''' is killed, she can be brought back. If you have not yet been offered '''Dualstone''', this should be a priority upgrade. It should also be prioritized when using Reanimation Lab, or when using Brain Transfer to move her {{IconLink|Reanimate}} repeatedly to another unit.

'''Frenzystone''' is a niche upgrade, but can sometimes be useful, particularly if you have the Reanimation Lab to boost her {{Attack}} whenever she dies, or Advanced Growth to permanently and quickly scale the damage of her equipment. [[Resin Block]] makes this option much stronger, if you happen to be partnered with the [[Melting Remnant]]; combined with Reanimation Lab, she gains {{Attack|+18}} for every {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stack burned.

'''Worthy Sacrifice''' lets you use one of '''Nine-Lived Nightmare''''s {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stacks in exchange for {{Ember|3}} every other turn, letting you play expensive cards like Tome of Horrors, [[Minds Of Their Own]], and [[Replicator Ray]]. It can also be used to get rid of [[Calcified Ember]]s.
summary: The Nine-Lived Nightmare is a rare [[Lazarus League]] [[banner unit]]. She enters combat with a huge amount of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}.

title: Reforming Ooze

flavor.value:
"I found it cowering amongst some broken beakers. I think I'll keep it and one day give it to my darling as a pet. If she ever awakens, that is."
—Baron Grael

tables: '''Frenzystone''' doubles its potentially enormous damage, letting it take down multiple heavy enemies, and can provide additional {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers if using [[Organ Harvester]].
'''Dualstone''' grants {{IconLink|Dualism}}, giving it {{IconLink|Reanimate|2}} by default, but more importantly doubling the stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} granted by an equipped Organ Harvester.

'''Immortalstone''' lets you repeatedly play the unit if it dies. Since taking advantage of its powerful permanent scaling requires it to be left vulnerable and repeatedly die, this can prevent it from being killed if you can't stack up enough {{IconLink|Reanimate}} quickly. If allied with [[Melting Remnant]], this is generally not worth taking, as you can simply '''[[Reform]]''' it instead.
'''Frankenstone''' is a cheap upgrade that provides an extra stack of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}.
summary: Reforming Ooze is a rare [[Lazarus League]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever it is {{IconLink|Reanimated}}, it permanently gains {{Attack|+6}}.

title: Goliath Infusion
summary: #REDIRECT [[Infusion]]

title: Blast Infusion
summary: #REDIRECT [[Infusion]]

title: Madman Infusion
summary: #REDIRECT [[Infusion]]

title: Enfeebling Infusion
summary: #REDIRECT [[Infusion]]

title: Explosive Reaction

flavor.value:
"My contraption taps into the celestial core of angels and makes them... well, let's just say they put on a good light show."
—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

tables: '''Stackstone''' is the strongest upgrade for '''Explosive Reaction''' doubling the {{IconLink|Unstable}} application which both doubles its explosion damage, and increases its effective damage to 55 letting it kill many more backlines such as [[Chosen Assassin]] or [[Cael, Lord of the Cherubs#Holy Cherub|Holy Cherub]] (after being {{IconLink|Eaten}} once), doubling its ability to charge your explosive reanimator.
'''Smolderstone''' reduces the {{Ember}} cost to 0, making the card easier to play as an early combat solution for backliners or as a way to get your explosive reanimator's damage up faster.

'''Powerstone''' can be considered to allow '''Explosive Reaction''' to set off its explosion more reliably in the lategame, such as against [[Harpist Protector]] in [[Heaven's Maw#Champion of Savagery|Champion of Savagery]] or [[Deafening Herald]] in [[Heaven's Maw#Harbinger of Entropy|Harbinger of Entropy]], and to be able to kill [[Chosen Supplicant]] by itself.
summary: Explosive Reaction is a common [[Lazarus League]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Unstable|25}} to its target, then deals 5 damage to it.

title: Forevermore Serum

flavor.value:
"The serum was meant to get rid of my wrinkles but ended up doing so much more."
—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

tables: '''Stackstone''' doubles this card's output. While not the highest-value upgrade on its face, this can make the card a better duplication target if you need more up-front {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. '''Twinstone''' can do this as well, but ideally with an {{Ember}} discount.

'''Seekstone''' can help set up a unit that intends to defend with {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, such as [[Reforming Ooze]]. They can be susceptible to dying early, but having this card on turn 1 helps fix that in addition to making the card not cost {{Ember}}.

'''Eternalstone''' lets you recast this spell multiple times. This is normally strongest when you receive this card without the Lazarus League via Gremlin Looter, as it will almost certainly be your only source of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} unless you get lucky and see [[Spike of the League]] through another event, and most clans can benefit from the safety net it provides.
summary: Forevermore Serum is a [[Lazarus League]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Reanimate|1}} to the target.

title: It's Alive!

flavor.value:
"When I awoke, I did not remember anything of my previous life. It was as if I had been born anew! And this time, I had a few extra special 'upgrades,' if you will."
—Hugo, assistant to Dr. Orechi

tables: '''Twinstone''' lets you play this card multiple times per turn, either to scale the same unit twice and give them reserve {{IconLink|Lifesteal}}, or to play it on one unit who needs healing, then move a different unit in front of it so that it can heal before it gets attacked.
'''Emberstone''' is a practical way to save {{Ember}}, especially with '''Twinstone'''.
summary: It's Alive! is a common [[Lazarus League]] spell. It [[Advance]]s its target to the front of its floor, and applies {{IconLink|Lifesteal|1}} and {{Attack|+7}} to it.

title: Pseudoscience

flavor.value: "I'm not sure how it works but I do know that, for some reason, shaking a bottle and making baby noises at my specimens makes them heal faster."

tables: '''Twinstone''' lets you play this card twice, potentially getting two different modes and making the card just a bit less random while also doubling its effect.
'''Emberstone''' is a practical way to save {{Ember}}, especially with '''Twinstone'''.
'''Stackstone''' can also be a way to double this card's effect without needing an {{Ember}}-saving upgrade or more {{Ember}} though it increases its variability.
summary: Pseudoscience is a common [[Lazarus League]] spell. It applies either {{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}}, {{IconLink|Reanimate|1}} or {{IconLink|Spikes|6}}.

title: Acid Shower

effect.value: Apply {{IconLink|Unstable|10}} and deal '''1''' damage to enemy units.

flavor.value:
"If water gets in your eyes, rinse them out immediately with acid."
—OHELL Safety Regulations and Guidelines

tables: '''Powerstone''' is usually important if you don't have another way of increasing this spell's damage, as it needs it to trigger explosions immediately against waves of backline enemies.
'''Keepstone''' is a solid upgrade to make this card your answer to backline enemies. It's quite effective against [[Heaven's Maw#Chosen of Dominion|Chosen of Dominion]].

In a pinch, '''Stackstone''' and '''Powerstone''' can allow this spell to kill [[Chosen Assassin]] in the waves in which it appears. It still won't kill the one that appears in the first wave of [[Heaven's Maw#Champion of Savagery|Champion of Savagery]] until the end of the turn on its own, however, often requiring you to set up higher. This upgrade also improves the incidental damage that tanks take from their backliners exploding.
summary: Acid Shower is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Unstable|10}} to all enemies, then deals 1 damage to them.

title: Faulty Body

flavor.value:
"Poor Baron, he found a way to strengthen his love's frail body but, just as beryllium is strong yet fragile, so too became Inga."
—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

tables: '''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Spikes}} gained, as does '''Twinstone'''. They can be used together for a total of {{IconLink|Spikes|160}}.

'''Emberstone''' and '''Seekstone''' reduce its {{Ember}} cost. '''Seekstone''' also ensures you have your {{IconLink|Spikes}} from the start of battle, provided you also have your way of keeping the unit alive online then. Both upgrades pair very well with '''Twinstone''' in particular.

'''Eternalstone''' can allow you to keep accumulating {{IconLink|Spikes}} throughout a battle, which can be especially strong in small decks. This also allows you to apply '''Smolderstone''' as an alternative to '''Emberstone''' if you need that elsewhere.

'''Entropic Stone''' makes '''Faulty Body''' grant {{IconLink|Spikes|120}}, or a total of {{IconLink|Spikes|240}} with '''Twinstone'''. Two copies of this card with '''Seekstone''', '''Twinstone''', and '''Entropic Stone''' can kill every non-boss enemy in the game with at least {{Attack|1}} except [[Avowed Gladiator]]s, which survive at a measly {{Health|20}}.
summary: Faulty Body is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Spikes|40}} to a friendly unit, but also adds {{IconLink|Fragile}}, meaning that the unit will die instantly if it takes unblocked damage.

title: Horrify

flavor.value: "Stay back! Stay back, you monster!" cried the assistant. "I'm not a monster. I'm Grael!" he cried. "Don't you recognize me?!"

tables: '''Twinstone''' and '''Stackstone''' both essentially doubles the amount of {{IconLink|Dazed}} on this card. One could even apply both upgrades to inflict up to {{IconLink|Dazed|4}} on one singular enemy.
'''Entropic Stone''' is just a better '''Stackstone''', so if you find this event and do not have a better target for the '''Triplestack''' then consider adding it to this card.
'''Keepstone''' allows you to play this card every turn in order to permanently inflict {{IconLink|Dazed}} on a dangerous enemy or to use it on different enemies each turn.

'''Freezestone''' is useful if you plan on using the effect of {{IconLink|Dazed}} to shut down a particular enemy or to buy more time during {{IconLink|Relentless}} and want to guarantee that you have this card in your hand when it is needed.
summary: Horrify is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Dazed|1}} to the target and moves them to the back of the floor.

title: Insatiable Hunger

flavor.value:
"Some return from the Reanimation Lab with a peculiar hunger that consumes their minds. My assistant Hugo implores that we stop and that our efforts are forbidden."
—from Dr. Orechi's notebooks

tables: '''Emberstone''' provides a no-frills way to improve your {{Ember}} economy, and this card's upgrade slots aren't contested. '''Freezestone''' adds the ability to wait to use it at the right moment, e.g. right before {{IconLink|Relentless}} combat.

'''Twinstone''' and '''Stackstone''' provide ways to stack more {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} if you're looking to make a {{IconLink|Lifesteal}}-based tank. The [[Lazarus League]] tends to prefer to use {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} to complement {{IconLink|Reanimate}}-based strategies than use {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} on its own, however.
summary: Insatiable Hunger is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It gives {{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}} to your units.

title: Mixology

flavor.value:
"I must admit, I do find myself sometimes getting a little whimsical with my concoctions. Just look at my Hair-Lifting Blueberry Fizzes!"
—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

tables: Putting '''Emberstone''' on '''Mixology''' helps you spam it more, and in many cases this is a straightforward way to get more value out of your turn.
'''Smolderstone''' lets you play it for {{Ember|0}} at the cost of [[Consume]], which is great for larger decks, or for ones where [[Infusion]]s are more necessary early than late.

'''Twinstone''' doubles the amount of mixing you can do, and '''Keepstone''' gives you consistent access to it. '''Keepstone''' is particularly good with [[Progress Pacemaker]], letting you consistently get your bonus [[Mix]]. While it's ambitious to add both, it's possible with [[Spell Sanctum]], [[Lightstone Casing]] and an {{Ember}} upgrade, or [[Boiler Room]].
summary: Mixology is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It [[Mix]]es twice, granting the player an [[Infusion]] or upgrading their existing one, and then upgrades the resulting infusion. See the [[Infusion]] page for more details.

title: Risky Operation

effect.value: Reduce friendly unit to '''1''' health. Apply {{Attack|+10}} and {{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}}.

flavor.value:
"Fascinating! The subject barely survived but look how strong they are!"
—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

tables: '''Twinstone''' lets you play this card multiple times per turn. '''Emberstone''' goes nicely with this, playing out both copies for {{Ember|0}} instead of {{Ember|2}}.
'''Keepstone''' can also be a way to consistently scale a unit throughout the battle.
summary: Risky Operation is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It reduces the target friendly unit to 1 health, but gives it {{Attack|+10}} and {{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}}.

title: Replicator Ray

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Remove equipment from a friendly unit. Copy the unit.

flavor.value:
"I found that I was burning, sometimes quite literally, through assistants faster than I liked. I made this little contraption to turn one assistant into two!"
—Dr. Orechi

tables: '''Freezestone''' gives an {{Ember}} discount while ensuring that you won't draw this card too early, e.g. before you can kill an [[Erratic Assistant]] to equip [[Scissor Hands]], or if you need to scale up the original a bit before duplicating them.

On the other hand, if you have a good target at the start of battle, such as a well-scaled [[Pincushion]], and a plan to have them equipped by then, '''Seekstone''' also gives an {{Ember}} discount and lets you duplicate on turn 1 to avoid leaking early waves.

In a deck with a lot of spare [[Equipment]] flying around that's also small enough to reasonably draw this multiple times, removing '''Consume''' to play this multiple times can be a spectacular way to scale. It also allows adding '''Smolderstone''' to defray the cost.
summary: Replicator Ray is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It creates a {{IconLink|Cardless}} copy of a targeted friendly unit with an [[Equipment]] attached, and removes that equipment.

title: Surgical Strike

effect.value:
'''[[Piercing]]'''.
Deal '''4''' damage.
{{IconLink|Slay}}: Add a copy of this card with '''[[Ephemeral]]''' to your hand.

flavor.value:
"I've found that the scalpel is mightier than the sword. It can cut with more deadly precision."
—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

tables: '''Emberstone''' (or '''Seekstone''') is more or less mandatory on this spell, as it lets you play it and its copies for {{Ember|0}}, which is crucial, as you'll be playing it many times. When considering drafting this spell, you should consider when your next [[Merchant of Magic]] will be. Luckily, you'll be guaranteed to see '''Emberstone''' as long as you can reroll.
'''Powerstone''' widens the list of enemies (and friends, like [[Pufferflesh]]) you can kill considerably, putting most backline enemies in your reach.

One subtle downfall of this card is that given how important the previous two upgrades are, it's hard to fit a '''Keepstone''' on it, which you might want considering how useful it is. But there are ways to fit it in. {{IconLink|Conduit}} and [[Enchanted Chamber]] can solve your damage issues instead of a '''Powerstone''', while [[Spell Sanctum]] or [[Boiler Room]] can replace '''Emberstone''', though both of these limit where you can play it somewhat. [[Lightstone Casing]] is also an obvious answer. Alternatively, you can simply thin your deck enough not to need it.

If you can line this up, the sky can be the limit with '''Entropic Growth''', as you'll soon become able to hit Chosen enemies too. Add [[Silver Ink]] and suddenly this spell might be killing every single enemy that dares set foot on your train!
summary: Surgical Strike is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It deals 4 damage, and creates an [[Ephemeral]] copy of itself if it kills any unit. The copy can in turn make another copy if it kills a unit, and this can continue indefinitely.

title: Weaponized Prosthetic

effect.value: Remove equipment from a unit. Apply {{Attack|+30}}.

flavor.value: "Look, Mom! Isn't my new arm cool?"

tables: It is normally quite difficult to play this spell more than once due to its reliance on equipment. '''Smolderstone''' therefore pulls double duty, making it free to play and giving it [[Consume]], so it is removed from your deck once used and you will not keep drawing it. If you have enough equipment in your deck that you will be able to benefit from repeated plays of this spell, '''Emberstone''' still improves your {{Ember}} economy.

'''Seekstone''' can be used if you have a weak piece of [[Deployable]] equipment that you don't mind removing for {{Attack|+30}}. It can also be used with {{IconLink|Red Crown}} units to ensure you can get rid of harmful equipment immediately.
summary: Weaponized Prosthetic is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It removes a unit's equipment but applies {{Attack|+30}}. The removed equipment does not return to the player hand nor to the discard pile.

title: Brain Transfer

effect.value:
'''[[Sacrifice]]'''.
Transfer {{Attack}} and all '''[[Buff]]''' and '''[[Debuff]]''' effects to front friendly unit.

flavor.value:
"While a body can still be usable if preserved correctly, brain matter must be transferred to a host within hours."
—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

tables: '''Seekstone''' guarantees that you will see this spell immediately, which is particularly important if you want to use it to instantly shift buffs from one unit to another. This makes it especially good with Nine-Lived Nightmare.
'''Keepstone''' allows you to play this spell every turn, making it particularly good if you plan to pass stats back and forth or use it repeatedly on an endless unit.
summary: Brain Transfer is a rare [[Lazarus League]] spell. It [[Sacrifice]]s its target, grants the front friendly unit the target's {{Attack}}, and moves all [[Buff]] and [[Debuff]] effects to the front friendly unit.

title: Minds Of Their Own

flavor.value: A scraping sound, like a dead fish being dragged across a plank, caused Hugo to turn. He froze. The hand he had just collected was gone!

tables: '''Emberstone''', or any other cost reduction upgrade, can make this spell much easier to play.
'''Keepstone''' is a strong option, allowing all of your units to attack early every turn. However, this requires you to pay the spell's significant cost consistently.
summary: Minds Of Their Own is a rare [[Lazarus League]] spell. It causes all friendly units on the floor to attack immediately, as long as they have equipment.

title: Mix-a-Lot

flavor.value:
"By the time I realized what her experiments were doing to her, it was too late. Inga's sanity was as small and weak as a flicker of light in an endless night."
—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

tables: '''Smolderstone''' drastically reduces this card's cost, making it only cost {{Ember|1}}, at the cost of giving it '''[[Consume]]'''. This is usually worth it, since this isn't a bad card to just play once at a low cost, but '''Eternalstone''' makes it much stronger, letting you replay it over and over.
Upgrades that reduce this card's {{Ember}} cost should be prioritized. This includes '''Emberstone''', '''Seekstone''', and '''Freezestone'''.
summary: Mix-a-Lot is a rare [[Lazarus League]] spell added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. When played, you [[Mix]] 5 times, with each infusion selected randomly.

title: Scrap for Parts

flavor.value:
"All these under-performing technicians are still good for something."
—Dr. Orechi

tables: '''Seekstone''', in addition to discounting this card to {{Ember|0}}, also gives it to you on turn 1 reliably. The ability to consistently get units you couldn't play during the [[Deployment Phase]] onto the field is a key selling point of "draw a unit" cards, making this upgrade highly desirable.

'''Twinstone''' gives you two of these for the price of one - especially nice if e.g. you duplicated a unit with the [[Mysterious Mirror]] event. If it's being used to gather [[:Category:Assistant units|Assistants]] or other units that want to die, the unit gathered on the first play can be [[Sacrifice]]d for the second play.

'''Eternalstone''' can be powerful if you're using this to scale an {{IconLink|Endless}} unit and have a small deck, or have the privilege of applying a {{IconLink|Keepstone}} with it, as its scaling on such units is impressive.
summary: Scrap for Parts is a rare [[Lazarus League]] spell. It requires the [[Sacrifice]] of a friendly unit but draws a friendly unit and applies {{Attack|+40}}.

title: Spike of the League

flavor.value: Once, Dr. Orechi was someone who would bristle at the thought of his creations being used for war. He sighed and drove his spike into the Rail. Times had changed.

tables: '''Seekstone''' on this card can be a crucial part of setting up a unit that intends to defend with {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, such as [[Reforming Ooze]]. They can be susceptible to dying early, but having this card on turn 1 helps fix that.
'''Stackstone''' doubles this card's output and is a valuable upgrade.

'''Eternalstone''' allows you to play this card more than once per combat, which is excellent if you need to keep a unit's {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stacks topped off. It also allows you to apply '''Smolderstone''', granting {{IconLink|Reanimate|2}} even when played at {{Ember|0}}.
summary: Spike of the League is a rare [[Lazarus League]] spell. It applies X {{IconLink|Reanimate}}.

title: Tome of Horrors

flavor.value:
"My assistant gifted me this journal so I could take meticulous notes of my experiments. He might have also said 'writing would help process my feelings.' I didn't pay much attention."
—Dr. Orechi

tables: To take maximum advantage of '''Tome of Horrors''', '''Eternalstone''' is highly desirable in small decks, as it has a lot of self-synergy. It also allows '''Smolderstone''' to reduce its cost significantly once '''Eternalstone''' has been applied. '''Tome of Horrors''' with these upgrades applied is one of the best possible choices for duplication at [[Empyrean Well]]s.
'''Stackstone''' doubles the impact of the spell both with respect to the size of the explosions and the {{IconLink|Reanimate}} that keeps them going.
In larger decks, '''Seekstone''' is valuable for reducing the card's cost and ensuring you will see it immediately, if this is your solution to backline units.
summary: Tome of Horrors is a rare [[Lazarus League]] spell. It applies both {{IconLink|Reanimate}} and a huge amount of {{IconLink|Unstable}} to a unit.

title: Combustion Suit

flavor.value:
"Per code LLH 2019.11, assistants must wear this suit at all times when applying the Destabilization Spray. The mixture tends to unbalance their minds."
—OHELL Safety Regulations and Guidelines

summary: Combustion Suit is an equipment from the [[Lazarus League]] clan. Whenever a unit wearing a Combustion Suit strikes an enemy, all enemies on the floor gain {{IconLink|Unstable|5}}.

title: Double-Edged Arms

flavor.value: Inspired by the Hell Lobster's own appendages, these pincers can grip, cut, and twist the most stubborn of materials.

summary: Double-Edged Arms is an equipment from the [[Lazarus League]] clan. It can only be obtained from the {{IconLink|Graft}} ability of [[Double-Edged Bearer]].

title: Organ Harvester

flavor.value:
"My experiments tend to take a toll on the bodies of my assistants. I made this contraption so I could collect new parts with more efficiency."
—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

tables: '''Bloodthirsty Blade''' allows you to better capitalize on the {{IconLink|Slay}}s you're already incentivized to get, and gives you a built-in way to scale {{Attack}}.
'''Glass Cannon''' gives you a surge of initial {{Attack}}, while its {{IconLink|Fragile}} is likely irrelevant as you aren't defending with {{Health}} anyway.
Bug Fix: [[Organ Harvester]] cannot be attached to enemies anymore.
summary: Organ Harvester is an equipment from the [[Lazarus League]]. It grants the equipped unit {{Attack|+10}} and gives it a {{IconLink|Slay}} ability that gives it {{IconLink|Reanimate|1}}.

title: Potion Kit

flavor.value:
"An essential collection of tools that every lab technician needs: powdered Titan bone, a beaker, a faulty burner, and chili, of course."
—OHELL Safety Regulations and Guidelines

summary: Potion Kit is an equipment from the [[Lazarus League]]. Its Ability lets the unit it's equipped on to [[Mix]] once every 3 turns.

title: Scissor Hands

flavor.value: "Well, at least making confetti will be easy."

summary: Scissor Hands is an [[equipment]] from the [[Lazarus League]] clan. Differently from normal equipment, this one can only be obtained by the Graft ability of [[Erratic Assistant]].

title: Spiky Skin

flavor.value:
"I took a sample from a demon's flesh whose skin was as strong as steel and combined it with a bristle brush. Voila! My sharpest creation!"
—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

summary: Spiky Skin is an equipment from the [[Lazarus League]] clan. It is only obtainable through the {{IconLink|Graft}} ability of [[Pufferflesh]].

title: Twisted Back

flavor.value: "I've been Dr. Orechi's intern for years now. When will i get an actual job offer?!"

summary: Twisted Back is an equipment from the [[Lazarus League]] clan. It can only be obtained from [[Twisted Assistant]]'s {{IconLink|Graft}} ability.

title: Vampire's Tooth

flavor.value:
"The name is a little tongue-in-cheek, my Assistant wanted eternal life so I made her an implant that would let her, let's say, 'drink the life force' of others"
—from Dr. Orechi's notebook

summary: Vampire's Tooth is an equipment from the [[Lazarus League]] clan. It can only be obtained through [[Sanguine Assistant]]'s {{IconLink|Graft}} ability.

title: Electricity Chamber

flavor.value:
"When an assistant has fallen, take them to the chamber so that their bodies can be reawakened with a little zap."
—OHELL Safety Regulations and Guidelines

summary: Electricity Chamber is a room from the [[Lazarus League]] clan. It gives friendly units {{IconLink|Spikes|8}} when {{IconLink|Summon}}ed or {{IconLink|Reanimated}}.

title: Reanimation Lab

effect.value: Friendly units gain {{Attack|+7}} and {{Health|+7}} on {{IconLink|Summon}} and {{IconLink|Reanimate}}.

flavor.value: The deeper and most secretive part os Orechi's lab. Only a few of his most trusted assistants are allowed inside and seem happy for the privilege. His other employees pray they never go there.

summary: Reanimation Lab is a room from the [[Lazarus League]] clan. It gives units {{AttackHealth|+7|+7}} on {{IconLink|Summon}} and {{IconLink|Reanimate}}.

title: Hellhorned

flavor.value: ''The aggressive demons of the Scorched plains have returned! Rally their imps and warriors to overwhelm Heaven.''

summary: Hellhorned [[file:ClanHellhorned.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]], returning from [[Monster Train 1]]. It is unlocked after unlocking 6 different [[Pyre Hearts]] and watching the [[Main_story_cutscenes#CoreDialogue_070_ClanReturnC|main story cutscene]].

title: Hornbreaker Prince

flavor.value: Cursed with no horns, the only son of Grrrg has taken to collecting the horns of his opponents, dispelling any doubt of his fighting prowess and convincing me of his rightful place as champion of the Hellhorned.

tables: Added {{PAGENAME}} without changes from the previous game.

Wrathful [[Hornbreaker Prince|Prince]]. Stats updated from {{AttackHealth|15/15}}, {{AttackHealth|25/25}}, {{AttackHealth|40/40}} >>> {{AttackHealth|25/25}},{{AttackHealth|35/50}}, {{AttackHealth|45/75}}. "{{IconLink|Revenge}}: Gain {{IconLink|Rage|3/4/6}} >>> '''4/5/6'''." Reaper [[Hornbreaker Prince|Prince]]. Added {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}: Culling. CD 6/3/1. "Attack immediately."
summary: Hornbreaker Prince is the default [[Champion]] of the [[Hellhorned]]. He is a basic but effective damage dealer, reliant on getting {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers, or potentially gaining a huge amount of {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. His starter card is [[Torch]].

title: Shardtail Queen

flavor.value: In my dreams, I see a demon more powerful than any of the Hellhorned. One with sharded tail and control over all imps. Did she save the Hellhorned from total destruction, this forgotten Queen?

tables: Added {{PAGENAME}} with with buffs. Imperialist does increased damage, 20/30/40 >>> 20/40/60

Imperialist [[Shardtail Queen]] effect updated to be an ability: "{{IconLink|Action}}: Kill all Imp units. Deal 20 damage per Imp to enemy units." >>> {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}: Imp Toss. CD 1. "Kill all Imp units. Deal 20/40/60 damage per Imp to enemy units". [[Shardtail Queen|Shardtail]] Royalty stats updated from {{AttackHealth|10/10}}, {{AttackHealth|10/20}}, {{AttackHealth|10/40}} >>> {{AttackHealth|10/15}}, {{AttackHealth|15/30}}, {{AttackHealth|25/60}}.
summary: Shardtail Queen is the alternate [[Champion]] of the [[Hellhorned]]. All of her paths revolve around [[Imps]], either producing them, killing them, or becoming stronger when they're played. Her starter card is [[Queen's Impling]].

title: Torch

flavor.value: The Hellhorned have learned to live with the unpredictability of the Scorched Plains, even going so far as to retain some of the flaming boulders for themselves, despite my attempts to dissuade them.

tables: '''Surgestone''' has a dual purpose on '''Torch''', making it able to snipe most important backline targets, and as a soft Purge.
'''Powerstone''' can be considered instead if you really need consistent backline removal and can't afford to replace it with a different card, as it will still hit most relevant threats at 13 power.

'''Emberstone''' pairs nicely with [[Powerstone]], and as '''Torch''' is fairly easy to play and its upgrade slots aren't in demand, this upgrade can be a no-frills way to improve your {{Ember}} economy.
summary: Torch is [[Hornbreaker Prince]]'s starter card. It hits any unit for 3 damage.

title: Queen's Impling

ability.value: {{IconLink|Summon}}: Deal '''16''' damage to the front enemy unit.

flavor.value: In these dreams, the Shardtail has shown me the result of her Exodus: the first cycling imps in the Scorched Plains. I've never encountered these sharded imps in Hell, but their resemblance to those I have met is uncanny. Perhaps these dreams are something more...

tables: '''Summon''': Deal '''10''' damage to the front enemy unit. -> '''Summon''': Deal '''16''' damage to the front enemy unit.
summary: Queen's Impling is [[Shardtail Queen]]'s starter card. When played, it deals 16 damage to the front enemy.

title: Fledgling Imp

flavor.value: These impish Hellhorned have just molted into their new forms, as evidenced by their tiny wings and heavy tail. Their horns will continue to grow each molting cycle, as will their love of their volcanic homelands.

tables: '''Immortalstone''' allows '''Fledgling Imp''' to be played multiple times per combat, repeatedly triggering its {{IconLink|Summon}} effect. It dies easily with its low base {{Health}} and can block one instance of damage if played in the frontline. It can also be manually killed using '''[[Sacrifice]]''' cards like [[Imp-portant Work]].
'''Dualstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Rage}} granted on {{IconLink|Summon}} from 5 to 10. This is especially impactful as [[Fledgling Imp]]'s ability has a floor-wide effect.
Added {{PAGENAME}} without changes from the previous game.
summary: Fledgling Imp is a common [[Hellhorned]] unit. It applies {{IconLink|Rage|5}} to all friendly units on the floor, including itself, when summoned.

title: Molting Imp

flavor.value: ''With each molting cycle comes a new body, one that inches the Imp closer to fully mutating into the more mature Horned Demons. After witnessing the process, it is not something for the faint of heart.''

tables: '''Immortalstone''' allows '''Molting Imp''' to be played multiple times per combat, repeatedly triggering its {{IconLink|Summon}} effect. It dies easily with its low base {{Health}} and can block one instance of damage if played in the frontline. It can also be manually killed using '''[[Sacrifice]]''' cards.
Added {{PAGENAME}} without changes from the previous game.
summary: Molting Imp is a common [[Hellhorned]] unit. When played, it deals 10 damage to all enemies on the floor.

title: Welder Helper

ability.value: {{IconLink|Summon}}: Apply '''[[Armor]] 20''' to the front friendly unit.

flavor.value: ''It was a surprise to learn that even the imps craft weapons and armor for the Hellhorned. Instead of hammers, they use their innate control of fire.''

tables: '''Immortalstone''' allows '''Welder Helper''' to be played multiple times per combat, repeatedly triggering its {{IconLink|Summon}} effect. Although '''Welder Helper''' is likely to be played in the backline to buff the front unit, '''[[Sacrifice]]''' effects and damaging spells can be used to kill it.
'''Dualstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Armor}} granted on {{IconLink|Summon}} from 20 to 40.

Though only available when partnered with the [[Melting Remnant]], '''Wickstone''' is an excellent option for '''Welder Helper''' when paired with '''Immortalstone''', as {{IconLink|Burnout|1}} means it is guaranteed to die at the end of the turn. While this is useful for all imps, it is especially good for '''Welder Helper''' due to the awkwardness of killing it off. However, this upgrade should not be taken alongside '''Dualstone''', as it will instead grant {{IconLink|Burnout|2}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Welder Helper is a common [[Hellhorned]] unit. When played, it provides {{IconLink|Armor}} to the front friendly unit. If the Welder Helper is played in front, it gets the {{IconLink|Armor}}.

title: Impish Scholar

ability.value: {{IconLink|Summon}}: Return a random consumed spell to your hand.

flavor.value: Having chosen to mature in knowledge rather than strength, these imps decided not to molt and instead to travel between the Rings as ambassadors of the Scorched Plains and advocates of our Covenant with Heaven. Now with no home to return to, they've helped to advance our research of more efficient defensive techniques.

tables: '''Immortalstone''' allows '''Impish Scholar''' to be replayed, which is crucial to unlocking its full potential, as described in '''Strategy'''.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Impish Scholar is an uncommon [[Hellhorned]] unit. When played, it returns a random card from the [[Consume]] pile to your hand.

title: Pyre Chomper

flavor.value: These imps have taken a rather strong liking to the Pyre as a snack food, making them horrible pests aboard my train. Though the sharp crystals don't digest well...

tables: Applying '''Immortalstone''' is an option on '''Pyre Chomper''', as it is with most [[:Category:Imp units|Imps]], but your deck would have to have a lot of expensive spells to justify this, especially given that constantly replaying this unit costs you a draw each turn.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Pyre Chomper is an uncommon [[Hellhorned]] unit. It grans {{Ember|4}} on {{IconLink|Summon}}.

title: Alpha Fiend

flavor.value: These ancient demons of the Hellhorned live a reclusive life on the edge of the Scorched Plains. Their isolated existence has made them even more difficult to communicate with, but they seem to understand the peril their clan is in since they've joined me on this perilous journey.

tables: The {{IconLink|Multistrike}} granted by '''Frenzystone''' generates more {{IconLink|Strike}} triggers and thus allows '''Alpha Fiend''' to gain more {{Attack}} per turn - while also letting it take advantage of its greater damage output twice. It may even be worth looking for two copies of this upgrade if that's possible, given how important it is!

'''Smidgestone''' can also be considered to handle '''Alpha Fiend's''' {{Capacity}} issue. Even if you're using floor overstacking to mitigate its {{Capacity}}, making it {{Capacity|1}} can still give you more options and make '''Alpha Fiend''' easier to duplicate.

'''Speedstone''' is a pseudo-defensive upgrade, letting '''Alpha Fiend''' attack before enemies, but it has a secondary use as well - if you have other powerful attackers on your floor, such as a [[Demon Fiend]] bolstered with plenty of {{IconLink|Rage}}, then {{IconLink|Quick}} guarantees that '''Alpha Fiend''' will hit first and therefore get as many {{IconLink|Strike}} triggers as possible every turn (instead of potentially losing some because other units were able to kill all available enemies first).

'''Burststone''' is only available with the [[Railforged]], but it can be a solid way to get a head start on [[Alpha Fiend]]'s scaling, letting him get in two extra {{IconLink|Strike}} triggers when first played. It is not a substitute for a proper {{IconLink|Multistrike}} source (unless you can replay him every turn, like with [[Magnetic Relay]]), but it can help get around how slowly he scales.

'''Wrath''', from the [[Path of the Angel]] event, is an extremely powerful upgrade on '''Alpha Fiend''' as long as you already have at least one source of {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. This helps mitigate its vulnerability to early waves and the slowness of its scaling, allowing it to get additional immediate attacks on the first turn of battle to jumpstart its scaling engine and potentially prevent leaks.
summary: Alpha Fiend is an uncommon [[Hellhorned]] [[banner unit]]. It gains {{Attack|+15}} on {{IconLink|Strike}}.

title: Branded Warrior

flavor.value: It is said that no one can match a fully matured Hellhorned Demon in combat. I have yet to see this proven false. Though I can't say I'm seeking out that opportunity...

tables: '''Dualstone''' doubles both the initial {{IconLink|Rage}} of '''Branded Warrior''', and the floor-wide {{IconLink|Rage}} gained upon {{IconLink|Slay}}, boosting both its initial offense and supportive capabilities.
'''Frenzystone''' makes it easier for '''Branded Warrior''' to trigger {{IconLink|Slay}} once per turn, and even makes it possible to trigger it twice in a turn.

As '''Branded Warrior''' will often be played in the backline, other units will normally attack before it. This may prevent {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers (e.g. on low {{Health}} units such as [[Misshapen Fiend]]s), especially if its allies have already gained {{IconLink|Rage}} from an early trigger. '''Speedstone''' inverts this order and allows it to attack before anything else on the floor. This is beneficial against weak frontline enemies, but renders '''Branded Warrior''' less helpful in any combat where the frontline unit is tanky. When fighting [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], every wave except the 7th has at least one Misshapen Fiend at the front of the floor, so this upgrade should be more strongly considered, and it should also be prioritized if you see [[Iron-tongue]]. The [[Breath of Heaven]] artifact is generally very weak, but it can pull a vulnerable backliner to the front and score a {{IconLink|Quick}} '''Branded Warrior''' another kill.

'''Largestone''' makes '''Branded Warrior''' much tankier, and the increased {{Capacity}} is easier to work around with '''[[Ascend]]''' effects. This upgrade is best considered when using '''Branded Warrior''' as a frontline unit and giving it {{IconLink|Spikes}}; otherwise it is usually a consolation prize when better upgrades cannot be found.

{{AttackHealth|10|5}} → {{AttackHealth|20|5}}, {{IconLink|Rage|4}} → {{IconLink|Rage|5}}, {{IconLink|Slay}}: Apply {{IconLink|Rage|3}} to friendly units. → {{IconLink|Slay}}: Apply {{IconLink|Rage|5}} to friendly units.
summary: Branded Warrior is an uncommon [[Hellhorned]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever it kills an enemy, it grants {{IconLink|Rage|5}} to all friendly units on the floor, including itself.

title: Demon Fiend

flavor.value: These demons, rumored to be the most ancient among the Hellhorned, do not speak in any known tongue. They don't appear to understand much, either, making any sort of relationship with them tricky to establish. Thankfully, they have a natural proclivity for fighting making communication unnecessary.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' grants {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, making efficient use of [[Demon Fiend]]'s naturally very high {{Attack}}, and {{IconLink|Trample}} ensures that no damage on the floor is wasted on low {{Health}} units. This is by far the most important upgrade for '''Demon Fiend''', and if possible, filling out both upgrade slots with '''Frenzystone''' is ideal.
'''Speedstone''' is a pseudo-defensive upgrade that allows '''Demon Fiend''' to get the jump on enemy waves, potentially wiping them out before they can move.

'''Smidgestone''' reduces '''Demon Fiend''' from {{Capacity|3}} to {{Capacity|1}}. This upgrade is not very useful if overstacking the floor with '''[[Ascend]]''' cards, but is much better if you are using [[Imp]] strategies, where {{Capacity}} is key.

'''Furystone''' grants a decent amount of {{IconLink|Rage}}, giving you a head start on scaling up '''Demon Fiend'''. This upgrade is best taken alongside synergies like Deranged Brute, Last Stand with {{IconLink|Seekstone}}, or [[Collection of Tails]], but it can also be worthwhile if you simply want to fill out its upgrade slots in case you are offered [[Celestial Alcove]] events that grant unit upgrades.

'''Ascetic Penance''' and '''Ascetic Absolution''' make it significantly easier to play '''Demon Fiend''', effectively making it a {{Ember|1}} unit. Additionally, the gained {{Ember}} will be boosted by [[Ashes of the Fallen]] and repeated by [[Transcendimp]].
summary: The Demon Fiend is an uncommon [[Hellhorned]] [[banner unit]]. Though highly expensive, it has excellent stats and the coveted {{IconLink|Trample}}.

title: Horned Warrior

flavor.value: Though slightly unwieldy with the recent loss of their tails, these maturing demons have grown into their horns, making them valuable soldiers of the Hellhorned and of our Rail.

tables: With an innate {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, '''Horned Warrior''' is already a good target for offensive buffs such as {{IconLink|Rage}}. Adding more {{IconLink|Multistrike}} via '''Frenzystone''' only makes these buffs an even better investment, as each bonus attack will benefit equally. However, it may be worth thinking about if another unit could use this upgrade better.
'''Speedstone''' gives '''Horned Warrior''' a small {{Attack}} boost while also letting it take down enemies before they can attack.

'''Largestone''' is a great upgrade if you need to survive the early rings, and it can even hold up later if you have movement options like [[Hidden Passage]] to get around the increased {{Capacity}}. The massive stat boost it provides makes '''Horned Warrior''' a formidable unit in the early game and nearly secures victory against the Ring 2 boss on its own.

Given its low health pool, '''Horned Warrior''' is susceptible to {{IconLink|Spikes}} and {{IconLink|Sweep}}. '''Heartstone''' helps its initial survivability and buys time to draw and play other defensive solutions (e.g. {{IconLink|Armor}}). '''Strengthstone''' and '''Furystone''', meanwhile, buff the unit's relatively low {{Attack}}. All of these upgrades are also available cheaply in the shop, so if you do not intend for '''Horned Warrior''' to be part of your long-term strategy, these upgrades are good to fill out its slots and make it more usable without breaking the bank.
Added {{PAGENAME}} without changes from the previous game.
summary: Horned Warrior is an uncommon [[Hellhorned]] [[banner unit]]. Its main draw is its natural {{IconLink|Multistrike}}.

title: Railbeater

flavor.value: These Hellhorned are some of the most respected blacksmiths in Hell from spending several cycles on steelwork. Not to mention, they're a fantastic help in the construction of our Rail.

tables: '''Dualstone''' increases both the initial {{IconLink|Armor}} gained by '''Railbeater''' (from 30 to 60) and the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} it applies (from 1 to 2).
'''Frenzystone''' is effective on '''Railbeater''' due to the greater impact of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} thanks to the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} it applies with each hit.
'''Largestone''' greatly improves [[Railbeater]]'s base stats, making it a more effective tank.

'''Titanstone''' grants {{IconLink|Titanite}}, making '''Railbeater''' take half damage from all sources. Combined with its high {{IconLink|Armor}}, this can give it the durability necessary for surviving later waves.

'''Immortalstone''' can be useful if you are not overstacking floors, as it is usually quite important for '''Railbeater''' to stay alive, both for tanking purposes and for applying {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}}. It should be considered especially strongly if you lack {{IconLink|Armor}} sources like [[Fortified Pauldrons]], or if you know '''Railbeater''' will eventually be overwhelmed, such as against [[Stryx]] & [[Hallow]] or [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]].

While somewhat niche, '''Speedstone''' makes '''Railbeater''' {{IconLink|Quick}}, ensuring that it strikes enemies first. Mainly, this is useful if you intend to '''[[Ascend]]''' '''Railbeater''' onto an overstacked floor, as it will end up at the back of that floor and therefore may not get the chance to apply {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} before its allies attack. It is also useful if you can apply {{IconLink|Quick}} both to '''Railbeater''' and whatever unit is going to benefit from the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}}; with Demon Fiend, for example, this combination can wipe out waves before they have a chance to move and therefore preserve [[Railbeater]]'s {{IconLink|Armor}} for the boss.

As a frontline attacker in the clan with many {{IconLink|Rage}} synergies, '''Savage Heart''' is an excellent pick for a '''Railbeater''' that has been upgraded with '''Dualstone''' and '''Frenzystone''', letting it permanently scale its power.

'''Dominating Control''' applies {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} on {{IconLink|Strike}}, which stacks with [[Railbeater]]'s natural application. It applies {{IconLink|Melee Weakness|2}} instead, or {{IconLink|Melee Weakness|4}} with {{IconLink|Dualism}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: The Railbeater is an uncommon [[Hellhorned]] [[banner unit]]. It enters with {{IconLink|Armor|30}} and applies {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} on {{IconLink|Strike}}.

title: Steelworker

flavor.value: Along with a team of imps, these demons are responsible for the creation of all Hellhorned armor and weapons. While not usually on the front lines, their centuries of working metal gives them a comfortable tendency towards combat.

tables: '''Dualstone''' grants {{IconLink|Dualism}}, which doubles the effectiveness of '''Steelworker''''s {{IconLink|Resolve}} effect, increasing the {{IconLink|Armor}} gained on all units from 6 to 12.
'''Smidgestone''' reduces '''Steelworker''' to {{Capacity|1}}, making it easier to fit on a floor if you are not using overstacking effects.
'''Heartstone''' bolsters '''Steelworker''''s durability before it can build up {{IconLink|Armor}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
'''Resolve''': Apply '''Armor 5''' to friendly units. -> '''Resolve''': Apply '''Armor 6''' to friendly units.
summary: Steelworker is an uncommon [[Hellhorned]] [[banner unit]]. It applies {{IconLink|Armor}} to allies on the floor on {{IconLink|Resolve}}.

title: Transcendimp

ability.value: When played, repeat all {{IconLink|Summon}} effects triggered so far this battle.

flavor.value: ''When a demon dies under the weight of their horns, they are reborn as impish infants, restarting their molting cycle. These imps are quite possibly the most powerful Hellhorned in existence -  seeing all that has come before and all that will come after. While this power is lost upon their first molting, they've been crucial in my research of their Ring.''

tables: '''Immortalstone''' grants {{IconLink|Endless}}, allowing the '''Transcendimp''' to be played multiple times per combat, activating its powerful effect more frequently.
'''Dualstone''' causes status effects from {{IconLink|Summon}} effects like [[Fledgling Imp]] and [[Waxcap]] to be doubled, regardless of whether the original unit had {{IconLink|Dualism}}.

Though only available with [[Melting Remnant]], '''Wickstone''''s {{IconLink|Burnout|1}} ensures that '''Transcendimp''' dies every turn, allowing it to be replayed when combined with {{IconLink|Endless}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: The Transcendimp is a rare [[Hellhorned]] unit. When played, it repeats all {{IconLink|Summon}} effects triggered so far in the battle.

title: Apex Imp

flavor.value: As I have recorded at great length, the cycling of Imps to Demons and back again is an often observed phenomenon. Their existence in a sort of "transition state," however, is rarely seen. These Imps, almost Demons, exhibit reserved behavior and a sort of misplaced confidence that I've only seen in human adolescents on their way to adulthood. I can understand the Hellhorned's hesitance to make these Imps known...

tables: As with any unit capable of achieving high {{Attack}}, '''Frenzystone''' is critical on '''Apex Imp'''. <!-- TODO: does this actually work? |-
Dualism doubles the amount of {{IconLink|Rage}} your ability applies, scaling your {{Attack}} to even greater values. -->
'''Titanstone''' instead doubles the impact of the {{IconLink|Armor}} you're applying to '''Apex Imp''', effectively doubling your defensive scaling instead.

If your run wants to duplicate '''Apex Imp''' to take advantage of floor-wide {{IconLink|Armor}} scaling but you do not have a way to overstack floors, '''Smidgestone''' can be a strong pickup to avoid having to take {{IconLink|Heaven's Light|png=BSG_HeavensLight}} after one of the boss fights.

Though only available with the [[Stygian Guard]] or by getting very lucky with [[Malicka's Shifting Pyre]] or [[Capricious Reflection]], '''Runestone''' is an obscenely strong upgrade on '''Apex Imp''', causing the unit to gain {{IconLink|Armor}} and therefore {{IconLink|Rage}} on {{IconLink|Incant}}. '''Dualstone''' can take things even further by doubling the {{IconLink|Armor}} gain from {{IconLink|Incant}}, or from the {{IconLink|Resolve}} provided by [[Fortified Pauldrons]].
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Apex Imp is a rare [[Hellhorned]] [[banner unit]]. He has a triggered ability upon being {{IconLink|Armored}} - he gains an equal amount of {{IconLink|Rage}}.

title: Consumer of Crowns

flavor.value: Truly a behemoth among beasts, this demon is the most decorated warrior in the Ring, having collected more horns than any living demon. It is highly respected amongst the Hellhorned and frequently avoided by me.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' doubles the amount of damage '''Consumer of Crowns''' deals when attacking and using its ability.
'''Smidgestone''' makes it much easier to fit '''Consumer of Crowns''' onto your train, giving you the {{Capacity}} to play the Imps it requires while still letting you protect it with a sturdy tank.

'''Speedstone''' makes '''Consumer of Crowns''' {{IconLink|Quick}}, making up for its poor {{Health}} by letting it kill enemies before they strike. This is quite useful if you do not have Welder Helper to provide it with {{IconLink|Armor}}, although this is usually not necessary as long as you have a steady stream of Imps, as it can use those Imps to attack first anyways.

'''Ascetic Penance''' and '''Ascetic Absolution''' make it easier to afford other units alongside '''Consumer of Crowns''', and make it a good duplication target, especially with '''Smidgestone'''. (Its {{Ember}} cost otherwise makes duplicating it difficult to afford.)
{{Ember|10}} >>> {{Ember|8}}, Costs {{Ember|-3}} per Imp unit in play. >>> Costs {{Ember|-1}} per Imp unit in your deck.

[[Consumer of Crowns]] cost reduced from {{Ember|8}} >>> {{Ember|4}}. Updated effect from: "Costs {{Ember|-1}} per Imp unit in your deck." >>> {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}: Warlord's Tithe. "'''[[Sacrifice]] Imp'''. Attack immediately. Cooldown 2."
Fixed bug where Consumer of Crowns's ability could target other floors and cause game breaking issues.
[[Consumer of Crowns]] ability Warlord's Tithe cooldown decreased from 2 to 0.
summary: Consumer of Crowns is a rare [[Hellhorned]] [[banner unit]]. It can [[Sacrifice]] an [[Imp]] in order to attack immediately.

title: Deranged Brute

ability.value: {{IconLink|Rage}} on friendly units adds {{Attack|+3}} per stack.

flavor.value: For a race that is bred on violence, even the Hellhorned have limits to the amount of aggression that is acceptable. But desperate times have forced the Hellhorned to agree to release their most dangerous prisoners.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' doubles '''Deranged Brute''''s damage output, and is useful if you will be using it as your primary damage unit, or if your source of {{IconLink|Rage}} affects the whole floor, such as with Branded Warrior or Fledgling Imp.
