'''Smidgestone''' allows you to fit more copies of '''Deranged Brute''' on the floor, or to add more recipients for its powerful scaling. It also frees up space to play Fledgling Imp or [[Transcendimp]], if those units are your sources of {{IconLink|Rage}}.

'''Largestone''' can be applied with no drawbacks once you already have '''Smidgestone''', bolstering '''Deranged Brute''''s {{Health}} and letting it work as a tank if necessary. It should generally not be applied unless you already have '''Smidgestone''', however.
'''Heartstone''' provides a simple boost to {{Health}}, which can be useful if using '''Deranged Brute''' purely as a support unit to protect it from {{IconLink|Spikes}} and {{IconLink|Sweep}}.
'''Furystone''' gives a solid baseline amount of {{IconLink|Rage}}, which can be useful in the early rings if you haven't found other good sources of it yet.

Although '''Deranged Brute''' is not typically a frontliner, '''Savage Heart''' provides it with absurd amounts of {{IconLink|Rage}} over the course of a game if you can protect it using {{IconLink|Armor}}. This upgrade may be more useful on another ally than on '''Deranged Brute''' itself, but '''Deranged Brute''' can send its already-powerful effect through the roof.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: The Deranged Brute is a rare [[Hellhorned]] [[banner unit]]. It amplifies the effect of {{IconLink|Rage}} on friendly units.

title: Vent

flavor.value: The Boneshaker is of my own design. Fueled by the last shards of the Pyre, the train is robust and dependable. One of its lesser-known features is the ability to unleash pressurized steam on invaders.

tables: '''Powerstone''' lets you play this for {{Ember|0}} for solid value, and lets you kill things like [[Harpist Protector]], and [[Ragewing Assassin]].
'''Surgestone''' also lets you kill [[Discordant Heretic]] for {{Ember|0}}, and adding [[Consume]] is nice for the lategame as you won't want this card to stick around then.

'''Smolderstone''' can be fine too if you need your '''Powerstone''' or '''Surgestone''' elsewhere, as it still lets this spell hit most of what it's going to hit for {{Ember|0}} or {{Ember|1}} while also getting it out of the way in the lategame.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Vent is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It deals 5X damage to enemy units.

title: Hidden Passage

flavor.value: Not all routes through the Boneshaker are immediately recognizable. I sealed many of them off to all but those who are willing to tear through steel and squeeze through the shreds.

tables: '''Seekstone''', in addition to discounting this card to {{Ember|0}}, also puts it in your hand on turn 1 reliably, letting you get your kill floor together faster and more consistently.
'''Twinstone''' gives you two of these for the price of one, letting you Ascend two units together and get your kill floor together faster.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Hidden Passage is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It [[Ascend]]s a chosen unit.

title: Horn Break

flavor.value: A defeated opponent's horns are broken as a ritualistic act of dominance. The horns are then collected by the victor as a trophy.

tables:
'''Powerstone''' ensures that '''Horn Break''' can kill just about any backliners, including [[Chosen Supplicant]] but just short of [[Chosen Assassin]]s. It also lets you kill [[Celestial Bastion]]s.

It might be worth putting two of these on Horn Break on Covenant 10 to be able to kill [[Chosen Assassin]] and [[Chosen Bastion]] too depending on what Seraph variant you have.
'''Keepstone''' lets you use this card to eliminate a problematic backliner (or sometimes frontliner) every turn.
'''Surgestone''' is an alternative if you don't mind '''Consume''' and want to be able to kill the aforementioned Chosen variants with just one upgrade.
'''Emberstone''' is a no-frills way to improve your {{Ember}} economy.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Horn Break is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It deals 8 [[Piercing]] damage, twice.

title: Ritual of Battle

flavor.value: I have learned that the Hellhorned can gain temporary strength through the self-infliction of pain. I find the ritual savage, but it proves to be even more effective when performed over the remains of their opponents.

tables: '''Emberstone''' and '''Seekstone''' reduce this card's {{Ember}} cost, making it easier to play. '''Seekstone''' also ensures you have your {{IconLink|Rage}} from the start of battle. Putting both of these on '''Ritual of Battle''' can be well worth it and makes the card an excellent duplication target.

'''Smolderstone''' massively decreases the cost of this spell, at the cost of making it Consume. Combined with '''Seekstone''', it will provide {{IconLink|Rage|12}} to a target of your choice instantly at no {{Ember}} or draw cost, making it an excellent duplication target. The [[Impish Scholar]] can also be used to recover the spell after it is consumed.
'''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Rage}} applied. {{IconLink|Twinstone}} can too, but this is hard to pull off given its {{Ember}} cost.

Two of [[Entropy's Crystals]] upgrades can be quite strong here. '''Entropic Energy''' eliminates its {{Ember}} cost, allowing you to duplicate and spam this card freely to scale immensely over the course of a fight, while '''Entropic Stone''' triples its output to {{IconLink|Rage|36}}, giving an enormous {{Attack|72}} boost.
summary: Ritual of Battle is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Rage|12}} to its target.

title: Imp-in-a-Box

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Add '''2''' random [[:Category:Imp units|Imp units]] to your hand.

flavor.value: ''Whoever thought to put imps in a confined space had clearly never interacted with the little devils. That didn't stop me from keeping a few boxes. Though, every once in a while, one finally does get out.''

tables: '''Twinstone''' is easy to add from an {{Ember}} standpoint. The challenge is being able to play 4 imp units! There's a ~60% chance you'll get at least one [[Pyre Chomper]] this way to pay for the {{Ember}} cost of the imps you get, but you'll still need {{Capacity}} and enough {{Ember}} to handle the situations where you don't get [[Pyre Chomper]].

'''Eternalstone''' keeps the imp parade going throughout the fight for small decks capable of consistently making good use of it. A '''Keepstone''' can then be added to guarantee getting it every turn.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Imp-in-a-Box is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It adds 2 random [[:Category:Imp units|Imp units]] to your hand that last for the combat.

title: Imp-portant Work

flavor.value: "Some Imps learn much about Horned. It is only through dying that Imps can teach Horned." -excerpt from Hell's Horns by Grrrg Onehorn on the posthumous transfer of knowledge in Hellhorned society.

tables:
'''Keepstone''' lets you keep playing this card every turn, which is great if you either have a steady supply of [[Imp]]s or one {{IconLink|Endless}} one. As this draws you a card, this doesn't cost per-turn draw, unlike other '''Keepstone''' applications. (If it's played on an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Imp]], killing that [[Imp]] '''does''' cost card draw, though in that case hopefully the Imp's {{IconLink|Summon}} trigger is worth it.)

Just be aware that you won't be able to play it and therefore won't be able to keep drawing it if you don't have an [[Imp]] on the train somewhere, which can be troublesome if you draw it before your {{IconLink|Endless}} Imp.

'''Freezestone''' prevents you from having to reshuffle this card if you happen to draw it with no imps on the train. This is especially useful alongside '''Keepstone''' to ensure you'll be able to start abusing this card on your {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Imp]] as soon as you draw it.

If you have a lot of [[Imp]]s, it's easy to benefit from more copies of this card. If you have an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Imp]], you'll be able to benefit from its {{IconLink|Summon}} effect twice - just target that imp twice! You can duplicate this card repeatedly with an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Imp]] to keep increasing its power.

'''Smolderstone''' does nothing but add [[Consume]], but with an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Impish Scholar]] and no other [[Consume]] cards in your deck, this can be a very simple [[Infinite]]. Play this on your [[Impish Scholar]], redraw the [[Impish Scholar]], then the [[Impish Scholar]] will retrieve this card. If you have an {{IconLink|Incant}}, {{IconLink|Rally}}, or {{IconLink|Harvest}} trigger to capitalize on it, or another {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Imp]] and a '''Twinstone''', this can break the game wide open.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
Fixed [[Echo Vault]] incorrectly sacrificing non-imp targets when recasting '[[Imp-portant Work]]'.
summary: Imp-portant Work is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It [[Sacrifice]]s the target [[Imp]], and upon doing so draws a card and provides {{Ember|1}}.

title: Rage Serum

flavor.value: Some Hellhorned grind the horns they've won and steep a potion for additional strength. It is a foul substance that I've had the distinct misfortune to try, but the Hellhorned can't seem to get enough.

tables: One advantage of this card being {{Ember|0}} is that '''Stackstone''' and '''Twinstone''' can both be applied to it relatively easily if shops allow, making it give {{IconLink|Rage|20}} and being an easy duplication target. It also becomes a great target for [[Impish Scholar]] to recur this way.
'''Eternalstone''' can be considered in a small, draw-rich deck, letting it serve as cheap {{IconLink|Rage}}.
summary: Rage Serum is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Rage|5}} to a unit.

title: Imp-pressive

effect.value:
'''[[Attuned]]'''. '''[[Sacrifice]] [[Imp]]'''.
Deal '''50''' damage to the front enemy unit.

flavor.value: "Some Imps eat Pyre. While Pyre tasty, Pyre not endless. Hungry imps then eaten by Pyre. And life continues." -excerpt from Hell's Horns by Grrrg Onehorn on Pyre-eating etiquette.

tables: '''Powerstone''' ups the damage on this spell to 100, keeping it relevant through the midgame.
'''Twinstone''' can be considered in very high-[[Imp]] runs, such as with [[Shardtail Queen]]'s '''Imp Parade III''' route, to allow you to keep playing them.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Imp-pressive is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It targets an [[Imp]] and [[Sacrifice]]s it, then deals 50 damage to the front enemy unit. It has [[Attuned]], gaining 5x damage from [[Magic Power]].

title: March of Shields

flavor.value: Only the bravest, or dumbest, Hellhorned are chosen to bear a shield and hold the line. They are trained to take the brunt of most attacks through an intense regimen of magma-walking that kills more often than not.

tables:
'''Twinstone''' lets you play this card multiple times per turn. '''Emberstone''' or another discounting upgrade goes nicely with this, playing out both copies for {{Ember|0}} instead of {{Ember|2}}.

It also allows you to use this on a frail backliner in combats like [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], as otherwise a weakness of this card is that especially in the lategame, you can't use it to protect your backliners because it will [[Advance]] them. With '''Twinstone''', you can apply it to your frail backliner, then use the copy to put your tank back in front.
'''Keepstone''' can also be a way to consistently scale a unit defensively throughout the battle. This is particularly appealing if you are using it to trigger {{IconLink|Shift}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: March of Shields is an uncommon [[Hellhorned]] spell. It moves a unit to the front and grants them {{IconLink|Armor|12}}.

title: Branding Rite

flavor.value: The focused application of heat on a Hellhorned hide will force it to calcify and provide a natural defense. Though I can tell you that the smell is truly...unique.

tables: Making '''Branding Rite''' more affordable is key to fitting it into your turn.
'''Stackstone''' doubles this card's ability to provide {{IconLink|Armor}} to your units, more than doubling its net output.

As a role-compressed card, '''Branding Rite''' can be nice with '''Keepstone''', as it means you'll always have something for spot removal, {{IconLink|Armor}}ing, or killing [[:Category:Imp units|Imps]]. The {{Ember}} and draw cost on this means your deck has to make good use of its modality to justify this, though.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Branding Rite is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It deals 3 piercing damage to any target, and then, if it survives, grants it {{IconLink|Armor|20}}.

title: Enflame

flavor.value: Deep within the Scorched Plains, Hellhorned Demons can sometimes be seen performing a "magma-walk" - a bizarre coming-of-age ritual involving full submersion into lava and a focused trek across the Plain. It's unbelievable that any Demons survive the ritual, but those that do are stronger for it.

tables: Putting '''Emberstone''' on '''Enflame''' helps you spam it more, and in many cases this is a straightforward way to get more value out of your turn.
'''Smolderstone''' makes it cost {{Ember|0}}, great if you're just using it to start up your {{IconLink|Rage}} and/or {{IconLink|Armor}} engine.
'''Stackstone''' can be considered to double its effect. It's not the most exciting recipient of this upgrade but if you can spam this card the benefits do add up.
Apply Rage 4 and Armor 5. -> Apply Rage 6 and Armor 10.
summary: Enflame is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Rage|6}} and {{IconLink|Armor|10}} to its target.

title: Tiresome Climb

flavor.value: Alongside the few remaining Hellhorned scholars, I designed the Boneshaker to change its shape at will, creating hallways that stretch to near infinity for the Winged who choose to walk them.

tables: '''Seekstone''' and '''Twinstone''' can be used in the same ways they are used on [[Hidden Passage]]. However, due to this card's higher price and {{IconLink|Dazed}} effect, this is often not the best choice, and you may be better served using these upgrades to disrupt more enemies or apply {{IconLink|Dazed}} for longer.

'''Stackstone''' can be considered instead if you're leaning into this as a boss/tanky enemy unit answer, applying {{IconLink|Dazed|4}}. It does mean you can't really use it for floor overstacking except as a last resort, but that is generally minor.

'''Keepstone''' is a fantastic solution to several of the biggest problems you can face during a run, letting you lock down flying bosses for the entire fight or consistently remove irritating backliners or tanky frontliners. This upgrade pairs especially well with '''Seekstone''' to reduce its cost and ensure you have this card from the start of every fight.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Tiresome Climb is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It [[Ascend]]s a unit and applies {{IconLink|Dazed|2}}.

title: Battering Ram

effect.value: Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to '''4x''' {{IconLink|Armor}} on friendly units.

flavor.value: Working with the Railbeaters, I was able to devise a series of interlocking shields that turn the Hellhorned into a mobile battering ram.

tables: '''Freezestone''' lets you hold this very context-specific spell for the time in the fight it can do the most damage. Perhaps it will let you line up that elusive boss one-hit knockout! It also makes it slightly more affordable.
'''Smolderstone''' gives a nice {{Ember}} discount, and if you're gunning for a boss kill, there's no need to play it more than once.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Battering Ram is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It deals a single hit of damage to the front enemy unit equal to four times the total {{IconLink|Armor}} on all friendly units on the floor.

title: Inferno

flavor.value: The Scorched Plains are known for frequent firestorms that can rain down at any moment, striking anyone unlucky enough to be caught below. This has made my travels through it particularly short.

tables: As '''Inferno''' asks you to reserve a room for it, you'll want to make sure that investment pays off, and '''Keepstone''' lets you play this every turn, provided you can afford it.

With '''Keepstone''', a way to defray this card's {{Ember}} cost is helpful. '''Seekstone''' is probably the best to ensure you can play this turn 1, though '''Freezestone''' or '''Emberstone''' can suffice, especially for smaller decks. '''Freezestone''' in particular means you can skip playing it for a turn if you need to without losing access to it next turn.
'''Entropic Energy''' deserves mention for immediately reducing this card's cost to {{Ember|0}}, making it a breeze to play.

If you leaned away from using this as a main part of your strategy, '''Smolderstone''' can be applied instead to make it easier to use as a one-off way to weaken early waves that might have escaped your units.
Wording change from friendly and enemy units to all units
summary: Inferno is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It deals 120 [[Piercing]] damage to all units on the floor, including both enemies and friendly units.

title: Spike of the Hellhorned

flavor.value: In an act of unity unheard of in Hellhorned culture, Grrrg the Railbeater snapped his own horn to seal the Rail in their Ring, bringing the Hellhorned into our Covenant. Grrrg the Railbeater was thereafter known as Grrrg Onehorn.

tables: '''Emberstone''' and other {{Ember}} upgrades can increase this card's potency.

'''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Rage}} and {{IconLink|Armor}} applied, which is potent if you can put a lot of {{Ember}} into it. '''Entropic Stone''' can be strong for the same reasons, and is better than '''Entropic Energy''' if you play it for {{Ember|3+}}.
'''Eternalstone''' can allow you to replay this card. Once you do so, adding '''Smolderstone''' adds {{IconLink|Rage|8}} and {{IconLink|Armor|8}} per play.
[[Spike of the Hellhorned]] '''[[Armor]]''' and {{IconLink|Rage}} increased from 2X >>> 3X.
[[Spike of the Hellhorned]] '''[[Armor]]''' and {{IconLink|Rage}} increased from 3X >>> 4X.
summary: Spike of the Hellhorned is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It applies 4X {{IconLink|Rage}} and 4X {{IconLink|Armor}} to its target.

title: Dark Deal

flavor.value: Even the residents of Hell serve something darker and more ancient than themselves. They make deals with the Shroud of the Crucible for metals they can find nowhere else.

tables: '''Stackstone''' and '''Entropic Stone''' are the best upgrades for '''Dark Deal''', increasing the {{IconLink|Rage}} applied to a respectable 14 and 21, respectively. This puts it on par with [[Ritual of Battle]], but much cheaper.

'''Twinstone''' is not necessarily ideal due to dealing damage twice, but if you can apply enough {{IconLink|Armor}} that the damage becomes insignificant, it can accelerate your {{IconLink|Rage}} application, or let you apply {{IconLink|Rage}} to multiple units.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Dark Deal is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It deals 5 damage to the target and applies {{IconLink|Rage|7}}.

title: Alloy of the Ancients

flavor.value: An alloy of unknown components said to come from the ancient Umbra. Some demons choose to drink it while others just pour it over themselves, letting the alloy create a natural defense.

tables: '''Twinstone''', coupled with an {{Ember}} discount, can double this card's {{IconLink|Armor}}, either on the same target or different ones.

'''Stackstone''' also doubles this card's {{IconLink|Armor}}, and unlike '''Twinstone''' doesn't require more {{Ember}} or an {{Ember}} upgrade to do so. It can also be used with '''Twinstone''' for an impressive {{Armor|120}}.
'''Eternalstone''' can be considered for small decks, letting you recur this efficient {{IconLink|Armor}}-applying card.
'''Emberstone''' is fairly practical here for {{Ember|-1}} on use, especially with '''Twinstone'''.
'''Seekstone''' is great if you need the {{IconLink|Armor}} it provides early in the fight, either to keep your units alive or to have {{IconLink|Armor}} to double with [[Reinforce]].
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Alloy of the Ancients is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Armor|30}} to a unit.

title: Imp-olate

effect.value: Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to '''25x''' the number of [[Imp]] units in your deck.

flavor.value: "Imps die for their horns to grow large. Demons die for their horns to grow sharp." -excerpt from Hell's Horns by Grrrg Onehorn, discussing the cyclical life of a Hellhorned and how their horns mature.

tables: '''Twinstone''' lets you double-dip on this card's damage. '''Emberstone''' goes nicely with this.
'''Keepstone''' can also be a way for this to consistently knock out a frontliner in very [[Imp]]-focused runs.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to 15x the number of Imp units in your deck. -> Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to 20x the number of Imp units in your deck.
summary: Imp-olate is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It deals 25x the number of [[Imp]] units in your deck to the front enemy unit.

title: Last Stand

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Double the amount of {{IconLink|Rage}} on friendly units.

flavor.value: It's impossible for the Hellhorned to regain their standing after their horns have been broken, but that doesn't mean they can't fight back against their aggressor to salvage what remains of their reputation.

tables: '''Eternalstone''' prevents '''Last Stand''' from being Consumed after use, which means with a thin enough deck you will be able to play it repeatedly. It also allows you to apply '''Smolderstone''' to reduce its cost to a mere {{Ember|1}}. If you get this combination of upgrades, '''Last Stand''' should be duplicated as much as possible in order to play it more often.

'''Freezestone''' lets you avoid one of the dangers of this card, which is drawing it before you have had a chance to apply much {{IconLink|Rage}} or on a turn where you cannot afford to play it. This way, you can hold onto it until the right moment. It also slightly reduces its {{Ember}} cost.

'''Twinstone''' is quite difficult to use due to this spell's cost - by default, you must spend {{Ember|6}} on a single turn just to play both copies. However, if you are able to make use of this upgrade, it is ''extremely'' strong, quadrupling all {{IconLink|Rage}} on the floor. '''Emberstone''' makes it cost a more reasonable {{Ember|4}} to play both copies, and should be a high priority. Some support for this upgrade might include [[Pyre Chomper]] with [[Ashes of the Fallen]], [[Perils of Production]] with [[Kindle]], or the [[Ancient Roots]] artifact with a large deck.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Last Stand is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. When played, it doubles {{IconLink|Rage}} stacks on friendly units.

title: Reinforce

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Double the amount of {{IconLink|Armor}} on a unit.

flavor.value: Armor forged by Hellhorned steelworkers is among the sturdiest defense known to Hell. It is not, however, known to be particularly comfortable, so the Hellhorned wear it only when absolutely necessary.

tables: '''Eternalstone''' will make it possible to play '''Reinforce''' multiple times per combat, letting it re-double {{IconLink|Armor}} applied to its target. The amount of {{IconLink|Armor}} exponentially scales with how many times you can play this! It also allows you to apply '''Smolderstone''' to make it affordable, and with these upgrades, it's an excellent duplication target and can easily let you hit the {{IconLink|Armor}} cap of 9999. Note that it's also possible to recur this card with [[Impish Scholar]], in which case these upgrades may be unnecessary, but they still allow you to make the card much cheaper and can let your Impish Scholar return a different card.

'''Emberstone''' can also be used to help play '''Reinforce''', as can '''Seekstone''' and '''Freezestone'''. Depending on whether you're using a unit with initial {{IconLink|Armor}} or are looking to spike it with e.g. [[Alloy of the Ancients]], '''Seekstone''' or '''Freezestone''' can also help you with timing it, and '''Seekstone''' is also helpful if you're using [[Impish Scholar]] to recur it, ensuring it'll be available to retrieve.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Reinforce is a rare [[Hellhorned]] spell. It doubles a target's {{IconLink|Armor}}.

title: Onehorn's Tome

flavor.value: "Hell's Horns, History of the Hellhorned", by Grrrg Onehorn. The terrible handwriting of the imp scribes has made this tome an excruciating read and something I don't plan on returning to soon.

tables: '''Emberstone''', '''Seekstone''', and '''Freezestone''' reduce this card's {{Ember}} cost, allowing it to be played without a source of ember generation. '''Seekstone''' also ensure you have your {{IconLink|Multistrike}} from the start of battle, while '''Freezestone''' prevents you from reshuffling the card if you must play more important cards on the turn you draw it.

'''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Multistrike}} gained while not affecting the {{IconLink|Fragile}} application. {{IconLink|Twinstone}} can too, but this is hard to pull off given its {{Ember}} cost.

'''Eternalstone''' can scale your units to spectacular heights if you have a small deck and enough {{Ember}} to repeatedly play this card. This also allows you to apply '''Smolderstone''' to make it semi-affordable as well.

Two of [[Entropy's Crystals]] upgrades can be extremely strong here. * '''Entropic Energy''' eliminates its {{Ember}} cost, allowing you to duplicate and spam this card freely to scale explosively over the course of a fight. * '''Entropic Stone''' means it gives you {{IconLink|Multistrike|3}}, quadrupling your offense with a single play, and potentially much more than that if you can afford to play it multiple times.
summary: Onehorn's Tome is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Fragile}} and {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} to a friendly unit.

title: Fortified Pauldrons

flavor.value: Leather is a common material among the Hellhorned, so I've lined my garb with the material for protection. Given the stench, I'm sure the source of it is better left a mystery.

tables: [[Fortify]] updated from Spell >>> Equipment. Renamed to "[[Fortified Pauldrons]]". "Apply '''[[Armor]] 8'''" >>> "'''[[Armor]] 6'''. {{IconLink|Resolve}}: Gain '''[[Armor]] 6'''."
summary: Fortified Pauldrons is a common [[Hellhorned]] equipment added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update, replacing [[Fortify]]. It grants a unit {{IconLink|Armor|6}} immediately and an additional {{IconLink|Armor|6}} on {{IconLink|Resolve}}.

title: Rage Room

flavor.value: On the rare night when the flames of Hell have dwindled to no more than smoldering embers, the Hellhorned tradition is to rekindle them by using their rage and destroying everything in sight.

summary: Rage Room is a rare [[Hellhorned]] room added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It grants friendly units {{IconLink|Rage|2}} on {{IconLink|Strike}} and {{IconLink|Revenge}}.

title: Awoken

flavor.value: ''Gather the Awoken of the Wildwood Forest. Hollows and Animus are supported by healing Channelers.''

summary: Awoken [[File:ClanAwoken.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]], returning from [[Monster Train 1]].  It is unlocked after unlocking [[Hellhorned]] first and then healing 300 lost health.

title: The Sentient

flavor.value: This Hollow was able to sever her connection to the Wildwood, slowly awakening to the prison her soul was trapped in, but still agreeing to champion our Covenant. Now she has repurposed her armor as makeshift shields to keep the rest of the vines at bay, becoming more aggressive with each attempt at recapture.

tables: Explosive Sentient HP increased from 25/50/100 >>> 30/60/120 Explosive Sentient III damage on Rejuvenate increased from 90 >>> 120.
summary: The Sentient is the primary [[Champion]] of the [[Awoken]]. She is intended as a tanky frontliner who can block large amounts of damage due to her high {{Health}} and access to healing, while also dealing damage to enemies, drawing extra cards and buffing your other units. Her starter card is [[Restore]].

title: Wyldenten

flavor.value: Something in the Wildwood unsettles my mind, granting me visions of its very Roots when I rest there. But these Roots form a creature predating both Hollows and Channelers. Was there some soul before the Wildwood?

tables: Wyldenten Strangler {{Health}} increased from 30/50/70 >>> 40/65/90. Wyldenten Thornlord {{Attack}} increased from 5/5/5 >>> 5/10/20.

Thornlord [[Wyldenten]]. Converted effect into an ability. "{{IconLink|Summon}}: Add 3 [[Sting]] spells with [[Frozen]] to your hand." >>> "{{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}: Needlebloom. (Add 3 [[Sting]] spells to your hand)."
summary: Wyldenten is the alternate [[Champion]] of the [[Awoken]] clan. Unlike [[The Sentient]], who is intended as a tank, Wyldenten is intended as an odd mix of damage dealer and support. With good damage scaling from your allied clan, he can be astonishingly powerful, and can take out whole waves of enemies on his own. His starter card is [[Rootseeds]].

title: Restore

flavor.value: One of the many strengths of the Channelers of the Wildwood is their ability to heal their fellow Awoken. Upon our completion of the Rail, they agreed to extend this practice to other Hellborne in need.

tables: '''Surgestone''' has a dual purpose on '''Restore''', allowing it to really save a unit's life once, and as a soft Purge.

'''Restore''' is fairly easy to play and with the right {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} abilities can even have a decent payoff. Since the Awoken clan has several ways to draw lots of cards, 0-cost '''Restores''', even without other upgrades, can actually become solid value cards!
'''Smolderstone''' applies the same cost reduction as '''Emberstone''', along with removing the card from your deck once played.
summary: Restore is [[The Sentient]]'s starter card. It restores {{Health|4}} and applies {{IconLink|Regen|2}}.

title: Rootseeds

flavor.value: In one of these dreams, that I'm beginning to believe are visions of the past, Wyldenten showed me the creation of the Wildwood itself: seeds taken from Wyldenten's own body. His final gift before his Exile.

tables: Putting '''Emberstone''' on '''Rootseeds''' is usually preferable to purging it, as it makes the card fully draw- and {{Ember}}-neutral while still providing a benefit.

'''Smolderstone''' also accomplishes what '''Emberstone''' does. While adding [[Consume]] isn't necessarily good, you can only get one '''Emberstone''' per Merchant of Magic anyway, and in decks with lots of "draw next turn" effects, you won't mind losing this card after its first play.

'''Seekstone''' makes '''Rootseeds''' 0-cost, but because it adds Intrinsic as well, it makes it draw-positive. It costs no draw on the first turn and draws an additional card on the second turn, accelerating your ability to draw through the deck. '''Seekstone''''s only real downside is its higher cost, and the opportunity cost of not putting it on a more important spell.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Rootseeds is [[Wyldenten]]'s starter card. It applies {{Attack|+3}} and draws 1 next turn.

title: Edge Prior

ability.value: Healing and {{IconLink|Regen}} spells cost {{Ember|-1}} on this floor.

flavor.value: A Channeler cannot die, but it can fade away, though I've yet to see this firsthand. Many choose to spend their fading time at the secluded edge of the Wildwood as part of the Edge Priory, crafting the armor that will protect new Awoken in their infancy.

tables: '''Heartstone''' makes the '''Edge Prior''' less fragile, protecting it somewhat from enemies with {{IconLink|Sweep}} or those which can apply {{IconLink|Corruption}} to backliners. It may be worth taking two '''Heartstones''', as the '''Edge Prior''' does not benefit significantly from other upgrades. Even then, this may not be worth the {{Gold}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
Changed [[Edge Prior]] unit's healing spell cost bonus to also include {{IconLink|Regen}} spells.
summary: Edge Prior is an uncommon [[Awoken]] unit. As a non-[[banner unit]], it can only be drafted from post-combat card rewards. It reduces the costs of [[:Category:Healing cards|healing spells]] and spells that directly apply {{IconLink|Regen}} played on its floor.

title: Wildwood Custodian

flavor.value: Once a soul has been transformed and released again from the vines, they are forever bound as a caretaker to the Wildwood. From my time with them it is clear that these Channelers take pride in aiding souls who have yet to be released.

tables: '''Largestone''' and '''Heartstone''' are the best upgrades for '''Wildwood Custodian''', helping it stay alive. '''Largestone''' in particular is better than usual, as '''Wildwood Custodian''' will usually not be on your main floor, so its extra {{Capacity}} is irrelevant. '''Titanstone''' is usually overkill if you're leaving it alone on a higher floor, but if you're using this as a tank with [[Stoic Platemail]] it can be quite useful.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Wildwood Custodian is an uncommon [[Awoken]] unit. It grants +1 draw per turn while on the train.

title: Animus of Speed

flavor.value: Newly formed, this Animus is no longer protected by its steel armor, making it quicker and deadlier. It is possessed by the soul of the Wildwood and the Channelers who guard it, often making my conversations with it obtuse and pointless.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' is by far the most important upgrade to put on '''Animus of Speed''', drastically increasing '''Swiftshot''''s efficacy. It may even be worth getting two copies, if you have faith in your scaling and do not plan to need other upgrades to mitigate '''Cooldown'''.

'''Immortalstone''' makes '''Animus of Speed''' {{IconLink|Endless}}, which lets you play it on the bottom floor, take out an important backliner or two, attack the front unit, die, and then be available to do it all again next turn.

'''Burststone''' is available only with the [[Railforged]], but if '''Animus of Speed''' is going to die each turn, it becomes a strong alternative to '''Frenzystone''' outside of {{IconLink|Relentless}}; it will hit with '''Swiftshot''' three times which is stronger than '''Frenzystone''', but only once on its actual attack. It is also much cheaper than '''Frenzystone''' and guaranteed to be seen with a reroll.

'''Smidgestone''' reduces it to {{Capacity|1}}, which can be vital if you plan to play around '''Cooldown 2''' with two copies of the unit, as now you can fit two copies in the same space it normally takes to fit one.

'''Largestone''' greatly increases [[Animus of Speed]]'s stats. Notably, it grants exactly enough {{Attack}} to kill a [[Chosen Assassin]] lacking {{IconLink|Titanskin}}, even without {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. This is a good option if you have alternate methods of reducing '''Cooldown''', or if you only need '''Swiftshot''' to be an occasional supplement to your strategy and consistency is less of a concern.
[[Animus of Speed]] new ability "Swiftshot: Attack any enemy immediately."
Fixed interaction between Animus of Speed and Iron Tongue where Animus of Speed's ability would not correctly Sweep.
summary: Animus of Speed is an uncommon [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. It has high {{Attack}}, {{IconLink|Quick}}, and its Swiftshot ability allows it to immediately attack any unit on the floor.

title: Animus of Will

flavor.value: These Animus have grown to see beyond their Ring. Preternaturally aware of the actions of their enemies, they can predict their movements and strike accordingly. I've learned that they are rarely created by Channelers since their gift of sight can expose them to the reality of their imprisonment.

tables: '''Largestone''' provides significant boosts to the [[Animus of Will]]'s very low starting stats, making it much less fragile and massively increasing its damage output. However, if you are scaling '''Animus of Will''' via '''[[Cultivate]]''', the huge boost to {{Health}} can be a detriment, as eventually its {{Health}} will be greater than the unit with '''[[Cultivate]]''' and its scaling will slow.

'''Smidgestone''' decreases its size, making it easier to fit on a floor with other units. It can be combined with '''Largestone''' to grant the benefits of both, turning the '''Animus of Will''' into an extremely powerful unit with {{Capacity|1}}, {{Attack|18x3}} and {{Health|58}}. This combination makes it an excellent target for duplication.
'''Speedstone''' provides a small boost to {{Attack}} while also granting {{IconLink|Quick}}, and can let '''Animus of Will''' kill enemies before they attack.

'''Dualstone''' grants {{IconLink|Dualism}}, which is useless by default. However, if you are using equipment with a {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger like [[Everlasting Light]], [[Twisted Back]], or [[Combustion Suit]], this can be a worthwhile upgrade. Only take this upgrade if you already know that you can make good use of it.

'''Frenzystone''' provides an additional {{IconLink|Multistrike}} stack, which is valuable if this unit is your primary damage source. However, consider carefully if there are other units that would appreciate this upgrade more, like [[Animus of Speed]], [[Shattered Shell]], or [[Steelsinger]], since it is relatively unnecessary on '''Animus of Will''' in comparison.

In the absence of '''Largestone''', '''Strengthstone''' and '''Heartstone''' can be combined as a cheaper alternative to boost its stats, with the advantage of being guaranteed in the shop if you can afford a reroll. If you cannot find more effective upgrades, these will serve you decently.
summary: The Animus of Will is an uncommon [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. It has low stats but starts with {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}}.

title: Awoken Hollow

flavor.value: These souls, imprisoned in steel, try to break free before they lose their minds to the Wildwood. I had no idea of this until the Channelers told me. It took me some time to trust them again after that revelation.

tables: '''Smidgestone''' reduces the unit's capacity from {{Capacity|3}} to {{Capacity|1}}, allowing it to more easily fit on floors and protect more units. While having more units can make the [[Cultivate]] triggers more spread out, it can still be worth just having more units on a floor. This also makes it better when using Morsels, as this grants an additional {{Capacity|+2}} to place them.

'''Titanstone''' grants {{IconLink|Titanite}}, an important upgrade for many units looking to survive on the front line into the late game. This is generally the most important upgrade for '''Awoken Hollow'''.

'''Frenzystone''' can be situationally strong if you happen to find a way to turn [[Awoken Hollow]]'s {{Health}} into {{Attack}}, and '''Awoken Hollow''' does not have many upgrades that dramatically improve it. Unfortunately, it's often difficult to know that you'll find those ways early in the run. If you have the {{Gold}} to afford it and no other units that need it, this can be a decent investment, but it should not generally be a high priority.

'''Heartstone''' grants a solid {{Health}} boost, which both makes '''Awoken Hollow''' a better tank and lets it Cultivate the same unit for longer before their max {{Health}} matches its own. '''Thornstone''' grants a smaller {{Health}} boost, but also applies {{IconLink|Spikes|3}}, which can at least clear out backliners through the midgame if you don't have another method of doing so. '''Mossystone''' is only available with the [[Underlegion]], but grants a solid amount of {{IconLink|Regen}} alongside a {{Health}} boost, giving some extra {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} triggers and filling out [[Awoken Hollow]]'s missing {{Health}}.

[[Savagery's Statue]] upgrades can all be good here - '''Savage Skin''' further increases [[Awoken Hollow]]'s durability, '''Savage Heart''' can amass a ton of {{IconLink|Rage}} (and make [[Adaptive Mutation]] all the more powerful), and '''Savage Spirit''' will give '''Awoken Hollow''' {{Attack|+120}} at the start of battle and can be strong with the [[Lazarus League]].

Unfortunately, you don't know you'll get [[Savagery's Statue]] in advance, making it risky to apply '''Frenzystone''' hoping for either '''Savage Heart''' or '''Savage Spirit''', so this can be less strong than it seems.
summary: Awoken Hollow is an uncommon [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. It gains 60 max {{Health}} on {{IconLink|Summon}} (which is unfilled), and has a {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} trigger that [[Cultivate]]s 3, letting it strengthen the frailest unit on the floor whenever it is healed.

title: Husk Hermit

flavor.value: Using Wildwood sap to expedite the growth of their vines, these Animus inhabit the remains of their armor. Their larger vines allow them to strike multiple enemies at once, while still being able to retreat into their shell if necessary.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' lets '''Husk Hermit''' strike twice, giving her better odds of quickly removing higher-health backliners like Chosen enemies, and putting bigger dents in heavy units.

'''Largestone''' massively bolsters [[Husk Hermit]]'s {{Health}} and grants a smaller {{Attack}} boost as well. Usually, she will be on a floor by herself, so the {{Capacity}} increase rarely matters.
'''Titanstone''' grants {{IconLink|Titanite}}, which lets '''Husk Hermit''' endure the punishment later rings will throw at her, especially in conjunction with ways to boost max {{Health}}.
If you are not using '''Husk Hermit''' as a tank and have other scaling methods for her, '''Speedstone''' is a classic choice for a {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
[[Husk Hermit]] {{Health}} increased from '''30''' >>> '''35'''. Added new effect: "{{IconLink|Revenge}}: {{Attack|+3}}." {{Attack|5}} >>> {{Attack|3}}
summary: Husk Hermit is an uncommon [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. She has {{IconLink|Sweep}} and gets {{Attack|+3}} on {{IconLink|Revenge}}.

title: Shattered Shell

flavor.value: When Husk Hermits grow too large for their already restrictive shell, they keep the shattered steel pieces for offensive use. Against my wishes, the Channelers have hoarded Pyre shards to further enhance the power of these creatures.

tables: '''Speedstone''' is key for a fragile {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit like '''Shattered Shell''', letting her mow down weak enemies before they have a chance to attack and boosting her damage in the process.

'''Frenzystone''' is an extremely important upgrade for '''Shattered Shell''', doubling her offensive potential. Adding {{IconLink|Multistrike}} to a {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit is one of the most damage-efficient upgrades one can make, and will allow '''Shattered Shell''' to severely dent enemy tanks, if not outright kill them.

Though not as good a recipient as Husk Hermit, '''Largestone''' is still perfectly functional on '''Shattered Shell''' if you want her to handle the bottom floor with as little outside maintenance as possible. However, be aware that this upgrade is counterproductive when scaling '''Shattered Shell''' via [[Cultivate]].
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Shattered Shell is an uncommon [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. She has low starting stats, but has {{IconLink|Sweep}} and gains {{Attack|+3}} whenever she kills an enemy.

title: Thorned Hollow

flavor.value: There is a clearing in the Wildwood where the vines turn brittle and become covered in thorns. While impossible for me to visit, I've heard that the Hollows that root there are afflicted with a similar transformation.

tables: '''Dualstone''' grants {{IconLink|Dualism}}, doubling the {{IconLink|Spikes}} gained per heal. This upgrade is vital if using '''Thorned Hollow''' as a carry, as it is extremely difficult to garner enough {{IconLink|Spikes}} to kill later ring enemies without it, but less necessary (though still useful) if only using it as a backline-eliminating tank.

'''Titanstone''' grants {{IconLink|Titanite}}, halving all incoming damage. This makes '''Thorned Hollow''' a far more effective tank, due to its high base {{Health}} and its frequent healing. '''Titanstone''' and '''Dualstone''' are the best combination of upgrades for using '''Thorned Hollow''' as your carry unit.
'''Smidgestone''' reduces [[Thorned Hollow]]'s {{Capacity}}, making it easier to stick on a floor.
'''Mossystone''' provides {{IconLink|Regen|10}}, letting '''Thorned Hollow''' heal up on its own. It also provides {{Health|10}} to make '''Thorned Hollow''' slightly more durable.
'''Heartstone''' grants a simple boost to {{Health}}, making '''Thorned Hollow''' tankier, as its initial {{Health|25}} is quite poor if you cannot immediately heal it.

'''Frenzystone''' should only be used under very rare circumstances, but if you happen to find the [[Gnarled Root]] artifact, it will turn the {{IconLink|Spikes}} generated by '''Thorned Hollow''' into {{Attack}}, making this a worthy option. It also makes the {{IconLink|Savage Spirit}} upgrade better, though that is of course unreliable and should not be built around.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
[[Thorned Hollow]] {{Health}} increased from '''15''' >>> '''25'''. {{IconLink|Spikes}} on Rejuvenate increased from 3 >>> 4.
summary: Thorned Hollow is an uncommon [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. It has a large amount of {{Health}} and builds {{IconLink|Spikes}} whenever it is healed.

title: Shard Channeler

ability.value: {{IconLink|Spikes}} on friendly units deal '''+1''' damage per stack.

flavor.value: Rather than nurture and care for the growth of the Wildwood, some Channelers choose to defend and protect it by channeling the power of the Pyre shards embedded throughout the forest, using a method I developed for them.

tables: '''Heartstone''' bolsters [[Shard Channeler]]'s {{Health}}, helping it stay alive a little longer against backline damage effects.

'''Immortalstone''' can sometimes be worthwhile against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]], as there is effectively no other way to keep the unit alive against [[Chosen Assassin]]s, but as long as you can replay it it doesn't really matter if it dies. However, this will cost you a card draw and {{Ember|1}} every turn.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Shard Channeler is a rare [[Awoken]] unit. It causes {{IconLink|Spikes}} on friendly units to deal +1 damage per stack on its floor, doubling the damage taken by attackers. Multiple copies will each add an extra point of damage for each stack of {{IconLink|Spikes}}.

title: Steelsinger

flavor.value: "Not of us, but of the Mother," as the Edge Priory says of Steelsingers. I often just nod at their rambling words, accepting them for the insanity they are, but their strange mention of the Mother — a Divinity no doubt — adds an air of validity to this crazy claim.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' is the most important upgrade for '''Steelsinger'''; without {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, it is simply too big, expensive, and difficult to scale to be worth it. If you can deal with its {{Capacity|4}}, two copies of '''Frenzystone''' maximizes its potential damage output.

'''Smidgestone''' drops '''Steelsinger''' down to a mere {{Capacity|1}}, making it far, far easier to stick other units behind it. This also makes better use of its titanic {{Health}}, since now it can block hits for its more fragile allies.

'''Titanstone''' makes '''Steelsinger''' virtually unkillable. This may seem somewhat silly, as a unit with {{Health|120}} that wants constant healing seems like it ought to survive anything that could be thrown at it already, but you would be surprised how quickly it can crumble against a constant barrage of massive damage, as you might face against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]] or in [[Clash with the Titans]].

All three upgrades from the [[Path of the Angel]] event are solid on '''Steelsinger'''. '''Wrath''' lets it attack immediately every three turns, '''Benevolence''' heals it and any allies to full health and grants {{Health|+5}}, and '''Courage''' heals it to full, moves it to the front of the floor, and grants it a tremendous amount of {{IconLink|Armor}}.

'''Discarded Wings''', from the [[Clipped Wings]] event, makes '''Steelsinger''' a lot less unwieldy, as it can fly to any position on any floor once deployed, ignoring {{Capacity}} constraints. Usually, it is worth it to simply take this upgrade, as if you continue to search you risk getting nothing. However, if you're feeling lucky, or you have other ways to address {{Capacity}} and therefore don't really need the upgrade, you can hunt for the '''Wings of Light'''. The '''Flying Strike''' ability lets '''Steelsinger''' do damage equal to its {{Attack}} when it flies to a different floor, and also grants {{IconLink|Titanite}} for free.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Steelsinger is a rare [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. It has one of the highest maximum {{Health}} values in the game, and gains {{Attack}} permanently whenever it is healed.

title: Vinemother

ability.value:
{{IconLink|End of Turn|png=EndOfTurn}}: '''[[Sting]]''' spells in your deck gain '''+4 [[Magic Power]]'''.
{{AbilityBox|Vinewrath|2|Add 2 [[Sting]] spells to hand.}}

flavor.value: These Awoken focus solely on the reproduction of the Wildwood, shedding their steel armor to further spread their thorns with each new surge of life. The Mothers are quite small in stature, but the shell around them provides immense natural protection. Along with the Channelers, they've been indispensable guides during my time in the Wildwood.

tables: '''Vinemother''' is a tank, and upgrades to her should help her stay alive and protect what's behind her.

'''Smidgestone''' makes it easier to fit other units behind '''Vinemother'''. It is also useful if, for some reason, you want to put down as many '''Vinemothers''' as possible to power up your Stings.

[[Vinemother]] updated from "{{IconLink|Resolve}}: Add a [[Sting]] spell to your hand" >>> "{{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}: Vinewrath (Add 2 [[Sting]] Spells to your hand. CD 2.). {{IconLink|End of Turn|png=EndOfTurn}}: [[Sting]] Spells in your deck gain '''+4 [[Magic Power|magic power]]'''."
Fixed Vinemother trigger procing during deployment phase.
summary: Vinemother is a rare [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. For every turn she is on the field, she makes [[Sting]]s in your deck stronger. Her {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, Vinewrath, provides two Stings every other turn.

title: Wilting Sapwood

flavor.value: As an Awoken prepares to leave its physical being to become a custodian of the Wildwood, they harden their bark for ensured protection. I've observed that they also put down more roots with each step towards death, strengthening the entire Wildwood in the process.

tables: '''Titanstone''' grants {{IconLink|Titanite}}, halving the damage '''Wilting Sapwood''' takes. As a pure tank, this boost to its longevity can ensure it survives until the end of the fight, and it effectively doubles the value of healing spells and effects that raise {{Health}}, of which the Awoken have plenty.
'''Immortalstone''' lets '''Wilting Sapwood''' be replayed if it dies. Its {{Ember|2}} cost will likely be a moot point due to the {{Ember}} generated prior to its death.
'''Smidgestone''' reduces '''Wilting Sapwood''' from {{Capacity|3}} to {{Capacity|1}}, allowing more units to fit behind it.

'''Heartstone''' provides a small boost to {{Health}} if you just want to fill out upgrade slots. '''Thornstone''' provides less {{Health}}, but adds {{IconLink|Spikes|3}} to let '''Wilting Sapwood''' damage backline units; however, {{IconLink|Spikes|3}} is extremely weak and must be supplemented with cards like [[Pyre Shards]] in order to kill backliners like [[Deafening Herald]]s and [[Ragewing Assassin]]s in the later rings.
summary: The Wilting Sapwood is a rare [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. It has high {{Health}} and provides {{Ember|1}} whenever it takes damage.

title: Steel Enhancer

flavor.value: I've used Wildwood sap as a mild steel polish as well, providing combat benefits to the Awoken that receive my treatment.

tables: '''Twinstone''' doubles the effect of '''Steel Enhancer''', while also adding a second {{IconLink|Incant}} trigger if your units can take advantage of it. However, it may be better used on a higher-impact card.
'''Smolderstone''' has no actual effect on this card's cost, but it can be used as a cheap pseudo-removal in later rings if this spell has outlived its usefulness.
summary: Steel Enhancer is an [[Awoken]] spell. It adds {{Attack|+4}} and {{Health|+4}} to the target.

title: Sting

effect.value:
Deal '''12''' damage to the front enemy unit.
Draw '''+1''' next turn.

flavor.value: Some trees drop acorns to seed new life - the Awoken shoot thorns. To protect myself, I wore thick leather armor on my first visit to the Wildwood. I can't say it helped much...

tables: '''Twinstone''' can allow you to hit twice and draw an additional card on the next turn, making '''Sting''' potentially draw-positive. However, there will almost always be a better target for this upgrade, and it is generally too valuable to use on a '''Sting'''.
'''Surgestone''' can allow '''Sting''' to deal more damage (though it is still rather unimpressive) while also removing it from your deck once played.
summary: Sting is an [[Awoken]] spell. It deals 12 damage to the front enemy unit, and draws 1 extra card on the next turn.

title: Vine Grasp

flavor.value: Vined Awoken have been known to lash out to control their enemies. While not an enemy, I too have been lashed and it is a less than pleasant experience.

tables: '''Powerstone''' and '''Surgestone''' can be considered if you aren't using this on your own units and just want to be able to kill more critical targets in later rings, or if you are using it on your own units to kill them but need a little more power to do that.

'''Keepstone''' can be considered if you need reliable access to this card, such as if you need it to kill [[:Category: Imp units|Imps]], [[:Category: Assistant units|Assistants]], and others that want to die, and have lots of card draw.

While this is mostly worse than [[Cursed Vines]], you won't always find [[Cursed Vines]], and it can be preferable to have this card with '''Keepstone''' in a card-draw rich environment, as [[Cursed Vines]] fails when you draw 10 cards and this doesn't. Plus, you can upgrade it with Magic Power too.
Reworded with the addition of the Advance keyword
Fixed [[Vine Grasp]] not targeting [[Dominion|Titan of Dominion]].
summary: Vine Grasp is an [[Awoken]] spell. It [[Advance]]s its target and does 3 damage to it.

title: Glimmer

effect.value: Restore '''3''' health to friendly units and deal '''3''' damage to enemy units.

flavor.value: If struck by a surge of electricity, a Sapwood will crystallize into glass. The sap within will become preserved as a supercharged healing solvent. But I can't seem to break the glass without losing much of this sap in the process.

tables: Due to '''Glimmer''' being a much weaker card lategame in ''Monster Train 2'', '''Surgestone''' is an apt upgrade for it, allowing it to dent a wave before removing itself on the redraw. Most notably, this will allow '''Glimmer''' to hit the threshold to kill [[Discordant Heretic]].

'''Powerstone''' is also a good upgrade for '''Glimmer''', particularly if you rely on it as part of a {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} line or you need to top up your units consistently over the course of a combat. A simple +10 lets '''Glimmer''' kill backliners up to Ring 6, including [[Profane Supplicant]] and [[Harpist Protector]].
'''Emberstone''' can be a no-frills way to improve your {{Ember}} economy, as you'll usually have a slot for it.

If you find the [[Entropy's Crystals]] event early, '''Glimmer''' can be a strong target for '''Entropic Growth''', allowing it to build up power over time and reach the numbers that it needs to crush lategame waves. Once powered enough, '''Keepstone''' can be a valid consideration, letting you wipe out a wave every turn while keeping your own units at full health. You may also opt to duplicate the card at [[Empyrean Well]]s instead.
Restore 2 health to friendly units and deal 2 damage to enemy units. >>> Restore 3 health to friendly units and deal 3 damage to enemy units.
summary: Glimmer is an [[Awoken]] spell. It deals 3 damage to enemies and restores {{Health|3}} to friendly units.

title: Razorsharp Edge

flavor.value: Dried out vines can deal more deadly blows, but they risk shattering more easily than their hydrated counterparts. My efforts at strengthening these embrittled appendages have proven fruitless.

tables: '''Twinstone''' lets you play this card twice per turn, assuming a sufficiently healthy target. An '''Emberstone''' complements this well by letting you do this for {{Ember|0}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.

Fixed exploit where cards that reduce a unit's Max Health could be used on the [[Ring 9|Titan fight]] to kill an individual [[Titan]] without the others being at {{Health|1}}. [[Razorsharp Edge]] {{Attack}} increased from '''10''' >>> '''12'''.
summary: Razorsharp Edge is an [[Awoken]] spell. It applies {{Attack|12}} to a unit, but also reduces their maximum {{Health}} by 2.

title: Restoration Detonation

effect.value: Restore '''15''' health to a friendly unit. Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to '''5x''' the amount healed.

flavor.value: Though usually avoided because of its potentially deadly outcome, an Awoken's ability to impale themselves with thorns allows them to become a walking nest of spores. Upon bursting, the spores provide additional life with the extra benefit of damage to those nearby.

tables: [[Restoration Detonation]]'s damage is essentially Attuned, dealing 50 extra damage for 10 extra Magic Power.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
Restore {{Health|10}} to a friendly unit. -> Restore {{Health|15}} to a friendly unit.
summary: Restoration Detonation is an [[Awoken]] spell. It heals its target for 15, then deals damage equal to 5x the amount of health the target actually gained - overhealing is not counted.

title: Wildwood Sap

flavor.value: When sap from Wildwood trees is consumed, it imparts the healing power of their reproductive spores. I also quite enjoy its floral sweetness.

tables: '''Twinstone''' doubles both the {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Regen}} applied. Since {{IconLink|Stackstone}} only doubles the {{IconLink|Regen}}, '''Twinstone''' is usually slightly preferable if you can afford it.
'''Emberstone''' makes '''Wildwood Sap''' free to play, and should also be a priority with '''Twinstone'''.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Wildwood Sap is an [[Awoken]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Regen|4}} and {{Health|+4}} to a unit.

title: Sharpen

flavor.value: I've found discarded Hollow armor serves as a perfect tool to sharpen dull weapons.

tables: '''Smolderstone''' eliminates this card's {{Ember}} cost, and its effect only needs to be applied once to be effective at killing backliners through the midgame.
'''Seekstone''' can also be used to ensure backliners are dying from the start of the fight while making the {{Ember}} cost more manageable.

Although there are often more important targets for '''Emberstone''', making '''Sharpen''' cheaper is always a positive effect. This is often better with [[Gnarled Root]] if you haven't found more efficient methods of {{Attack}} scaling.
'''Stackstone''' means this applies {{IconLink|Spikes|12}}, potentially allowing it to kill a wider range of lategame backliners.
summary: Sharpen is an [[Awoken]] spell. It increases the target's {{Attack}} by 6 and applies {{IconLink|Spikes|6}}.

title: Ensnare

flavor.value: The Wildwood of Hell encases those that linger too long underneath its draping canopy. These living trees scare me more than I care to admit.

tables: '''Keepstone''' allows you to play this card every turn. Unlike most Holdover spells, it does not cost a draw each turn, as the +1 draw will cancel it out. This can hold a given enemy in place for the entire battle, until they are killed by the boss.

'''Twinstone''' allows you to play this card twice, giving +2 draw on the next turn and holding two enemies in place, or holding a single enemy in place for two turns. This works extremely well with '''Keepstone''', giving the equivalent of a [[Limbo's Solace]] as long as you play it continually.
'''Freezestone''' lets you hold onto this card until you need it.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
Updated [[Ensnare]] to be able to target any unit.
summary: Ensnare is an [[Awoken]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Rooted}} to the target, holding them in place for a turn.

title: Pyre-Gro

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Draw '''-2''' next turn.
{{Ember|+1}} per turn for the rest of battle.

flavor.value: The Sentient once told me that the Wildwood was created when Pyre shards were scattered throughout the soil, fertilizing it with an otherworldly energy. Repeating that process now has a similar, though reduced, effect.

tables: '''Seekstone''' gives you this card on turn 1, making its benefits more consistently applicable starting with turn 2. It also potentially lets you plan around its downside, e.g. with [[Wyldenten]]'s '''Thornlord''' path's [[Sting]]s, or with another '''Seekstone''' applied to [[Invigorating Solution]].

'''Freezestone''' gives you more flexibility as to when you play this card, which is good, as you may not want to play it immediately because of its draw penalty. You could also put this on [[Preserved Thorns]] or [[Invigorating Solution]].
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Pyre-Gro is an [[Awoken]] spell. It gives you -2 draw next turn, but gives you {{Ember|+1}} for the rest of combat.

title: Engraft

flavor.value: When in a dangerous situation, the Awoken sometimes cannot afford the time it takes to regrow limbs. While less effective, they will splice together severed appendages in favor of speed, but in my experience the binding does not last long.

tables: '''Twinstone''' is great on '''Engraft''', as you'll just about always be able to afford the copy of this card. You'll double any synergistic interactions, and this card becomes draw-positive, cycling your deck faster than if it wasn't there.
'''Emberstone''' makes '''Engraft''' {{Ember}}-positive, which is great in a card draw heavy deck. This pairs excellently with '''Twinstone''', making this generate {{Ember|2}} per turn.
'''Powerstone''' can help make '''Engraft''' meaningfully heal your units, if you need that and don't need {{Ember}} (or have an [[Edge Prior]] on the floor you intend to use it on).
'''Keepstone''' redraws '''Engraft''' every turn, thus providing one additional card- and {{Ember}}-neutral {{IconLink|Incant}} and {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} trigger each turn.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Engraft is an [[Awoken]] spell. It restores {{Health|1}}, gives {{Ember|1}}, and allows you to draw 1 more next turn.

title: Invigorating Solution

flavor.value: After their first visit aboard my train, the Edge Priory concocted a solution of Wildwood sap and condensed train steam to coax more performance from the Boneshaker's engines.

tables: '''Seekstone''', in addition to discounting this to {{Ember|0}}, also gives you this card on turn 1 reliably, helping you see key cards sooner. It's particularly nice with [[Lost Luggage]], giving you a huge hand on turn 1 and 2. '''Emberstone''' can be fine too.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Invigorating Solution is an [[Awoken]] spell. It gives +3 draw next turn when played.

title: Preserved Thorns

flavor.value: Through my research, I've learned that Wildwood sap can extend the efficacy of thorns. This has led to my preservation of thorns in sap for later use.

tables: '''Emberstone''' makes it easier to play this card, and its upgrade slots aren't in too high of demand.
'''Seekstone''' can turn this card into a pseudo-[[Lost Luggage]] that triggers on turn 2, making your turn 2 hand large and ensuring you can cycle your deck quickly.

'''Twinstone''' can give you twice the [[Sting]]s, possibly adding up to a decent amount of damage with supporting Artifacts, and giving you lots of draw next turn. Just be careful not to flood your deck with too many [[Sting]]s!
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Preserved Thorns is an [[Awoken]] spell. It adds three [[Sting]] spells to your hand. These spells last for the rest of the combat, but are not permanently added.

title: Pyre Shards

flavor.value: To protect the Pyre should it ever feel threatened, I enhanced it to change its shape into something sharper that would damage the attacker. If broken off, these shards can be ingested by the Awoken to achieve the same effect.

tables: '''Seekstone''' is the most important upgrade if using this card as backline removal, ensuring you can put {{IconLink|Spikes}} on your tank immediately.

'''Stackstone''' and '''Twinstone''' accomplish the same goal of doubling the {{IconLink|Spikes}} applied by this card, and are interchangeable if you already have '''Seekstone'''. If not, '''Stackstone''' is preferable, costing only {{Ember|1}} instead of {{Ember|2}}. {{IconLink|Spikes|20}} is enough to kill [[Discordant Heretic]]s, but does not meaningfully change any other matchups, so this is best considered if you are fighting [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]].
summary: Pyre Shards is an [[Awoken]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Spikes|10}} to any unit.

title: Bramble Lash

effect.value: Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to '''10x''' {{IconLink|Spikes}} on friendly units.

flavor.value: A single, concentrated influx of Wildwood sap can enlarge the thorns of an Awoken for a short time. Through some ill-advised experiments, I've discovered that several simultaneous injections can have devastating effects.

tables: '''Emberstone''', '''Seekstone''', and '''Freezestone''' all make this card less expensive. '''Seekstone''' allows you to have it immediately without costing a draw, while '''Freezestone''' lets you wait for the right moment.

While a fairly rare take, '''Keepstone''' can be valid in combination with a cost-reduction upgrade from above if you need this card's ability to kill frontliners consistently. This is most likely to come up while using [[Thorned Hollow]], which can fairly easily build enough {{IconLink|Spikes}} to kill off all backliners, but struggles to take out tanks.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Bramble Lash is an [[Awoken]] spell. It deals damage to the front enemy equal to ten times the total {{IconLink|Spikes}} on all friendly units on the floor.

title: Focused Growth

flavor.value: I've observed from those of the Wildwood that with great concentration comes great healing. The Awoken can channel their will into sprouting spores on the surface of their form to heal broken parts of their vined bodies.

tables: '''Powerstone''' and '''Surgestone''' provide twice as much benefit as normal, as this spell's healing is divided into two hits.

If you have a strong {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} trigger, such as that of [[Oldgrowth]], it can be worth using '''Keepstone''' to play '''Focused Growth''' every turn. This will also provide consistent extra draw, unlike most Holdover cards, which decrease your net draw per turn.
'''Emberstone''' is a solid pick, saving you one {{Ember}} each time the card is played.
'''Seekstone''' provides the same discount as '''Emberstone''', while also letting you play this spell immediately and start drawing extra cards as soon as possible.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
[[Focused Growth]]. "Restore 25 health. Draw +2 next turn" >>> "Restore 20 health, twice. Draw +2 next turn."
summary: Focused Growth is an [[Awoken]] spell. It restores {{Health|20}} twice, and draws 2 extra cards on the next turn.

title: Restoring Retreat

flavor.value: After inhabiting the Boneshaker for some time, the Awoken vines have implanted themselves throughout the train. This allows them, and our enemies, to travel great distances in a short amount of time, recharging in the process.

tables: '''Seekstone''', in addition to discounting '''Restoring Retreat''' to {{Ember|0}}, also puts it in your hand on turn 1 reliably, letting you get your kill floor together faster.
'''Twinstone''' lets you play this card twice, if you have multiple units you need to Descend.

'''Keepstone''' is best if you need to consistently keep a boss away from your main floor throughout the fight, such as '''Bloody Harvest''' [[Stryx]], [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], or '''Furious Frenzy''' [[Arkion]]. It also lets you consistently disrupt enemy lines, or keep a single enemy trapped on the bottom floor for the entire fight.
[[Restoring Retreat]] cost increased from {{Ember|1}} >>> {{Ember|2}}. HP restored increased from 10 >>> 25.
[[Restoring Retreat]]'s Ember cost reduced back down from {{Ember|2}} >>> {{Ember|1}}. Healing reduced back down from 25 >>> 10.
summary: Restoring Retreat is an [[Awoken]] spell. It restores {{Health|10}} to a unit and moves it down to the floor below.

title: Awoken's Rail Spike

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Draw '''X''' and apply {{Ember|-1}} to those cards.
Cannot draw additional cards this turn.

flavor.value: Though reluctant at first to allow the Rail to come through the Wildwood, the Edge Priory eventually agreed with me to let it pass and uphold the Covenant with Seraph.

tables: '''Eternalstone''' is probably the most powerful upgrade available, letting you repeatedly use this card. As its discounts stack, the more you play this card, the better it gets, as more and more cards become playable when drawn with it, and more and more cards become {{Ember|0}}. Those in turn can be played before playing '''Awoken's Rail Spike''' on future turns, further increasing your effective ability to draw cards. It also allows you to put '''Smolderstone''' on it to increase its draw by 2, meaning you'll be cycling through your deck very quickly.

'''Emberstone''' can be a solid incremental improvement to this spell if you can't get the above combo together. That said, you may prefer to put it on other spells in your deck that cost {{Ember|2}} to make them play better with this. '''Awoken's Rail Spike''', like many X cost cards, is also a good candidate for '''Entropic Energy''' if you can find that. (That being said, beware the [[Entropic Crystals]] that come with that upgrade - if you draw Entropic Crystals with this card, you won't have any {{Ember}} to play it!)

'''Freezestone''' can be a solid improvement to this spell as you may want to wait until you have an otherwise unimpressive hand to play it, both to make your turns more consistent and to have a better chance at discounting cards you really care about.

But, like '''Emberstone''', it might be better placed on {{Ember|2+}} cost cards so that you don't miss out on them when you draw them with '''Awoken's Rail Spike'''.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
[[Awoken's Rail Spike]] updated to not allow additional card draw during the current turn after casting to prevent [[Infinites|infinites]].
Fixed [[Awoken's Rail Spike|Awoken's Railspike]] sometimes not applying cost bonus to drawn cards.
summary: Awoken's Rail Spike is an [[Awoken]] spell. It draws X cards and applies {{Ember|-1}} to each of them for the rest of combat, but prohibits you from drawing more cards this turn.

title: Channelsong

flavor.value: The Channelers of the Wildwood prefer to keep their involvement in its growth to a minimum. However, their intervention is sometimes required to achieve more "aggressive" expansion.

tables: '''Seekstone''' in addition to discounting this to {{Ember|0}} also gives you this card on turn 1 reliably. As most units really want to be on the field from the very start of the fight, this upgrade is highly desirable.
'''Twinstone''' gives you two of these for the price of one - especially nice if e.g. you duplicated a unit with the [[Mysterious Mirror]] event or have two non-banner units you'd like to retrieve.
'''Freezestone''' is very useful, guaranteeing that you can hold onto '''Channelsong''' until the next turn if you happen to draw it alongside the desired unit and need its buffs.

'''Eternalstone''' can be powerful if you're using this to scale an {{IconLink|Endless}} unit, if you also happen to have a way to kill it mid-turn. It can also be strong if you have a unit with {{IconLink|Fecundity}} or just a large pool of units to draw.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Channelsong is an [[Awoken]] spell. It draws a unit, reduces its cost to {{Ember|0}}, and applies {{Attack|+20}} and {{Health|+20}}.

title: Unleash the Wildwood

effect.value: Restore friendly units to full health.

flavor.value: The vines of the Wildwood stockpile harvested energy to use during unexpected droughts. When these stores are tapped into, the energy provides a surge of new life and power to the host.

tables: '''Seekstone''' can be useful if you need '''Unleash the Wildwood''' to immediately fill out the empty maximum {{Health}} gained by [[Awoken Hollow]], [[Thorned Hollow]], [[Steelsinger]], or units in an [[Awakening Thicket]]. It also makes the card free.
As above, '''Freezestone''' discounts the card to {{Ember|0}}, and ensures you will have it in your hand when your units will have taken enough damage that they need the full heal.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Unleash the Wildwood is an [[Awoken]] spell. It fully heals all friendly units on the floor.

title: Wildwood Tome

flavor.value: An ancient text of the Channelers of the Edge Priory, this tome outlines its creation. Sadly, the language is closely guarded by the Priory and I've had little luck in translating it.

tables: '''Seekstone''' can make your build more reliable if a speedy unit is a core part of your strategy and you leak enemies otherwise, especially if you have a large deck, and additionally discounts it by {{Ember|1}}.
'''Twinstone''' can be considered if you need multiple units to have {{IconLink|Quick}} - it is a self-synergistic mechanic. The more {{IconLink|Quick}} damage you have, the better it does.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Wildwood Tome is an [[Awoken]] spell. It gives the targeted unit {{IconLink|Quick}}.

title: Adaptive Mutation

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Restore a friendly unit to full health then swap {{Attack}} and {{Health}}.

flavor.value: After the soul within has succumbed to the will of the Wildwood, a Hollow is free to evolve into something more suitable for its eventual purpose, growing new vines or sloughing them off as necessary.

tables: '''Eternalstone''' can allow this spell to be played multiple times, and also allows you to take '''Smolderstone''', making it much cheaper to play. If a unit has large quantities of buffs that are increasing its {{Attack}}, this can be a massive increase in power to it each time it's applied, making spamming this card a powerful way to scale.

'''Seekstone''' synergizes specifically with '''Little Icarus''', ensuring you will draw this card immediately to beef up her {{Health}}. Without it, you may be forced to Reform her even if she has hundreds of {{Health}} left.

If you have the {{Ember}} to support it, '''Twinstone''' ensures you can immediately reap the benefits of casting '''Adaptive Mutation''' twice on a unit with {{IconLink|Rage}}, {{IconLink|Valor}}, or {{IconLink|Mageblade}}, increasing their {{Attack}} tremendously.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Adaptive Mutation is an [[Awoken]] spell. It fully heals a friendly unit, then sets its maximum {{Health}} equal to its current {{Attack}} and its base {{Attack}} equal to its {{Health}}.

title: Spreading Spores

effect.value: Restore '''3''' health. Apply {{IconLink|Regen|3}} and {{IconLink|Spikes|3}}. Add a copy of this card to your discard pile.

flavor.value: When thorns find their mark, they release spores into the air to incapacitate unsuspecting victims. These poor souls soon transform into Awoken and feed the vines that first spread the spores. On the embarrassingly frequent occasions that I'm stung by these thorns, I remove them before any real damage occurs.

tables: '''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Regen}} and {{IconLink|Spikes}} applied, making it much easier to build up an impenetrable defense for the boss.
'''Emberstone''', '''Seekstone''', and '''Freezestone''' all make '''Spreading Spores''' free, making it much easier to spam.
If you need immediate healing more than {{IconLink|Spikes}} or {{IconLink|Regen}}, '''Powerstone''' makes it restore a respectable {{Health|13}} per cast.
[[Spreading Spores]]. {{IconLink|Regen|2}} and {{IconLink|Spikes|2}} >>> {{IconLink|Regen|3}} and {{IconLink|Spikes|3}}. Now also restores 3 health
summary: Spreading Spores is an [[Awoken]] spell. It heals 3 health, applies {{IconLink|Regen|3}} and {{IconLink|Spikes|3}}, and creates a copy of itself each time it is played. The copies are identical, and will also create copies, but are not permanently added to the deck and will be removed at the end of the battle.

title: Cycle of Life

flavor.value: When a soul is trapped by vines, the Wildwood gives it new life. And when the soul is released after the vines wilt away, that life is returned to the Wildwood and the others trapped within it.

tables: The biggest problem with this card is how expensive it is. '''Smolderstone''' and '''Emberstone''' both make it much cheaper, and the '''[[Consume]]''' applied by '''Smolderstone''' is generally not an issue since this card isn't really worth casting multiple times.

'''Entropic Energy''' makes this card free. However, you will almost always have a spell in your deck that can benefit more from either this upgrade or one of the others offered through [[Entropy's Crystals]].
summary: Cycle of Life is an [[Awoken]] spell. It increases the target's {{Health}} by 10 and applies {{IconLink|Spikes|8}}.

title: Oldgrowth

flavor.value: Where the Hollow leave behind their husks, there are vines that refuse to die. They grow and grow, forestalling their inevitable decay. The Channelers say this is because "She" still lives. Few know what they could mean and even fewer find comfort in their words.

summary: Oldgrowth is a rare [[Awoken]] equipment added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It grants a unit 10 max {{Health}} immediately and an additional 10 max {{Health}} on {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}}.

title: Awakening Thicket
