effect.value: Friendly units have '''+20''' max health and restore '''10''' health on {{IconLink|Resolve}}.

flavor.value: A soul, once put to sleep by spores, is trapped by the vines of the Wildwood only to become Awoken. It's not a very pleasant event to witness, but there is a certain beauty in it all.

tables: [[Awake|Awaken]] updated from Spell >>> Room. "Awaken" >>> "[[Awakening Thicket]]". "Restore 40 health. Apply {{IconLink|Regen|3}}." >>> "Friendly units have +20 Max Health and restore 10 health on {{IconLink|Resolve}}."
Fixed [[Awakening Thicket]], [[Engine Upgrade]], and [[Crucible Extension]] being missing from certain card pools.
summary: Awakening Thicket is an uncommon [[Awoken]] room added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update, replacing [[Awake]]. It grants friendly units +20 max health and restores 10 health on {{IconLink|Resolve}}.

title: Stygian Guard

flavor.value: ''The ancient Guard of the Stygian Sea emerges once more. Mystical Sirens and ancient Totems work together to eliminate the hostile Titans from Heaven.''

summary: Stygian Guard [[File:ClanStygian.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]], returning from [[Monster Train 1]]. It is unlocked after unlocking [[Hellhorned]] first and then casting 5 spells in a turn.

title: Tethys Titansbane

flavor.value: Do not be fooled by her harmless demeanor. Tethys was the first to agree to the containment of the Titan for our Covenant's sake. She has since become the most revered member of the Stygian Guard and my most helpful supporter in the defense of Hell.

tables: Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' with significant buffs to her champion paths.
Handheld Totem Tethys atk increased from 5/10/20 >>> 10/20/30.
Handheld Totem [[Tethys]] new ability "Runespeak: Draw a damage spell and apply '''+5/10/20 [[Magic Power]]'''." Cooldown 3.
Excluded cards that can't have their damage upgraded in shop (ones that damage the pyre) from [[Tethys]]'s Runespeak ability, and [[Gifts for a Guard]] spell.
summary: Tethys Titansbane is the primary [[Champion]] of the [[Stygian Guard]]. She is a glass cannon-type character with low health, but the ability to put out large amounts of damage, power up your spells, and even reduce their {{Ember}} cost. Her starter card is [[Frozen Lance]].

title: Solgard the Martyr

flavor.value: For the first time, I've spoken with these dream beings! Solgard, the priest of the Stygian's Titan, spoke of a mass Exodus of martyrs. Martyrs who gave up their souls for the sake of Heaven and Hell. But why does no one living know of this great sacrifice? These answers only create more questions...

tables: Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' with significant buffs to his champion paths.
Solgard Direchannel III damage increased from 4/8/12 >>> 4/8/16.

Titanchannel [[Solgard]] updated to be an ability. Stats reduced from {{AttackHealth|60/60}}, {{AttackHealth|120/20}}, {{AttackHealth|250/250}} >>> {{AttackHealth|0/5}}. "{{IconLink|Incant}}: Gain {{IconLink|Shard|1}}. At 4 {{IconLink|Shard}} stacks, remove {{IconLink|Stasis}}." >>> "{{IconLink|Incant}}: Gain {{IconLink|Shard|1}}. {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}: Resurgence. (Remove {{IconLink|Stasis}} and gain {{AttackHealth|+6/10/15}} per {{IconLink|Shard}}.)".
Titanchannel [[Solgard]] tier I & II stat gain from Resurgence increased from {{AttackHealth|6/6}}, {{AttackHealth|10/10}} >>> {{AttackHealth|8/8}}, {{AttackHealth|12/12}}.
summary: Solgard the Martyr is a [[Champion]] from the [[Stygian Guard]]. All of his paths revolve around {{IconLink|Shard}}, a unique status effect which increases with each spell played on his floor. These have different effects depending on which paths are chosen. His starter card is [[Forgone Power]].

title: Frozen Lance

effect.value: Deal '''10''' damage to the front enemy unit.

flavor.value: An ancient relic of a time before the Covenant. When I first came to the Stygian Sea, every resident of the Ring carried one to aid in their defense of the reigning Titan. There still lies some magic within the surrounding ice.

tables: '''Surgestone''' has a dual purpose on '''Frozen Lance''', making it able to make a bigger dent in a frontline unit, and as a soft Purge.
summary: Frozen Lance is [[Tethys]]' starter card. It hits the front enemy unit for 10 damage.

title: Forgone Power

effect.value:
Apply {{IconLink|Frostbite|8}} to the front enemy unit.
Discard a card at random.

flavor.value: The Martyr speaks of the power a name has over the soul, that the Titan released its name for the good of Heaven, Hell, and Humans. Perhaps the same practice observed by the Stygian Guard is an evolution of this and grants them some minimal power as well.

tables: '''Smolderstone''' is the only upgrade worth using on '''Forgone Power'''. It does not make it any stronger or cheaper to play, but it does mean that you can remove it from your deck after playing it once. Given how weak '''Forgone Power''' is, it is generally worth spending a bit of {{Gold}} to get rid of it, and this upgrade is much cheaper than an actual removal.
summary: Forgone Power is [[Solgard the Martyr]]'s starter card. It applies {{IconLink|Frostbite|8}} to the front enemy unit and discards a card at random.

title: Cuttlehex

ability.value: {{AbilityBox|Freeze Ray|2|Apply [[Frozen]] to a card in hand.}}

flavor.value: Together with the Cold Sirens, these Stygian were among the first to embrace the freeze, becoming crucial in the Ring's survival post-Armageddon and our mounting resistance.

tables: '''Heartstone''' can help keep '''Cuttlehex''' alive against backline damage.

'''Immortalstone''' lets you use '''Cuttlehex''' as a decent chump blocker thanks to its {{Capacity|1}} and {{Ember|0}}. It also lets you immediately reuse '''Freeze Ray''' when it dies and gets replayed.

[[Cuttlehex]] updated from: "{{IconLink|End of Turn|png=EndOfTurn}}: Apply [[Frozen]] to a random card in hand" >>> "{{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}: Freeze Ray: Apply [[Frozen]] to a card in hand. Cooldown 2."
summary: Cuttlehex is a common [[Stygian Guard]] unit. Its {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, Freeze Ray, applies [[Frozen]] to a card of your choice in your hand, similar to [[Preserve]].

title: Molluscmage

flavor.value: These dark mages have made themselves known through their control of the power that radiates from the Titan. Though small in nature, these mages have a striking resemblance to the Titan itself, which has resulted in the spread of many unproven theories of their origin.

tables: '''Dualstone''' gives '''Molluscmage''' {{IconLink|Conduit|20}}. Make sure when considering this upgrade that you don't have another unit that could use it better, and that you wouldn't be better off saving your {{Gold}}.
'''Heartstone''' helps '''Molluscmage''' stay alive against enemies like [[Penitent Prayerstone]]s and [[Ragewing Assassin]]s.
Wording change with the addition of Conduit Keyword.
summary: Molluscmage is a common [[Stygian Guard]] unit. It has {{IconLink|Conduit|10}}, strengthening spells on its floor.

title: Glacial Seal

flavor.value: Enchanted granite pegs were used in the sealing of the Titan's tomb. When the Sea froze, ice formed around each bolt, prying it loose to drift through the open water.

tables: '''Dualstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Frostbite}} applied, making '''Glacial Seal''' twice as effective as usual.
'''Heartstone''' can keep it alive, as can '''Runestone''', especially because you will want to trigger {{IconLink|Incant}} frequently anyway.
summary: Glacial Seal is an uncommon [[Stygian Guard]] unit. Whenever a spell is played on its floor, it applies {{IconLink|Frostbite|2}} to all enemies on the floor.

title: Guardian Stone

flavor.value: I've been told these stones predate even the Guard. They have been etched by its various members, marking the only true record of each Stygian who has been inducted.

tables: '''Dualstone''' increases its {{IconLink|Armor}} application to 2 per {{IconLink|Incant}}, improving its ability to fortify its floor. With [[Founding Seal]], this can be increased to 4 per {{IconLink|Incant}}, allowing it to provide solid protection to your frontliner too. It doesn't matter as much if you have [[Railhammer]] as it only increases {{IconLink|Armor}} per {{IconLink|Incant}} from 5 to 6.

'''Heartstone''' can keep '''Guardian Stone''' alive. That being said, its own {{IconLink|Incant}} trigger protects itself too. If this is necessary, there's a good chance it isn't actually protecting what it needs to be.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Guardian Stone is a uncommon [[Stygian Guard]] unit. It has an {{IconLink|Incant}} ability that applies {{IconLink|Armor|1}} to all friendly units on the floor.

title: Coldcaelia

flavor.value: These Sirens have used the freezing of Hell to their advantage, enchanting their blades with ice to damage their enemies more deeply. They lack formal training in classical combat, but make up for it in their magical prowess.

tables: '''Speedstone''' is one of the most critical upgrades for any unit with {{IconLink|Sweep}}. A {{IconLink|Quick}} sweeper will kill all enemies on the floor with lower {{Health}} than the attacker's {{Attack}} before they can retaliate, ensuring that dangerous backline enemies will never get to attack. This will keep '''Coldcaelia''' and your other units healthy throughout a combat, and allow her to continue eliminating enemy waves.

'''Largestone''' is a strong upgrade if '''Coldcaelia''' will be placed alone on a lower floor, further increasing her survivability while increasing her {{Attack}} threshold to be able to comfortably clear many lategame backliners.

'''Frenzystone''' is a strong consideration for any unit with {{IconLink|Sweep}}. If you have ways of scaling {{Attack}} quickly, giving {{IconLink|Multistrike}} to a sweeper is one of the most damage-efficient upgrades you can make. '''Frenzystone''' is especially good on '''Coldcaelia''' as she will apply her {{IconLink|Frostbite}} {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger multiple times, inflicting heavy damage over time to sturdier enemies that cannot normally be killed with two swings. This upgrade is preferred if '''Coldcaelia''' will be part of your main floor as a recipient of powerful buffs, or if you have a dedicated tank downstairs to protect her and do not want her {{Capacity}} to increase.

'''Heartstone''' and '''Runestone''' serve similar purposes, giving '''Coldcaelia''' extra survivability in a pinch. '''Runestone''' offers scaling defense and is better with other {{IconLink|Incant}} units, while '''Heartstone''' provides a simple frontloaded boost to health.

'''Dualstone''' is a viable upgrade for '''Coldcaelia''', doubling her {{IconLink|Frostbite}} application. However, the other major upgrades are usually preferred for consistency and sustainability, and it is generally better to find ways to buff her {{Attack}} directly while reaping those upgrades' benefits instead.
{{AttackHealth|1|15}} -> {{AttackHealth|3|15}}, '''Strike''': Apply '''Frostbite 3''' to the attacked unit. -> '''Strike''': Apply '''Frostbite 6''' to the attacked unit.
summary: Coldcaelia is an uncommon [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. She possesses {{IconLink|Sweep}} as well as a {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger that applies {{IconLink|Frostbite|6}} to enemies on hit.

title: Guard of the Unnamed

flavor.value: Original captors and protectors of the titan, these Sirens have existed almost since the creation of the sea itself. They were the first to follow Tethys in recognizing the importance of the Titan's survival and that its imprisonment would be the only way to ensure it.

tables: '''Dualstone''' can double the amount of {{IconLink|Armor}} per {{IconLink|Incant}}. The ability to take this upgrade is generally the only reason you might want to choose this unit over Siren of the Sea.
'''Runestone''' increases your {{IconLink|Armor}} gain from 3 to 5, and with '''Dualstone''' from 6 to 10.
'''Titanstone''' grants {{IconLink|Titanite}}, doubling the effect of {{IconLink|Armor}}, and is generally strong on tanks.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Guard of the Unnamed is an uncommon [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever a spell is played on his floor, he gains {{IconLink|Armor|3}}.

title: Icy Cilophyte

flavor.value: Even further communion with the ice has allowed these Sirens to master its freezing nature. This leads me to believe that the Stygian may be the only clan that has benefited from the Freeze.

tables: '''Speedstone''' is one of the most critical upgrades for any unit with {{IconLink|Sweep}}. A {{IconLink|Quick}} sweeper will kill all enemies on the floor with lower {{Health}} than the attacker's {{Attack}} before they can retaliate, ensuring that dangerous backline enemies will never get to attack. This will keep '''Icy Cilophyte''' and your other units healthy throughout a combat, and allow her to continue eliminating enemy waves.

'''Largestone''' is a strong upgrade if '''Icy Cilophyte''' will be placed alone on a lower floor, further increasing her survivability while increasing her {{Attack}} threshold to be able to comfortably clear many lategame backliners.

'''Frenzystone''' is a strong consideration for any unit with {{IconLink|Sweep}}. If you have ways of scaling {{Attack}} quickly, giving {{IconLink|Multistrike}} to a sweeper is one of the most damage-efficient upgrades you can make. '''Frenzystone''' is solid on '''Icy Cilophyte''' as she will apply her {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger multiple times; in decks with powerful damage spells, this can significantly alleviate the pressure of double-heavy waves by allowing you to easily kill one (or both) of them before they can cause trouble for higher floors. This upgrade is preferred if '''Icy Cilophyte''' will be part of your main floor as a recipient of powerful buffs, or if you have a dedicated tank downstairs to protect her and do not want her {{Capacity}} to increase.

'''Dualstone''' is a viable upgrade for '''Icy Cilophyte''', doubling her {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} application and helping you take out high-{{Health}} tanks on future turns even more easily; this can stack multiplicatively with a '''Frenzystone''' for {{IconLink|Spell Weakness|4}} every attack.

'''Heartstone''' and '''Runestone''' serve similar purposes, giving '''Icy Cilophyte''' extra survivability in a pinch. '''Runestone''' offers scaling defense and is better with other {{IconLink|Incant}} units, while '''Heartstone''' provides a simple frontloaded boost to health.
summary: Icy Cilophyte is an uncommon [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. She possesses {{IconLink|Sweep}} as well as a {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger that applies {{IconLink|Spell Weakness|1}} to enemies on hit.

title: Nameless Siren

flavor.value: Those that enter the resting place of the Titan rarely emerge. But those that do are permanently imbued with some of its power, relinquishing their names as part of this new communion. While I've tried to wring an account from them on their time with the Titan, their minds seem to have expelled any contact with this Unnamed power.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' is a good choice on any high-damage unit, doubling [[Nameless Siren]]'s output.
'''Dualstone''' allows her to gain {{IconLink|Rage|6}} on {{IconLink|Incant}}, greatly improving her scaling.
'''Speedstone''' can sometimes make up for her low {{Health}}, killing enemies before they have a chance to hit back.
'''Smidgestone''' allows you to fit more copies of '''Nameless Siren''' or other {{IconLink|Incant}} allies on the floor.

'''Runestone''' grants {{IconLink|Armor|2}} on {{IconLink|Incant}}, making up for her low {{Health}} and letting her function more like Siren of the Sea, possessing both damage output and durability. It is also a cheap upgrade if you are looking to fill out her slots.
summary: The Nameless Siren is an uncommon [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. She gains {{IconLink|Rage|3}} whenever a spell is played on her floor.

title: Siren of the Sea

flavor.value: While most of the Stygian Guard is magic focused, these Sirens form a melee contingent of the clan. I've still helped them enchant their blades to reap the benefits of the Titan's power.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' is a good choice on any high-damage unit, doubling [[Siren of the Sea]]'s offensive output. As you'll often want to copy her, this is often the upgrade of choice, as the copies benefit from it too. (In contrast, defensive upgrades are less helpful on any unit that you'll want to stack multiple copies of on a floor.)
'''Titanstone''' doubles the power of your defense instead, which can also be valuable, though it isn't as desirable for duplication purposes.
'''Smidgestone''' allows you to fit more copies of '''Siren of the Sea''' or other {{IconLink|Incant}} allies on the floor.

'''Immortalstone''' is a solid safety net if you fear that '''Siren of the Sea''' will be overwhelmed eventually by damage. It's especially good against the [[Titans]] or [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], where being able to let her die and replay her to cleanse {{IconLink|Corruption}} is highly valuable. It's a better choice if you have units like [[Nameless Siren]] who can handle offense for you, and '''Siren of the Sea''' is primarily a tank that helps keep them alive.

'''Runestone''' is a solid, cheap upgrade that gives '''Siren of the Sea''' more durability per {{IconLink|Incant}}, and is especially useful in the early game for survivability, or if you want to fill out her slots in anticipation of [[Celestial Alcove]] events.

'''Heartstone''' or even '''Largestone''' can sometimes be useful to help shore up [[Siren of the Sea]]'s initial survivability, which can be an issue if using her as a frontline tank, especially in later rings. It's preferable to set up on higher floors to avoid needing this.
summary: Siren of the Sea is an uncommon [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. She gains {{AttackHealth|3/3}} on {{IconLink|Incant}}.

title: Titan Sentry

flavor.value: Stationed all across the Sea floor, generations of these Guardians have been tasked with the protection of the Unnamed Titan. Their role was entirely ceremonial until now.

tables: '''Dualstone''' grants {{IconLink|Dualism}}, applying twice as much {{IconLink|Frostbite}} to all enemies.

'''Titanstone''' grants {{IconLink|Titanite}}, halving the damage taken from all sources. This can keep the '''Titan Sentry''' alive for much longer, especially if your allied clan has ways to protect it like {{IconLink|Valor}} or {{IconLink|Reanimate}}.

'''Largestone''' bolsters '''Titan Sentry''' with a considerable amount of {{Health}} and a bit of {{Attack}}, increasing his survivability. The increased {{Capacity}} is often not an issue, as he will often hold down a floor on his own.

'''Immortalstone''' allows you to simply replay the unit if he is killed, making other defensive upgrades unnecessary. As long as you can deal with losing {{Ember|1}} and 1 card draw each turn, you can simply throw it into the thick of battle against bosses like [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]] and allow it to die every turn. Due to the limited in-clan defensive options, even a '''Titan Sentry''' with '''Titanite''' and '''Largestone''' will generally not last long in the late game, making '''Immortalstone''' more valuable.

'''Runestone''' is a cheap upgrade which provides a solid source of defense as long as you can continually play spells on the same floor as the unit. This generally means that you want to have your other {{IconLink|Incant}} units on the same floor. However, this may not be a good idea, as it prevents him from killing units like the [[Ragewing Assassin]] before they can target your vulnerable backliners. If you can deal with that downside, or if your other units are not {{IconLink|Incant}}-based, this is a very solid way to keep '''Titan Sentry''' alive and even build up his defenses to deal with the boss.
summary: Titan Sentry is an uncommon [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. He applies {{IconLink|Frostbite|3}} to all enemies on the floor each time he takes damage.

title: Eel Gorgon

flavor.value: The Titan's name has been lost to time, the Titan now trapped and harmless. But the name's power has lingered within the Sea and seeped into the life of all those around it.  Creatures that once listened only to the needs of their survival have now become intelligent guardians of the Ring. The Power of the Name has not faded, only found new owners. It is a cycle unlike I've seen elsewhere.

tables: '''Largestone''' is the biggest statistical boost '''Eel Gorgon''' can receive in a single upgrade, greatly improving its potential.

'''Smidgestone''' completely offsets the downsides of '''Largestone''' and allows '''Eel Gorgon''' to be played on a floor alongside other {{IconLink|Incant}} units. These are the only major upgrades '''Eel Gorgon''' can receive, and it uses both well.
'''Strengthstone''' and '''Heartstone''' are cheap, readily-available upgrades that improve [[Eel Gorgon]]'s potential and are solid choices to fill out any empty upgrade slots.

'''Dominating Power''' and '''Dominating Control''' both give '''Eel Gorgon''' a {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger, which can be exploited as it can easily attack five or six times a round. The {{IconLink|Corruption}} applied by '''Dominating Power''' can make short work of bosses, while if you can get its {{Attack}} high enough, the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} offered by '''Dominating Control''' can let it shred through enemy waves.

'''Frailty Penance''' and '''Frailty Absolution''' allow '''Eel Gorgon''' to permanently scale its {{Attack}} on {{IconLink|Celebrate}}, offering up to {{Attack|+50}} by Ring 8. Additionally, while '''Frailty Absolution''' is certainly worth taking once offered, '''Eel Gorgon''' will naturally clear the {{IconLink|Fragile}} status upon {{IconLink|Resolve}}, making it far less risky to take this upgrade.
summary: Eel Gorgon is a rare [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. It gains {{IconLink|Multistrike}} after each {{IconLink|Incant}}, but loses all [[Buffs]], [[Debuffs]], and yellow [[Effects]] - including {{IconLink|Multistrike}} - at the end of the turn.

title: Lodestone Totem

flavor.value: Of the totems that the founding Guardian built, the Lodestones are possibly the most important. They provide energy for the Stygian Guard by siphoning power from those around them using some ancient technology that's eluded my understanding.

tables: '''Dualstone''' is the only really desirable upgrade for '''Lodestone Totem''', but it is an '''extremely''' desirable upgrade. With {{IconLink|Dualism}}, '''Lodestone Totem''' can easily {{IconLink|Sap}} entire waves to {{Attack|0}}.

'''Runestone''' is a cheap upgrade that provides '''Lodestone Totem''' with protection against {{IconLink|Corruption}} effects like [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]]. It can also let the unit serve as your tank during {{IconLink|Relentless}}, where you may not have as much time to apply {{IconLink|Sap}} to the boss.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Lodestone Totem is a rare [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever a spell is played on its floor, it will apply {{IconLink|Sap|1}} to all enemies on the same floor.

title: Offering Monument

flavor.value: I created monuments as signposts for the offering sites across the seafloor. But my shoddy work has made them vulnerable to the energy from the Unnamed below, destabilizing them entirely.

tables: '''Offering Monument''' really doesn't need much in terms of upgrades. '''Heartstone''' and '''Runestone''' both provide it with a safety net against effects like {{IconLink|Sweep}} to prevent it from dying. '''Strengthstone''' can be considered if you are very early on and don't like your chances against early bosses, letting it pitch in during {{IconLink|Relentless}}, but generally requires one of the other upgrades alongside it to protect it from {{IconLink|Spikes}}.
Incant: Draw 1 and this unit gets {{Health|-5}}. -> Incant: {{Health|-5}}. Draw 1
Updated [[Offering Monument]]: "{{IconLink|Incant}}: -5 Max HP. Draw 1." >>> "{{IconLink|Incant}}: Draw +1 next turn." {{Health}} reduced from '''40''' >>> '''1'''.
Fixed text on card [[Offering Monument]] shrinking too much.
summary: Offering Monument is a rare [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. It causes you to draw an additional card next turn on {{IconLink|Incant}}.

title: Energy Siphon

flavor.value: Lodestones require direct operation to absorb the energy gained from any living beings around them. Through mechanisms I've not been able to understand, the energy retrieved is many times the source's power.

tables: '''Twinstone''' makes this card mildly more useful, applying twice as much {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} and triggering {{IconLink|Incant}} again for free due to costing {{Ember|0}}. However, there will usually be better cards in your deck to put this upgrade on, such as [[Offering Token]]. '''Stackstone''' does not trigger {{IconLink|Incant}}, but still applies twice as much {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
Updated [[Energy Siphon]] to be able to target any unit.
summary: Energy Siphon is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Spell Weakness|1}} to a single unit.

title: Offering Token

flavor.value: Making offerings to the Unnamed Titan has become a religious experience among the Stygian Guard. These offerings are made with such frequency that I helped to create tokens to represent a Guard's offering to the Titan and simplify the process.

tables: '''Twinstone''' is likely the most important upgrade one can put on '''Offering Token'''. This makes the card draw-positive, letting you cycle your deck faster, and grants two {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers and two targeted discards per turn. At high Covenant and especially during fights like [[Clash with the Titans]], discarding two cards of your choice every turn is almost always a positive, either eliminating irritating [[Scourge]]s or playing powerful [[Offering]] cards like [[Guardian's Amulet]].
'''Keepstone''' is draw-neutral, but gives one free {{IconLink|Incant}} and one free discard per turn. It is especially potent with '''Twinstone''', increasing your draw every turn.
If you have the [[Emot Tome]] artifact or [[Lightstone Casing]], '''Seekstone''' is a good consideration in combination with the two prior upgrades to guarantee that you see this card immediately.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
'Offering Token' (Draw 1, Discard 1) updated so that any Ephemeral Offering Token copy in hand is ineligible for the discard requirement, not just ones made via Spellchain upgrades.
Fixed an undo failure related to [[Offering Token]]. Fixed undo of [[Echo Vault]] with [[Offering Token]] showing choice at start of turn.
summary: Offering Token is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It allows the player to draw a card, then discard a card.

title: Flash Freeze

flavor.value: After the freezing of Hell, the Stygian Sea's weather became much more erratic. Instant freezes are now frequent occurrences, much to the dismay of anyone unlucky enough to be caught in their icy grasp.

tables: '''Powerstone''' lets this card kill a few more enemies immediately in the late game, like [[Deafening Herald]]s and [[Harpist Protector]]s, and it will remove two stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} from [[Deformed Duo]]s. The {{IconLink|Frostbite}} also lets it kill [[Discordant Heretic]]s at the end of the turn.
'''Emberstone''' is a cheap way to give yourself more {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers and stretch your {{Ember}} per turn further.

'''Surgestone''' and '''Smolderstone''' accomplish the same effects as the other two upgrades, respectively, but also grant '''[[Consume]]''', removing this card from your deck after play if it has outlived its utility.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Flash Freeze is a common [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It deals 3 damage and applies {{IconLink|Frostbite|8}}.

title: Titan's Gratitude

effect.value:
'''[[Attuned]]'''.
Deal '''60''' damage to the front enemy unit. Discard a card at random.

flavor.value: From what Tethys has told me, the Unnamed below is not dead, but it is also not quite alive. The Stygian take responsibility for its well-being by providing sustenance, in return for occasional protection in the form of expelled energy.

tables: '''Surgestone''' increases this spell's damage by 100 while also removing it from your deck after one play.
'''Smolderstone''' removes this card from your deck while also reducing its cost. '''Emberstone''' can provide the same cost reduction, if you don't want it to [[Consume]].
summary: Titan's Gratitude is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It deals 60 damage to the front enemy unit and has [[Attuned]], but discards a random card when played.

title: Helical Crystalis

effect.value: Deal '''35''' damage to the front enemy unit, twice.

flavor.value: Physical combat has never been a strong suit of the Stygian Guard. Thankfully, their control of the energy coming from the Unnamed has made them deadly protectors of the inner Rings of Hell.

tables: '''Surgestone''' has a dual purpose on '''Helical Crystalis''', allowing it to deal a respectable {{Health|110}}, which is enough to severely dent if not kill frontliners through Ring 6, while also soft-purging it from your deck for later rings.

'''Smolderstone''' also has a dual purpose, making '''Helical Crystalis''' spammable for {{IconLink|Incant}} purposes while also soft-purging it from your deck for later rings. This works nicely with a deck rich in card draw. You will have to choose between this and '''Surgestone''' generally.
'''Emberstone''' pairs nicely with '''Surgestone''', or as a standalone upgrade, for a no-frills way to improve your {{Ember}} economy.
summary: Helical Crystalis is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It hits the front enemy twice, dealing 35 damage each time.

title: Crypt Builder

effect.value:
'''[[Offering]]'''. '''[[Attuned]]'''.
'''[[Retreat]]''' the front enemy unit and deal '''80''' damage.

flavor.value: Massive hammers were used to seal the Titan in its crypt. Requiring the strength of multiple Guards to swing true, these tools have not been moved since their last use.

tables: '''Powerstone''' is a cheap upgrade that offers a large damage boost, giving '''Crypt Builder''' enough damage to kill a [[Blightbound Guardian]].
As an expensive card that can often be played for free, '''Holystone''' is worth consideration as a way to keep your Pyre healthy if you can consistently discard this card.
Deal 60 damage -> Deal 80 damage, Rewording with addition of the Retreat keyword.
summary: Crypt Builder is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It deals 80 damage to the front unit and pushes them to the back. If discarded, it is instantly played for free.

title: Crystalline Seeds

flavor.value: I've been able to capture shards of ice from the now-frozen sea and distill them into seed crystals, making the instantaneous freezing of objects even easier.

tables: '''Twinstone''' doubles the amount of {{IconLink|Frostbite}} applied, and allows you to trigger {{IconLink|Incant}} twice for {{Ember|0}}. However, you will usually have better cards to give this upgrade instead.
Apply Frostbite 6 to enemy units. -> Apply Frostbite 8 to enemy units.
summary: Crystalline Seeds is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Frostbite|8}} to enemy units.

title: Preserve

effect.value:
'''[[Permafrost]]'''.
Apply '''[[Frozen]]''' to a card in your hand.

flavor.value: Many precious artifacts of Hell were frozen when the Pyre was destroyed. Thankfully, this did not diminish their power, but only rendered their energy dormant until I am able to release them from their icy prison.

tables: '''Twinstone''' allows you to freeze two cards and gain two {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers. However, it may be more useful on another, more impactful spell.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Preserve is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It lets you choose a card in hand and apply [[Frozen]], which makes it remain in hand between turns until it is played. Preserve itself starts with [[Permafrost]], so it will be Frozen when drawn.

title: Unnamed Tome

flavor.value: When the Titan was finally put to rest, the Stygian Guard was formed. Tethys and I wrote this tome to record the existence of the Unnamed Titan and prophesize its return.

tables: For all but the fastest of decks, you'll want more {{IconLink|Mute}} to deal with flying bosses. '''Twinstone''' allows you to choose between applying {{IconLink|Mute|6}} on a single floor or {{IconLink|Mute|3}} on two different floors.

'''Stackstone''' also doubles the {{IconLink|Mute}} output of this card, albeit slightly less flexibly. With '''Twinstone''', it can shut down [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] or the [[Titans]] for the whole fight.

'''Seekstone''' can be considered to be able to reliably apply {{IconLink|Mute}} on turn 1, perhaps for very fragile builds facing [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], for example. It also means this card will never cost any draw, even if you don't cast it on the first turn, thanks to its Permafrost. This effectively makes your deck thinner.

'''Eternalstone''' can be considered in smaller decks if you need it to also {{IconLink|Mute}} enemy waves, e.g. for a top row setup against a fight with [[Terrifying Amalgam]]s. '''Keepstone''' can also be worth considering in this case.
Gave Silence before Mute keyword existed.
summary: Unnamed Tome is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It has [[Permafrost]] and applies {{IconLink|Mute|3}} to enemy units.

title: Urchin Spines

flavor.value: Electrified urchins swarm around the openings of the Titan's seafloor resting place. Their spines shock any predators, providing a natural defense in the dangerous depths of the sea. Unbeknownst to Tethys, I collected some of these specimens for my studies.

tables: In decks where this is strong, you'll generally want to play this often, making '''Eternalstone''' a worthy investment if you can get your deck small enough for it to matter. Or, if shops allow, you could also apply '''Keepstone''' to make a per-turn strategy out of it if you have a good payoff for doing so.

'''Twinstone''' and '''Stackstone''' both double the amount of {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} on this card. One could even apply both upgrades to inflict up to 8 stacks of {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} on an entire floor.
'''Entropic Stone''' is just a better '''Stackstone''', so if you find this event and do not have a better target for the '''Triplestack''' then consider adding it to this card.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Urchin Spines is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Spell Weakness|2}} to enemy units.

title: Drain

flavor.value: While the Guard claims that the Titan still sleeps, it seems to show a base level awareness when it is near another soul, helping its kin and hurting everyone else. I've yet to be subjected to either, so I can't say which I am considered.

tables: As this card has good self-synergy, '''Twinstone''' works well on it, and it won't discard its own copy. If you have cards with [[Offering]], this can make '''Drain''' trigger Offering on them more reliably.
'''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Sap}} applied too. The more {{IconLink|Sap}} you apply, the better it gets.
'''Keepstone''' makes your {{IconLink|Sap}} generation more consistent, improving its defensive utility.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
Fixed an undo failure related to [[Drain]].
summary: Drain is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Sap|3}} to an enemy unit, but causes you to discard a card at random.

title: Frenzied Swarm

effect.value: Apply {{IconLink|Dazed|1}} to enemy units. Discard your hand.

flavor.value: When generous offerings are made to the Titan, groups of Winged often attempt to take the treasures for themselves. This makes them perfect prey for the swarms of Sirens waiting in the shadows.

tables:
'''Keepstone''' is a crucial upgrade unless your deck is small. With a '''Keepstone''', your units will be safe from attack every turn, almost entirely ensuring your units will survive to the end of the fight. You'll be able to fill your deck with as many [[Offering]] cards as you can fit, and they are prime duplication targets with this upgrade.

A '''Seekstone''' complements this by discounting it to {{Ember|0}} and ensuring you'll have access to '''Frenzied Swarm''' from the start of the fight, making sure your units won't die by then.

'''Stackstone''' and/or '''Twinstone''' can be considered to make this somewhat of a Pyre defense too, especially if applied on the third floor, and it will also accumulate {{IconLink|Dazed}} on [[Flying Bosses]] with either if you need help during {{IconLink|Relentless}} or to reduce how much [[Savagery]] can attack your Pyre on other floors. '''Twinstone''' in particular can capitalize on '''Twinstone''' applied to any [[Offering]] card, as the copy will be able to trigger those copies' [[Offering]].
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Frenzied Swarm is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Dazed|1}} to enemy units, but then discards your hand.

title: Icestorm

effect.value: Deal '''1''' damage to a random enemy unit, five times.

flavor.value: When Hell was frozen, the Stygian Sea was cursed with an eternal storm, making my travel across it near impossible. Fortunately, I was later saved by the Guard, but the invaders of Hell were not so lucky.

tables: '''Powerstone''' applies 5 times, and allows this card to be able to kill many backliners with one hit and some others with more than one hit in the lategame.
'''Surgestone''' applies 5 times, and allows this card to be able to kill most backliners with one hit and have a modest chance of killing Chosen variants.
'''Icestorm''' is an exceptional candidate for '''Entropic Growth''' if found early, as given enough [[Magic Power]] it can become a major threat.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Icestorm is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It deals 1 damage 5 times, targeting a random enemy unit each time.

title: Guardian's Amulet

flavor.value: Given only to the most respected of Guardians, these amulets were used both to identify and to protect the keepers of the Titan Monuments. As the only Stygian allowed to interact directly with the Titan, these Guardians wore the amulets to shield themselves from the Titan's immense power.

tables: '''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Sap}} applied. The more {{IconLink|Sap}} you apply, the better it gets.
'''Twinstone''' also doubles your {{IconLink|Sap}} applied, though this upgrade requires you to have a lot of discard tools on hand (or just a lot of {{Ember}}) to take advantage of both copies.

If you plan to play '''Guardian's Amulet''' primarily by discarding it, '''Holystone''' is worth consideration, as even though you are not paying its {{Ember|3}} cost it will still heal your Pyre for 3.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Guardian's Amulet is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Sap|2}} to enemy units, and has [[Offering]].

title: Ice Tornado

effect.value:
'''[[Permafrost]]'''.
Deal '''30''' damage to a random enemy unit, three times.

flavor.value: The brutal ecosystem of the Stygian Sea has evolved into a favorable place for tornadoes to destroy anything standing above the surface of the water. Thankfully for the Guard, their gills allow them to take refuge beneath the waves.

tables: '''Smolderstone''' makes it much easier to play this spell, and removing it once played is generally a benefit.
Common -> Uncommon (switched rarity with [[Cuttlehex]]), Deal 20 damage -> Deal 30 damage.
summary: Ice Tornado is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It deals 30 damage three times, targeting a random enemy each time. It is not discarded at end of turn.

title: Titanstooth

effect.value:
'''[[Offering]]'''.
Deal '''5''' damage to enemy units and apply {{IconLink|Frostbite|10}}.

flavor.value: Ceremonial spears are given to the Stygian Guard to aid them in their protection of the Unnamed's resting place. Originally just part of tradition, these spears have recently become essential in our defense of Hell.

tables: '''Powerstone''' is an important upgrade, as between the immediate damage and the {{IconLink|Frostbite}} applied, this card will kill all backliners except for Cael's Cherubs and Chosen enemies. Thanks to the {{IconLink|Frostbite}}, it will also strip two {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stacks from Deformed Duos and kill [[Purified Soul]]s through their {{IconLink|Spell Shield}}.

'''Smolderstone''' makes this card easier to play if you do not have consistent discard. The added '''[[Consume]]''' is not a big deal, as if you lack consistent discard you probably don't want to keep drawing this card anyway.
Like all Offering cards, '''Holystone''' is a good choice if you plan to play this card primarily by discarding it, as you will heal {{PyreHealth|3}} for free.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Titanstooth is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It deals 5 damage and applies {{IconLink|Frostbite|10}} to all enemies on the floor. As an [[Offering]] card, it can be played by discarding it instead of paying {{Ember|3}}.

title: Spike of the Stygian

flavor.value: The Stygian Guard was formed with our Rail of the Covenant, created by Tethys to protect the sealed Unnamed Titan. The Guard was wary of our Covenant from the beginning, worried that it would make the Pyre vulnerable to outside attacks. Unfortunately, they were correct.

tables: '''Emberstone''' and other {{Ember}} upgrades can increase this card's potency. '''Freezestone''' in particular can be good if you plan to save it for a boss (and don't have random discard effects), letting you not need to continually re-draw it.

'''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Sap}} and {{IconLink|Frostbite}} applied, which is potent if you can put a lot of {{Ember}} into it. '''Entropic Stone''' can be strong for the same reasons, and is better than '''Entropic Energy''' if you play it for {{Ember|3+}}.
'''Eternalstone''' can allow you to replay this card, and adding '''Smolderstone''' can provide a strong boost to its potency.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Spike of the Stygian is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It uses all {{Ember}} and applies {{IconLink|Sap|1}} and {{IconLink|Frostbite|5}} for each {{Ember}} spent.

title: Harness the Titan

effect.value: Apply '''+10 [[Magic Power]]''' to spells in hand.

flavor.value: "When the Titan whose name has been sealed is released again, the Sea shall be illuminated with its awesome power." - Tethys Titansbane's account of the Titan's return to our defense.

tables: If you have a lot of damage spells that need to be buffed, or a specific card that you need to buff repeatedly, '''Keepstone''' lets you draw this card every turn.

'''Emberstone''' reduces this card's cost, which means you will have more {{Ember}} to play the spells it buffs. '''Freezestone''' achieves the same effect, but also lets you hold onto this spell until you have a good hand of spells to buff.
'''Twinstone''' lets you add 20 Magic Power to all spells in hand when you draw this card. This is best with an {{Ember}}-reducing upgrade.
Apply +5 Magic Power -> Apply +10 Magic Power
summary: Harness the Titan is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It adds 10 [[Magic Power]] to all spells in hand, increasing direct damage or healing by 10.

title: Ice and Pyre

effect.value:
'''[[Pyrebound]]'''. '''[[Attuned]]'''.
Deal '''90''' damage to the front enemy unit.

flavor.value: Having only limited control over the elements, the Stygian have learned to harness the energy of the Pyre and freeze it for even greater impact. Unfortunately, we've only been able to perfect this defense within a limited range.

tables: '''Freezestone''' reduces the cost of Ice and Pyre to {{Ember|0}}, while also allowing you to hold onto it until it is needed. This can give you a panic button in case an enemy manages to sneak through your defenses and reach the top floor.

'''Powerstone''' gives +50 damage rather than +10, significantly boosting this spell's ability to kill frontline units. '''Surgestone''' instead adds 100 damage, though adding Consume can be a significant downside if you want to keep this card.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Ice and Pyre is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It deals 90 damage and has [[Attuned]], multiplying any [[Magic Power]] it has by 5, but can only be played on the third floor or in the Pyre Room due to its [[Pyrebound]] keyword.

title: Deep Offering

flavor.value: From what I can tell, the resting place of the Unnamed spans the length of the Styx Sea. So, the Stygian have created shrines all over the seafloor to offer sustenance and other treasures to the sleeping Titan.

tables: '''Eternalstone''' and '''Smolderstone''' are the bread and butter of this card, and are practically necessary for it to function as a realistic option.
If you aren't offered '''Eternalstone''', adding '''Emberstone''' or an equivalent is an acceptable option, though it will preclude using the card for infinite purposes.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Deep Offering is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It discards all cards in hand, then draws 5 new cards.

title: Ancient Synergy

effect.value: Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal  to '''2x''' the number of spells in your deck, three times.

flavor.value: When mages channel the energy of the Titan, it is often released uncontrollably and violently at first. It takes many years of studying to control the flow, and while I've studied with the Stygian for a long time, the power still escapes me.

tables: '''Smolderstone''' addresses this card's cost, and in the larger decks that this card prefers you're not likely to draw it again anyway.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
Fixed [[Ancient Synergy]] counting [[Ephemeral|ephemeral]] spell cards as "in deck".
summary: Ancient Synergy is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It deals 2x the number of [[:Category:Spells|Spell]] cards in your deck to the front enemy unit 3 times.

title: Gifts for a Guard

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Draw '''3''' damage spells and apply '''[[Consume]]''', '''+30 [[Magic Power]]''', and {{Ember|0}}.

flavor.value: ''Induction into the Guard is considered each Stygian's last step before becoming a fully mature member of the Sea. They are asked to give up all possessions and only carry the tools of their creed. A different life than I would prefer to lead, but most likely much more honorable.''

tables: '''Freezestone''' can allow you to hold '''Gifts for a Guard''' in hand until the right moment. This way, you can either wait until a spell you want to target is discarded if you draw them together, or wait until a spell you ''don't'' want to target is drawn.

'''Eternalstone''' allows you to play '''Gifts for a Guard''' multiple times, which can clear out all of the weak damage spells from your deck, repeatedly scale a single spell, or both. However, it is generally better to put '''Eternalstone''' on a damage spell you want to draw with this spell, and only put it on '''Gifts for a Guard''' itself if you see it again at a later [[Merchant of Magic]].
Updated [[Gifts for a Guard]] to have [[Consume]] and only target damage spells.
Excluded cards that can't have their damage upgraded in shop (ones that damage the pyre) from [[Tethys]]'s Runespeak ability, and [[Gifts for a Guard]] spell.
summary: Gifts for a Guard is a rare spell from the [[Stygian Guard]]. It draws 3 damage spells at random, sets their cost to {{Ember|0}}, applies +30 [[Magic Power]], and makes them [[Consume]] when played. Like all "draw a card" spells, it cannot draw cards that are currently in hand.

title: Hoarfrost Effigy

effect.value: Transfer all {{IconLink|Frostbite}} on this floor to a unit, then double the amount of {{IconLink|Frostbite}}.

flavor.value: Even before the freeze, the granite monuments of the Titan dotting the sea were cold structures. Now they've become permanently frozen fixtures of the seascape, ominous presences easily recognizable by their sharp profiles.

tables: '''Smolderstone''' drastically reduces this card's {{Ember}} cost, making it a more realistic option to play during a turn. If you have this upgrade already, you can then apply '''Eternalstone''' if you have a small enough deck.
Combined with '''Smolderstone''', '''Twinstone''' allows you to quadruple an enemy's {{IconLink|Frostbite}} for only {{Ember|2}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Hoarfrost Effigy is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It moves all {{IconLink|Frostbite}} from units on the floor to the target, then doubles the amount of Frostbite on that unit.

title: Frostpiercer

effect.value: {{IconLink|Strike}}: Apply {{IconLink|Frostbite}} equal to half the damage dealt.

flavor.value: "When my father's friends returned from the Void, so too did this spear appear along the banks of the Stygian Sea. And while the Guard rejoiced at the return of their sacred spear, I could not help but worry. Why would the sea return the spear now?"—Tales of the Inferno

summary: Frostpiercer is a rare [[Stygian Guard]] equipment added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It applies {{IconLink|Frostbite}} equal to half the damage dealt by the equipped unit to foes struck.

title: Siren's Song

effect.value:
'''[[Pyrebound]].'''
At the start of combat, '''[[Ascend]]''' non-boss enemy units on this floor and apply {{IconLink|Dazed|3}}.

flavor.value: I've heard no song as beautiful or as deadly as that of the Sirens of the Stygian. Their luring voices can disarm even the most hardened of hearts.

tables: Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
[[Siren's Song]] updated from Spell >>> Room card. Effect now happens at the start of combat and only affects non-boss units. Cost increased {{Ember|1}} >>> {{Ember|2}}.
Changed Siren Song to use its previous singing sound effect.
Prevented [[Manifold Mirror]] artifact from incorrectly duping '[[Siren's Song]]' room card to all floors.
summary: Siren's Song is a [[Stygian Guard]] room. Each turn, before combat, it [[Ascend]]s all enemy units on the floor and applies {{IconLink|Dazed|3}} to them. It can only be played in the room just below the Pyre.

title: Umbra

flavor.value: ''Commune with the Ancient Umbra Shroud. The original residents of Hell mine the Crucible for precious materials to help in the fight against the Titans.''

summary: Umbra [[File:ClanUmbra.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]]  in [[Monster Train 2]], returning from [[Monster Train 1]]. It is unlocked after unlocking [[Hellhorned]] first and then increasing {{Capacity}} 20 times.

title: Penumbra

flavor.value: I have no hard facts on its origin, but it is rumored to be the beginning of the Shroud itself, formed in the long forgotten depths of the Crucible and giving life to the rest of Hell. This would make it the first being of Hell. It has yet to confirm or deny my questioning on the matter.

tables: Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' with increased Damage in Monstrous champion path.
summary: Penumbra is the main [[Champion]] of the [[Umbra]] clan. As the leader of the gluttonous Shroud, they are a champion that usually requires a lot of attention, either in the need for [[Morsels]] or {{Capacity}}. Their starter card is [[Shadesplitter]].

title: Primordium

ability.value: {{IconLink|Buffet|3}}. </br> {{IconLink|Eaten}}: Add this unit's {{Attack}} and {{Health}} to the eater.

flavor.value: I can feel the end of my days loom near as these visions become more frequent and more confusing. It seems even the Umbra Shroud has origins beyond my prior knowledge. This Primordial shadow rumbles with the weight of the entire Shroud under its cloak. But what happened to this ancient creature?

tables: Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' with increased damage for Aggressive Edible.

Fixed bug where Superfood [[Primordium]] would give double its status effects to a unit with {{IconLink|Dualism}}. [[Primordium|Stalwart Snack]] III stats updated from {{AttackHealth|3/3}} >>> {{AttackHealth|10/10}}.
summary: Primordium is the alternate [[Champion]] of the [[Umbra]] clan. It works very differently than any other Champion, as it is intended to be {{IconLink|Eaten}} by other units rather than fighting on its own. Although not considered a [[Morsels|Morsel]], it fulfills a similar purpose, intended as a sacrifice to power up your other units. Its starter card is [[Plink]].

title: Shadesplitter

effect.value: Add a common or uncommon Morsel unit to your hand.

flavor.value: While the Umbra Shroud cannot do any physical labor on its own, it can create Antumbra Morsels to follow simple instructions and extract the full value of the Crucible. The splitting of the Shroud is like nothing I've ever seen before, and, frankly, prefer not to see again.

tables: Putting '''Emberstone''' on '''Shadesplitter''' helps you spam it more, and in many cases this is a straightforward way to get more value out of your turn.

'''Smolderstone''' also accomplishes what '''Emberstone''' does, while sort-of purging it too. Adding [[Consume]] is generally a nice upside for later in the run so that this card can get out of the way for better ones.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Shadesplitter is [[Penumbra]]'s starter card. It creates a random [[Morsel]] unit from the "common and uncommon" pool (see [[Morsel]] page for details).

title: Plink

effect.value:
Deal '''2''' damage to a random enemy unit, twice.
{{IconLink|Slay}}: Add a common or uncommon Morsel unit to your hand.

flavor.value: The Primordium does not speak through words but through floods of feeling. The bounds of its mind seem endless. It's no wonder that the ultimate split of the Primordium created a varying number of personalities, not the least of which are my friendly Morsels.

tables: '''Surgestone''' has a dual purpose on '''Plink''', making it able to snipe most important backline targets (if it hits them), and as a soft Purge. '''Smolderstone''' does the same, but while it does not boost [[Plink]]'s power, it makes it free to play, letting you get it out of your deck without expending resources.

'''Powerstone''' can be considered instead if you really need backline removal and Morsels and can't afford to replace it with a different card, as it will still have a chance of doing something useful at 12 power. But even then, it's just a chance.
Deal 1 damage to a random enemy unit, twice. -> Deal 2 damage to a random enemy unit, twice.
summary: Plink is [[Primordium]]'s starter card. It picks a random target and deals 2 damage, then does it again. For each kill it gets, it creates a random Morsel unit from the "common and uncommon" pool (see [[Morsel]] page for details).

title: Rubble Morsel

flavor.value: These low ranking Morsels are tasked with clearing out the Crucible of wreck and rubble. As such, there are many of them throughout the Crucible. Slowly, they've taken a liking to me.

summary: Rubble Morsel is a [[Morsel]] of the [[Umbra]] clan. Like all Morsels, its main purpose is to be {{IconLink|Eaten}}. It provides {{AttackHealth|+3/+3}} and {{Ember|1}} upon being eaten.

title: Morsel Jeweler

flavor.value: At the very bottom of the mines, the rock has been compressed into beautiful gems. These gems are valued above all else by the Shroud for their allure as well as their mystical abilities. I've been able to hoard a few for myself, conveniently forgetting to notify the Umbra.

tables: Health and granted health increased from {{Health|3}} -> {{Health|5}}.
Health and granted health increased from {{Health|5}} -> {{Health|6}}.
summary: Morsel Jeweler is one of the four uncommon Morsels of the [[Umbra]] clan. When {{IconLink|Eaten}}, it grants a small {{Health}} boost, as well as {{IconLink|Damage Shield|1}}.

title: Magma Morsel

flavor.value: Originally heated by the nearby Pyre, molten rock can be found throughout the Crucible. Morsels excavate it like anything else, but there was no use for it until I showed them how to use the residual energy to strengthen themselves.

tables: Attack and granted attack increased from {{Attack|6}} -> {{Attack|8}}.
Attack and granted attack increased from {{Attack|8}} -> {{Attack|9}}.
summary: Magma Morsel is one of the four uncommon Morsels of the [[Umbra]] clan. When {{IconLink|Eaten}}, it grants {{Attack|+9}}.

title: Morsel Excavator

flavor.value: Before the Pyre was extinguished, it had rooted itself throughout the edges of the Crucible, creating volatile shards of crystal that were bursting with violent energy. The Shroud had no use for these Void Shards and chose to remove them to gain access to whatever they concealed.

tables: Attack and granted attack increased from {{Attack|3}} -> {{Attack|5}}.
Attack and granted attack increased from {{Attack|5}} -> {{Attack|6}}.
summary: Morsel Exacavator is one of the four uncommon Morsels of the [[Umbra]] clan. When {{IconLink|Eaten}}, it grants a small {{Attack}} boost, as well as {{IconLink|Lifesteal|1}}.

title: Antumbra Morsel

flavor.value: These precursors of the souls of Hell, called Antumbra, are fragments of the Umbra Shroud. Their friendly personalities make them my constant companions anytime I travel to the Crucible.

tables: Health and granted health increased from {{Health|6}} -> {{Health|8}}.
Health and granted health increased from {{Health|8}} -> {{Health|9}}.
summary: Antumbra Morsel is one of the four uncommon [[Morsel]]s of the [[Umbra]] clan. When {{IconLink|Eaten}}, it grants {{Health|+9}}.

title: Morsel Miner

flavor.value: Antumbra Morsels are tasked with the bulk of the physical labor throughout the mines of the Crucible, collecting precious metals and returning them to the main stockpile for smelting and smithing. They don't say much, but they've been quite friendly during my time in the Crucible.

summary: Morsel Miner is the only rare [[Morsel]] of the [[Umbra]] clan. When {{IconLink|Eaten}}, it grants {{AttackHealth|+9|+9}}.

title: Ember Forge

flavor.value: Both for improved construction and visibility, forges were built throughout the Crucible, but the Shroud was soon mining faster than they could build them. Instead of building new ones. Penumbra tasked Morsels with adding mobility. The technology is crude, but is the first mobile engine I have on record.

tables: '''Shieldstone''' grants {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} to help '''Ember Forge''' stay alive a little longer against {{IconLink|Sweep}} units, [[Flying Bosses]], and {{IconLink|Corruption}}. It also lets you use it to block attacks.

'''Heartstone''' and '''Largestone''' offer additional bulk to help keep '''Ember Forge''' alive. '''Largestone''' adds {{Capacity}}, but if using '''Ember Forge''' on an otherwise empty floor, this does not especially matter.
summary: Ember Forge is an uncommon [[Umbra]] unit. It has no combat abilities, and simply generates {{Ember|2}} per turn.

title: Alloyed Construct

flavor.value: As their understanding of the world around them grew, the Umbra were able to create autonomous machines to do the work of one thousand Morsels. They've since served the additional roles of Crucible defender and my personal guard into the depths of Hell.

tables: '''Dualstone''' is not an aggressive upgrade, but it doubles the amount of {{IconLink|Fuel}} gained (and its initial {{IconLink|Fuel}}), giving the unit more sustainability even when your Morsel production is inconsistent.

'''Frenzystone''' is always a solid choice for a unit that is likely to be your main heavy hitter, and '''Alloyed Construct''' requires enough attention that it is not usually worth using if not your main unit.
'''Speedstone''' can help make up for '''Alloyed Construct''''s low {{Health}} by attacking before enemy units.
'''Shieldstone''' provides {{IconLink|Damage Shield|3}}, giving '''Alloyed Construct''' a safety net against the first few hits it takes before Morsels can scale its {{Health}}.
summary: Alloyed Construct is an uncommon [[Umbra]] [[banner unit]]. Despite its solid stats and inherent {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, this unit cannot attack at all unless constantly fed [[Morsel]]s.

title: Crucible Collector

flavor.value: These former Wardens have left their post as an overseer of Morsel workers to become a collector of all variety of gems. They've found that ingesting the metals of the Crucible gives them strength they've never known otherwise. The rest of the Umbra Shroud, however, does not seem to appreciate their newfound independence as much as I do.

tables: '''Titanstone''' is very valuable when tanking with '''Crucible Collector'''; {{IconLink|Titanite}} will tremendously boost its survivability so long as you can buff its {{Health}}, and the effect of healing is essentially doubled.

The extra {{Health}} boost from '''Largestone''' lets you focus more on [[Crucible Collector]]'s {{Attack}}. Make sure you can still support it with Morsels even with the extra {{Capacity}} before buying this upgrade.

As '''Crucible Collector''' has innate {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} gain, it can easily heal from going down to {{Health|1}} after {{IconLink|Reanimate}} triggers, making this a good cheap alternative to other defensive upgrades if on a run with the [[Lazarus League]] clan.

'''Savage Heart''' and '''Savage Spirit''' are both extremely powerful on '''Crucible Collector'''. As a frontline tank, '''Savage Heart''' can provide hundreds of {{IconLink|Rage}} stacks over the course of a run, especially if combined with '''Dualstone'''. Meanwhile, '''Savage Spirit''' provides nearly as much {{Health}} as a '''Largestone''', making it much tankier, while also dramatically boosting its {{Attack}} as it loses {{Health}}, which allows it to absorb a wave's attacks, hit the front unit extremely hard, and immediately heal back to full.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Crucible Collector is an uncommon [[Umbra]] [[banner unit]]. It gains {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} on {{IconLink|Gorge}}.

title: Crucible Warden

flavor.value: The dreaded patrols of the Crucible Mines, wandering the long pathways in search of slacking Morsels and idle researchers. Though originally a mark of their lowly status, the Void that protudes from their shadowed torso serves as a useful guard against worker uprisings.

tables: Thanks to having in-clan options to add {{IconLink|Trample}} and {{IconLink|Multistrike}} to this unit, '''Speedstone''''s {{IconLink|Quick}} effect helps a strong enough '''Crucible Warden''' to avoid unnecessary loss of its {{IconLink|Damage Shield}}.
If you plan on using '''Crucible Warden''' for damage, '''Frenzystone''' will facilitate it immensely by giving this unit {{IconLink|Multistrike}}.

If you instead plan on using '''Crucible Warden''' more as a tank, {{IconLink|Dualism}} from '''Dualstone''' will help you acquire twice as much {{IconLink|Damage Shield}}, giving you much more survivability and leeway to focus on other units.

Starting with 3 extra stacks of {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} helps '''Crucible Warden''' survive the early game much more easily and may save your unit on some occasions, such as against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]]. This is better taken when you intend for this unit to be a tank. Doubly useful if taken together with '''Dualstone'''.

'''Savage Heart''' is a fantastic upgrade for '''Crucible Warden'''. As a tanky frontliner, it will build up tons of permanent {{IconLink|Rage}} over time, which can give it the damage output to take on lategame enemies even if you cannot find sources of scaling like [[Shroud Spike]]. '''Crucible Warden''' is also generally a better recipient of '''Frenzystone''' than the similar Crucible Collector, letting you double dip on damage scaling. This upgrade synergizes extremely well with '''Dualstone''', but is somewhat worse with '''Speedstone'''.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Crucible Warden is an uncommon [[Umbra]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever it eats a [[Morsel]] or [[Primordium]], it gains 1 stack of {{IconLink|Damage Shield}}.

title: Morselmaker

ability.value: {{IconLink|Resolve}}: Summon an [[Antumbra Morsel]] and a [[Magma Morsel]].

flavor.value: Neither Umbra nor Antumbra, these in-between shades roam the mines as independent troublemakers, often splitting their own Morsels to undo the work done in the Crucible. I've been unable to decipher any sort of motive other than spite.

tables: '''Shieldstone''' gives '''Morselmaker''' a much needed survivability buff in the form of {{IconLink|Damage Shield}}. Putting two '''Shieldstones''' on this unit is a great investment.
'''Heartstone''' grants a simple {{Health|+20}}, and can help it survive longer.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Morselmaker is an uncommon [[Umbra]] [[banner unit]]. It provides you with a constant supply of [[Morsels]] for your units.

title: Morselmaster

ability.value: When you summon a [[Morsel]] unit on this floor, create a copy.

flavor.value: These Umbra rogues no longer have the need to create new Morsels of their own flesh. Instead, they attract existing ones to their nefarious calling by disrupting their connection to the hivemind. I have little other information on these creatures as i prefer not to spend any more time with them than necessary.

tables: '''Shieldstone''' gives '''Morselmaster''' much needed survivability in the form of {{IconLink|Damage Shield|3}}.
'''Heartstone''' gives '''Morselmaster''' much needed survivability in the form of {{Health}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Morselmaster is an uncommon [[Umbra]] [[banner unit]]. It creates a copy of any [[Morsel]] units summoned, doubling the scaling of your front units.

title: Shadoweater

ability.value: {{IconLink|Gorge}}: Restore '''10''' health. Deal '''20''' damage to enemy units.

flavor.value: A piece of the Umbra Shroud, blindly searching for morsels and metals to collect, returning them to the collective Shroud consciousness. Though when I say collect, I really mean eat them whole.

tables: '''Titanstone''' helps make the most out of '''Shadoweater''''s naturally high {{Health}} and healing, turning it into a solid wall.

'''Smidgestone''' greatly reduces the unit's {{Capacity}}, which helps you fit additional Morsels onto its floor. If you have taken this upgrade, '''Largestone''' becomes a viable pick to grant a large {{Health}} boost, but it should not otherwise be taken.

'''Immortalstone''' is a valid choice against enemies like [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], who will eventually overwhelm '''Shadoweater''' with {{IconLink|Corruption}}. Each time '''Shadoweater''' is replayed, its stats will be higher from having eaten Morsels.

Since '''Shadoweater''' will always be at the front of the room, '''Savage Heart''' is a solid choice. It can arguably turn its downside - its inability to kill enemy units before they can attack - into a positive. Since the Umbra can apply effects like {{IconLink|Multistrike}} and {{IconLink|Trample}} manually, via [[Furnace Tap]] and [[Umbra Stone]], '''Shadoweater''' does not necessarily require any different upgrades from the [[Merchant of Steel]] if given this upgrade.
Deal 10 damage to enemy units. -> Deal 20 damage to enemy units.
summary: Shadoweater is an uncommon [[Umbra]] [[banner unit]]. Instead of attacking, this unit deals damage after eating [[Morsels]].

title: Morsel-Made

flavor.value: As the mines of the Crucible twist farther into the depths of Hell, Morsels find themselves safe from the Shroud in their solitude. In the furthest reaches of the Crucible, the Morsels have banded together to create singular entities that further increase their collective chances of survival.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' lets you double its offensive scaling and is practically always a priority. If you can afford to search out two of them, that is often the optimal choice, although it does fine work even with one.

'''Heartstone''' and '''Largestone''' can give it initial survivability. As long as you have good Morsel generation, this unit should become fairly hard to kill once it's scaled, especially with {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} and {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} regularly applied to it. '''Largestone''' is easier to use than usual due to its ability.

Similarly to the above upgrades, '''Shieldstone''' gives '''Morsel-Made''' some immediate protection while it's at its most vulnerable. By the time enemies have depleted its {{IconLink|Damage Shield|3}}, it should have plenty of {{Health}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Morsel-Made is a rare [[Umbra]] [[banner unit]]. It eats any unit with an {{IconLink|Eaten}} ability as soon as that unit is played.

title: Overgorger

flavor.value: A seasoned collector of Antumbra Morsels to the detriment of its own well-being. I've learned to steer clear of these creatures, as each new morsel they eat is a danger to all around them.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' is an excellent upgrade, letting you gain twice as much benefit from the [[Overgorger]]'s high {{Attack}}.
'''Speedstone''' can let the '''Overgorger''' kill enemies before they can kill it.
'''Shieldstone''' can protect the '''Overgorger''' until it has time to scale its {{Health}} by eating Morsels.

'''Smidgestone''' allows you to play multiple pre-scaled '''Overgorgers''' together on a single floor after duplicating at an [[Empyrean Well]]. It also lets you play more Morsels on its floor while scaling it up.
summary: Overgorger is a rare [[Umbra]] [[banner unit]]. Each time it eats a [[Morsel]] or [[Primordium]], it gains {{Attack|+2}} permanently.

title: Shadowsiege

flavor.value: I was told that the first Constructs were made of discarded stone and a coordinated Antumbra effort. It is considered a prestigious position among Morsels. These were able to speed up the excavation of the Crucible tenfold.

tables: '''Smidgestone''' negates one of [[Shadowsiege]]'s flaws entirely by reducing it to {{Capacity|1}}.
'''Frenzystone''' helps '''Shadowsiege''' deal much more damage and is practically a necessity on this unit, notably allowing it to hit 500 damage to kill an [[Avowed Gladiator]] on its own.
If you lack a tank, '''Titanstone''' lets you play '''Shadowsiege''' at the front much more comfortably, thanks to its naturally high {{Health}}.

'''Ascetic Penance''' and '''Ascetic Absolution''' can be used either on '''Shadowsiege''' itself, so that other units can be played after it during Deployment, or on one of its allies to generate enough {{Ember}} to play '''Shadowsiege'''. Duplicating an ally with '''Ascetic Penance''' and playing both copies will provide the necessary {{Ember}} for a '''Shadowsiege'''. Umbra is also more capable than other clans of dealing with the {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} applied by '''Ascetic Penance''', though without [[Perils of Production]] this will combine with its natural {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} and potentially leave you unable to play any cards for several turns.

'''Shadowsiege''' will usually be a frontliner owing to its absurd stats, which means it will be taking plenty of damage. '''Savage Heart''' lets its damage scale to the point that it can more comfortably take on the tanks of later rings.

As the only unit in the game with a purely negative card text, '''Purified Essence''' can be used to remove it and give it some extra stats, at the cost of making it unable to take any other upgrade, although if you have already applied a '''Smidgestone''' beforehand, it will stay {{Capacity|1}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
Cost decreased from 6 >>> 4. Atk/Health increased from 200/150 >>> 250/250. Now starts with {{IconLink|Emberdrain|3}}.
summary: Shadowsiege is a rare [[Umbra]] [[banner unit]]. It has the highest base {{Attack}} and {{Health}} of any unit, at the cost of being the biggest individual unit in the game, costing a great amount of {{Ember}}, and possessing inherent {{IconLink|Emberdrain}}.

title: Mine Collapse

effect.value:
Deal '''3X''' damage to a unit.
{{IconLink|Slay}}: Gain {{Ember|2}}.

flavor.value: While Morsels seem to be quick workers in their mine, they do not appear to be the most intelligent and have been the cause of many easily avoided accidents. I can only hope this will not be the case aboard the train.

tables: '''Powerstone''' lets you play this for {{Ember|0}} and still get solid value, allowing you to kill things like [[Harpist Protector]] and [[Ragewing Assassin]]. This also enables it to be played in {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} strategies.
'''Surgestone''' also lets you kill [[Discordant Heretic]]s, and adding [[Consume]] is nice for the lategame most of the time as you won't want this to stick around.

'''Smolderstone''' can be fine too if you need your '''Powerstone''' or '''Surgestone''' elsewhere, as it still lets this spell hit most of what it's going to hit for {{Ember|0}} or {{Ember|1}} while also getting it out of the way in the lategame.

As mentioned, this spell can be used to do something similar to what [[Perils of Production]] does when you're losing all your {{Ember}} to {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} with '''Keepstone'''. It is only reliable, however, if you have an expendable friendly unit to kill when there isn't a suitable enemy.

'''Freezestone''' can be considered instead, as you can't rely on being able to do this every turn, and hopefully if you're resorting to this for {{IconLink|Ember}} in a {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} strategy, you don't have too many cards you actually need {{IconLink|Ember}} for.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
[[Mine Collapse]] can now also target friendly units.
summary: Mine Collapse is an [[Umbra]] spell. It deals 3X damage to a single unit, then gives {{Ember|2}} if its target dies.

title: Prismal Dust

flavor.value: ''The dust gathered from mining Prism stones can be collected to create a similar, though less effective, defensive support around the owner.''

tables: '''Stackstone''' doubles the amount of {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} generated, and is most effective with good {{Ember}} generation.

'''Eternalstone''' lets '''Prismal Dust''' be a permanent part of your deck, giving you more stacks in the long run and enabling the use of '''Smolderstone''', which grants a minimum of {{IconLink|Damage Shield|2}} even if used with {{Ember|0}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Prismal Dust is an [[Umbra]] spell. It applies a stack of {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} for each {{Ember}} spent on it.

title: Immortal Trade

effect.value: Apply {{IconLink|Lifesteal|4}} and {{IconLink|Emberdrain|2}} to a friendly unit.

flavor.value: ''An unfortunate outcome of our invention, Void consumption has become an addictive practice amongst the Umbra. When that no longer satiates their hunger, the entire replacement of self with these Void shards becomes the only way to gain any satisfaction.''

tables: Playing a free card twice for {{IconLink|Lifesteal|8}} is very good so long as you have a method to mitigate the more severe {{IconLink|Emberdrain}}, as playing two of these will make you unable to play anything that isn't free.
'''Stackstone''' provides the same utility as '''Twinstone''', without having to play the card twice. The primary difference is that '''Stackstone''' cannot be used on multiple units.

If the {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} is the only thing keeping your units alive, the amount of {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} won't matter in the end. Make sure you have a lot of free cards before doing this or that you can mitigate the {{IconLink|Emberdrain}}. There are other, more important Umbra cards that want '''Keepstone''' too, and should be prioritized more highly, such as Perils of Production.
'''Freezestone''' keeps this card in hand until necessary. If you save it for when the boss arrives, you can play it with no consequence.
summary: Immortal Trade is an [[Umbra]] spell. It grants a lot of survivability in the form of {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} and is free, but costs you {{Ember}} over subsequent turns.

title: Packed Morsels

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Add '''3''' uncommon or rare [[Morsel]] units to your hand.

flavor.value: ''Through an unusual course of events, I've found that bottling many Morsels together allows them to be easily transported to quickly provide labor where it's needed. It also had the added benefit of soothing the little creatures.''

tables: '''Twinstone''' doubles the Morsels produced, bringing the total up to six. Be careful that you don't run out of room in your hand while playing this! Because the Morsels will take up so much space, this is best used with [[Heaven's Light]], [[Bogwurm's Growth]] or [[Morsel-Made]].

The first turn can be quite awkward for Umbra, and with the wrong card draw it might take some time until you can start scaling. '''Seekstone''' lets you have more Morsels on the first turn for better scaling, and it is a sort of purge, as '''Packed Morsels''' will never take a draw from you this way.

If you desperately need Morsel production, '''Eternalstone''' makes this card a permanent part of your deck. Combined with '''Keepstone''', this can provide a constant supply of Morsels in return for losing a draw each turn.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Packed Morsels is an common [[Umbra]] spell. It provides three uncommon or rare [[Morsels]] when played.

title: Perils of Production

effect.value:
Apply {{IconLink|Rage|3}} and {{IconLink|Emberdrain|2}} to a friendly unit.
Gain {{Ember|3}}.

flavor.value: ''To power the Constructs of the Crucible, the Umbra Shroud feeds them excavated fuel. If fed mined Ember, the furnaces go into overdrive, working doubly hard at the cost of even more Ember. This discovery was crucial in the construction of the furnaces within the Boneshaker.''

tables: '''Keepstone''' is the most important upgrade for this card, and there are very few cards where this upgrade is more valuable. It effectively negates any {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} you gain and enables '''Perils of Production''' to be a game-winning card.
'''Twinstone''' lets you double your {{Ember}} and {{IconLink|Rage}} production, doubling both your scaling and your available {{IconLink|Ember}} for the rest of the game.

If your deck can handle only having {{Ember|3}} each turn rather than the {{Ember|6}} you'll get with '''Twinstone''', '''Seekstone''' can be considered to ensure you have this card in your opening hand and can immediately begin playing {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} cards with no repercussions.

If, and only IF, you didn't find any '''Keepstone''' through your game but you need '''Perils of Production''''s {{Ember}} or {{IconLink|Rage}} scaling to win the game, '''Freezestone''' can be used in a pinch to make sure you always have one copy of '''Perils of Production''' on hand for the immediate {{Ember}} gain. It's almost a necessity to have more copies of '''Perils of Production''' for this to be worth it.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
