summary: Perils of Production is an [[Umbra]] spell. It is one of the few spells which directly produces {{Ember}}, but it also forces the player to pay it back on future turns through {{IconLink|Emberdrain}}.

title: Space Prism

flavor.value: ''In addition to their ability to refract light for defensive use, Prism Stones can bend the space around them, creating something out of nothing.''

tables: Since '''Space Prism''' costs {{Ember|0}}, '''Twinstone''' gives you one extra {{Capacity}} for no additional cost.
If your strategy needs the space to be available immediately for e.g. non-banner units or [[Morsels]], '''Seekstone''' can make sure you draw this before the units that need the space.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Space Prism is an [[Umbra]] spell. It increases the {{Capacity}} of the floor by 1.

title: Antumbra Assault

effect.value:
Deal '''5''' damage.
{{IconLink|Slay}}: Add '''2''' uncommon or rare Morsel units to your hand.

flavor.value: As the first line of defense in the Crucible, Morsels will rocket towards an intruder, often sacrificing themselves in the process. If they succeed in their defense, they live to mine another day.

tables: '''Powerstone''' increases its damage to 15, letting it kill most backliners in later rings that are not Chosen. '''Surgestone''' lets it kill Discordant Heretics as well, and removes it from your deck after play if you do not want to keep drawing it.
'''Freezestone''' lets you keep this card in hand until there is a backliner that you can kill with it. It also reduces its {{Ember}} cost.

While not an ideal option for backline removal, sometimes this card is all you will find, and in those cases '''Keepstone''' can be valuable in order to draw it every hand. This usually requires '''Powerstone''' to be worthwhile later unless you have {{IconLink|Conduit}} or [[Enchanted Chamber]] or something similar.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Antumbra Assault is an [[Umbra]] spell. It provides [[Morsels]] when used to kill a target.

title: Making of a Morsel

effect.value: Add a '''[[Morsel Miner]]''' to your hand.

flavor.value: ''Only the most trusted of Morsels are allowed to mine the most precious of metals. Even fewer are allowed to forge the valuable creations of the Umbra Shroud. So, to be allowed into these sacred forges was an honor indeed.''

tables: '''Twinstone''' doubles the output of this card if you need more [[Morsel Miner]]s.

'''Emberstone''' is a no-frills way to improve your {{Ember}} economy, as other upgrades aren't necessary. This is ideal with '''Twinstone''', effectively making the card grant {{AttackHealth|+18|+18}} for {{Ember|0}} and triggering {{IconLink|Gorge}} twice.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Making of a Morsel is an [[Umbra]] spell. It creates a [[Morsel Miner]] and adds it to your hand.

title: Prism Retrieval

flavor.value: Prism stones have the unique ability to refract both light and space, providing protection and creating matter from nothing. I've been able to reverse engineer this power to transport objects and beings across small distances.

tables: '''Seekstone''' in addition to increasing X by 1 also gives you this card on turn 1 reliably. As most units really want to be on the field from the very start of the fight, this upgrade is highly desirable.

'''Twinstone''' gives you two of these for the price of one. Unlike this card's cousins, for this upgrade to be worth it, you need to have an energy discount upgrade with it for it to work at all, and with it, you're limited to units costing {{Ember|1}} or less.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
Fixed bug where stats granted through [[Sacrificial Resurrection]] or [[Prism Retrieval]] would not carry over to a [[Reform|reformed]] unit.
summary: Prism Retrieval is an [[Umbra]] spell. It spends all of the player's ember and draws a random unit from their deck, reducing its cost by 1 {{Ember}} and increasing its {{Attack}} by 5 for each ember spent.

title: Feast

effect.value: Trigger feeding on friendly units with {{IconLink|Eaten}}.

flavor.value: Gorgers patrol the mines to collect errant Morsels, consuming them to return them back to the Shroud. They take great pleasure in their purpose, often consuming more Morsels than necessary.

tables: If you are using this card for backline removal with Shadoweater, '''Keepstone''' is highly advisable to ensure that you can trigger pre-combat feeding every turn. You can combine this with '''Seekstone''' to ensure that you draw the card immediately. It can also be useful if you are routinely producing too many Morsels per turn, or if you have a [[Morselmaker]] or [[Morselmaster]] and want to clear up {{Capacity}} consistently. Note, however, that this will take up a draw every turn, so the benefit it provides must be worth the cost of cycling through your deck slower.

'''Twinstone''' is particularly useful when using this card in conjuction with Primordium. This can allow '''Aggressive Edible''' or '''Superfood''' to be fully eaten in a single turn if you draw it immediately, while with '''Stalwart Snack''' you can get through many more stacks of {{IconLink|Buffet}} per turn.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Feast is an [[Umbra]] spell. It causes all units with {{IconLink|Eaten}} on its floor to be eaten immediately.

title: Cannibalize

effect.value:
'''[[Sacrifice]]'''.
Add '''3''' uncommon or rare Morsel units to your hand.

flavor.value: Despite being a hive-minded creature, the Umbra Shroud still falls victim to the petty squabbles observed in the other clans. It's unclear how this hive-minded creature can argue with itself, but the ensuing scuffles can be deadly and something I've learned to detect and avoid.

tables: If you need even more [[Morsel]] generation, '''Twinstone''' provides it. You'll be guaranteed to be able to play the second copy by sacrificing one of the Morsels generated by the first, producing five in total. If you're stacking {{IconLink|Damage Shield}}, you can sacrifice [[Morsel Excavator]]; if you're stacking {{IconLink|Lifesteal}}, you can sacrifice [[Morsel Jeweler]].

There aren't too many impactful upgrades for '''Cannibalize''', and especially with '''Twinstone''', saving {{Ember|1}} with '''Emberstone''' is nice. If you pick up a [[Retch]] and this is producing too many [[Morsels]], '''Smolderstone''' can limit that while providing the same benefit.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Cannibalize is an uncommon [[Umbra]] spell. It requires a friendly unit to be killed, but gives you three [[Morsels]] chosen from the uncommon or rare pool.

title: Ember Cache

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Add '''3''' '''[[Excavated Ember]]''' cards to your discard pile.

flavor.value: I created fortified steel boxes to house the dormant Ember mined in the Crucible, increasing its effectiveness through pressure and time.

tables: '''Twinstone''' doubles the amount of [[Excavated Ember]]s you receive, making you receive a total of {{Ember|12}}.

'''Eternalstone''' allows this card to stick around in your deck after being played. Usually, due to its relatively slow payoff, this is unnecessary, but it has a strong niche in {{IconLink|Etch}} builds, especially ones built around The Great Decay. With both '''Eternalstone''' and '''Twinstone''', this card alone can represent six {{IconLink|Etch}} triggers every turn after you have thinned down your deck.

'''Emberstone''' goes nicely with [[Twinstone]] to make this card playable twice for no {{Ember}} cost.

While this card doesn't need '''Seekstone''' usually, it does prevent the unfortunate scenarios where '''Ember Cache''' ends up on the bottom of the deck and you shuffle your discard into your draw before getting a chance to play it.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Ember Cache is an [[Umbra]] spell. It adds 3 copies of [[Excavated Ember]] to your discard pile.

title: Void Binding

flavor.value: When Void shards were first found, they were considered to be of little value. So, they were collected and dumped to the depths of the Crucible. Later, the Umbra and I found that the shards can mimic the effects of any nearby gems, making them incredibly useful tools if bound directly to the body.

tables: '''Keepstone''' lets you play this card every turn. However, if you plan to use an {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} strategy then this upgrade may be better used on [[Perils of Production]].

'''Emberstone''' reduces the cost of '''Void Binding''' to {{Ember|0}}. Not only does this make it easier to play, it also allows you to play it regardless of how much {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} you have. '''Freezestone''' has the same effect, but allows you to hold onto this card for when you absolutely need it in case you cannot handle the {{IconLink|Emberdrain}}.

'''Stackstone''' doubles the effect of this card, but keep in mind that this includes the {{IconLink|Emberdrain}}. Don't use this unless you simply don't care about how much {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} you stack up.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Void Binding is an [[Umbra]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Damage Shield|2}}, {{IconLink|Rage|6}}, and {{IconLink|Emberdrain|3}}.

title: Cave In

flavor.value: I've only seen the aftermath, but when a level of the Crucible collapses, very few Morsels survive. The Umbra don't even care to check for survivors, choosing instead to spawn new Morsels.

tables: '''Freezestone''' reduces [[Cave In]]'s {{Ember}} cost and allows you to hold onto it until it is necessary. This is useful if you plan to use it to bring your main floor down to the boss.
If the only thing you need this card to do is consolidate a floor once, '''Smolderstone''' lets you play it for free and then gets it out of your deck.
'''Seekstone''' puts this card in your hand immediately for overstacking purposes.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Cave In is an [[Umbra]] spell. It [[Descend]]s all units on the current floor, including both friendly and enemy units.

title: Grovel

effect.value: Apply {{IconLink|Damage Shield|1}}. Add '''2''' uncommon or rare Morsel units to your hand.

flavor.value: Some errant Morsels, in an effort to please the Wardens, will offer their valuable jewels to try and get in their good graces. This behavior has been noted for future bribes that occur within the Boneshaker.

tables: '''Stackstone''' lets '''Grovel''' apply {{IconLink|Damage Shield|2}}, which is worthwhile if you need this card for its defensive purposes.
'''Emberstone''' reduces this card's cost to {{Ember|1}}, making it much more affordable.

If you reduce its cost with '''Emberstone''' or another upgrade, '''Twinstone''' lets this card produce four Morsels for {{Ember|2}}, and also allows you to apply its {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} to two different units.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Grovel is an [[Umbra]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Damage Shield|1}} to a unit and adds two [[Morsels]] from the "uncommon or rare" pool. See [[Morsels]] for Morsel probabilities.

title: Excavation Eruption

effect.value:
Deal '''25''' damage to a random enemy unit, three times.
{{IconLink|Slay}}: Gain {{Ember|2}}.

flavor.value: With little regard for their own lives, these Morsels seem to explode carelessly in the mines, paying no mind to the possible consequences of their actions. I've seen this backfire on more than one occasion...

tables: As this card is useful early on but will often be a dead draw late, '''Surgestone''' and '''Smolderstone''' are generally the best upgrades, ensuring that '''Excavation Eruption''' is removed from your deck when played. '''Smolderstone''' is typically the better choice as it makes the card cost only {{Ember|1}} and it is therefore far less of an investment to play, but '''Surgestone''' can be considered if you want to use this card to hit Dominion harder.
summary: Excavation Eruption is an [[Umbra]] spell. It deals 25 damage to a random enemy three times, granting {{Ember|2}} for each enemy it kills.

title: Gem Trove

effect.value: Apply {{IconLink|Damage Shield|1}} to friendly units. Add '''3''' uncommon or rare [[Morsel]] units to your hand.

flavor.value: It is said that the Crucible was formed when the Pyre first ignited, molding and melting the nearby ground to create endless, winding caverns. The Umbra have done their best to direct me through these tunnels, but the maze of caves has still been enough to trap me for days at a time.

tables: '''Stackstone''' doubles the amount of {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} generated, which can be important if you don't have other answers for threats to your backline. If you can deal with [[Ragewing Assassin]] before it attacks, this can keep your floor alive against one round of [[Chosen Assassin]] on Covenant 10 (though this won't include the Morsels this card generates, generally).
'''Seekstone''' reduces this card's cost while also guaranteeing that you will see it immediately, allowing you to get your defenses set up quickly and providing an initial supply of Morsels.

'''Keepstone''' can be applied in larger decks if you need consistent access to Morsels every turn and can afford its {{Ember}} cost. It will also build up a floor that bosses will have a hard time getting through.
Cost-reducing upgrades make this card far more affordable, though ideally this can be solved with the [[Umbra]]'s ways of amassing {{Ember}}.
summary: Gem Trove is an [[Umbra]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Damage Shield|1}} to friendly units on the floor and adds three [[Morsels]] from the "uncommon or rare" pool. See [[Morsels]] for Morsel probabilities.

title: Forever Consumed

effect.value: Deal '''80X''' damage to the front enemy unit.

flavor.value: Of a collective mind, the massive Umbra Shroud can wreak devastating damage upon the unfortunate soul who has been targeted by its wrath. On the one occasion I was witness to such an event, I was unable to return to the Crucible for months, afraid of the slightest chance it could happen to me.

tables: '''Freezestone''' applies [[Permafrost]], as well as increasing its power by 80. This can let you save it for the right moment - when you have {{Ember}} to spare, a tanky frontliner to hit, or even enough {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} set up on your boss.

Other {{Ember}} discounting upgrades will also increase its power by 80 per {{Ember}} discounted. '''Entropic Energy''' in particular is notable for giving the spell a minimum of 320 damage even played with {{Ember|0}}, on par with powerful '''[[Attuned]]''' spells. This makes it a strong option to duplicate or upgrade with {{IconLink|Keepstone}} or {{IconLink|Twinstone}} as a way to blast through [[Avowed Gladiator]]s and similar tanks.
summary: Forever Consumed is an [[Umbra]] spell. It deals 80X damage to the front enemy unit when played.

title: Kindle

flavor.value: The Umbra Shroud mines the depths of the Crucible, creating more vents to the surface above. These allow the ember below to burn ever more fiercely, and when applied to the Boneshaker, the same technique has allowed us to increase our fuel efficiency for short amounts of time.

tables: '''Freezestone''' greatly helps with lining up this card with the (probably) X-cost card you're looking to pair it with, and even gives you slightly more bang for your buck due to reducing the card's {{Ember}} cost. ('''Freezestone''' can also be put on the other card too.)

'''Seekstone''' pairs nicely with '''Freezestone''' to ensure you'll line this card up with its intended target during your first deck cycle, while increasing its potency too. Alternately, you could apply this to both '''Kindle''' and its intended target to be guaranteed to line up the combo on turn 1 without needing '''Freezestone'''.
'''Twinstone''' functionally makes this quadruple your {{Ember}}production, doubling your potency again.

'''Holystone''' can potentially get some insane healing, making '''Kindle''' double as its own payoff. If you pair it with '''Twinstone''', you can get 3x your starting {{Ember}}/turn as a heal. If you can then duplicate it and play the copies together, or use [[Emot Tome]] to duplicate it, you can get a whopping 15x your starting {{Ember}}/turn in healing - a great pick-me-up for the [[Titans]] fight!

That being said, this upgrade may be better on the X-cost card that this is being paired with, as you'll actually heal slightly more this way. It depends on where you need the upgrade slots.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Kindle is an [[Umbra]] spell. It gives you twice the {{Ember}} you spend on it.

title: Shroud Spike

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]].'''
Trigger feeding on a friendly [[Morsel]] unit '''2X''' times.

flavor.value: The Umbra Shroud was the first clan to agree with me that the Rail was crucial to the survival of Hell. This alliance proved my proposed Covenant's importance to the other clans.

tables:
'''Seekstone''' both increases the potency of this spell by {{Ember|1}} and makes it reliable. With this upgrade, you can have your {{IconLink|Gorge}} unit have several {{IconLink|Gorge}} triggers on turn 1, as long as you can guarantee a [[Morsel]] being available then, and ideally a good one.

This can be paired with [[Making of a Morsel]] with a '''Seekstone''' or [[Commemorative Spike]] to ensure a [[Morsel Miner]] target, maximizing the stats this spell can give you.

'''Twinstone''' can be a particularly spicy choice on this card. If you can have the first cast of this spell hit a Rubble Morsel, it'll function as a [[Kindle]], and you'll be able to play the second copy for twice the {{IconLink|Ember}} on a different Morsel. This triples your {{IconLink|Gorge}} triggers and doubles your {{IconLink|Eaten}} triggers on the second Morsel.

This can be unreliable in the lategame, even if you still have your [[Shadesplitter]]s or [[Plink]]s, as [[Rubble Morsel]]s can have a habit of not appearing when you actually need them. [[Abandoned Antumbra]] can help here too.

This flexible, {{Capacity}}-efficient way of scaling [[Umbra]] units can be something you want throughout the fight, making '''Eternalstone''' a solid choice, especially in smaller decks. As an added bonus, this upgrade allows you to put '''Smolderstone''' on the card too (which, if you see '''Eternalstone''' in your [[Merchant of Magic]] before a reroll, you know you'll have the opportunity to apply before or after the reroll), making it a great duplication target. It will always let you feed four times for {{Ember|0}}, making it strong even in the worst case where you draw multiples of this card in one hand without a [[Rubble Morsel]].

While not as exciting a choice as the others listed here, '''Freezestone''' has solid utility if you can wait for a turn where you have lots of {{IconLink|Ember}}, e.g. alongside [[Kindle]], and/or the right Morsel to use it on.

'''Emberstone''' lets you eat two extra times, which is respectable, especially if you duplicate this spell. For the same reason, this spell is an excellent target for '''Entropic Energy''' if you can manage to line these up.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Shroud Spike is an [[Umbra]] spell. It allows your frontmost unit to eat a target [[Morsel]] unit 2X times, triggering {{IconLink|Eaten}} and {{IconLink|Gorge}} that many times.

title: Retch

effect.value: Return eaten units to your hand.

flavor.value: Even the Shroud knows little restraint, sometimes consuming Morsels when, as far as I can tell, no hunger remains. This compulsion, unfortunately, can lead to… "involuntary expulsion."

tables: '''Keepstone''' lets you play this strong card every turn, letting your Morsel engine hum at maximum capacity.

'''Twinstone''' can double the output of this card, and with '''Keepstone''' can be truly busted, if you have [[Feast]] or [[Morsel-Made]] to re-eat the Morsels this card gets. You can then eat your entire Eaten pile twice this turn!

But beware! If you have too many Morsels in your Eaten pile, '''there won't be room for this card in your hand, and you'll waste the copy!''' With this upgrade, you'll really need to extra careful to keep your Eaten pile at a manageable size, so that after this card is played, your hand size plus the size of your Eaten pile is 9 or less.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
Made [[Retch]] only return units to hand, and not overflow to the draw pile when hand is full.
summary: Retch is an [[Umbra]] spell. Any units which are {{IconLink|Eaten}}, including both [[Morsels]] and [[Primordium]], are placed in a separate Eaten Pile, and playing Retch will immediately put as many of these cards as possible back in your hand, up to the hand size limit of 10. Other cards will remain in the Eaten pile.

title: Shroud Mitosis

effect.value: Create '''3''' copies of a friendly [[Morsel]] unit.

flavor.value: I thought that only the Umbra could split themselves off into more Morsels, but it seems that the Antumbra can create even more copies of themselves. I guess that's why there's a saying about a Morsel in a dark mine...

tables: '''Freezestone''' discounts this to {{Ember|0}} and smooths over problems such as a [[Morsel]] not being ready to duplicate.
'''Seekstone''' also discounts it to {{Ember|0}} and works with [[Commemorative Spike]] or a [[Making of a Morsel]] with '''Seekstone'''.
'''Emberstone''' is fine too if you don't need the above listed - its upgrade slots aren't in high demand, making this an easy way to save {{Ember}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Shroud Mitosis is an [[Umbra]] spell. It duplicates a [[Morsel]] unit three times, giving you four in total.

title: Furnace Tap

flavor.value: Much to my dismay, the Umbra are able to withstand the heat output from the furnaces on the Boneshaker, allowing them to commune with its power and use it for themselves - at the cost of energy to the train.

tables: '''Stackstone''' gives you {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}} and enough {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} to never have starting {{Ember}} again. '''Entropic Stone''' takes this even further if you can find it.

'''Eternalstone''' can let you keep scaling your {{IconLink|Multistrike}} if you have a smaller deck, and lets you add '''Smolderstone''' to make it cost {{Ember|0}}, making it possible to keep playing it even absent a [[Perils of Production]] engine or similar.
'''Freezestone''' can lets you save this card for when you need it, potentially giving you time to play spells before you lock yourself down with {{IconLink|Emberdrain}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Furnace Tap is an [[Umbra]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} to a unit, but also applies {{IconLink|Emberdrain|4}}.

title: Umbra Stone

flavor.value: As a single mind, the Umbra had no need for written text. But when I finally discovered them, they created a language to converse with me and the other lowly residents of Hell.

tables: '''Seekstone''' can make your build more reliable if a {{IconLink|Trample}} unit is a core part of your strategy and you leak enemies otherwise, especially if you have a large deck, in addition discounting it by {{Ember|1}}.

'''Emberstone''' makes it easier to play '''Umbra Stone''' - as you'll often need to play it the moment you draw it, discounting it makes it less likely you'll have to make an awkward choice between it and another important spell.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Umbra Stone is an [[Umbra]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Trample}} to a target unit.

title: Blazing Bolts

effect.value:
'''Purge'''.
Deal '''60''' damage to the front enemy unit. Add a stronger version of this card to your discard.

flavor.value: Constructed bolts I gifted to the Umbra to dig deeper into the stone. When Morsels cannot break through it, these white-hot steel bolts should get the job done.

tables: '''Smolderstone''' and '''Surgestone''' both apply [[Consume]] in exchange for potent benefits, either reducing its cost to a mere {{Ember|1}} or granting it an extra +80 damage total. '''Surgestone''' also lets it kill [[Chosen Sniper]]s in one hit. However, note that these upgrades can '''only''' be applied to the final stage of '''Blazing Bolts''', not its first two (since they Purge).
'''Eternalstone''' is a decent option with either of the two upgrades above, letting you keep the card around if you need it.

'''Powerstone''' is an acceptable choice, adding a total of 40 damage to the card, though this doesn't change any breakpoints aside from letting it kill [[Blightbound Guardian]]s in two hits rather than three.
'''Entropic Energy''' makes '''Blazing Bolts''' completely free, turning it into a solid target for duplication.
Deal 30 damage -> Deal 40 damage, successive versions change from front unit to random unit.
[[Blazing Bolts]] damage at all tiers increased from 40 >>> 60.
Fixed the strongest tier of [[Blazing Bolts]] erroneously dealing damage 5 times instead of 4.
summary:
{{SpellCard                
|name = Blazing Bolts
|image = CRD_BlazingBoltsII.png
|clan = [[Umbra]]
|rarity = Rare        
|cost = 3
|effect = Purge.Deal 60 damage to a random enemy unit, twice. Add a stronger version of this card to your discard.
|flavor = Constructed bolts I gifted to the Umbra to dig deeper into the stone. When Morsels cannot break through it, these white-hot steel bolts should get the job done.
|artist = Jordan Thomas
}}

title: Glutton's Maw

ability.value: {{AbilityBox|Chomp|1|Destroy a friendly unit and gain {{Attack|+15}} and {{Health|+15}}. Triggers {{IconLink|Gorge}} and {{IconLink|Eaten}}.}}

flavor.value: The Shroud's hunger will push the Umbra towards innovation to satisfy its unending hunger. With this contraption, each creature of the Shroud can consume shards and armor as easily as flesh.

summary: Glutton's Maw is an rare [[Umbra]] equipment card added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. Its Chomp ability lets the equipped unit "eat" any friendly unit in the game, even units without the {{IconLink|Eaten}} keyword.

title: Crucible Extension

flavor.value: The number of Morsels within the Crucible seems to be endless, making the work they accomplish proceed near instantaneously. Should I need to do future work on the Boneshaker, I will remember to take this into account.

tables: Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
[[Crucible Extension]] updated from Spell >>> Room card. "{{Capacity|+1}} on this floor" >>> "{{Capacity|+4}}."
Fixed [[Awakening Thicket]], [[Engine Upgrade]], and [[Crucible Extension]] being missing from certain card pools.
summary: Crucible Extension is an [[Umbra]] room. It gives its floor {{Capacity|+4}}.

title: Engine Upgrade

flavor.value: A substantial upgrade to the furnaces in the Boneshaker will eventually be necessary to ensure more efficient energy output. These upgrades will require considerable room to function, though.

tables: Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
[[Engine Upgrade]] updated from Spell >>> Room card. Cost reduced from {{Ember|1}} >>> {{Ember|0}}.
Fixed [[Awakening Thicket]], [[Engine Upgrade]], and [[Crucible Extension]] being missing from certain card pools.
summary: Engine Upgrade is an [[Umbra]] room. It reduces the {{Capacity}} of its floor by 1, but increases the {{Ember}} gained at the start of each turn by 1.

title: Melting Remnant

flavor.value: ''Recruit the Melting Remains of the Waxen Arches. Melting souls and greedy thugs band together to take the fight to Heaven.''

summary: Melting Remnant [[File:ClanMeltingRemnant.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]]  in [[Monster Train 2]], returning from [[Monster Train 1]]. It is unlocked after unlocking [[Hellhorned]] first and then Reanimating or Reforming 50 Units.

title: Rector Flicker

flavor.value: Both priest and gang leader, Rector Flicker has taken advantage of the Armageddon at hand and played the Reformed and the Wickless off each other, creating an endless cycle of profit through deceit. I don't agree much with his methods, but his charm is hard to ignore.

tables: Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' with Dark Calling Damage increased from 5/10/15 to 10/15/20
Burn Bright Rektor Flicker stats increased from 50/50, 80/80, 145/145 >>> 50/50, 90/90, 180/180.
Rector Flicker Burn Bright II & III stats increased from 50/50, 90/90, 180/180 >>> 50/50, 100/100, 200/200.

Dark Calling [[Rector Flicker|Rektor Flicker]] effect updated to be an ability: "{{IconLink|Resolve}}: [[Reform]] 2 random units and apply {{Attack|+10/15/25}}." >>> {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}: Cryptcall. CD 1. "[[Reform]] 2 random units and apply {{Attack|+10/15/25}}."
summary: Rector Flicker is the primary [[Champion]] of the [[Melting Remnant]]. He takes advantage of the Remnant's ability to constantly die and [[Reform]], either Reforming other units, growing stronger when they die, or risking death himself in exchange for enormous stat boosts. His starter card is [[Dreg]].

title: Little Fade

flavor.value: For all that I've learned of these Exiles, it should be no surprise to me that the Exile of the Melting Remnant is a thieving child. My visions with her have been brief, but she looks to be free of the wax for which her Ring is known. Perhaps her sacrifice, and the sacrifice of each Exile, granted immortality to the clans.

tables: Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' with Little Icarus Path starting with Spikes 5 instead of Spikes 1
Fixed bug where {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers would not always happen if the unit with the trigger died or was reanimated simultaneously.
[[Little Fade]] path Little Icarus starting {{IconLink|Spikes}} increased from '''5''' >>> '''7'''.
summary: Little Fade is the alternate [[Champion]] of the [[Melting Remnant]]. She is intended to die frequently, buffing herself or your other units as she does so. To help with this, her starter card is [[Primitive Mold]], which [[Reform]]s a single unit chosen at random.

title: Dreg

flavor.value: Waxers believe that once they've melted away their bodies, they will be released from Hell. Unfortunately, there seems to be little evidence to support this belief, though I will not be the one to tell them that.

tables: '''Wickstone''' boosts the [[Dreg]]'s stats and gives it one more turn of staying power.
'''Strengthstone''' is another way of upping [[Dreg]]'s power, albeit slightly less effectively.
summary: Dreg is [[Rector Flicker]]'s starter card. It is a cheap, expendable unit that will eventually die to its own {{IconLink|Burnout}}.

title: Primitive Mold

flavor.value: Fade brought me to the site of a rock split in two. The shape reminded me of the molds used by the Melting Remnant, and the drips of wax made this theory more plausible. Fade says she split the rock because she was bored, but her subsequent silence seems to suggest a more altruistic purpose. Why are they showing me these things?

tables: Putting '''Emberstone''' on '''Primitive Mold''' can be a straightforward way to get more value out of your turn if you can structure your turn around it.

'''Keepstone''' actually can be applied to this card for certain builds that intend to just reform the same unit over and over every turn (and if you want to Reform the same two over and over, you can copy it too). While [[Molded]] is a more reliable way to do this, if you can keep your Reform pool under control, this card can be just as good without needing to add another card to your deck. ('''Emberstone''' pairs very well with this.)
'''Freezestone''' can be applied to this card for similar reasons if you don't need to Reform every turn but still need consistent ability to do so.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Primitive Mold is [[Little Fade]]'s starter card. It [[Reform]]s a random unit in the exhaust pool.

title: Draff

flavor.value: When wax has been melted and reapplied over and over again, it can turn into fragile resin. This makes the edges of a Waxer sharper and more dangerous, but much more brittle.

tables: '''Wickstone''' gives '''Draff''' a notable stat boost and {{IconLink|Burnout|2}}, so it won't die immediately. It is also a cheap upgrade.
'''Speedstone''' grants {{IconLink|Quick}}, which is probably the most useful major upgrade for '''Draff''', as it can attack before enemies move and then die.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Draff is a common [[Melting Remnant]] unit. It starts with {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, but also has a single stack of {{IconLink|Burnout}}, killing it instantly at the end of the turn.

title: Entombed Explosive

ability.value: {{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Deal '''65''' damage to the front enemy unit.

flavor.value: A common, but unfortunate, occurence for the Melting Remnant is the entrapment of inanimate objects within their melting wax. While often considered an inconvenience, the Wickless have utilized this phenomenon for more combat focused applications.

tables: '''Immortalstone''' can allow you to replay the '''Entombed Explosive''' every turn, at the cost of needing to spend {{Ember|1}} and lose a card draw. It also keeps it out of your [[Reform]] pool if you'd prefer to be [[Reform]]ing other things.

'''Wickstone''' gives it {{IconLink|Burnout|1}}, which when paired with '''Immortalstone''' guarantees that it will die at end of each turn. It's less useful if you're [[Reform]]ing it to recur it.

(The [[Melting Spout]] can replace '''Wickstone''' here; if you've already added '''Immortalstone''' + '''Wickstone''' to an '''Entombed Explosive''' that you're relying on, you should probably skip [[Melting Spout]] as it will give you {{IconLink|Burnout|2}}.)

The [[Inscryption]] event's upgrades can all go quite well on '''Entombed Explosive''', especially if you've found [[Waxer Snuffer]]. '''Many Lives''' in particular stands out, as both [[Molten Encasement]] and [[Remnant Host]] are slightly awkward with it for the purposes of {{IconLink|Harvest}} builds (due to applying {{IconLink|Stealth}} to itself and summoning [[Draff]]s to block hits, respectively), making '''Entombed Explosive''' arguably the best option and allowing it to deal a much more respectable 260 damage before it dies. If you can manage all three upgrades (see the [[Inscryption]] page for how to do that), you can amass an army of '''Entombed Explosives''' to kill waves by a thousand cuts. Just be sure to also have a boss answer.
summary: Entombed Explosive is a common [[Melting Remnant]] unit. When killed, it explodes, dealing 65 damage to the front enemy.

title: Molten Encasement

flavor.value: If a Waxer gutters too quickly, a rare phenomenon can occur where the wax trapped inside is still molten. Over time, the heat generates an enormous amount of pressure and steam. When the host's exterior has finally cracked, the steam bursts out and engulfs all those around it.

tables: '''Immortalstone''' can allow you to replay the '''Molten Encasement''' every turn, at the cost of needing to spend {{Ember|1}} and lose a card draw. It also keeps it out of your [[Reform]] pool if you'd prefer to be [[Reform]]ing other things.

'''Dualstone''' doubles '''Molten Encasement''''s {{IconLink|Stealth}}, allowing it to stack enough {{IconLink|Stealth}} to protect multiple floors or to potentially trivialize the {{IconLink|Relentless}} boss phase.

'''Wickstone''' gives it {{IconLink|Burnout|1}}, which when paired with '''Immortalstone''' guarantees that it will die at end of each turn. It's less useful if you're [[Reform]]ing it to recur it.

(The [[Melting Spout]] can replace '''Wickstone''' here; if you've already added '''Immortalstone''' + '''Wickstone''' to a '''Molten Encasement''' that you're relying on, you should probably skip [[Melting Spout]] as it will give you {{IconLink|Burnout|2}}.)
The [[Inscryption]] event's upgrades can all go quite well on '''Molten Encasement''', although '''Fecundity''' might belong on one of the units with {{IconLink|Stealth}} you're protecting instead.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Molten Encasement is a common [[Melting Remnant]] unit. When it dies, it applies {{IconLink|Stealth|2}} to all friendly units on the floor.

title: Remnant Host

flavor.value: Tombs are usually formed as a consequence of some horrible accident when guttering. If a Waxer happens to be caught in the wax drip of another, they can be trapped inside until their host melts away.

tables: '''Immortalstone''' allows you to replay '''Remnant Host''' every turn.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Remnant Host is an uncommon [[Melting Remnant]] unit. On death, it spawns a pair of [[Draff|Draffs]].

title: Votivary

flavor.value: These Reformed attendants of the Votive Houses are some of my closest allies throughout the Ring. Their reduced stature gives them a natural affinity for the weak, finding them to be kindred spirits of sorts. Their sharp resin hands, however, make their embrace of these fellow souls considerably more dangerous.

tables: '''Wickstone''' is a great upgrade for '''Votivary'''; it's cheap and guarantees that the unit will always die after one turn.

'''Frankenstone''' is only available with the [[Lazarus League]], but is quite powerful as long as you can ensure '''Votivary''' will be hit twice each turn (not difficult to accomplish), as it allows its {{IconLink|Extinguish}} effect to trigger twice and therefore grant +4 draw each turn (+3 if you count '''Votivary''' itself).

'''Shieldstone''' comes from the [[Umbra]] clan, but when combined with '''Wickstone''' makes '''Votivary''' a fantastic chump blocker, as it blocks four hits every turn instead of one, is guaranteed to die, and even increases your draw!

As discussed above, both '''Worthy Sacrifice''' and '''Many Lives''' are great on '''Votivary''', granting extra {{Ember}} to go along with your increased draw or acting as a combination of both '''Frankenstone''' and '''Shieldstone''' which is available to every clan.

'''Ascetic Penance''' and '''Ascetic Absolution''' is a incredible upgrade for '''Votivary''', allowing it to also grant {{Ember|3}} every turn in addition to the increased draw; as it wants to die every turn anyways, the {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} is inconsequential.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
[[Votivary]] updated from "{{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Draw 1." >>> "{{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Draw 2 next turn."
summary: Votivary is an uncommon [[Melting Remnant]] unit. It has low stats, but starts with {{IconLink|Endless}} and grants two additional card draws next turn when it dies.

title: Lady of the House

flavor.value: In a cruel joke, the souls trapped as Remnants retained their wealth, or lack of it, from their previous life, making Hell either very comfortable or very punishing. Some of the more generous Remnants decide to fund the Votive Houses scattered throughout the Ring, though I have long suspected that their motives are less than selfless.

tables: As an offensively inclined unit, '''Frenzystone''' is an important upgrade for '''Lady of the House''', doubling her damage output and the scaling from {{IconLink|Burnout}}.
'''Dualstone''' grants her {{IconLink|Burnout|6}}, keeping her alive for longer and boosting her damage. However, if you have Lady of the Reformed, this upgrade is generally better on her instead.

'''Lady of the House''' tends to scale well with additional copies of herself, as many of the most efficient {{IconLink|Burnout}} extenders target the whole floor. '''Smidgestone''' allows you to fit more copies of her on the floor together.

If you are not scaling her with Lady of the Reformed or Little Fade, '''Speedstone''' can be considered, as her {{Health|45}} is solid but not enough to keep her alive on its own in the later rings, and {{IconLink|Quick}} lets her take out enemies before they can attack.
'''Wickstone''' provides a decent boost to stats and an additional stack of {{IconLink|Burnout}}. As a minor upgrade, it is a cheap way to fill her slots and is guaranteed with a reroll.
Changed [[Lady of the House]] to have {{Attack|+5}} for every stack of {{IconLink|Burnout}}. Base {{Attack}} reduced from '''45''' >>> '''25'''.
summary: Lady of the House is an uncommon [[Melting Remnant]] [[banner unit]]. She has high stats and gains a extra {{Attack|+5}} for each stack of {{IconLink|Burnout}} she has, but she starts with {{IconLink|Burnout|3}}, meaning that she will die after a few turns if you cannot apply more.

title: Lady of the Reformed

flavor.value: In a move towards self fulfillment, these Waxers have become part of the Reformed, seeking wealth in the spirit. Despite their high spiritual ranking. I can't say that they are the most welcoming of Hellborne.

tables: '''Titanstone''' grants {{IconLink|Titanite}}, which helps keep '''Lady of the Reformed''' alive and lets her tank for longer without being Reformed.

'''Dualstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Burnout}} she applies on {{IconLink|Revenge}}. This is usually unnecessary, but it is an extremely strong choice if you are using her to scale Lady of the House.
'''Heartstone''' provides a cheap boost to her {{Health}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Lady of the Reformed is an uncommon [[Melting Remnant]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever she takes damage, she grants a stack of {{IconLink|Burnout}} to all friendly units on the floor which already have {{IconLink|Burnout}}, including herself.

title: Paraffin Enforcer

flavor.value: Once a footsoldier has been promoted to an Enforcer, they are no longer considered the punching bags of the Wickless Remains. But that doesn't mean that they won't haze new recruits the same way they were.

tables: '''Dualstone''' increases the {{IconLink|Rage}} applied on {{IconLink|Strike}} from 3 to 6.

'''Wickstone''' makes '''Paraffin Enforcer''''s {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger buff himself, too. However, you will need a consistent source of {{IconLink|Burnout}} (like [[Lady of the Reformed]]) or [[Reform]] to keep him alive after giving him {{IconLink|Burnout|1}}.
'''Frenzystone''' allows for multiple {{IconLink|Strike}} procs per turn.
'''Speedstone''' guarantees that the unit will act first, applying {{IconLink|Rage}} to the other units before they attack. This is especially useful with [[Hallowed Halls]].
'''Smidgestone''' lets you fit more {{IconLink|Burnout}} units on his floor. It also lets you duplicate the unit if you have floor-wide {{IconLink|Burnout}} application like [[Waxen Spike]].
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Paraffin Enforcer is an uncommon [[Melting Remnant]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever he attacks, he grants {{IconLink|Rage}} to all friendly units on the floor which have {{IconLink|Burnout}}, including himself if he has {{IconLink|Burnout}}.

title: Paraffin Thug

flavor.value: A part of the Wickless Remains who have shaped themselves into lowly foot soldiers. They collect the remains of those they slay to add to their own, and they'll pick a fight with you to get it. Even though I am without wax, I've still been the target of many Wickless hasslings.

tables: '''Paraffin Thug''' is an early-game unit, and '''Largestone''' is an early-game upgrade. This grants him a much beefier statline of {{AttackHealth|55|60}} and can let you breeze through the first few rings while triggering {{IconLink|Slay}} several times. If he can get at least four kills, you will have made back all the {{Gold}} spent on this upgrade, and any kills beyond that are pure profit. '''Strengthstone''' can be added as a cheap secondary upgrade, as it will give him enough {{Attack}} to kill a [[Fallen Champion]] from full health, virtually guaranteeing that he gets a {{IconLink|Slay}} trigger every turn. Since it's unlikely for him to be important to your build later on, the increased {{Capacity}} and opportunity cost don't matter.

'''Frenzystone''' gives '''Paraffin Thug''' two hits per turn, making it easier for him to trigger {{IconLink|Slay}}. This upgrade might be better served on a unit that will be more useful to you later in the game, however.
'''Speedstone''' lets '''Paraffin Thug''' attack before enemies, providing some security against his very poor {{Health|10}}.

If you have '''[[Reform]]''' synergies, like [[Primitive Mold]]s or '''Dark Calling''' [[Rector Flicker]], '''Wickstone''' can be a solid choice. It provides as much {{Attack}} as '''Largestone''', but is cheaper, easier to find, and still lets him hide behind a [[Shield Steward]]. Any time he dies and comes back, he will get a little bit stronger, making it easier to get kills.

Though only available with the [[Awoken]], '''Thornstone''' can be an oddly solid choice, especially in combination with '''Largestone''' or '''Heartstone'''. It will fall off quickly, but the {{IconLink|Spikes}} and {{Health}} granted can earn you a ''lot'' of {{Gold}} across the first three combats, which you can use to snowball into a victory.
summary: Paraffin Thug is an uncommon [[Melting Remnant]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever he kills an enemy, he grants the player {{Gold|30}}.

title: Wickless Baron

flavor.value: Some Waxers would prefer to stay in this Ring of Hell, finding their current predicament to be rather comfortable. Even fewer will decide to make that choice more permanent by removing their wicks entirely.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' grants {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, effectively doubling your {{Attack}} scaling and making it much easier for '''Wickless Baron''' to deal out lethal damage.

'''Smidgestone''' is a strong consideration on '''Wickless Baron''', since all copies on a given floor will scale equally from {{IconLink|Harvest}}. It can also help make up for a lack of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} if you are not offered '''Frenzystone''', though this requires more {{DeploymentEmber}}.

'''Titanstone''' halves all incoming damage, making '''Wickless Baron''' much sturdier, allowing him to stick around more easily during the first few turns in order to start scaling his {{Health}}. It also lets him take twice as many hits during {{IconLink|Relentless}}, effectively doubling his {{Attack}} output during it.

'''Immortalstone''' makes you able to resummon '''Wickless Baron''' should he perish, without dealing with {{IconLink|Burnout}}. Remember that '''Wickless Baron''' keeps all {{Health}} and {{Attack}} gained during the combat.
summary: Wickless Baron is an uncommon [[Melting Remnant]] [[banner unit]]. He gains {{AttackHealth|+5|+5}} on {{IconLink|Harvest}}.

title: Wickless Tycoon

flavor.value: These wealthy residents of Hell are considered among the few to reside in the upper echelon of Remnant Society. They pay the bills for the endeavors of the Wickless, partial to the benefits it allows them. And since the Rail has brought them much business, some of that coin has made its way to our train.

tables: '''Smidgestone''' makes it easier to fit the '''Wickless Tycoon''' in, leaving more space to trigger {{IconLink|Harvest}} or fit in other {{IconLink|Harvest}} units.
The {{IconLink|Titanite}} granted by '''Titanstone''' makes him a much more durable tank.
'''Heartstone''' can increase his {{Health}}, allowing him to double as a reasonably effective tank.
summary: Wickless Tycoon is an uncommon [[Melting Remnant]] [[banner unit]]. He grants the player {{Gold|10}} whenever any unit (except himself) dies on his floor.

title: Devourer of Death

ability.value:
{{IconLink|Harvest}}: Gain {{IconLink|Soul|1}}.
{{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Deal damage to enemy units equal to 15x the {{IconLink|Soul}} count.

flavor.value: The unfortunate souls who are unable to melt must instead feed off the deaths of those around them. They accumulate more energy as others souls are freed from their waxen forms, but they are doomed to never be able to free their own.

tables: '''Dualstone''' doubles the amount of {{IconLink|Soul}} generated on {{IconLink|Harvest}}, doubling the Devourer's damage output.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Devourer of Death is a rare [[Melting Remnant]] unit. Whenever another unit dies on its floor, it gathers {{IconLink|Soul}}, which it unleashes in a destructive blast when it is killed.

title: Formless Child

ability.value: {{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Return a random defeated unit to your hand and apply {{Attack|+40}}.

flavor.value: Children are rarely seen in the Melting Remnant, but they're easy to spot by their transparent wax and inner glow. However, this unusual phenomenon makes these children less mobile, as this glass-like wax isn't very flexible.

tables: '''Immortalstone''' can allow you to play '''Formless Child''' every turn. However, this prevents it from being Reformed itself (and then dying to {{IconLink|Burnout}} to Reform another unit) and means it will retain its high cost at {{Ember|2}}. It may be helpful or harmful depending on the rest of your deck.

'''Worthy Sacrifice''' can allow you to infinite into a second copy of '''Formless Child''' with '''Worthy Sacrifice''' producing infinite {{Ember}} and scaling their {{Attack}} as much as wanted. With a {{IconLink|Harvest}} / {{IconLink|Rally}} unit or artifact you can convert this infinite to other effects.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Formless Child is a rare [[Melting Remnant]] unit. It does nothing on its own, but when killed it returns a random defeated unit to your hand with {{Attack|+40}}. This resurrection is not a [[Reform]], so no {{IconLink|Burnout}} is added.

title: Big Sludge

flavor.value: Even wax dripping has its limits. While it makes the target incredibly large and near unkillable, it also forces them into an eternal state of dripping. Wick or no, this compels them to continue to gutter more and more wax if their wish to retain this power.

tables: '''Frenzystone''' lets '''Big Sludge''' hit twice, taking advantage of his incredibly high damage potential.
'''Smidgestone''' allows '''Big Sludge''' to fit far more easily behind your other units, allowing him to remain safe and rack up {{IconLink|Harvest}} triggers faster.

'''Speedstone''' can act as a pseudo-defensive upgrade, killing enemies before they can kill you. With any source of {{IconLink|Trample}} and a strong {{IconLink|Harvest}} engine, '''Big Sludge''' can take out whole waves of enemies before they attack. However, this might make it harder for your other units to die quickly, limiting how many {{IconLink|Harvest}} triggers he can get.
'''Dualstone''' can double the amount of {{IconLink|Rage}} gained on {{IconLink|Harvest}}, scaling up '''Big Sludge''''s {{Attack}} twice as fast.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Big Sludge is a rare [[Melting Remnant]] [[banner unit]]. He gains {{IconLink|Rage|5}} whenever a unit dies on his floor.

title: Bounty Stalker

flavor.value: Contracted assassins often employed by the Wickless to accomplish what even they cannot. Their incredible prowess in hunting Waxers has made them feared across the entire Ring, from Reformed to Wickless alike. I can't say I much like them myself.

tables: '''Immortalstone''' is by far the most important upgrade for '''Bounty Stalker'''. This allows him to die to his own {{IconLink|Burnout}} and gain {{Attack|+10}} permanently every turn and eliminates the need for Reform effects. He gain easily gain an {{Attack}} stat in the hundreds this way.
'''Frenzystone''' doubles the benefit of his enormous {{Attack}} scaling, and should be a high priority if offered.

'''Burststone''' is only available with the [[Railforged]], but is arguably even stronger than '''Frenzystone''' on '''Bounty Stalker''' when combined with a source of {{IconLink|Endless}}. Since the {{IconLink|Burst|2}} will be reset every time he dies, this is effectively like applying two '''Frenzystones''', and '''Burststone''' is both much cheaper and guaranteed to be available with a reroll. It only comes out worse in prolonged {{IconLink|Relentless}} combats, but even then [[Bounty Stalker]]'s tremendous {{Attack}} should make short work of bosses regardless.

All three upgrades from the [[Inscryption]] event are very powerful on '''Bounty Stalker'''. '''Worthy Sacrifice''' eliminates any worries about efficiently scaling him or making him {{IconLink|Endless}} and instead makes [[Reform]] much stronger, as he can be instantly killed the moment he is drawn and then [[Reform]]ed with a card like [[Molded]], for permanent {{Attack}} scaling and {{Ember|3}} all at once. '''Many Lives''' grants him {{IconLink|Reanimate|3}}, which is an improvement upon his normal scaling; his {{IconLink|Extinguish}} trigger will activate four times over two turns instead of two, and if he is {{IconLink|Endless}} you will not need to re-draw him every turn. '''Fecundity''' is only really useful in the late game, but it is ''extremely'' useful then, granting an additional copy of '''Bounty Stalker''' with his tremendous {{Attack}} already scaled.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
Attack increased from 10 to 30. Attack gain on {{IconLink|Extinguish}} increased from 8 permanent attack to 10 permanent attack. Gained {{IconLink|Burnout|1}} (not in patch notes).
summary: Bounty Stalker is a rare [[Melting Remnant]] [[banner unit]]. He gains {{Attack|+10}} permanently each time he dies, and enters with both {{IconLink|Stealth}} and {{IconLink|Burnout}}.

title: Legion of Wax

ability.value: {{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Summon '''2 Twin of Wax''' and apply this unit's upgrades, equipment, and stat changes.

flavor.value: When Waxers are reduced to almost nothing, but still cling to what life is left within, they will sometimes band together for protection. This creates a new form that is collectively controlled by this collection of dying Waxers.

tables: With '''Smidgestone''', '''Legion of Wax''' becomes a {{Capacity|1}} unit, as do the '''Twins of Wax'''. This makes '''Legion of Wax''' much easier to summon, as well as to resummon with [[Reform]]. In addition, it makes '''Legion of Wax''' an even better recipient of [[Overgrowth Carapace]].
'''Twin of Wax''' and '''Mote of Wax''' inherit the {{IconLink|Multistrike}} from '''Frenzystone''', so this upgrade often represents a lot of additional attacks.

If '''Legion of Wax''' is meant to be resummoned frequently, e.g. via [[Primitive Mold]] or [[Rector Flicker]]'s '''Dark Calling''' path, then having it start with {{IconLink|Burnout|1}} can make this much easier. In addition, the {{AttackHealth|+15/+5}} stat bonuses are passed on to the '''Twins of Wax''' and '''Motes of Wax''', although the {{IconLink|Burnout}} is as well.

The immense {{AttackHealth|+15/+50}} stat bonuses of '''Largestone''' are passed on to the '''Twins of Wax''' and '''Motes of Wax''', as is the {{Capacity|+1}}. Note that if your deck relies on the summoned units to deal damage, then you'll need a way to kill '''Legion of Wax''' on command, such as [[Resin Blades]], or the [[Intent on Death]] card to trigger its {{IconLink|Extinguish}} effect without killing it.

'''Speedstone''' grants {{IconLink|Quick}}, which is very useful if you are trying to keep '''Legion of Wax''' at low {{Health}} for ease of dying. It helps the '''Motes of Wax''' attack before enemies get a chance to kill them.

Obtained from the [[Inscryption]] event, both '''Many Lives''' and '''Worthy Sacrifice''' are ridiculously powerful on '''Legion of Wax'''. '''Many Lives''' makes it virtually unkillable, since each spawned unit will also have {{IconLink|Reanimate|3}}. '''Worthy Sacrifice''' enables you to kill it off whenever you choose and gain {{Ember|3}} for doing so, and you can even instantly kill off the '''Twins of Wax''' as well for {{Ember|9}} total and four active '''Motes of Wax''' - if wanted e.g. for an X-cost card, you can instakill the '''Motes of Wax''' too for a total of {{Ember|21}}! {{IconLink|Fecundity}} is quite potent too, although the second copy will be rather expensive to play at {{Ember|3}} and it should not be prioritized over the other two.

While nowhere near as powerful as '''Many Lives''', '''Frankenstone''' is still a viable choice if using it as a tank; a '''Legion of Wax''' with a single '''Frankenstone''' will be able to tank 42 hits, with two it can tank 129 hits.

'''Discarded Wings''' helps '''Legion of Wax''' get around its {{Capacity}} issues, especially in tandem with [[Intent on Death]] or {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. The '''Twins''' and '''Motes of Wax''' inherit the Flight ability and are summoned with a refreshed ability cooldown, so they can simply be flown to other floors until the train is full to bursting with '''Motes of Wax'''.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
[[Legion of Wax]] base stats increased from {{AttackHealth|8/8}} >>> {{AttackHealth|16/16}}. (Smaller versions updated to match).
Fixed a bug when activating the {{IconLink|Worthy Sacrifice|bold=f}} ability on [[Legion of Wax]] wouldn't work.

*Fixed bug where spawner-type units like [[Legion of Wax]] could spawn in the wrong location if another unit on the floor died during combat during the same turn the spawn/hatch happens. This issue dates back to MT1. *Updated behavior of units that split into other units to copy the parent unit's equipment into the spawned unit. This affects [[Legion of Wax]] and [[Bog Chrysalis]] for example.
summary:
{{UnitCard
|name = Twin of Wax
|image = PLR_TwinOfWax.png
|clan = Melting Remnant
|type = Waxer
|size = 2
|stats = 8/8
|ability = {{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Summon 2 Mote of Wax and apply this unit's upgrades, equipment, and stat changes.
|artist = Aaron Lovett
}}

title: Hallowed Drippings

flavor.value: Those of the Melting Remnant who want to continue living must attend a Votive House to receive a Blessing of Wax. But on some rare occasions, the Reformed will grant a soul some of the sacred wax for use outside the House.

tables: '''Stackstone''' doubles the {{IconLink|Burnout}} applied. This probably only makes sense if you have Lady of the House, but if you do it applies {{Attack|+55}} to her.

'''Twinstone''' can achieve the same thing, either with a lot of {{Ember}} or an Ember discount upgrade, and has the benefit of applying {{Attack|+5}} twice. With '''Stackstone''', Lady of the House gets a whopping {{Attack|+110}} in total from this card.

'''Eternalstone''' prevents this card from being Consumed after use. Like other upgrades, this is generally only useful if you are using Lady of the House (ideally, a full floor of them), but it is a good way of continually scaling her.

'''Seekstone''' puts this card in your hand immediately while also reducing it to {{Ember|0}}. This can let you get a head start on scaling Lady of the House, but it can also prevent {{IconLink|Wickstone}} units like [[Paraffin Enforcer]] from dying immediately.

'''Freezestone''' has a somewhat niche use, but it can add a significant amount of {{IconLink|Burnout}} right before {{IconLink|Relentless}}, in case you are using a strategy involving units like [[Bounty Stalker]] or '''Dark Calling''' [[Rector Flicker]]. This lets your units survive several more rounds before burning out.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.

Updated [[Hallowed Drippings]]: "Apply {{IconLink|Burnout|5}} to friendly {{IconLink|Burnout}} units." >>> "Apply {{IconLink|Burnout|5}} and {{Attack|+5}} to friendly {{IconLink|Burnout}} units." Cost increased from {{Ember|0}} >>> {{Ember|1}}.
summary: Hallowed Drippings is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Burnout|5}} and {{Attack|+5}} to all friendly units on the floor which already have at least {{IconLink|Burnout|1}}.

title: Purifying Cleanse

effect.value: Restore '''15''' health and apply {{IconLink|Burnout|3}} to a friendly unit.

flavor.value: Before entering a wax drip and applying new wax, a process I've been told is called "guttering", Waxers are asked to cleanse themselves of any blemishes and impurities to keep the wax as clean as possible.

tables: Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Purifying Cleanse is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It heals {{Health|15}} and applies {{IconLink|Burnout|3}}. Like all {{IconLink|Burnout}} spells, it can only be played on friendly units.

title: Dripfall

flavor.value: ''While Wax Drips are beneficial for those who refuse to melt, getting caught in the downfall can have violent consequences. Consequently, I've decided only to study them from a safe distance.''

tables: '''Twinstone''', coupled with an {{Ember}} discount, can double this card's disruptive power, either on the same target or different ones.
'''Stackstone''' increases this card's utility against [[Flying Bosses]] by keeping them {{IconLink|Dazed}} for one more turn.

'''Keepstone''' lets you draw this card every turn, allowing you to keep a single enemy on lockdown for the entire fight. This is especially useful against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], or against dangerous backline units like [[Chosen Assassin]]s or [[Chosen Supplicant]]s.
'''Emberstone''' is fairly practical here for {{Ember|-1}} on use, especially with '''Twinstone'''.

'''Seekstone''', especially with '''Twinstone''', is great for a floor overstacking card, and this card can be used that way if needed. '''Dripfall''' isn't the most practical card for this purpose, but perhaps you could use it to overstack on the second floor, dropping units from the third floor, so that the {{IconLink|Dazed}} turn doesn't matter. Alternatively, if you have a large enough bottom floor, the one-turn {{IconLink|Dazed}} may not matter.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Dripfall is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It [[Descend]]s a unit and applies {{IconLink|Dazed|1}}.

title: Molded

flavor.value: Once a Waxer has melted away, only the wick remains. Should these Waxers choose to return to their previous forms, the Reformed will pour new wax into the original molds to revive the remaining wicks' soul.

tables: '''Freezestone''' can be applied to this card to ensure that you can reform any unit precisely when you need to.
'''Keepstone''' is a reliable way for certain builds to just reform the same unit over and over every turn. This makes no additional demands on your Reform pool.
'''Twinstone''' can be added if there's a pair of key units you need together, or just as an alternative to duplicating the card if you need more Reform effects in general.
This card sees heavy play in most builds it's part of, especially with '''Keepstone''' or '''Twinstone''', so '''Emberstone''' saves quite a bit of {{Ember}}.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Molded is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It [[Reform]]s a unit of your choice.

title: Wicklash

effect.value: Apply {{Attack|+10}} and {{IconLink|Burnout|2}} to a friendly unit.

flavor.value: Those who truly cannot wait for their wax to melt can fasten additional wicks to their bodies, ensuring they burn with a brief, but beautiful, light.

tables: '''Twinstone''' lets you play this card twice per turn. Unlike cards like [[Razorsharp Edge]], this card actually gets better the more you play it on a single unit, since the {{IconLink|Burnout}} applied will keep the unit alive for much longer. '''Emberstone''' goes nicely with this, bringing the cost of playing both copies down from {{Ember|2}} to {{Ember|0}}.
'''Keepstone''' can also be a way to consistently scale a unit throughout the battle.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Wicklash is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It applies {{Attack|+10}} and {{IconLink|Burnout|2}} to a friendly unit.

title: Sacred Wicks

flavor.value: While a soul of the Melting Remnant can be reformed in waxen molds, they are not truly reborn until they are given a new wick. The Reformed treat the practice of this ritual as highly sacred and secretive and I've been able to record little of its specifics.

tables: '''Freezestone''' addresses this card's tendency to appear on turn 1, letting you save it until you need it, as well as generally helping smooth out draw order problems that Reform engines can have.
'''Twinstone''' is easy to add from an {{Ember}} standpoint. The challenge is having 4 units to Reform, but if you do, this value this provides is immense.
'''Eternalstone''' keeps this card around so that your Reform economy remains strong after playing it, and allows you to start purging less efficient Reform cards more zealously.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Sacred Wicks is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It [[Reform]]s two random units.

title: Crushing Demise

effect.value:
Kill a random non-boss enemy unit.
Kill a random friendly unit.

flavor.value: A hazard of guttering at a Votive House is the melding together of various Waxers into a massive, uncontrollable boulder that will kill anything in its path.

tables: '''Twinstone''' lets you use it twice, increasing both its consistency and power in clearing waves with tanky enemies.
'''Keepstone''' can be used to use it as a consistent strategy for dealing with heavy tanks that otherwise threaten your Pyre.

An {{Ember}} discount works well with either of the above or on its own, and '''Seekstone''' and '''Freezestone''' both have their merits given how timing-specific this spell is - '''Seekstone''' for aiding decks that need time to scale and '''Freezestone''' for a specific problem wave.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Crushing Demise is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It instantly kills a random enemy unit on the floor where it is played, along with a random friendly unit.

title: Resin Removal

effect.value: Remove all '''[[Debuff]]''' effects from friendly units and all '''[[Buff]]''' effects from enemy units.

flavor.value: When wax hardens into resin, it is possible to chip away the crystallized exterior to expose the soft wax underneath. The process does not come without risks, though.

tables: '''Keepstone''' allows you to take advantage of this spell's powerful effect every turn, which is especially useful when being constantly bombarded by {{IconLink|Corruption}}.

'''Seekstone''' lets you play this card immediately, which is very useful against Savagery Seraph's {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}}. It also reduces the card's {{Ember}} cost, making it more affordable with the aforementioned '''Keepstone''' if you plan to play it every turn. '''Emberstone''' serves the same purpose.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Resin Removal is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It removes all [[Debuff]]s (red status effects) from friendly units on a given floor, and removes all [[Buff]]s (green status effects) from all enemies on that floor.

title: A Fatal Melting

effect.value: Deal damage to enemy units equal to '''3x''' the number of friendly unit deaths this battle.

flavor.value: Charged with both the extension of life and the acceleration of melting, the Reformed tend to large flames at each Votive House, allowing for Waxers to congregate and melt more quickly than they would on their own.

tables: '''Powerstone''' lets this spell hit weaker backliners even on turn 1.

'''Surgestone''' gives it [[Consume]] and lets you hit [[Discordant Heretic]]. [[Consume]] means you won't be able to take advantage of it powering up later in the fight, but as mentioned, that usually isn't that important.
'''Smolderstone''' gives it [[Consume]] and defrays its {{Ember}} cost, making it easier to play.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: A Fatal Melting is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It deals damage to all enemies on the floor equal to 3x the number of friendly unit deaths this battle.

title: Engulfed in Smoke

flavor.value: In the dangerous depths of Hell, it's important to have the means for quick concealment. If needed, I've found that wicks bundled together will burn slowly and create large quantities of smoke.

tables: '''Keepstone''' lets you cast this spell every turn, building up lots of {{IconLink|Stealth}} to protect your units even into {{IconLink|Relentless}}.
'''Stackstone''' makes this card apply {{IconLink|Stealth|4}}, for four turns of protection.
'''Emberstone''' defangs the card's cost, making it much easier to play repeatedly.

'''Seekstone''' is very useful, granting your units protection from the jump and also making it cost {{Ember|1}}. It's especially useful with '''Keepstone''', ensuring you can keep up {{IconLink|Stealth}} for the entire combat.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Engulfed in Smoke is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Stealth}} to all friendly units on the floor, protecting them from being targeted by enemy attacks.

title: Subsuming Blade

flavor.value: This blade grows larger with each use, slowly accumulating more wax and becoming more dangerous. Reluctantly, I created it with the Wickless when Hell was invaded to defend against the advancing Winged.

tables: '''Keepstone''' lets you keep scaling this spell while also making it available every turn.
'''Emberstone''' or '''Seekstone''' is very good on a spell you want to use often, with '''Seekstone''' providing the added bonus of giving you access to it from the start of combat.
'''Twinstone''' can let you hit two enemies if you have {{Ember}} under control with e.g. [[Boiler Room]] or have [[Lightstone Casing]]. (The copy won't scale the original.)
summary: Subsuming Blade is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It starts by dealing 5 [[Piercing]] damage and permanently adds 3 to its damage on {{IconLink|Slay}}.

title: Wicked Blaze

flavor.value: Though not entirely under their control, the burning of a Waxer's wick can accelerate with a great deal of focus and help from other Waxers. The resulting melting wax is then collected and donated to reform one of their kin.

tables: '''Freezestone''' can be applied to this card to ensure that you can reform any unit precisely when you need to.

'''Keepstone''' is a reliable way for certain builds to just reform the same unit over and over every turn. This makes no additional demands on your Reform pool, and can scale your {{Attack}} to impressive heights.
This card sees heavy play in most builds it's part of, but has a hefty {{Ember}} cost, so '''Emberstone''' is often a practical necessity.
'''Twinstone''' is harder to place here than on [[Molded]], but if you have enough {{Ember}} to manage it, it ''is'' quite strong.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Wicked Blaze is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It [[Reform]]s a unit and applies {{Attack|+10}}.

title: Memento Mori

effect.value: Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to '''10x''' the number of friendly unit deaths this battle.

flavor.value: In memory, a Waxer is never truly dead. Through a process we developed together, their faces are embossed on deadly weapons and serve as a reminder of what once was and what will be.

tables: '''Smolderstone''' drastically reduces this card's cost, and also gets it out of your deck after you play it, which is about as useful of an effect as you can hope for with this card. It's usually better to just not draft it in the first place, though.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Memento Mori is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It deals damage to the front enemy unit equal to 10x the number of friendly unit deaths so far this battle.

title: Mortal Entrapment

effect.value:
'''[[Attuned]]'''.
Deal '''25''' damage and apply {{IconLink|Dazed|3}} to an already damaged unit.

flavor.value: While molds are used in the resurrection of Waxen, the invasion of Hell has forced the Waxen to repurpose these molds for a more deadly effect. They are now positioned to trap unsuspecting targets who've already been injured, making them easier to encase in the hot wax.

tables: '''Stackstone''' means that one hit from this card will put an enemy out of commission entirely, or a flying boss for a long, long time.

'''Emberstone''', '''Seekstone''', and '''Freezestone''' all help make this card more affordable. For '''Seekstone''', you will have to have a way to ensure you have another way of damaging your target on turn 1 before you play it, but in exchange you'll be able to shut them down consistently from the start of the fight. '''Freezestone''', meanwhile, prevents you from drawing this card when it's not usable, letting you hold onto it until you can play it.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Mortal Entrapment is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It deals 25 damage, gains 5 extra damage for each point of [[Magic Power]], and applies {{IconLink|Dazed|3}}. However, it can only be used on units which are not at full {{Health}}.

title: Waxen Spike

flavor.value: The alliance of the Rings of Hell also created an alliance between the Reformed and the Wickless Remains, bringing together the separate groups under Flicker. To seal their pact, they created a Railspike from their collective wax and drove it into our Rail.

tables: '''Twinstone''' and '''Stackstone''' accomplish the same purpose, which is increasing the {{IconLink|Burnout}} applied. They are effectively interchangeable for this purpose, since it can be played at {{Ember|0}} and still grant {{IconLink|Burnout}}. You can even use both, which will let you apply {{IconLink|Burnout|16}} for one card and potentially {{Ember|0}}.
'''Seekstone''' ensures that you will have this card in your opening hand, which is great for Paraffin Enforcer builds to ensure you won't miss a single turn of scaling.

'''Eternalstone''' lets you hold onto this card if you need to play it repeatedly. This may be necessary if it's your only method of {{IconLink|Burnout}} application, in which case it's probably a good idea to duplicate it as well. If you already have Eternalstone, {{IconLink|Smolderstone}} can provide an extra {{Attack|+8}} to the entire floor each time it is played.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Waxen Spike is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It boosts the {{Attack}} of friendly units and gives them {{IconLink|Burnout|4}}.

title: Sacrificial Resurrection

effect.value: '''[[Consume]]''' cards in hand. Add a '''[[Draff]]''' unit to your hand and apply {{Attack|+10}} for each card consumed.

flavor.value: When new wax is unavailable to reform a fallen Waxer, the more selfless Reformed choose to donate a portion of their own form to the resurrection.

tables: '''Freezestone''' can help you line up this card with the cards you're looking to [[Consume]] with it like [[Vengeful Shard]], allowing you to trim your deck more reliably. It also means you don't have to spend a draw re-drawing this card once you've [[Consume]]d everything you intend to.
'''Keepstone''' is also useful, especially if you're looking to boil a large deck down to a small number of cards quickly, for e.g. [[Infinite]]s.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
Fixed bug where stats granted through [[Sacrificial Resurrection]] or [[Prism Retrieval]] would not carry over to a [[Reform|reformed]] unit.
summary: Sacrificial Resurrection is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It sends all other cards in hand to the Consume pile, including those which cannot ordinarily be consumed. It then adds a [[Draff]] to the player's hand, and adds {{Attack|+10}} for each card consumed.

title: Wickless Recruitment

effect.value: Remove all {{IconLink|Burnout}} and '''[[Debuff]]''' effects on a unit.

flavor.value: ''Initiation into the Wickless Remains is a rite performed in the underbelly of the Waxen Arches, involving the sacrifice of a Waxer's wick to forever tie them to their hellish homeland. Even after the many I've witnessed, the ritual still gives me pause.''

tables: '''Twinstone''' lets you play '''Wickless Recruitment''' on two different units, making it function a bit more like Resin Removal.
'''Keepstone''' lets you play this card every turn, if you need consistent debuff removal.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Wickless Recruitment is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It removes all [[Debuff]]s from a given unit, along with all {{IconLink|Burnout}}.

title: Intent on Death

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Trigger a unit's {{IconLink|Extinguish}} ability without killing it.

flavor.value: Votive Houses can become crowded and melting away is a long process. To avoid the wait, I've seen some Waxers increase the intensity of their flame through extreme focus, though they typically lose consciousness briefly after doing it.

tables: '''Eternalstone''' prevents this card from disappearing after its first use. Decks that want to make use of this card can generally make use of it more than once, so keeping it around tends to be positive.
'''Emberstone''' makes this card free. {{IconLink|Seekstone}} and {{IconLink|Freezestone}} have the same effect and some other perks, but are more expensive and not guaranteed.
'''Twinstone''' allows you to trigger {{IconLink|Extinguish}} twice. If you have reduced the card's cost with '''Emberstone''', this is often quite useful.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Intent on Death is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It activates a unit's {{IconLink|Extinguish}} ability while keeping the unit alive.

title: Remnant Pact

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Apply {{IconLink|Endless}} to a friendly unit for the rest of the battle.

flavor.value: Despite their age-long feud, the Wickless and the Reformed were able to come to an armistice when the Covenant was formed. That doesn't mean that the rules put in place for their peace were easy to follow.

tables: '''Seekstone''' can be a valuable way to make sure that you can rely on your intended target having {{IconLink|Endless}}. This can be particularly valuable against hard-hitting enemies like [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]] that won't wait to kill your units.

'''Freezestone''' is excellent in combination with '''Seekstone''' if you intend to apply {{IconLink|Endless}} to a unit that you are not necessarily guaranteed to see on turn one, like [[Green Recruit]] or [[Transcendimp]]. This lets you hold onto the card until you need it.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
[[Remnant Pact]] updated to clarify "for the rest of battle."
summary: Remnant Pact is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It grants {{IconLink|Endless}} to the chosen unit.

title: Hallowed Halls

effect.value:
Kill friendly units.
'''[[Reform]]''' random units to this floor until it exceeds its {{Capacity}}.

flavor.value: ''Wurmkin stoneform speaks of passageways deep below those controlled by the Wickless, further even than the caverns of the Reformed. These halls of stone sleep in the dark, their floors covered in the wicks of lost Waxers. Should Wax ever fall from the Ring above, and flame come to the wicks that lay there, a soul is said to live again for a brief moment of time. In my darkest nightmares, I rest in these wicked halls forever flickering between life and death.''
