tables: '''Keepstone''' is the most important upgrade for this spell, allowing it to be played every turn. This should always be added if possible, unless you are ''very'' confident in your ability to fill your deck with copies of this spell or thin it down enough to draw it every turn.
'''Seekstone''' guarantees that you will be able to play '''Hallowed Halls''' from the very beginning of combat, as well as decreasing its cost.

'''Twinstone''' allows '''Hallowed Halls''' to be played twice each turn. This is best with a small deck, where '''Seekstone''' is less important, or if you have [[Lightstone Casing]]. A [[Boiler Room]] can give you enough {{Ember}} to play the spell multiple times each turn, which is otherwise difficult due to its {{Ember|3}} cost.

The combination of '''Smolderstone''' and '''Eternalstone''' reduces this card's cost to {{Ember|1}}, making it much more affordable if you have a way of making lots of duplicates of it. Keep in mind that '''Smolderstone''' on its own is usually fairly bad due to adding '''[[Consume]]''', but you cannot apply '''Eternalstone''' unless you have already applied '''Smolderstone''', so this combination of upgrades can be hard to pull off. [[Lifemother's Pyre]] makes this upgrade set much more desirable, as once you have a {{Ember|1}} '''Hallowed Halls''', you can simply focus all your {{Gold}} on duplicating it as much as possible, especially if you have Wickless Tycoon or [[Memorial Fund]].

As an alternative to the above, you can simply add two {{Ember}}-reducing upgrades instead, like '''Emberstone''', '''Freezestone''', or the aforementioned '''Seekstone'''. This is easier to pull off, but might require visiting two [[Merchant of Magic|Merchants of Magic]]. Like the above, this is a much better choice with Lifemother's Pyre for on-demand duplication.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
Fixed [[Hallowed Halls]] failing to put cards back in the Consumed pile if the units die while being spawned. Originally reported in the context of [[Curse of Friendly Fire]] endless mode artifact.
summary: Hallowed Halls is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It instantly kills all friendly units on the floor, then [[Reform]]s units at random until either there are none left to Reform, or the floor is overstacked. It can Reform the same units which it just killed. Units are killed from right to left, which can be important when considering {{IconLink|Extinguish}} or {{IconLink|Harvest}} triggers.

title: Resin Blades

effect.value:
{{IconLink|Burnout|1}}.
{{IconLink|Multistrike|1}}.
Return to hand when equipped unit is destroyed.

flavor.value: It is because of blades such as these that the Reformed lament the process of molding the remains of their brethren into new weapons. They understand that each time the steel reforms itself, the trapped soul within the wax is struggling to be free.

summary: Resin Blades is a rare [[Melting Remnant]] equipment added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It grants a unit {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} and {{IconLink|Burnout|1}}. Additionally, unlike other equipment, it is immediately returned to your hand when the equipped unit dies.

title: Memorial for the Melted

flavor.value: The Reformed, a group of Waxers dedicated to the melting of others, believe in respecting the already melted. The Reformed keep the wicks of each Waxer they've helped to melt, burning the wicks briefly to remind themselves of their own impermanence, but extinguishing the wicks quickly to remember that their purpose is not yet fulfilled.

tables: [[Memories of the Melted]] updated from Spell >>> Room. Renamed to "[[Memorial for the Melted]]". "Gain {{Ember|1}} for each friendly unit death this battle." >>> "Friendly units have {{IconLink|Endless}}." Cost increased from {{Ember|0}} >>> {{Ember|1}}.
summary: Memorial for the Melted is an uncommon [[Melting Remnant]] room added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update, replacing [[Memories of the Melted]]. It grants friendly units {{IconLink|Endless}}.

title: Clanless
summary: Clanless [[file:ClanClanless.png|20x20px]] cards are [[Cards]] that do not belong to any specific clan, and can therefore be acquired on any given run. In the case of [[Spells]] and [[Units]], these cards are typically acquired from [[Celestial Alcove|Celestial Alcoves]], while [[Equipment]] and [[Rooms]] can be obtained from drafts and the [[Merchants#Merchant_of_Arms|Merchant of Arms]] as normal.

title: Shield Steward

flavor.value: ''After the Boneshaker disappeared, Heph took it upon herself to build upon her father's work. The bulkier train steward design is one of the results of her efforts.''

tables: '''Strengthstone''' and '''Heartstone''' are cheap upgrades that provide a lot of security into the early game, if you can spare around {{Gold|40}}. They might let you survive [[Legion]] or [[Elebor the Wall]] where you would otherwise die. Most other clan-specific upgrades, like {{IconLink|Bravestone}}, {{IconLink|Mossystone}}, and {{IconLink|Furystone}} will accomplish roughly the same job, so you don't need to reroll the shop.

Assuming you have [[Steward's Quarters]], '''Frenzystone''' gives '''Shield Steward''' {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}}, allowing it to scale quite well with {{Attack}} buffs. Be absolutely certain you don't have a better unit to take this upgrade, though.
Assuming you have [[Steward's Quarters]], '''Smidgestone''' can help you assemble a room full of '''Shield Stewards'''.

If find the [[Beacon]] event and you do not want to take [[Beacon's Light]], '''Purified Essence''' provides a tremendous stat boost with no downside, since '''Shield Steward''' already has no card text. This can be an especially good choice if this event comes just before the Ring 3 boss, and can let the unit still serve decently into the later game.
summary: The Shield Steward is an common [[Clanless]] banner unit. Each run starts with two of them. It has no special abilities.

title: Spear Steward

flavor.value: The original Boneshaker was built during a time of peace. Herzal had the foresight to build several sentient guards should the worst come to happen. In the end, they've proved quite useful.

tables: Assuming you have [[Steward's Quarters]], this gives '''Shield Steward''' {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}}, allowing it to scale quite well with {{Attack}} buffs.

Assuming you have [[Steward's Quarters]], you will need to account for how fragile this unit is against {{IconLink|Sweep}}, {{IconLink|Spikes}} and backline {{IconLink|Corruption}}, and Heartstone can do that.
summary: The Spear Steward is a common [[Clanless]] banner unit. Each run starts with two of them.

title: Bone Dog

flavor.value: This cute pup appeared when I hammered the Covenant Outpost's first nail. I could not leave him behind. Also, his [[Bone Dog's Pendant|collar]] seemed familiar... It looked like the work of a certain forger I once knew.

tables: '''Heartstone''' or similar upgrades can make '''Bone Dog''' less fragile and help him survive the fight.
summary: The Bone Dog is a rare [[Clanless]] unit. It is obtained at a [[Celestial Alcove]] event, as an alternative to [[Bone Dog's Pendant]].

title: Follower

flavor.value: Every cult needs its leader and a loyal flock of followers. The devotees of this cult pledge their devotion to whoever bears the Red Crown.

tables: '''Largestone''' provides both {{Attack}} and {{Health}}, allowing the '''Follower''' to survive for longer and deal much more damage. Its tiny starting size makes this upgrade's size increase easier to deal with.
'''Speedstone''' provides an {{Attack}} boost as well as {{IconLink|Quick}}, allowing it to attack before enemies and making up for its low {{Health}}.

'''Strengthstone''' is a very cheap upgrade which can turn the '''Follower''' into a powerful damage dealer at little cost. If you are focusing your upgrades on one '''Follower''', then it is usually worth putting a cheap upgrade like '''Strengthstone''' on the other.
summary: The Follower is a common [[Clanless]] unit, obtained only from the [[Cult of the Lamb]] event. It has very low stats but starts with {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}}.

title: Jack in the Box

flavor.value: A well-crafted music box with a surprise inside!

tables: Fixed {{IconLink|Graft}} + [[Jack in the Box]] interaction if the box gets duplicated or upgraded with {{IconLink|Endless}}.
Added {{IconLink|Cardless}} state to [[Jack in the Box]] units when they spawn.
summary: {{version}}

title: Dante the Dependable

ability.value: {{IconLink|Summon}}: Add a permanent '''[[Dante's Candle]]''' to your deck. Gain a stack of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} for each Blight card in your deck.

flavor.value: Dante, the only man who can sip tea with an angel at noon and share a pint with a demon by dusk. Heaven and Hell are just stops on his cultural itinerary, each with its own charms to savor.

tables: '''Largestone''' adds much needed base stats to '''Dante''', improving survivability and multiplying the effectiveness of {{IconLink|Multistrike}}.
'''Speedstone''' can be a pseudo-defensive upgrade by killing enemies before they are able to attack, while also giving him a small but appreciable {{Attack}} boost.

'''Strengthstone''' multiplies the effectiveness of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} by granting '''Dante''' a respectable amount of {{Attack}}, and it's a cheap upgrade that is always guaranteed in the shop if you can afford a reroll. Depending on your secondary clan, '''Furystone''' and '''Wickstone''' will accomplish a similar purpose.

'''Immortalstone''' allows '''Dante''' to be summoned multiple times per battle, filling your deck with additional copies of [[Dante's Candle]]. This will power up '''Dante''' himself, as well as [[Dante's Inferno]] and any other [[Blight]] synergies the player may have.

Although '''Dualstone''' may seem strange, since '''Dante''' cannot naturally benefit from it, it will double the effects of Buffs and Debuffs from any equipment he holds. For example, [[Everlasting Light]] will apply {{IconLink|Valor|4}} to all allies on {{IconLink|Strike}}, and [[Combustion Suit]] will apply {{IconLink|Unstable|10}} to all enemies. This is a niche upgrade, but it has a lot of potential if you know you will be able to make good use out of it.
Dante the Deceptive -> Dante the Dependable, Summon trigger added. {{Ember|1}} -> {{Ember|2}}
summary: Dante the Dependable is a rare [[Clanless]] unit. He is obtainable only from the [[Dante Returns|Celestial Alcove event]]. Once you have played Dante twice, you will get a follow-up event during which you are offered a choice between [[Dante's Inferno]] and [[Dante's Candelabra]].

title: Beacon's Light

effect.value: Apply {{IconLink|Dazed|1}} to enemy units on all floors.

flavor.value: The Beacon's light swallows up every shape and shadow. Those foolish enough to meet its gaze will leave with their senses seared away.

tables: '''Smolderstone''' reduces its cost to a mere {{Ember|1}}, making it significantly easier to play at the cost of granting '''[[Consume]]'''. If you plan to use this card multiple times, adding '''Eternalstone''' will remove the downside of '''Smolderstone''' and makes it a strong duplication target.

'''Seekstone''' and '''Freezestone''' both reduce this card's cost, and can guarantee that you will have it in hand when you need it most if applied together. '''Emberstone''' does not provide either of those upgrades' extra advantages, but still reduces its cost.

'''Stackstone''' lets you apply {{IconLink|Dazed|2}}. This means, among other advantages, that enemies that survive the top floor will still be {{IconLink|Dazed}} when they enter the Pyre room and it will get a free hit on them, potentially killing them before they can attack. It also shuts down flying bosses for longer.

Though it usually requires [[Lightstone Casing]] or an effect like [[Split Anvil]] to be viable, '''Keepstone''' lets this card act as an extremely strong and consistent defense. Note that casting this spell every turn will greatly prolong the Titans fight as you will not get any [[Pyre Light]]s, although this will also shut them down from damaging the Pyre entirely, so you can usually take as long as you want, as long as you can clear the enemy waves and tank [[Entropy]] who is immune to {{IconLink|Dazed}}.
summary: Beacon's Light is a rare [[Clanless]] spell. It can be obtained from the [[Beacon]] event.

title: Dante's Inferno

effect.value:
'''[[Piercing]]'''. '''[[Consume]]'''.
Deal damage to enemy units on all floors equal to '''10x''' the number of '''[[Dante's Candle]]''' cards in your deck.

flavor.value: Little is known of Dante, but what I've seen of his magic puts fear in my heart. I am just glad he is on our side, for now.

tables:
'''Eternalstone''' should be the highest priority for an upgrade on this card. Being able to replay this card is extremely strong on its own, but it enables several synergies that bring it from solid to game-winning. '''Keepstone''' lets you have this card in your hand every turn, hitting the entire train for consistently high damage and easily slaying all but the highest-{{Health}} enemies. '''Smolderstone''', meanwhile, reduces this card to {{Ember|0}}, drastically improving your {{Ember}} economy.

Ideally, with [[Lightstone Casing]], you would have all three of these upgrades active simultaneously. Without it, '''Keepstone''' is probably a better choice than '''Smolderstone'''. This will prevent this spell from being buried in the many copies of Dante's Candle which will fill your deck, and {{Ember|2}} each turn is generally manageable.

With Lightstone Casing and '''Keepstone''', '''Seekstone''' is a reasonable alternative to '''Smolderstone'''. It only reduces the card's cost by {{Ember|1}}, but in exchange it ensures that you can cast it every turn right from the start of the fight.
summary: Dante's Inferno is a rare [[Clanless]] spell. It deals damage to all enemies on the train based on the number of [[Dante's Candle]]s you have in your deck. It is obtained from a follow-up event after acquiring [[Dante the Dependable]].

title: Excavated Ember

flavor.value: ''Even the pressures of time can reverse the effects of calcified Ember. It only takes a worthy soul to carry the load, but one much worthier than myself.''

tables: '''Eternalstone''' removes '''Consume''', allowing the card to be played multiple times per combat, which for streamlined decks allows it to generate a ton of {{Ember}}.

'''Twinstone''' makes this both {{Ember}} and draw-positive. With [[Eternalstone]], this can result in an [[Infinite]] if you can get your whole deck in hand - just play any card, play this, draw your card back and get a copy, play the copy to draw the original, and repeat as needed.
'''Keepstone''' lets you keep playing this each turn, giving you {{Ember|+2}} per turn.
Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' with no changes from the original Monster Train.
summary: Excavated Ember is a common [[Clanless]] spell. It is obtained permanently from [[Perkeo]] (after transforming a specific [[Calcified Ember]]) and temporarily from [[Ember Cache]].

title: Pyre Light

effect.value:
'''Purge'''. '''[[Ephemeral]]'''.
Apply {{Attack|+10}} to the Pyre. The Pyre then attacks immediately.

flavor.value: The Pyre clearly has a mind of its own, as anyone who has been near it will tell you. Perhaps it's the latent mind of the former Titan it once was. Thankfully, it still seems to be on Hell's side.

summary: Pyre Light is a common [[Clanless]] spell. It is obtained from [[Dominion]] as a {{IconLink|Resolve}} effect in the [[Titans]] fight. It cannot be permanently added to the deck or upgraded.

title: Small Gift Box

effect.value:
'''[[Consume]]'''.
Add all '''3''' contained spell cards to your hand.

flavor.value: A gift box with a large card saying: "It isn't the trip, it is the journey. It isn't the gift, it is the container."-Reese P. Taculum

summary: Small Gift Box is an uncommon [[Clanless]] spell. It is obtained from a [[Celestial Alcove]] event, where the player can choose to obtain one of [[Small Gift Box]], [[Jack in the Box]], or [[Large Mystery Box]].

title: Bloodthirsty Blade

flavor.value: Pulled from the embers of the Pyre, legend tells that one day a leader bearing this sword will lead Hell and Heaven to peace.

summary: Bloodthirsty Blade is an uncommon [[Clanless]] equipment. Its {{Attack}} increases by 1 whenever the unit carrying it kills another unit.

title: Exile's Diadem

flavor.value: "My father's eyes widened when they fell on the crown with the missing Shardsoul. His skin grew pale. His breath quickened. And that is when I realized he remembered more than he let on."—Tales of the Inferno

summary: Exile's Diadem is an uncommon [[Clanless]] equipment added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It grants a unit {{Capacity|-2}}.

title: Glass Cannon

flavor.value: As powerful as this weapon is, it is just as fragile. Handle with care.

summary: Glass Cannon is an uncommon [[Clanless]] equipment. It grants {{Attack|50}}, but also applies {{IconLink|Fragile}}, causing the equipped unit to die instantly on losing {{Health}}.

title: Iron-tongue

effect.value:
{{IconLink|Sweep}}.
This unit's {{Attack}} is set to '''30''' and cannot be changed.

flavor.value: "I used to think my father was naive for believing peace was possible. Until one day I stumbled upon a weapon in the dunes of Limbo that had both angelic and demonic markings."—Tales of the Inferno

summary: Iron-tongue is an uncommon [[Clanless]] equipment added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It grants a unit {{IconLink|Sweep}} while fixing its {{Attack}} to 30. This value is unaffected by {{IconLink|Rage}}, {{IconLink|Sap}} or any other status effects, though it can still be multiplied by {{IconLink|Multistrike}}.

title: Meat Shield

flavor.value: A small plate made for the Bone Dog during a birthday 'paint your own ceramics' party.

summary: Meat Shield is an uncommon [[Clanless]] equipment. It grants {{Health|15}}, and heals {{Health|10}} at the end of each round of combat.

title: Stoic Platemail

flavor.value: A suit of armor tailor-made for warriors whose bark is louder than their bite.

summary: Stoic Platemail is an uncommon [[Clanless]] equipment. It applies a significant amount of {{Health}} and {{Armor}}, but also applies {{IconLink|Silence}} to the user.

title: Swiftsteel Dagger

flavor.value: Angels and Hellborne used all kinds of armaments, but only the Angels made them to be this sleek.

summary: Swiftsteel Dagger is an uncommon [[Clanless]] equipment. It grants {{Attack|+15}} and {{IconLink|Quick}}.

title: Equalizing Rings

effect.value: This unit's {{Attack}} is equal to its max health.

flavor.value: Two gold rings that might have once belonged to a couple who loved each other with a deep, true love. Along the edge, there is a faint inscription and the words 'for my beloved' can be read.

summary: Equalizing Rings is a Clanless equipment card. It sets the unit's {{Attack}} equal to its {{Health}}, and overrides every other effect in the game that would change the unit's {{Attack}}.

title: Heph's Hammer

flavor.value: What was once Herzal's hammer, it has now passed down to his daughter Heph. Over the years, it forged the Rail and the trains that ride it, yet it shows no signs of wear.

summary: Heph's Hammer is a rare [[Clanless]] equipment obtained in the [[Heph's Blueprints (event)|Heph's Blueprints]] event. It gives its wielder {{Attack|+20}}, and gives them a {{IconLink|Slay}} trigger that adds {{Capacity|+1}} to the floor.

title: Overgrowth Carapace

effect.value: {{IconLink|Resolve}}: Gain {{Capacity|+1}}, {{Attack|+20}}, and {{Health|+20}} if there is {{Capacity}} available.

flavor.value: Don't think too hard about what is in this supplement. Just know that it will certainly make you FEEL stronger.

tables: Fixed an [[Overgrowth Carapace]] bug allowing upgrade to apply to a unit's card when the spawned unit was no longer eligible.
summary: Overgrowth Carapace is a rare [[Clanless]] equipment card that is primarily obtained at the [[Merchants#Merchant of Arms|Merchant of Arms]]. On [[Resolve]], a unit with this equipment will attempt to grow in size, gaining {{AttackHealth|+20|+20}} and {{Capacity|+1}} if the floor has empty {{Capacity}}.

title: Stasis Crystal

effect.value:
{{IconLink|Stasis}}.
{{IconLink|Resolve}}: Gain {{Attack|+20}}, and {{Health|+20}} while under {{IconLink|Stasis}}.
{{AbilityBox|Emerge|1|Remove {{IconLink|Stasis}}. Starts battle on cooldown. Removes ability on use.}}

flavor.value: "I am happy the Exiles escaped and all, but...how? Have the Shardsouls been weakened by the corruption? If so, who knows what else might escape..."—Tales of the Inferno

tables: [[Stasis Crystal]] ability 'Emerge' initial cooldown reduced from 3 >>> 1.
summary: Stasis Crystal is a rare [[Clanless]] equipment added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It places the target unit in {{IconLink|Stasis}}, during which the unit gains {{AttackHealth|+20|+20}} per turn. After 1 turn, the Emerge ability can be activated to remove {{IconLink|Stasis}}.

title: Void Armament

effect.value: {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}}. {{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Purge this unit from your deck.

flavor.value: When Void shards were first found, they were considered to be of little value. No one expected that they could be pulled together in a weapon that doubled any attack's force.

summary: Void Armament is a rare [[Clanless]] equipment. It grants {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, but will purge any unit that dies with it equipped. Note that Void Armament itself will not be purged, only the unit holding it.

title: Boiler Room

flavor.value: Herzal's original design was for the trains to be fueled only by the Pyre. Heph's updated design allows the train to be fueled by traditional methods as well, making the system more efficient overall.

summary: Boiler Room is an uncommon [[Clanless]] room. All units that die in that room give you {{Ember|1}}.

title: Enchanted Chamber

flavor.value: Building the train was a true test of engineering. But not all solutions could be hammered away. Sometimes it's useful to know a thing or two about magic.

summary: Enchanted Chamber is an uncommon [[Clanless]] room. It grants +15 [[Magic Power]] to all spells played in that room.

title: Fight Club

flavor.value: First rule: don't talk about it.

summary: Fight Club is an uncommon [[Clanless]] room. It grants {{Attack|+15}} to all friendly units.

title: Steward's Quarters

effect.value: {{Capacity|+1}}. '''[[Shield Steward]]''' and '''[[Spear Steward]]''' units gain {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} and {{Attack|+20}}.

flavor.value: Once the train car where Herzal kept his creations, Heph now tinkers deep into the night on her father's Stewards.

summary: Steward's Quarters is an uncommon [[Clanless]] room. It gives {{Attack|+20}} and {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} to [[:Category:Steward units|Train Stewards]] (but not to [[Railforged]] Automaton units with "Steward" in their names), and increases the room's {{Capacity}} by 1 when played.

title: Weapons Cache

effect.value: When you summon a friendly unit, draw an [[Equipment]] and apply {{Ember|-2}}.

flavor.value:
"Although I do not know who forged these weapons, I do know the Skull Crusher's armory always seemed to know when I needed them most."
—Tales of the Inferno

summary: Weapons Cache is an uncommon [[Clanless]] room added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. When you summon a friendly unit in the room, you draw a random [[Equipment]] card from your deck and apply {{Ember|-2}}.

title: Echo Vault

effect.value: At the end of the turn, the last spell played on this floor is played again.

flavor.value: "Any good spell is one that repeats itself," she murmured. The Stone before her hand seemed to drain, no, absorb her magic. The wall trembled, just like a bowstring being pulled back.

tables: Fixed an issue with [[Echo Vault]] incorrectly recasting X Cost spells with zero ember. Disallowed Infusion spells being recast by [[Echo Vault]]. Infusion cards are not meant to be copy-able for any reason. Fixed an issue with [[Echo Vault]] targeting when recasting [[Tiresome Climb]] spell into an empty unit position.

Fixed an undo issue affecting certain spells recast by [[Echo Vault]]. Fixed [[Echo Vault]] previewing a Boss deathblow incorrectly disabling further hand card interaction. Fixed [[Echo Vault]] incorrectly applying [[Freezestone]] bonus on recast spells. Fixed [[Echo Vault]] incorrectly sacrificing non-imp targets when recasting '[[Imp-portant Work]]'.
Fixed [[Mix]] spells breaking Undo feature when recast by [[Echo Vault]]. Fixed [[Echo Vault]] incorrectly resetting selected hand card after casting a spell.

Fixed [[Echo Vault]] not correctly previewing unit {{IconLink|Incant|bold=f}} effects for its recast spell. Fixed a bug with X cost spells upgraded with {{IconLink|Holystone|bold=f}} when recast by [[Echo Vault]]. Fixed undo of [[Echo Vault]] with [[Offering Token]] showing choice at start of turn.
summary: Echo Vault is a rare [[Clanless]] room added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It causes the last spell played on its floor to be played again at the end of the turn.

title: Hall of Mirrors

effect.value: {{Capacity|-2}}. When you play a unit, create a copy of it.

flavor.value:
"This one took a bit of creative engineering. Anything you put in here, you get another one back. Neat trick, eh?"
—Heph

tables: Create a copy of friendly units on Summon. >>> When you play a unit, create a copy of it.
summary: Hall of Mirrors is a rare [[Clanless]] room. It decreases the floor's {{Capacity}} by 2 when played but creates a copy of any units played.

title: Inferno Room

effect.value: Deal '''50''' damage to all units at the start of combat.

flavor.value: Let's just say that if you spray Pyregel everywhere, things tend to get a bit... 'fiery'.

summary: Inferno Room is a rare [[Clanless]] room. It deals 50 damage to all units, friendly and enemy, at the start of combat. This damage is not [[Piercing]], but it is not considered magic damage and so it ignores {{IconLink|Spell Shield}}.

title: Spell Sanctum

flavor.value:
"Carved these runes myself. A bit of magic here, and some engineerin' there."
—Heph

summary: Spell Sanctum is a rare [[Clanless]] room. It makes [[Spell]]s played on its floor cost {{Ember|-1}}.

title: Zone of Silence

flavor.value: A space made for silent meditation.

summary: Zone of Silence is a rare [[Clanless]] room. It applies {{IconLink|Silence}} to non-boss enemy units on the floor.

title: Calcified Ember

flavor.value: Most Ember, a byproduct of the energy within the Pyre, was encased in stone and ice when Hell froze. This made it inaccessible, and unusable, by our train.

tables: Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Calcified Ember is a playable [[Blights|Blight]]. At [[Covenant Ranks|Covenant 6]] and higher, each set of card rewards will randomly choose one card to add a Calcified Ember to the deck if chosen. It is also generated by [[Perkeo]]. It will be permanently removed from your deck if played, but is expensive to do so.

title: Dante's Candle

flavor.value: I've seen Dante roam beyond the walls of the Outpost, collecting souls to store and burn when he most needs them.

tables: Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' with no gameplay changes from the previous game, but new art.
summary: Dante's Candle is a playable [[Blights|Blight]]. It is obtained from [[Dante the Dependable]]'s {{IconLink|Summon}} trigger, and cannot be removed from your deck afterwards. It deals 3 damage to your Pyre on [[Reserve]].

title: Deadweight

flavor.value: A chunk of the Pyre now devoid of any power. It just takes up space and is a bit of an eyesore. I've been unable to remove it from the train due to its enormous size and weight.

tables: Added '''{{PAGENAME}}''' without changes from the previous game.
summary: Deadweight is an unplayable [[Blights|Blight]]. It is obtained from the Mutator [[Heavy]]. It can also be obtained as a negative modifier in [[Endless Mode]] in Monster Train 2.

title: Dominion's Eye

effect.value:
'''[[Unpurgeable]]'''.
Non-Scourge and non-Blight cards in hand cost {{Ember|+1}}.

flavor.value: When I first saw Dominion's effect on my fellow angels, I thought I had fallen into a nightmare. For their bodies were no longer their own, torn apart and reassembled by monster limbs.

summary: Dominion's Eye is a playable [[Blights|Blight]]. It is obtained from the [[Celestial Alcove]] event [[Fountain of Dominion]], in which the player can opt to take a powerful unit upgrade ({{IconLink|Dominating Power}}, {{IconLink|Dominating Authority}}, or {{IconLink|Dominating Control}}) in exchange for adding the Blight to their deck.

title: Entropic Crystals

flavor.value: I've seen angels who were once my friends stumble from the weight of Entropy's possession: crystal shards that grow beneath the skin and pierce the body once full control has been established.

summary: Entropic Crystals is a playable [[Blights|Blight]]. It is obtained from a [[Entropy's Crystals|Celestial Alcove event]] in which the player can opt to take a powerful spell upgrade in exchange for adding the Blight to their deck. The effect of making all spells more expensive only lasts for the current combat; it does not permanently increase {{Ember}} costs.

title: Savage Shackles

flavor.value: To my knowledge, the effects of Savagery are more on the mind than on the body. A bloodlust consumes once peaceful angels and turns them into murderous monsters.

tables: Fixed [[Purified Soul Shard]] artifact and [[Savage Shackles]] blight modifying combined unit card cost incorrectly.
summary: Savage Shackles is a playable [[Blights|Blight]]. It is obtained from the [[Celestial Alcove]] event [[Savagery's Statue]], in which the player can opt to take a powerful unit upgrade ({{IconLink|Savage Skin}}, {{IconLink|Savage Heart}}, or {{IconLink|Savage Spirit}}) in exchange for adding this deployable Blight to their deck. The Blight will be drawn during the [[Deployment Phase]] and will then be shuffled into the deck on the subsequent turn.

title: Vengeful Shard

flavor.value: When Hell was frozen, the Pyre itself was largely extinguished. The remains that I was unable to collect have been scattered throughout Hell, with Seraph controlling most of them. Some have been corrupted entirely, lashing out at their previous host if they come into too close of contact.

summary: Vengeful Shard is a playable [[Blights|Blight]]. The player's deck starts with two copies when playing at [[Covenant Ranks|Covenant 5]] or higher, and an additional Shard is added to the deck after each combat when using the [[Pyre of Entropy]].

title: Chime of Despair

flavor.value: ''Before being turned by Dominion those lost souls claimed to first hear the faint sound of a bell.''

summary: Chime of Despair is a playable [[Scourges|Scourge]]. It is obtained from [[Lurking Miscreant|Lurking Miscreants]]. It does nothing, and is permanently Purged if played. Like all Scourges, it is permanently removed from your deck at the end of the battle.

title: Curse of Entropy

effect.value:
'''[[Ephemeral]]'''.
Apply {{IconLink|Sap|4}} to friendly units on all floors.
'''[[Reserve]]''': Your Pyre takes '''3''' damage.

flavor.value: The Titans, within their nature, each worked towards their own twisted form of peace. For Entropy, eternal peace can only be achieved through the stasis of all things.

summary: Curse of Entropy is a playable [[Scourges|Scourge]]. It can either be played at the cost of applying significant {{IconLink|Sap}} to all your units, or if left unplayed at turn end, it will damage your Pyre and remove itself. It is obtained from [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]] or [[Entropy]] in [[Clash with the Titans]]. Both bosses shuffle Curse of Entropy into your draw pile on {{IconLink|Resolve}}. This trigger can be blocked by {{IconLink|Mute}}.

title: Discordant Toll

flavor.value: As Dominion arrived upon Heaven its acolytes began to ring the bells, their hands bloodied until they could ring no more.

summary: Discordant Toll is a playable [[Scourges|Scourge]]. It is obtained from [[Profane Supplicant|Profane Supplicants]] and [[Chosen Supplicant|Chosen Supplicants]] ([[Covenant Ranks|Covenant 10]] only).

title: Resonant Ruin

flavor.value: Do you not hear the sound? It tolls for you, and the sweet embrace of madness.

summary: Resonant Ruin is a playable [[Scourges|Scourge]]. It is obtained from [[Discordant Heretic|Discordant Heretics]].
